items.title: The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST
items.abstract: The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. Here, we compare both self-consistent radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) and retrieval atmosphere models to high-SNR 1--18~$μ$m spectra of two field L-dwarfs from JWST, J0624 (L5) and J2148 (L6--L6.5). Our observations include spectral features from H$_2$O, CO, CO$_2$, CH$_4$, Na, and K and cover approximately 98\% of the outgoing thermal emission from the two objects. We first compare the data to three independent grids of 1D-RCE models: BT-Settl, exoREM, and Sonora Diamondback. While exoREM provides the best fit of the grid models, no 1D-RCE model provides a satisfactory fit to the data, highlighting the complexity of fitting cloudy L-dwarf spectra. Nonetheless, the temperature and cloud properties can be constrained with the 1D-RCE models, while metallicity, C/O ratio, and surface gravity are not well-measured. Next, we use petitRADTRANS to retrieve atmosphere and cloud properties, finding strong evidence for the presence of SiO$_2$ clouds in both objects. The SiO$_2$ is found to be amorphous in structure for J0624 but crystalline in J2148, highlighting important differences in objects of similar spectral type. We also used a non-Bayesian optimization framework to explore a wider variety of cloud scenarios, finding evidence for the inclusion of iron-rich magnesium silicates (Mg$_{0.5}$Fe$_{0.5}$SiO$_3$, MgFeSiO$_4$) in addition to SiO$_2$ in both objects. These results show both the complexity and diversity of brown dwarf cloud properties, while also highlighting the constraining power of broad-wavelength JWST observations of cloudy L-dwarfs.

items.title: Combining TTVs, RVs, and astrometry to characterize distant giant companions of transiting hot Jupiters: Application to WASP-4
items.abstract: The origins and architectures of hot Jupiter (HJ) systems remain unclear, with potential explanations for the tight orbits being in-situ formation, disk-migration, or high-eccentricity migration. These mechanisms can leave different imprints on the orbital architecture, but tidal interactions act to erase these imprints for HJs, leading to orbital circularization, realignment, and potentially orbital decay. The latter can be mimicked by the introduction of light travel-time effects (LTTE) caused by an outer giant companion, as for WASP-4$\,$b. We examine the WASP-4 system using newly obtained ESO$\,$3.6/HARPS radial velocity (RV) observations and archival transit-timing data, leveraging the LTTE. Furthermore, we present a novel approach of analyzing HJ systems in sight of $\textit{Gaia}$'s Data Release 4. We propose combining RV, transit-timing, and astrometry data, making use of the LTTE as a proxy for the orbital motion of a possible outer companion. We combine and fit all currently available data and simulate $\textit{Gaia}$ DR4 and DR5 astrometric measurements of WASP-4 and perform an injection and recovery procedure to estimate their impact on the recovered planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c. The procedure employs a combined model that describes RVs, transit timing variations (TTVs) via the LTTE, and astrometry simultaneously. Analyzing the existing data, we improve the planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c, finding a minimum mass of $9.3\pm1.7\,M_\mathrm{Jup}$ with an orbital period of $10\,600^{+1100}_{-1000}\,$d, or about $29\,$yr. Furthermore, we find that there is no significant orbital decay taking place for WASP-4$\,$b. In simulations of $\textit{Gaia}$ DR5, our three-pronged approach reduces the error bars of WASP-4$\,$c's parameters by about $10\%$, $25\%$, and $33\%$ for its orbital period, time of inferior conjunction, and RV semi-amplitude, respectively. items.title: Global climate modeling of the Martian water cycle. I) Improved parameterizations of physical processes
items.abstract: We implement four new physical parameterizations relevant to the water cycle in the Mars PCM (previously Mars Laboratoire de M{é}t{é}orologie Dynamique GCM)\,: the latent heat of ground ice sublimation, a temperature-dependent nucleation scheme in cloud microphysics, differentiated albedos for water frost and perennial ice and scavenging of water ice clouds by CO2 particle formation. After a new tuning of the poorly known model parameters, we find that combining these parameterizations allows for an improved agreement of the modeled water cycle compared to Thermal Emission Spectrometer column-integrated vapor and ice retrievals. We show that latent heat cooling prevents the formation of surface liquid water at present and likely in the recent past on Mars. Using two albedos corrects the overestimation of the northern sublimation event, a major defect of the model. Our study highlights that each parameterization has indirect consequences amplified by the radiatively active clouds. We stress that the increasingly complex water cycle in the Mars PCM should be studied in the future using numerical methods tailored for climate modeling, in addition to the effect of each individual component.

items.title: Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities
items.abstract: Research on pay dispersion has long asked whether unequal rewards increase or depress performance. Tournament theory expects stronger effort, while social comparison accounts expect withdrawal. Both perspectives, however, treat performance as a single scale on which workers can be ranked. Scientific work often resists such ordering. Some contributions extend recognized lines of inquiry and can be evaluated against prevailing standards; others revise the frames through which value is judged and become legible only later. We argue that intellectual tournaments more readily reward the first kind of contribution than the second. Pay dispersion may therefore be associated not only with how much scholars produce but also with what kinds of intellectual exploration are encouraged. We test this argument with administrative payroll records for 105,050 tenure-line faculty in 4,839 departments at 93 U.S. public universities from 2004 to 2026, linked to publication histories in OpenAlex. For each department, we estimate a separate pay equation using rank, contract basis, and seniority, then measure the Gini of the salary variation this local ladder cannot explain. Scholars in departments with greater unexplained pay dispersion publish more papers and receive more citations, but their work is less disruptive, less novel, and more conventional. Additional analyses show that compensation premiums above the ladder go disproportionately to scholars with broad collaborations and topical breadth. Although the design cannot fully separate treatment from selection, the evidence shows that inequality is not only a distributional outcome but also an evaluative structure, shaping which forms of knowledge are recognized, rewarded, and reproduced within organizations and communities.

items.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
items.abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2σ$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

items.title: Validating Updated Precession and Nutation Formulations for the Next IERS Conventions
items.abstract: An international effort via the IAU/IAG Joint Working Group on Consistent Improvement of Earth's Rotation Theory (CIERT) aims to update the nutation theory to meet the milliarcsecond accuracy required by GGOS. While a companion article provides the theoretical background to the proposed precession-nutation corrections, this work presents their VLBI-based observational validation. The analysis systematically evaluates the revised models within practical application in VLBI analysis. These results provide critical empirical input for the upcoming integration of consistent, validated Earth rotation models into the next IERS Conventions.

items.title: Persistent structural regimes in Bitcoin transactions relate to market cycles
items.abstract: Bitcoin's blockchain is a public record of every on-chain transaction, while the price of bitcoin is set by trading on external markets. We ask whether on-chain activity alone reveals regimes associated with market trends, and whether this association remains stable over time. We summarise each week of blockchain activity from 2012 to 2026 using four measures of transaction structure and fit a two-state hidden semi-Markov model without price data. The sole market-informed constraint is an asymmetry in regime persistence, motivated by the observation that Bitcoin's price increases tend to outlast its declines. During earlier market cycles, the inferred regimes exhibit distinct transaction structures and align with periods of rising and falling prices more closely than random sequences with the same regime-duration distributions. The ongoing downturn, however, breaks this correspondence: the blockchain remains in the longer-lived regime, while its transaction structure resembles neither previous downturns nor previous upturns. Our findings support a relationship between on-chain activity and market dynamics, while highlighting its potentially time-dependent nature.

items.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Spacecraft performance in the L2 environment
items.abstract: The Euclid mission was designed around the need for thermo-optical and mechanical stability, stray-light suppression, low outgassing, and precise guiding. After three years in space, a wealth of data is available to assess the performance in these areas. We review the L2 halo-orbit design and consumables budget. Solar stray-light gradually increases by 14\% per year and is consistent with meteoroid puncturing, but remains low overall. Data loss from high solar activity has declined notably since the maximum of the 25th Solar cycle passed. The thermodynamical response of the optical elements to a thermal step impulse follows sigmoidal growth curves, entering the asymptotic equilibration regime after 21--46 hours. Water-ice contamination has affected data from both instruments and requires continued monitoring; we review detection and decontamination methods, and Euclid's contamination history. High-precision measurements of the zodiacal background reveal, at eight sigma significance, the subtle modulation caused by the changing perspective on the dust distribution due to the L2 halo-orbit libration. These data also show that conservative pre-launch estimates overestimated the out-of-field stray-light by factors of 4 (H band) to 27 (I band). Telemetry data demonstrate excellent guiding, and enable highly significant detections of solar radiation pressure and of thermal-emission recoil from Euclid's unilluminated dark sides. Lastly, we present a list of 34 meteoroid impacts, discuss their mechanical and optical signatures, and derive a minimum detectable impactor mass of 5e-7 g.

items.title: Scale-rich network metamaterials grow by local rules on a recursive cell division
items.abstract: Scale-rich (SR) metamaterials are planar ligament networks grown by nucleating a segment at a random point and angle and extending it until it meets the existing structure. In the dual graph, where ligaments are nodes and junctions are links, the degree distribution has a $k^{-3}$ tail. We show that the SR construction is Cowan's iterated cell division with area-weighted selection, so the cell genealogy is a random binary search tree, and that the dual grows by a face-local rule: a new node joins two nodes on the boundary of one face. Preferential attachment on face incidences would give the Barabási--Albert law, but the geometry works differently. A ligament is hit in proportion to its length, fixed at birth, and its degree is close to a Poisson variable with mean $4\ell_i(\sqrt T-\sqrt i)/c_L$, without reinforcement. Length is a fitness assigned by the cell hierarchy, $\ell_i\propto i^{-1/2}$, and the $k^{-3}$ tail follows. Integral geometry gives the probability that a new ligament cuts off a corner of its cell, which sets the triangle closure and the clustering spectrum $C(k)\simeq2p/k$. Square-closing splits raise the shortest-path multiplicity above its value at fixed degree sequence. Thickness, jamming, angle sets and density gradients leave $γ=3$; coherent orientation fields give $γ\simeq2.4$--$2.5$. For plates in three dimensions the fitness is the birth area and $γ=5/2$, whereas preferential attachment would give $2.44$; fluctuation tests select the fitness mechanism. The reported per-ligament energy law cannot distinguish degree from length or age.

items.title: Inheritance of Connectivity: Modeling Higher-Order Dynamic Networks with the Birth-Death Process
items.abstract: Higher-order networks extend pairwise interactions to represent group relationships and provide a useful framework for modeling complex systems. Understanding their dynamic evolution is important for explaining emergent structural and functional properties. However, constructing dynamic higher-order network models with stable topology remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a higher-order dynamic network model based on an inheritance-based deletion (IBAD) mechanism, which probabilistically redistributes connections when nodes or hyperedges are removed. The model combines birth-death dynamics with preferential attachment, enabling the analysis of evolving higher-order systems. Inheritance is guided by a Gaussian similarity measure based on the distance between degree histories. We derive stationary population distributions and conditional relations for connection retention and degree evolution. Simulation results show that the model generates networks with statistically stable node and hyperedge populations and heterogeneous degree distributions. The degree distributions and local clustering can be adjusted through the node and hyperedge attachment parameters. Comparisons with alternative mechanisms show that inheritance enhances connectivity relative to direct deletion, while the similarity measure influences degree heterogeneity. Comparisons with empirical networks from ecological and communication systems quantify distributional differences using Jensen-Shannon and Kullback-Leibler divergences and reveal discrepancies in clustering and within-hyperedge node-pair counts. These results provide a framework for studying population stability and structural evolution in dynamic higher-order networks.

items.title: Tracing dependency networks explains how origins shape downstream vulnerability
items.abstract: Many systems sustain outcomes through chains of prerequisites, yet these dependencies are often partially observed. We trace backward from sampled outcomes to recover dependency structure and measure edge importance by the fraction of outcomes lost after an edge fails. Across 1,620 synthetic networks, revealing 90% of origins required tracing 7.24% of outcomes on average. We define pair thickness as the number of origin and outcome pairs connected through an edge. Under strict dependency, where every input is necessary, thickness counts each affected outcome once per upstream origin, whereas loss counts it once. Edges therefore form origin groups with distinct thickness and loss relations, also seen in software, citation and river topologies. Within a network, greater origin diversity corresponds to lower strict loss at equal complete thickness. We develop a growth model that predicts how edges populate these groups and how losses are distributed under partial observation, tested on 2,560 independent networks. Separating origin counts from downstream reach improves identification of edges causing the greatest losses among unsampled outcomes in strict synthetic tests. Substitutable inputs reduce losses and change which importance scores perform best. Edge importance thus measures a dependency's contribution to sustaining later outcomes, guiding the protection of critical connections.

items.title: C$_2$ Swan, CH and CN emission, surface temperature and luminous efficiency of the Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule from ground-based spectroscopy
items.abstract: The Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule entered the atmosphere over South Australia on 5 December 2020 at 12 km/s. A slitless spectral video, taken from the ground with a hand-tracked consumer camera, shows the capsule alone from 80 to 49 km. In the first ten seconds of heating the shock layer emits the CN violet system, the CH A-X band and the C$_2$ Swan bands, the latter for the first time in remote observations of a capsule entry. C$_2$ ($T_{\rm rot}\approx9200$ K, $T_{\rm vib}\approx7800$ K) and CN (about 7000 K) are far hotter than the surface. C$_2$ and CH disappear while the heat flux is still rising and CN persists, which we relate to the early pyrolysis of the carbon-phenolic ablator and to the changing boundary-layer chemistry. The colour temperature of the heat shield rises from 2720 to 3080 K, in agreement with airborne results. The radiated energy is one to two orders of magnitude below that of natural fireballs, because the light comes from the hot surface rather than from ablation vapour. A faint persistent train lights up about 1 s after the passage and fades within a few seconds, probably chemiluminescence in the cooling wake.

items.title: Decisions at the end of the world
items.abstract: International treaties are often described as tigers without teeth, failing to secure compliance or change outcomes. Cooperation also depends on how states maintain the rules they have already made -- especially where no sovereign stands above the states. Here we map more than six decades of decision-making under the Antarctic Treaty, linking submitted proposals to recorded responses and tracing how instruments act on earlier ones. Shared references tie decisions together across the agenda. Recurring revision concentrates in specialised histories, above all the management of protected areas, beyond what activity, popularity and reference age predict. Periodic administrative reviews retire outdated instruments in bulk, joining otherwise separate histories without coordinating policy across subjects. Binding Measures build overwhelmingly on earlier Measures, with little direct succession from non-binding Resolutions. Distinguishing these layers shows how a shared rule system is sustained by consensus, and provides a basis for comparing cooperation across global commons.

items.title: Self-Consistent Microscopic Description of the 146Sm Half-Life for Early Solar System Chronology
items.abstract: The extinct \textit{p}-process radionuclide $^{146}$Sm, decaying to $^{142}$Nd, is a key short-lived chronometer for the formation and early evolution of terrestrial planets and planetesimals. However, there has been a long-standing discrepancy in both the experimental measurements and the theoretical evaluations of the $^{146}$Sm half-life. To address this, a self-consistent microscopic framework for $α$ decay is developed in this work, in which the $α$ particle is treated as a four-nucleon quartet. Its formation amplitude in the nuclear interior is constructed from a coherent superposition of multiple pure single-particle configurations weighted by the pairing occupation amplitudes. Coupling this shell amplitude to the $α$ cluster that survives in the low-density surface region yields a self-consistently determined two-state (shell~$\oplus$~cluster) preformation weight and effective potential. The calculated half-lives for the neighboring emitters of $^{146}$Sm are in good agreement with the measured values. Cross-validation over the neighboring emitters reproduces each excluded half-life without any nucleus-specific adjustment, and yields $^{146}$Sm predictions consistent to within $\pm 6\%$ of the resulting half-life $T_{1/2}=75.1^{+6.1}_{-5.6}$~Ma. This provides a solid calibration for theoretical studies of the early solar system.

items.title: Synthetic torpor in the rat protects the heart from ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
items.abstract: During times of environmental stress, many animals enter torpor: a reversible protective physiological state typically characterised by reductions in core temperature, heart rate, and oxygen consumption. Species that naturally enter this hypothermic and hypometabolic state are tolerant of ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Consequently, there is a growing interest in utilising aspects of torpor for clinical applications such as protection from stroke or myocardial infarction. It is currently unknown, however, whether a torpor-like state is protective in animals that do not naturally enter torpor. Using viral vector-mediated chemogenetic activation of the medial preoptic area of the hypothalamus, we induced synthetic torpor in the rat, a species that does not naturally enter torpor. We demonstrate this state is cardioprotective in an ex vivo ischaemia-reperfusion injury model with an ~40% reduction in infarct size. Synthetic torpor-induced cardioprotection of the normothermic, isolated heart is not dependent on prior hypothermia in vivo. Phosphoproteomic analysis of cardiac tissue indicates that the protective effects of synthetic torpor may be mediated by parallel activation of cell survival and stress tolerance pathways and inhibition of cell death pathways. These findings provide important insights into the mechanisms of organ protective effects of synthetic torpor states with implications for future clinical translation in humans.

items.title: Glia and CED-1/MEGF10 independently drive dopamine neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease models.
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is marked by progressive dopamine neuron degeneration, but the phagocytic receptors and cells that clear neuronal corpses remain ill-defined. Moreover, while other cell types like glia, epithelia, and muscle are also impacted in PD, their roles in disease progression are unclear. We report that multiple nonneuronal cell types modulate dopamine neurodegeneration in Caenorhabditis elegans. Astrocyte-like CEPsh glia respond to neuronal stress and regulate dopamine biosynthesis enzyme CAT-2/TH and transporter DAT-1/SLC6A3. They are neurotoxic by downregulating neuroprotective dopamine levels. Degenerating dopamine neurons expose phosphatidylserine (PS) via the necrotic phospholipid scramblase ANOH-1/TMEM16F and ABC transporter CED-7/ABCA1. Epithelia and muscle cells then phagocytose dopamine neuron corpses and drive neuron death and clearance via the conserved PS receptor CED-1/Draper/MEGF10. Depleting ced-1 protects against loss of dopamine neurons and associated animal behaviors in a PD model. Evolutionary conservation of the underlying components and their effects across PD models suggests that multi-organ engagement may be a shared feature of dopamine neurodegeneration in PD.

items.title: Learning-associated flexibility of cortical taste coding is impaired in Shank3 knockout mice.
items.abstract: The ability to update the valence of sensory perception to influence behavior is crucial for survival. A common phenotype in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) is defects in sensory processing, but whether these defects impair flexible sensory encoding is largely unexplored. In particular, how genetic risk factors such as Shank3 deletion affect the adaptability of cortical taste processing and downstream behavior is unknown. To address this gap, we performed two-photon calcium imaging during a conditioned taste aversion (CTA) learning paradigm, an ethologically relevant form of associative learning that depends on taste processing in the gustatory cortex (GC), to examine how Shank3 knockout alters taste-related neuronal activity in GC and influences CTA learning. We found that GC neurons in Shank3 knockout mice exhibited reduced stimulus-evoked suppression and increased trial-to-trial correlated variability during the acquisition of CTA memory. These activity changes, which likely reduced signal-to-noise ratio in GC, were associated with slower CTA acquisition in Shank3 knockout mice. In both genotypes, CTA learning enhanced, while subsequent extinction reduced, taste discriminability in GC, and both extinction and the associated reduction in discriminability were faster in Shank3 knockout than in wild-type mice. Together, these results show that Shank3 loss is associated with destabilized cortical activity dynamics in GC, which may contribute to inefficient encoding and maintenance of learned taste aversion. These findings show that loss of Shank3 compromises the ability of animals to update behavior to incorporate negative outcomes, and suggest this loss of flexibility may be an important feature of monogenic ASDs.

items.title: Association Between Stroke Subtype and Outcomes of Edaravone Dexborneol: A Subgroup Analysis of the EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) Study.
items.abstract: Background The effectiveness of edaravone dexborneol among acute ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We evaluated its association with clinical outcomes by stroke subtype. Methods This secondary analysis of the prospective EXPAND (Effectiveness and Safety of Edaravone Dexborneol in Acute Ischemic Stroke) study included patients with acute ischemic stroke treated at 72 Chinese stroke centers from December 2022 to October 2023. Patients were classified as having large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) or non-LAA stroke and grouped by edaravone dexborneol use. Primary outcomes were 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 or 1 and 0 to 2 and ordinal mRS shift. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality, intracranial hemorrhage, and in-hospital adverse events. Results Among 4401 patients, 1061 (24.1%) had LAA and 3340 (75.9%) had non-LAA stroke; the median age was 65 years, and 66.8% were men. Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in the non-LAA group, including higher odds of achieving mRS 0 or 1 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.25 [95% CI, 1.06-1.47]), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.15-1.71]), and a favorable mRS shift (aOR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; all P P =0.50), mRS 0 to 2 (aOR, 0.88; P =0.43), or mRS shift (aOR, 0.92; P =0.50). Significant interactions were observed between edaravone dexborneol and stroke subtype ( P for interaction=0.03 for mRS 0 or 1, P =0.005 for mRS 0 to 2, and P =0.009 for favorable mRS shift). Safety outcomes were comparable between treatment groups. Conclusions Edaravone dexborneol was associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in non-LAA but not LAA stroke.

items.title: A patent review of GDF15 inhibitors 2020-present.
items.abstract: Introduction Growth/differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) is a secretory protein of the TGF-β superfamily that signals through the GFRAL/RET receptor complex. It plays a dual role in metabolic regulation and immune tolerance, with elevated levels frequently associated with chronic inflammatory conditions, advanced cancer, and cachexia. Area covered This review analyzes the patent landscape for GDF15 inhibitors from January 2020 to present. The patents reviewed were originally written in English and classified according to different functional categories and disease types. We searched for 'GDF15 inhibitor' on Patentscope and Espacenet. Expert opinion Monoclonal antibodies currently dominate the landscape due to their high specificity and favorable safety profile, showing significant clinical promise in treating cancer cachexia and overcoming resistance to checkpoint inhibitors. However, challenges such as high production costs and the need for parenteral delivery and its consequences are driving a shift in the research toward simpler molecular structures. Emerging trends suggest that peptides and peptidomimetics offer a viable alternative by maintaining high selectivity while being available through cost-effective synthesis that also allows for tunable properties.

items.title: Proteomics and Risk of Incident Ischemic Stroke: Meta-Analysis of the ARIC Study and CHS.
items.abstract: Background Ischemic stroke preventive therapies have been slow to emerge due to a limited understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. We aimed to discover new protein risk factors that are potential etiologic factors and may be candidates for therapeutic intervention. Methods We included ARIC study (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) and CHS (Cardiovascular Health Study) participants without prevalent stroke at the time of proteomic profiling (1990-1992 in ARIC and 1992-1993 in CHS). Relative concentrations of proteins in blood were assessed with aptamers (n=4954). Ischemic stroke events were adjudicated through 2019 in ARIC and 2015 in CHS. Study-specific Cox regression adjusting for ischemic stroke risk factors was used to estimate associations between proteins and incident ischemic stroke. Study-specific estimates were combined using fixed-effects meta-analysis. Replication was conducted in 2 independent cohorts (AGES-Reykjavik, UK Biobank). Proteins with a false discovery rate q value Results Median follow-up was 25 and 12 years in ARIC and CHS. 1397 out of 14 139 (10%) participants experienced an ischemic stroke. 44 proteins were significantly associated with ischemic stroke risk ( P -5 ), of which 26 are novel. In 2 independent cohorts, 37 (84%) associations were directionally concordant, and 26 (59%) met criteria for replication. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested MMP12 (matrix metallopeptidase-12) and CNTN1 (contactin-1) may be causally related to ischemic stroke risk. In multivariable Mendelian randomization analyses, higher MMP12 levels had a direct protective effect on ischemic stroke risk, while CNTN1 had a direct harmful effect. Conclusions This proteomic and genomic investigation of ischemic stroke identified novel risk biomarkers and 2 potential etiologic CNTN1 factors that are regulated in response to atherosclerosis and obesity. If future studies confirm our findings, these results may have implications for the development of new preventive therapies.

items.title: Pain management for the twenty-first century - reports from the 2025 meeting.
items.abstract: After the 17th 'Royal Marsden opioid, cannabinoid, and gabapentinoid conference,' it was time to reappraise the title and content of the meeting. Without AI help, I renamed this successful and lauded meeting, 'Pain Medicine for the 21st Century.' It amazes me that whomsoever I invite, no matter how renowned, all seem keen to come to the Royal Marsden to confer their expert knowledge. The first meeting with the new moniker attracted speakers of the highest quality, covering key aspects of pain medicine. The medications from the previous title were represented with novel, informative, and insightful talks with the additional category of psychedelics for pain included. Intrathecal pumps, findings of the recent POPPY study, topical analgesics, and the immune system in pain all added to the rich blend of thoughtful topics. Not only was psychology discussed, but the often ignored treatise of social factors in pain was deliberated. Add in pain after combat injuries, crossing the translational gulf, sodium channel blockers, and how we make research more trustworthy, and we have a magnificent maelstrom of instructional education. Enjoy. - Dr Paul Farquhar-Smith, Conference Chair of Pain Medicine for the twenty-first Century 2025.This Meeting Report shares summaries of the talks at Pain Medicine for the 21st Century 2025. items.title: Equipoise for Laminoplasty Versus Fusion for Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy: Is a Randomized Trial Feasible?
items.abstract: Background and objectives There is global variation and uncertainty regarding the utilization of laminoplasty in the treatment of patients with degenerative cervical spondylotic myelopathy. We asked whether clinical equipoise can be established among cervical spine surgeon experts for a possible trial comparing laminoplasty with fusion. Methods Fifty randomly selected cases from a cervical spondylotic myelopathy trial [NCT-02076113] were presented to 26 cervical spine experts to determine the suitability of randomization to laminoplasty vs fusion surgery. A brief clinical vignette, sagittal T2-weighted MRI, and appropriate axial images were reviewed by the experts. Each expert assessed the randomizability of each case and then stated the choice of approach: laminoplasty, fusion (anterior or posterior), arthroplasty, or no surgery. After 6 months, the same 50 cases were reviewed by all experts. Results Among 50 cases, 46 (92%) were deemed suitable for randomization by a simple majority at both time points. The response rate of the expert panel members was 100% at both time points. Among 2600 surgeon responses over 2 time points, experts stated their choice of approach as laminoplasty in 40% of instances and selected fusion (anterior or posterior) in 57% of cases. Temporal stability of decision-making was high with mean stability = 0.85 (SD = 0.09), indicating that surgeons generally maintained similar treatment decisions over 6 months. A subset (12 experts) of the expert panel who reviewed these 50 cases over 10 years ago demonstrated a significant increase in the preference for laminoplasty from 18% to 40% ( P Conclusion Among cervical spine experts, laminoplasty utilization has increased over 10 years. Global cervical spine experts demonstrate equipoise for comparing laminoplasty with fusion. The results suggest that a significant proportion of patients with cervical myelopathy would be eligible for a future trial and the results would be likely to affect global practice.

items.title: Simultaneous sPIV and PLIF characterization of diverse airborne odor plumes
items.abstract: Abstract Many animals must navigate airborne odor plumes for successful foraging, mating, and habitat selection, but such navigation presents a challenging task due in part to chaotic transport of the odor through turbulent air. Despite broad ecological, industrial, and environmental importance, experimental investigation of such plumes remains limited, due largely to significant technical challenges associated with acquiring gaseous plume measurements at sufficient spatiotemporal resolutions. Here, we use simultaneous stereo particle image velocimetry and planar laser-induced fluorescence to jointly measure time-resolved velocity and scalar concentration fields for airborne odors transported by low Reynolds number grid turbulence in a recirculating wind tunnel. We introduce six datasets, including a baseline case (isokinetic, freestream release with neutral buoyancy) and five cases with perturbations to the source configuration (size, mass flow rate, buoyancy, bed proximity) or flow configuration (turbulence grid geometry). For each case, we present representative instantaneous flow and odor fields along with select statistical properties, highlighting Gaussian mean plumes, single-point concentration PDFs well-characterized by one-parameter Gamma distributions, and turbulence intensities that exhibit a combination of grid turbulence and a wake structure from the source tube. Finally, we leverage the multimodal data to compute turbulent odor fluxes and illustrate the connection between the velocity-derived finite-time Lyapunov exponent field and evolving structures in the odor field. These high-resolution measurements provide a rich suite of experimental data for use in fundamental studies of plume dispersion, olfactory neuroscience, and odor navigation in the data-scarce regime of low Schmidt number, low Reynolds number scalar transport.

items.title: Electroconvulsive therapy for the treatment of depression: from convulsive treatment to precision neuromodulation.
items.abstract: Introduction ECT remains one of the most effective treatments for severe depression, including psychotic and treatment-resistant presentations and high-acuity cases requiring rapid response. This review examines ECT as a parameter-sensitive neuromodulation procedure rather than a fixed convulsive treatment. Areas covered We review historical development, clinical efficacy, safety, relapse prevention, and mechanistic models involving seizure induction, electric-field effects, inhibitory plasticity, neurochemical and neuroendocrine signaling, network change, and postictal brain states. The literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar from database inception to June 2026, supplemented by reference-list screening, with evidence evaluated according to study design, clinical relevance, and technological maturity. Established components of contemporary ECT practice are distinguished from near-term optimization strategies and experimental technologies. Expert opinion Precision ECT should be regarded as an emerging framework rather than an established standard of care. Patient-specific electric-field modeling, biomarker-guided dosing, amplitude optimization, and adaptive stimulation are promising strategies for improving the therapeutic index, but require prospective validation against optimized standard ECT using clinical, cognitive, and patient-reported outcomes.

items.title: Colourful psittacofulvin-containing parrot feathers do not resist bacterial degradation.
items.abstract: Animal colours are often associated with signalling, but these colours can also have important non-signalling functions. For example, melanin in black feathers has been shown to protect them against mechanical damage as well as bacterial degradation. This protection is critical to the myriad functions of feathers. However, whether other feather pigments play a similar role is unclear. Parrots (Order Psittaciformes) use unique pigments known as psittacofulvins to produce many of their colours, and previous work has suggested that these pigments might offer protection against bacterial degradation. To test this hypothesis, we performed experimental bacterial degradation of parrot feathers spanning a wide range of colours. Contrary to previous work, we found that feathers of psittacofulvin-based colours (red, yellow, orange, green) are more susceptible to bacterial degradation than feathers of other colours (black, blue, grey, white). Our results suggest that while incorporation of psittacofulvins into feathers allows parrots to produce a wide range of vibrant colours, it might also make these feathers more susceptible to bacterial attack.

items.abstract: Agricultural waters have been identified as one of the primary sources of Salmonella contamination, which has resulted in numerous outbreaks associated with the consumption of contaminated produce. Consequently, an improved understanding of Salmonella contamination of agricultural waters could facilitate the development of control strategies to prevent food contamination. The objective of this study was to examine the diversity and spatiotemporal recurrence of Salmonella isolates in surface water related to agricultural activities. Water samples ( n = 2,690) were collected between 2019 and 2024 in central Chile using modified Moore swabs, and whole-genome sequencing was carried out for 1 to 10 Salmonella isolates per sample. Non-clonal genomes from each sample ( n = 1,034) were analyzed, showing that the most frequently identified serovars were Infantis (14.6%), Typhimurium (10.8%), Newport (8.5%), and Enteritidis (5.8%). The highest antimicrobial resistance burden was shown by Salmonella Infantis, which carried up to 11 antimicrobial resistance genes simultaneously. Importantly, phylogenomic analyses revealed a highly clonal population structure among the most prevalent serovars and identified recurrent subpopulations that were repeatedly detected across multiple watersheds and consecutive years, including lineages associated with human infections. These findings provide genomic evidence that agricultural surface waters may serve as reservoirs and dissemination routes for recurrent Salmonella subpopulations in central Chile, including multidrug-resistant strains. Our work underscores the critical importance of continuous environmental surveillance and the integration of environmental and clinical genomic surveillance data to improve our understanding of the Salmonella ecology and inform evidence-based mitigation strategies aiming to protect public health.IMPORTANCE Salmonella enterica is a leading cause of foodborne illness worldwide, and contaminated irrigation water is an important pathway by which this pathogen can reach fresh produce. By analyzing more than 1,000 Salmonella genomes collected from agricultural waters in central Chile over 5 years, we found that specific bacterial lineages persisted across multiple watersheds and years, including multidrug-resistant strains linked to human infections. These findings indicate that agricultural surface waters in Chile can serve as reservoirs and dissemination routes for recurrent Salmonella subpopulations. Our study highlights the value of continuous environmental surveillance and the need to integrate data from environmental and human sources to identify potential contamination sources and reduce the risk of foodborne disease.

items.title: Karst habitat islands drove a largely nonadaptive and allopatric radiation in Petrocodon (Gesneriaceae).
items.abstract: Whether evolutionary radiations are primarily driven by ecological or neutral processes remains an unresolved question. The karst-endemic genus Petrocodon, distributed across southern China and northern Indochina, provides a powerful system for testing these alternatives. We generated whole-genome sequencing data for 54 of the 60 described species and integrated these with morphological, geographic, and paleoclimatic data to evaluate the relative roles of ecological and neutral processes in diversification. Our analyses revealed a robust nuclear phylogeny but extensive cytonuclear discordance, likely due to pervasive ancient hybridization and introgression. Macroevolutionary and biogeographic analyses indicate that diversification began during a favorable climatic period enabling range expansion, but subsequent species accumulation was primarily driven by geographic isolation and allopatric divergence rather than ecological niche differentiation. Morphological evolution decoupled from lineage diversification, with most morphological diversity accumulating relatively late. Further analyses support genetic drift in small, isolated populations driving morphological evolution, although stabilizing selection cannot be excluded, and reticulate evolution may have additionally contributed to phenotypic innovation. Together, these results support a largely nonadaptive radiation in Petrocodon, in which spatial opportunity played a central role in species accumulation, while demographic and reticulate processes may have contributed to its striking phenotypic diversity.

items.title: Dog-assisted scat sampling reveals genetic diversity, structure, and relatedness in black-footed cats ( Felis nigripes )
items.abstract: Advances in molecular techniques for non-invasive genetic sampling have strengthened wildlife genetics, enabling researchers to study elusive and difficult-to-study species with minimal disturbance, and conservation detection dogs can greatly increase sample numbers and the area covered. However, this combination is rarely used in Africa and has perhaps never been applied to a small carnivore on the continent. Here we use dog-assisted scat surveys to carry out the first fine-scale population genetic study of the black-footed cat ( Felis nigripes ), Africa's smallest and most range-restricted endemic felid, and a threatened species for which conventional survey methods are largely ineffective. Using 130 successfully genotyped scat samples (nine microsatellite loci) from two populations about 650 km apart, we identified 65 individuals and assessed genetic diversity and fine-scale relatedness to explore aspects of dispersal and reproductive ecology. Both populations exhibited similar observed heterozygosity (H o = 0.67-0.69) and allelic richness, with no heterozygote deficit (F IS = −0.02 to −0.08). Differentiation between the southern Namibia and central South Africa sites was low but detectable (F ST = 0.03-0.05). We used pairwise relatedness and candidate pedigree results to explore hypotheses about sex-specific relatedness patterns. Female-female dyads were more related than male-male dyads at the shortest distance class (0-2 km), a pattern compatible with female philopatry. There were more half-sibling than full-sibling assignments and uneven representation of candidate fathers, which may indicate polygamy and reproductive skew. These results provide baseline genetic data for a Vulnerable species and show that this approach is feasible for Africa's small, elusive carnivores, whose dispersal, mating systems and population structure remain largely unknown. Broader spatial and temporal sampling could help assess population connectivity and reveal how threats and changing land use impact genetic diversity and structure.

items.title: Blood-meal analysis indicates preferential feeding on humans and non-commensal rodents by Culex mosquitoes in Tanzania
items.abstract: Arthropod-borne viruses are important emerging and re-emerging pathogens worldwide, yet information on mosquito feeding ecology and associated transmission networks remains limited in many African regions. This study investigated mosquito host-feeding patterns and arbovirus occurrence along an urban-rural gradient in Morogoro, Tanzania. Mosquitoes were collected at four locations representing different levels of human influence during wet and dry seasons. Vertebrate blood-meal sources were identified using a Nanopore-based metabarcoding approach, while viral screening was performed using RT-qPCR assays targeting Orthoflavivirus and Alphavirus genera. A total of 8,917 mosquitoes were collected, of which more than 90% belonged to the Culex genus. Blood-meal analyses of 310 blood-fed and gravid mosquitoes identified 35 molecular operational taxonomic units, which we grouped into 11 host categories. Humans were the most frequently utilized hosts (68%), followed by non-commensal rodents (22%) and crows (18%). Culex mosquitoes showed broad host use and frequently fed on multiple taxonomic units, with an average of 1.36 taxonomic units detected per individual. Co-feeding network analyses revealed extensive host sharing between humans and wildlife, with non-commensal rodents showing significantly higher co-feeding probabilities with humans than any other host group. No human-pathogenic arboviruses were detected. Viral detections were limited to insect-specific viruses, an endogenous viral element in chromosome 2 of Aedes aegypti, and two detections of bird-infecting Bagaza virus, indicating ongoing viral circulation within the mosquito community. Our findings demonstrate broad and flexible host use by Culex mosquitoes and highlight non-commensal rodents as an underappreciated component of mosquito feeding with potential relevance for arbovirus transmission and spillover between wildlife and humans.

items.title: LifeDive: Cross-kingdom phenotype estimates for 35,856 species
items.abstract: Dense, standardized species-by-trait matrices support comparative biology and ecology, but theircoverage remains uneven. LifeDive uses a general-purpose, web-search-enabled language modelwithin a scripted annotation pipeline to estimate traits across animals, plants, and fungi. Theworkflow assembled 35,856 species by 196 phenotype questions, yielding 7,027,776 entries in acompleted matrix; 16.6% of entries were imputed from other machine-derived annotations. Fourordered substantive responses express model judgments about trait statements, with a separatecode for unknown or inapplicable cases. An exploratory 14-factor representation summarized broadbiological contrasts, although statistical factor-retention criteria suggested substantially moredimensions. A benchmark screened 168 external criteria, with selected results reported for 44;many biologically direct associations were strong, particularly for taxonomy and selected ecologicaltraits. A separate model-assisted audit reported 96.5% directional agreement in a selectedtaxonomy-rule subset and approximately 237 agreements among 240 selected species-specificchecks. These audit subsets do not estimate accuracy across the whole matrix, and theAmphiBIO-derived benchmark results require qualification because unrecorded categories weretreated as negative indicators. Trait profiles also produced recognizable taxonomic and functionalgroupings. LifeDive offers a broad computational phenotype resource for exploration, hypothesisgeneration, and prioritizing expert review. Individual values remain estimates, and downstreaminference requires attention to imputation, sampling, source dependence, and trait-specificverification. The reported application programming interface and computing expenditure wasapproximately US$10,000.

items.title: Microbial diversity and insights into feeding behavior of the two-spot cotton leaf hopper (Amrasca biguttula)
items.abstract: Abstract Recent invasion of the two-spot cotton leaf hopper (TSCL) ( Amrasca biguttula ) into the U.S. now threatens row and vegetable crops as well as ornamentals. TSCL ecology and biology, including microbial diversity, are understudied. Insect-specific microbes could influence host biology and ecology including insect-plant interactions. Here, microbiota (bacteria and viruses) within TSCL along with its feeding behavior were characterized using high throughput sequencing, microscopy, and Electrical penetration graph (EPG). Results revealed low diversity of bacteria dominated by Wolbachia and confirmed the absence of obligate (primary) symbionts. Two distinct and differentially abundant Wolbachia strains (B-supergroup) were found co-infecting midgut tissues of 60% of TSCL tested. Virome analysis uncovered a diverse complex of at least eight dsDNA genomes (12–17 kb) of adintoviruses ( Eupolintoviridae ), but no RNA viruses commonly found in other leafhoppers were identified. The mesophyll feeding nature of TSCL was identified by observing chlorophyll derived autofluorescence in midguts and higher abundance of chloroplast transcripts (photosystem I, II, Rubisco, cytochrome b6 and ATP synthase complex) in TSCL (whole insects) compared with thrips and aphids. EPG recordings showed a cell-rupture style of feeding with differences between adults and nymphs. Lastly, consistent with its cell-rupturing feeding style, no evidence for the presence of plant-pathogenic bacteria or viruses that could induce hopperburn was found. These results overall provide insights into the microbial diversity and feeding pattern of TSCL and lay a foundation for future research.

items.title: Trophic variation in the Southern hagfish Myxine australis under contrasting bottom- trawling scenarios
items.abstract: Abstract The trophic ecology of hagfishes remains one of the least understood among marine vertebrates, and the limited knowledge available has led them to be considered primarily scavengers. Consequently, an important role in the consumption of fisheries discards has been attributed to them. In this study, we analyzed, for the first time, the trophic ecology of a hagfish, Myxine australis , under contrasting bottom-trawling scenarios using gastrointestinal content analysis and stable isotope analysis of carbon and nitrogen. The results revealed a generalist and opportunistic feeding strategy based on the consumption of fish and invertebrates, with no evidence of ontogenetic changes in diet. The species also occupied a tertiary consumer position, with a marked dependence on benthic resources. In areas subjected to bottom trawling, the isotopic niche during the trawling period was approximately three times larger than that observed during the pre-trawling period. Differences in isotopic values and C:N ratios suggested periods of fasting followed by high food intake. Overall, these results indicate that M. australis exhibits trophic plasticity, shifting its feeding strategy according to resource availability, exploiting both natural resources and potential anthropogenic subsidies associated with fishing activity.

items.title: Interprofessional Pedagogy for the Anthropocene: Faculty Perspectives on the imperative for Climate Change and SDG-Aligned Planetary Health Education in Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, and Conservation and Marine Ecology programs
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Climate change is one of the planetary boundaries that has been transgressed and is increasingly affecting human, animal, and ecosystem health. Its impacts include the expansion of vector-borne diseases, food and water insecurity, extreme weather events, poor air quality, and adverse mental health outcomes. Despite growing recognition of these threats, climate change and planetary health education remain inconsistently integrated across health professions curricula. Faculty perspectives on embedding planetary health education through interprofessional education (IPE) remain underexplored, particularly in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) where climate vulnerability is acute. Methods: This qualitative study explored faculty perceptions of planetary health education and the role of IPE in its delivery. Heterogeneous focus groups and one individual interview were conducted with 49 faculty members representing Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, Public Health, Biology/Ecology, Marine Conservation, and pre-medical/pre-veterinary programmes across 18 geographical regions. The focus group/interview questions are provided in Appendix 1. Data were analysed using thematic analysis guided by two research questions addressing the importance of planetary health education and strategies for interprofessional curricular integration. Results: Three themes emerged. First, faculty expressed strong consensus on the need to align planetary health competencies with the Sustainable Development Goals and identified key curricular topics, including vector-borne and zoonotic diseases, food and water security, heat stress, marine health, mental health, and social determinants of health. Second, participants proposed strategies for curricular integration, including curriculum mapping, vertical integration of competencies, simulation- and case-based learning, shared electives, and experiential learning through institutional partnerships. Third, faculty identified barriers to implementation, including limited accreditation requirements, insufficient faculty development, curriculum overcrowding, and a hidden curriculum in which relevant content exists across programmes but remains poorly coordinated and largely siloed. Conclusions: Faculty across disciplines view planetary health education as an urgent professional responsibility and support its delivery through interprofessional approaches. However, institutional barriers continue to impede implementation. Existing climate- and One Health-related content across programmes provides a foundation for developing integrated, competency-based planetary health curricula, particularly in climate-vulnerable regions seeking to strengthen health system resilience.

items.title: Understanding community perceptions to integrate Traditional and Cultural Ecological Knowledge in the conservation of an endangered and endemic species
items.abstract: Abstract Traditional and Cultural Ecological Knowledge (TEK and CEK) integrate social, cultural, and environmental dimensions developed through generations of interactions with nature, with CEK emphasizing the cultural contexts that shape relationships between communities and biodiversity. Environmental perception, shaped by knowledge, values, and lived experiences, influences human attitudes toward wildlife and can inform conservation planning. We investigated 43 communities within Lear’s Macaw ( Anodorhynchus leari ) distribution range in the Caatinga of Bahia, Brazil, to assess community perceptions, ecological knowledge, and values attributed to the species. Between 2023 and 2025, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 460 interviewees, on species recognition, ecological knowledge, perceived threats, natural resource use, and attributed values. Among interviewees, high species recognition (93.9%) and frequent observations in the wild (95.2%) indicated strong local familiarity. Most interviewees (52.8%) perceived a recent population increase, consistent with population monitoring data. Knowledge of feeding ecology emphasized the importance of licuri palm ( Syagrus coronata ) and maize ( Zea mays ), resources of socioeconomic importance that are also associated with human-wildlife interactions and conflicts. Electrical infrastructure (38.1%) and retaliatory hunting associated with crop damage (14.8%) were among the most frequently perceived threats. Most respondents (87.6%) rejected removing animals from the wild. Values attributed to the species were predominantly aesthetic (e.g., beautiful), ecological (e.g., seed dispersal), and moral (e.g., living being, preservation). These findings show that local ecological knowledge can complement ecological monitoring by revealing how communities perceive population trends, ecological relationships, threats, and coexistence with Lear’s Macaw. Integrating CEK and community perceptions into participatory conservation and educational initiatives can strengthen locally grounded strategies for the long-term protection of the species.

items.title: Microbiomes in Sexual and Gender Minority Populations: Anatomy, Identity, Exposure and Clinical Outcomes
items.abstract: Microbiome studies in lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and other sexual and gender minority populations encompass partner-associated ecology, gender-affirming care, infection and prevention. This critical narrative review integrates human evidence by sex assigned at birth, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation and practices, current anatomy, and clinical state. Prevotellaceae-enriched intestinal profiles recur in several MSM cohorts, with geographical, behavioral and HIV-related heterogeneity. Female-partner studies capture both stable Lactobacillus-associated communities and transitions toward bacterial vaginosis. Testosterone-exposed vaginas and surgically reconstructed genital tissues show different relationships between composition, symptoms and inflammation; direct neovaginal testing demonstrates poor diagnostic performance of Nugent scoring. Oral, urinary, seminal and fungal studies broaden the clinical scope, while separately analyzed gender-expression, nonbinary and asexual evidence remains sparse. Intervention findings further distinguish microbial modulation from clinical benefit: resistance determinants can increase without broad taxonomic change, and a dietary trial links baseline community features to exploratory metabolic response. The comparative synthesis identifies tissue, endocrine state and measured endpoint as central to interpreting microbial markers. Clinical translation requires longitudinal exposure contrasts, expressed-function measurements and trials with validated patient-important outcomes.

items.title: Rational design in single-atom nanoalloys for electrochemical carbon dioxide and nitrate conversion: a minireview.
items.abstract: Single-atom nanoalloys (SAAs), consisting of atomically dispersed guest metals embedded within conductive metallic host lattices, have emerged as a promising class of electrocatalysts for the sustainable conversion of carbon and nitrogen. Compared with conventional alloy nanoparticles and single-atom catalysts, SAAs provide local atomic coordination and intermetallic charge transfer, enabling efficient regulation of intermediate adsorption, proton-coupled electron-transfer kinetics, and catalytic selectivity. However, few reviews have systematically elucidated the rational design of atomically engineered metal sites for carbon and nitrogen conversion. To bridge this gap, this minireview focuses on rationally designed SAAs for electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction, nitrate reduction, and C-N coupling, emphasizing the relationships among electronic structure modulation, intermetallic charge transfer, coordination environments, and intermediate adsorption. Moreover, the fundamental reaction mechanisms of carbon dioxide reduction, nitrate reduction, and C-N coupling are discussed to emphasize the pathways among reaction intermediates. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed, including scalable synthesis, durability enhancement, structural uniformity, electrochemical technologies Integration, and fundamental understanding. By integrating these perspectives, this minireview aims to provide a comprehensive framework for the rational design of next-generation atomically mixed nanoalloys for sustainable electrocatalytic carbon and nitrogen.

items.title: A practical HPLC-UV method for the simultaneous screening of decabromodiphenyl ethane and its debromination products in environmental matrices.
items.abstract: A high-efficiency, high-performance liquid chromatography-ultraviolet detection (HPLC-UV) method was developed for the simultaneous determination of decabromodiphenylethane (DBDPE) and its eight debromination products (one nona-, four octa-, two hepta-, and one hexa-brominated compounds) in soil and water samples. Key steps in the sample preparation process, such as solid-phase extraction and liquid-liquid extraction, were systematically optimized to enhance extraction efficiency and purification. This resulted in the average recovery rate of soil and water increasing by 40% and 20%, respectively, compared with that before optimization, meeting the requirements for trace organic pollutant analysis. Using an Agilent Zorbax Eclipse PAH column (2.1 mm × 100 mm × 1.8 µm) with a mobile phase of water containing 5 mM ammonium acetate aqueous solution and acetonitrile, gradient elution (flow rate of 0.4-0.7 mL min -1 ) was employed. At a UV detection wavelength of 230 nm, baseline separation of all target compounds was achieved. The method demonstrated good linearity across a wide concentration range ( R 2 > 0.992). The method's limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) for soil matrices ranged from 0.013-3.093 ng g -1 dry weight (dw) and 0.042-10.310 ng g -1 dw, respectively. For water matrices, the LOD and LOQ ranged from 0.250-61.860 ng L -1 and 0.833-206.200 ng L -1 , respectively. The relative standard deviation (RSD) ranged from 0.27% to 1.59%, indicating high precision. The main advantage of this method is its simplicity, providing a practical screening tool for routine environmental monitoring laboratories. It can complement high-resolution mass spectrometry techniques and is suitable for large-scale environmental surveys and preliminary risk assessments of DBDPE and its transformation products.

items.title: Relationship Satisfaction Predicts Life Satisfaction Independent of Questionnaire Order: A Preregistered Test of the Focusing Illusion.
items.abstract: The focusing illusion suggests that making a life domain salient can inflate its weight in global life satisfaction judgments. However, order effects may be weaker for important domains whose information is already chronically accessible. We conducted a preregistered between-subjects experiment ( N = 478) to test whether questionnaire order moderates the association between relationship satisfaction and life satisfaction. Participants completed the Satisfaction With Life Scale and the Couple Satisfaction Index in counterbalanced order. Relationship satisfaction was a strong positive predictor of life satisfaction; however, this association did not vary by questionnaire order, and no gender moderation emerged. Bayesian model comparison favored a model including relationship satisfaction without interaction terms. These findings suggest that the association between romantic relationship satisfaction and life satisfaction did not depend on questionnaire order in the present study.

items.title: Examining Heterogeneity in Sexual, Body, and Personal Relationship Satisfaction Among LGBTQA+ Adults.
items.abstract: Although personal and interpersonal satisfaction foster well-being, few studies have examined how different domains of satisfaction covary within the LGBTQA+ community. We addressed this oversight via latent profile analysis of body, sexual and personal relationship satisfaction in a large sample of LGBTQA+ adults ( N = 3,723). Six unique profiles emerged: Highly Satisfied (high satisfaction across domains; 31.1%), Connected Satisfied (middling body and sexual satisfaction, high personal relationship satisfaction; 31.6%), Connected Dissatisfied (low-to-middling body and sexual satisfaction, high personal relationship satisfaction; 14.5%), Moderately Satisfied (middling satisfaction across domains; 11.3%), Dissatisfied (low satisfaction across domains; 7.6%) and Sexually Satisfied (low body and personal relationship satisfaction, high sexual satisfaction; 4.1%). Profile membership varied by gender, sexual orientation and other relevant socio-demographic variables. Profiles also differed across social and psychological well-being. Our results emphasize the need for targeted interventions to improve satisfaction and well-being among distinct subgroups of the LGBTQA+ population.

items.title: Associations of severe violence exposure with substance use, internet addiction, and telomere length among Taiwanese children.
items.abstract: Few studies have examined the longitudinal association between severe childhood violence exposure, substance use, Internet addiction, and telomere length. This study sought to investigate this under-researched association, utilizing a sample of Taiwanese children. The sample included a control group of 126 children (girls: 48.4%) not exposed to violence and a high risk group of 119 children (girls: 29.4%) exposed to severe violence (polyvictimization, severe parental physical abuse, or repeated sexual victimization). Buccal cell telomere length (TL) was measured at 10-years old (2014). Substance use and Internet addiction were measured at 10-years old (2014), 12-years old (2016), 14-years old (2018), and 17-years old (2021). Multivariate regression analysis revealed that those in the high-risk group had significantly higher rates of alcohol use experience (ORs: 4.622-18.140, ps ps p = .043) and psychological disorders or symptoms ( p = .048) in 2014. Those in the high-risk group with shorter TLs exhibited elevated rates of substance use ( ps < 0.0167 with Bonferroni correction), from 10-years old (2014) to 17-years old (2021). Our findings, representing the first longitudinal study with an Asian population, highlight the long-lasting effects of severe child maltreatment on substance use. Timely preventive interventions should be implemented for children exposed to severe violence, especially those with telomere erosion.

items.title: Associations Between Neighborhood Service, Religious, and Civic Organizations and Cognitive Decline for Older Mexican Americans Residing in Urban and Rural Areas.
items.abstract: ObjectivesNeighborhood resources are protective factors for healthy cognitive aging, yet the impact of these resources may vary by urbanicity. We examined urban-rural differences in the association between the availability of neighborhood social services, religious, and civic organizations, and cognitive decline among older Mexican Americans.MethodData from 628 participants ( M Age = 80) in 2004-2013 Hispanic Established Populations for the Epidemiologic Study of the Elderly were linked to the National Neighborhood Data Archive. Cognitive impairment was measured with the Mini-Mental State Examination.ResultsAmong urban residents, the presence of religious organizations was associated with better cognition levels, but a higher number of civic organizations were linked to worse levels and a steeper decline in cognition. There were no effects of neighborhood resources on cognition among rural residents.DiscussionThe differential impacts of organization types and urbanicity should be considered when promoting cognitively protective neighborhood resources for older Mexican Americans.

items.title: Associations between harm perceptions of secondhand nicotine and cannabis exposure and use among adolescents.
items.abstract: Perceptions of secondhand exposure may influence adolescent use of cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and cannabis. In Spring 2024, 4760 Connecticut high school students completed an online survey assessing perceived harms from secondhand exposure to cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and smoked or vaped cannabis. Compared to never use, low perceived harm of secondhand exposure to cigarettes, e-cigarettes, smoked and vaped cannabis were significantly associated with higher odds of current use of cigarettes, e-cigarettes, smoked and vaped cannabis, respectively (all p s p s < 0.05). Low harm perceptions of secondhand exposure to cigarettes, e-cigarettes, or cannabis were associated with current use of these products. Public health interventions should provide evidence-based information about the potential risks of secondhand exposure to smoked and vaped nicotine and/or cannabis products and support informed perceptions of these risks among adolescents.

items.title: Predictors of learning the memory support system in individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment.
items.abstract: Objective The Memory Support System (MSS) is a memory compensation tool that utilizes a calendar/notebook. Although baseline global cognition, declarative memory, and personality have been shown to predict MSS learning, the learning efficiency across amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) subtypes remains unclear. To address this gap, this study compared MSS learning in participants with single-domain aMCI (SD-aMCI) versus multi-domain aMCI (MD-aMCI). Methods Five hundred and thirty-six participants with aMCI (SD-aMCI = 268; MD-aMCI = 268) participated in 10-day MSS training during the Healthy Action to Benefit Independence in Thinking ® (HABIT) program. Ordinal logistic regression tested for differences in MSS learning between SD-aMCI and MD-aMCI, with age, gender, education, depression, and baseline global cognition as covariates. Results Younger age, male gender, fewer years of education, and better baseline global cognition were associated with higher MSS learning efficiency. Participants with SD-aMCI had significantly higher odds of achieving higher MSS final learning score at training end, after controlling for age, gender, education, depression, and baseline global cognition. Conclusion While age, gender, education, and global cognition are important in MSS learning, having cognitive deficits in domains beyond memory further reduces the ability to learn the MSS. Clinicians may need to tailor training sessions according to participants' cognitive profiles to facilitate learning outcomes.

items.title: Is gig work the same for everyone? Psychosocial job demands, resources, and well-being in platform work across Europe: evidence from the GIG-OSH study.
items.abstract: Objectives Research on digital platform work increasingly highlights unclear employment arrangements and pressures related to algorithmic management. This study aimed to describe psychosocial working conditions in web-based and on-location gig work using the job demands‑resources (JD-R) model and examine associations between job demands, job resources, factors preventing resource depletion (FPRD), and health outcomes among platform workers. Material and methods Cross-sectional data were drawn from the GIG-OSH project conducted in 7 European countries (Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Poland, Spain, Sweden, and the United Kingdom). Data were collected through an online survey in November 2023 - April 2024. The analytic sample comprised 3299 platform workers (1476 on-location, 1823 web-based). A project-specific questionnaire assessed socio-demographic characteristics, employment conditions, workload, occupational safety and health hazards, psychosocial working conditions, algorithmic management, and health outcomes. Psychosocial factors were classified as job demands, job resources, or FPRD within an extended JD-R framework. Results Platform work was characterized by an imbalance between job demands and resources, particularly among onlocation workers. Compared with web-based workers, they reported greater exposure to emotionally disturbing situations, aggression, violence, discrimination, and sexual harassment. Working alone was common in both groups but more prevalent in web-based work. Factors preventing resource depletion indicators, especially absence of fines and protection against fraudulent bookings, were more favourable in web-based work. Higher job demands were significantly associated with poorer health outcomes, with emotionally disturbing situations showing the strongest effect. Job resources demonstrated modest protective associations, whereas FPRD indicators, particularly not working while ill, were consistently associated with better health. Conclusions Platform work involves substantial psychosocial risks linked to poorer well-being and health, supporting the JD-R model. Distinct psychosocial profiles of web-based and on-location work highlight the need for targeted occupational health and platform policy interventions. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).

items.title: A Mixed-Methods Examination of Patterns of Response and Nonresponse in Group Interpersonal Psychotherapy.
items.abstract: Objective Interpersonal psychotherapy (IPT) has been found to be an effective therapeutic approach for improving depressive symptoms, but little is known about the therapeutic processes associated with these benefits. This study aimed to further understand the therapeutic processes involved in group IPT (IPT-G) by thematically analyzing participant contributions and comparing themes across those whose depressive symptoms were responsive or unresponsive to treatment. Methods Using data from a pilot trial of IPT-G for college students with mild to moderate depressive symptoms, the present study conducted reflexive thematic analysis on group psychotherapy transcripts and detailed session notes to generate themes of participant (N=9) contributions. Analyses of variance (ANOVAs) were conducted to explore differences in patterns of theme expression between those whose elevated depressive symptoms responded or did not respond to treatment and those who maintained initially mild symptoms. Results Across participants, 31 codes embedded within six themes emerged from the reflexive thematic analysis. ANOVA findings revealed no significant differences between responders, nonresponders, and maintainers, but effect sizes suggested distinctions. Conclusions By identifying trends in content shared by responders, nonresponders, and maintainers, the study provides further information on treatment-specific response patterns of those participating in IPT-G and can aid clinicians and researchers in developing and tailoring treatments for individuals struggling with interpersonal relationships and depressive disorders.

items.title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
items.abstract: Background Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI. Methods We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved). Results Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P =0.445; C statistic=0.77). Conclusions One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.
