items.title: Impact of Hearing and Vision Loss on Quality of Life in Older Adults Living With Cognitive Impairment: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Previous reviews have established that hearing and vision impairments are common among people living with cognitive impairment and that these comorbidities can exacerbate effects of cognitive impairments on cognitive, social and functional outcomes. This scoping review aimed to extend on this knowledge, by identifying and evaluating evidence regarding the effect of hearing and vision impairment on quality of life among older adults living with cognitive impairment, to: (i) determine if a compounding effect exists between hearing and/or vision and cognitive impairments; (ii) compare the effects on hearing, vision and health-related quality of life, and (iii) evaluate quality of life outcomes for hearing and vision interventions for this population. Seven electronic databases were searched systematically from inception to February 2026 for studies reporting quality of life outcomes among older adults living with cognitive impairment and hearing and/or vision impairment. Results were summarised then categorised by aim. Thirteen studies met inclusion criteria. The limited evidence suggests that (i) individuals living with comorbid vision and cognitive impairments may have substantially worse quality of life than those with either impairment alone, (ii) the effect is similar in size across different quality of life outcomes and (iii) sensory support interventions, involving counselling and assistance with device use, appear to be a more promising method of improving quality of life among this population. Further research is necessary to understand the relationship between hearing and vision impairments and quality of life among people living with cognitive impairment. Recommendations for future research include focusing on dual sensory impairment, utilising mixed methods approaches and inclusive selection criteria for people living with dementia. Further development and implementation of sensory support programs, codesigned with individuals with lived experience, is also recommended for improving the quality of life for people living with dementia globally.

items.title: Reduced recall of death-related words suggests automatic death-thought suppression.
items.abstract: According to terror management theory, humans automatically suppress death-related thoughts when reminded of their own mortality. We evaluated this claim of automatic death-thought-suppression using a think/no-think paradigm. If people automatically suppress death-related thoughts, recall of death-related target words should reduce compared to other word categories both after suppression-induced forgetting, but also in the baseline condition. 182 participants took part in a think/no-think paradigm with death-related words, neutral words, and a semantic category (i.e., animals) as target words. As expected, participants recalled less death-related target words without instruction to suppress death-related target words in the baseline condition. In the no-think condition, recall of death-related target words was lower than recall of animals. Participants did not show a general suppression-induced forgetting effect, potentially because fewer cognitive resources were available for suppression-induced forgetting. Overall, our results suggest a distinct processing of death-related thoughts.

items.title: Reproductive costs of anhydrobiosis: female tardigrades protect stored sperm better than males.
items.abstract: Anhydrobiosis is a reversible process that allows organisms to survive prolonged periods in a desiccated state. Very little is known about the costs of anhydrobiosis on reproduction beyond a hiatus in activity. Tardigrades are suited to investigate such effects on male gamete function, since the latter can be tracked non-invasively. We compared the effects of three anhydrobiotic state durations (from one day to one month) on male-stored and female-stored sperm function in Macrobiotus dolosus. Our study shows that in-testis sperm motility upon rehydration is considerably impaired after long anhydrobiosis periods, and that its recovery is significantly slowed (up to several days). In contrast, we found no evidence for a negative impact of anhydrobiotic state on the fertilisation ability of spermatheca-stored sperm. Therefore, tardigrade female sperm storage structure can protect stored sperm even during long-term desiccation. Ultimately, our results highlight the need to further study on tissue-specific physiological adaptations to anhydrobiosis.

items.title: Employment in Veterans With Mental Illness: An Exploratory Penalized-Regression and Random-Forest Analysis.
items.abstract: ImportanceReturning to civilian and community life after military service represents a critical and often challenging transition. Employment can contribute to social identity, financial security, social participation and community reintegration, and overall quality of life among veterans.ObjectiveTo examine candidate factors of employment among veterans who reported a current mental health diagnosis.DesignCross-sectional survey study.SettingOnline data collection.ParticipantsA total of 156 veterans who reported having a current mental illness were recruited; 151 with complete data (mean age = 37.85 years) were analyzed. Most participants identified as male (67%), White (70%), and married or living with a partner (62%).Outcomes and MeasuresEmployment status was the outcome, and candidate predictors included demographic and military characteristics, mental health, physical health and functioning, and psychosocial and behavioral factors.ResultsThe BIC-LASSO model revealed that greater disability severity and pain intensity were each associated with lower odds of employment, with moderate bootstrap selection recurrence (57.1% for disability severity and 56.9% for pain intensity) that remained robust after sensitivity analysis. The random forest model did not exceed majority-class accuracy.Conclusions and RelevanceGreater disability severity and greater pain intensity emerged as plausible, though not yet confirmed, correlates of employment status among veterans with mental illness. Because these exploratory findings require replication in larger, more diverse, and longitudinal samples, they do not yet justify changes to practice; in the interim, they support attending to everyday functioning and pain, alongside psychiatric symptoms, when occupational therapy practitioners evaluate work participation with this population.

items.title: From reproductive access to family sustainability: lessons from single-father families formed through surrogacy.
items.abstract: Single-father families formed through oocyte donation and surrogacy provide a revealing, but not uniquely problematic, case for considering responsibilities after assisted reproduction. Early studies report reassuring parenting and adjustment, yet samples are small and selective, direct accounts from children are sparse, and adolescence and adulthood remain largely unstudied. Family-sustainability planning must therefore complement, not displace, child-centred longitudinal research. This Opinion uses single-father surrogacy to examine four treatment-related domains: portable legal parenthood, identity stewardship, continuity of care, and developmentally timed support. Their relevance extends to other donor-conceived, surrogacy and one-legal-parent families when comparable risks arise. A parent-held Family Sustainability Plan is offered as one testable handover tool, not a fitness assessment or mandatory global document. Its content should be tailored through shared decision-making and paired with navigation, affordable legal and psychosocial support, durable record systems, and structural reform. To avoid surveillance or discriminatory gatekeeping, its preparation should be proportionate, offered on a universal route- and risk-based basis, kept outside treatment-eligibility decisions, and open to refusal or later re-entry without penalty. Cross-border legal disagreement, unequal resources, provider fragmentation, and the possibility of added burden limit what any plan can achieve. Assisted reproduction should nevertheless be accountable for preventable legal and informational discontinuities beyond live birth, while evaluating whether proposed supports are useful, equitable, and acceptable to fathers and children themselves.

items.title: Investigating the Relationship Between Music and Human Psychology Through Big Data Analytics
items.abstract: Abstract Human emotional responses to music are commonly described using the valence–arousal model, which represents emotions according to their positivity (valence) and intensity (arousal). Predicting these dimensions from musical features enables researchers to better understand the relationship between music and human psychology. This study proposes a scalable, data-driven framework that integrates acoustic feature extraction, statistical feature engineering, exploratory data analysis (EDA), and supervised machine learning to predict valence and arousal from music. The Database for Emotional Analysis in Music (DEAM) dataset is used because it contains listener-annotated valence and arousal ratings that reflect perceived emotional responses to musical stimuli. A comprehensive feature set is extracted, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), spectral features, and energy-based features. A LightGBM regression model is employed to capture nonlinear relationships between audio characteristics and emotional dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate strong predictive performance, achieving Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) values of 0.1492 for valence and 0.1416 for arousal, with Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values of 0.1108 and 0.1085, respectively. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for modeling music-induced emotional responses and highlight its potential applications in personalized music recommendation, emotion-aware multimedia systems, and music therapy.

items.title: Multimodal Engagement Practices of Teacher Influencers Across Disciplines on Social Media
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the multimodal engagement strategies employed by teacher influencers on TikTok as an emerging digital genre for public knowledge dissemination. The corpus consists of 40 TikTok videos collected from 40 teacher influencer accounts representing eight disciplines: four soft science disciplines (English, Psychology, Economics, and History) and four hard science disciplines (Mathematics, Biology, Physics, and Chemistry). Findings reveal that teacher influencers strategically deploy textual, visual, and audio resources across five TikTok features: captions, embedded text, react options, visual support, and audio. Attention-getting resources were the most frequently used strategy, followed by directives, reader mentions, and questions. The study also uncovers clear disciplinary variation: soft science teachers predominantly employed authentic visual resources, such as popular public figures and real-world objects. In contrast, hard science teachers relied more on pedagogical resources such as mannequins, whiteboards, and markers to illustrate complex concepts.

items.title: When Experience Becomes Metric: Systemic Model of Distress in Intelligent Digital Environments (SMDIDE)
items.abstract: Abstract The disruptions generated by AI within production systems alter the human experience at work and outline the emergence of digital distress in contemporary labor environments. The model was developed through a conceptual methodology based on interdisciplinary synthesis, integrating sociotechnical studies, cognitive psychology, labor theory, and critical AI scholarship. As a result, the SM-DIDE model conceptualizes distress as a dynamic process that arises during human-machine interaction, where cognitive and technological overload is processed as cognitive demand through the functional articulation of six interdependent subsystems. The activation, modulation, and feedback among these subsystems explain the variability in the presentation, course, and trajectories of distress. Three subsystems describe the progression from the perception of cognitive and technological demand to the emergence of evolutionary trajectories. This progression is neither linear nor deterministic: it is modulated by the transversal subsystem of involuntary regulation and by the dysfunctional coping subsystem, both of which interact with the direct influence of the structural modulation subsystem to determine the load exerted on the worker during the interaction with AI. The model reframes distress as a process and directs research toward work environments centered on human experience, integrating domains rarely articulated together—cognitive, epistemic, affective, existential, and sociotechnical—and advancing toward a unified theory of digital distress.

items.title: Geometric Properties of Human High-Performing Buildings: A Review of the Evidence and the Implications for Practice
items.abstract: Building performance is conventionally assessed in structural, thermal, energy, and functional terms, while architectural character is treated as a matter of taste. Yet a growing body of research suggests that the geometric characteristics of buildings also affect performance experienced directly by people—perceptual engagement, restoration and well-being, perceived safety, social affordance, and patterns of movement and use—both within buildings and in adjoining streets and public spaces. This paper reviews that evidence and develops a conceptual model and theoretical account of how the relevant characteristics arise. Drawing on environmental psychology, experimental aesthetics, neuroaesthetics, urban design, and the mathematics of form, it identifies recurring geometric characteristics associated with favorable human responses, centered on symmetry and symmetry-breaking, multiscale organization, and contextual relationship. It proposes that these are traces of generative processes rather than attributes of style, and it introduces “deep symmetry”: a progression of correspondence from the isolated object through scale and context to the perceiving human participant, with a candidate mechanism grounded in embodied perception and processing fluency. The framework reframes stylistic debates as questions of human performance, geometry, and process, and sets out a falsifiable research agenda, candidate measures, and broader implications for practice.

items.title: Evaluating the Impact of SNAP-Ed Classes on College Students' Cooking and Food Skills.
items.abstract: Objective To assess changes in cooking and food skills among college students eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in a cooking-focused nutrition intervention. Methods A pretest-posttest design was used to evaluate program outcomes among participants (N = 124) on 11 campuses in the California State University system from 2021 to 2023. The Cooking and Food Skills Assessment measured skills in cooking techniques, meal planning, grocery shopping, and managing food budgets. Paired-samples t tests were used to investigate changes in mean scores for each cooking and food skills item. Results Participants showed significant improvements in skills in planning how much food to buy, knowing one's food budget, balancing meals using nutrition advice, and preparing healthy meals with few ingredients. Participants reported the lowest confidence in planning meals ahead of time at both pretest and posttest. Conclusions and implications Cooking-focused nutrition programming for college students may improve food resource management skills.

items.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Heterogeneity in Clinical Evidence: JACC Evidence Review.
items.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

items.title: Environmental Tobacco Smoke and Gastric Cancer: Evidence from the Stomach Cancer Pooling (StoP) Project and a Comprehensive Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background Few studies have investigated environmental tobacco smoke (ETS), commonly known as secondhand smoke, and gastric cancer (GC) risk, and the findings have been inconsistent. We conducted a pooled analysis from StoP Project and a comprehensive meta-analysis to evaluate the potential impact of ETS exposure on GC risk. Methods Five case-control studies with ETS information from the StoP project were included (1,560 GC cases and 2,497 controls). Study-specific odds ratios (ORs) and the corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using unconditional logistic regression models, adjusting for potential confounders. Pooled effect estimates were computed using random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed using I2 (%) statistics. A comprehensive meta-analysis was conducted including the StoP project and published studies (n=14), with publication bias assed via funnel plot and Egger's test. Results Study-specific estimates were heterogeneous, with stronger associations observed among never-smokers. A strong positive association was observed in the Iran study (aOR = 2.38; 95%CI: 1.11, 5.09) among never-smokers. ETS exposure was not associated with GC risk in the pooled StoP analysis. In the comprehensive meta-analysis, the H. pylori-adjusted subgroup showed a positive association (aOR = 1.41; 95% CI: 1.21-1.64). The overall aOR was 1.25 (95% CI: 0.98-1.59, I2 = 69.9%). Conclusions The results support the hypothesis that ETS could be a risk factor for GC, underscoring the importance of targeted preventive measures and public health policies to reduce ETS exposure. Impact This study provides the most comprehensive evaluation to date of ETS exposure and highlights ETS as a preventable GC risk factor.

items.title: Hepatitis C, Hearing Loss, and Healthcare Utilization Patterns, a Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES Data: 1999-2012.
items.abstract: Objectives Hearing loss is a chronic condition in the U.S. with diverse causes, including viral infections, and significantly affects quality of life. Despite the rising incidence of Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, research on its relationship with hearing loss remains limited. Early and consistent interactions with the healthcare system have been shown to improve outcomes in extrahepatic manifestations of HCV and enhance quality of life. Design We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of HCV history, identified via HCV antibody and RNA testing obtained by the mobile examination center, and hearing loss, measured by pure-tone audiometry, using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (1999-2004, 2011-2012) for adults aged 20 to 69. We utilized multivariable logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for important covariates. Results were stratified by degree of healthcare utilization. Results Among 6705 participants, hearing loss prevalence was 27.7% in those with HCV versus 12.7% in those without. The adjusted OR for hearing loss in individuals with HCV was 1.81 (95% confidence interval: 1.06, 3.10). Notably, the magnitude of association between HCV history and hearing loss was higher in the low healthcare utilization group than in the high healthcare utilization group (aOR: 2.82 versus 0.72). Conclusions Our findings suggest an association between HCV and hearing loss, with healthcare utilization modifying this relationship. This study fills a gap in the literature and highlights the need for increased clinical monitoring of hearing health in individuals who have had an HCV infection.

items.title: Effect of phaco-tip orientation during phacoemulsification surgery (TIPS) on endothelial cell loss: Results of a randomized clinical trial.
items.abstract: Purpose To compare corneal endothelial cell (CEC) loss, central corneal thickness (CCT) and intraoperative complications 1 month post-phacoemulsification using bevel-up versus bevel-down tip orientation with the direct-chop technique. Methods Design: Multicentre, triple-masked, randomized controlled parallel group trial. Participants Adults (≥18 years) with cataracts. Methods Participants were randomized 1:1 to undergo phacoemulsification with either a bevel-up (n = 241) or bevel-down (n = 239) using a standardized direct chop technique; Main outcome measures: Mean difference in CEC at 1 month, adjusted for baseline CEC using analysis of covariance with the intention-to-treat principle. Secondary outcomes included change in CCT and intraoperative complications. Subgroup analyses were conducted by cataract grade and baseline endothelial cell density (ECD). Results Of 480 participants, 435 (90.6%) completed follow-up. Baseline characteristics and phaco parameters were comparable across groups. At 1 month, mean CEC loss was similar between the groups (mean difference: 5.04 cells/mm 2 ; 95% CI: -54.37 to 64.46; p = 0.868; mean CEC loss %: 9.19 (95% CI: 7.7-10.7) (bevel-up) and 9.07 (95% CI: 7.2-10.9) (bevel-down); p = 0.919). Exploratory subgroup analyses by baseline endothelial cell count and cataract hardness showed no statistically significant differences in CEC loss between bevel orientations. Changes in CCT were comparable and complications infrequent across treatment arms (bevel-up (5.8%); bevel-down (5.0%)). Conclusion In routine direct-chop phacoemulsification with adequate preoperative endothelial counts, bevel orientation (bevel-up vs. bevel-down) results in a negligible difference in one-month endothelial cell loss and infrequent intraoperative complication rates. Bevel orientation is not a major determinant of endothelial cell loss in uncomplicated cases, allowing surgeons to select either orientation based on personal preference.

items.title: National Early Warning Score 2-Guided Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle Care for Adults With Suspected Sepsis in the Emergency Department: A Hybrid Type 1 Effectiveness-Implementation Stepped-Wedge Randomized Controlled Trial Pilot Study (NEWS-1 TRIPS).
items.abstract: Objectives To increase the uptake of the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle, we implemented a novel sepsis care model (National Early Warning Score [NEWS]-1 care), in which the Hour-1 Bundle is objectively triggered by a high NEWS-2 (≥ 5). We aimed to determine the feasibility of a full-scale type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial of this model. Design A pilot type 1 hybrid trial, comprising a stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial and mixed-methods implementation evaluation with staff focus group interviews and an anonymous survey guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework. Setting Four emergency departments in Hong Kong. Patients Adult patients of 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of infection requiring hospitalization and a NEWS-2 greater than or equal to 5. Interventions Implementation of the Hour-1 Bundle when NEWS-2 was greater than or equal to 5. Measurements and main results The primary outcome was the feasibility of a full-scale hybrid trial, evaluated based on 14 progression criteria. Preliminary clinical effectiveness and safety were assessed, alongside implementation barriers and facilitators. During the implementation phase, compliance with lactate, blood culture, and antibiotics increased significantly. All progression criteria were met, except for suboptimal overall bundle compliance (56.1%). Exploratory intention-to-treat analysis (standard care group, n = 102; NEWS-1 group, n = 98) showed no significant between-group difference in 30-day all-cause mortality (standard care group, 3.9%; NEWS-1 group, 9.2%; absolute risk difference, 5.3%; 95% CI -1.6% to 12.1%); in-hospital, 90-day all-cause, or sepsis-related mortality; need for mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, intensive care, or surgery; or ventilator-free days and adverse events. Implementation evaluation identified 15 barriers and 13 facilitators. Conclusions The effectiveness of NEWS-1 care remained uncertain, though adverse events were rare. A full-scale hybrid stepped-wedge trial is feasible but requires a much larger sample size. Real-world implementation barriers and facilitators should be considered in sepsis management guidelines.

items.title: The Impact of Hospital Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Volume and Its Distribution Across ICUs on Adult Patients' Outcomes: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
items.abstract: Objectives Research from a prior era of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) found that higher hospital ECMO volume was associated with higher survival rates, but it did not examine whether distributing ECMO volume across multiple ICUs affected this relationship. Design Retrospective analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry. Setting ECMO centers contributing to the registry. Patients Adult patients required ECMO support from 2012 to 2023. Interventions None. Measurements and main results We analyzed adult patients from the ELSO registry (2012-2023), adjusting for hospital factors and case mix using multivariable hierarchical logistic regression. The main outcome was in-hospital mortality. Hospital experience was measured by the annual number of adult ECMO cases and total ECMO hours. Volume-outcome associations were modeled for all centers and by total adult ICUs per center. We included 115,849 adults on ECMO across 495 hospitals. Model estimates showed small decreases in mortality odds with higher annual case counts (odds ratio [OR], 0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99 per 10-case increase) and ECMO hours (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr increase). Hospitals with one ICU had a median of 10 cases (interquartile interval [IQI], 3-25 cases), while those with four or more ICUs had a median of 50 (IQI, 28-91). Adjusted mortality was higher in centers delivering ECMO across four+ ICUs compared with one ICU (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.06-1.31), the annual case model (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06-1.26), and the annual ECMO hours model. Higher volume was associated with a reduction in the odds of mortality for hospitals with four+ ICUs compared with those with one ICU (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.96-1.00 per 10 cases and OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr). Conclusions Higher hospital ECMO volume is associated with reduced mortality. Hospitals with more adult ICUs that perform ECMO may experience higher mortality, which may be explained by increased patient complexity and is offset by the higher center volume. More research is needed to better understand the optimum design of ECMO centers.

items.title: Real world data to improve hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance in cirrhosis.
items.abstract: Background and aims Surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains suboptimal due to poor adherence and limited diagnostic accuracy. We aimed to develop and validate a simple risk score to predict HCC in patients with cirrhosis. Methods A total of 667 patients with cirrhosis were followed for up to 60 months or until HCC development, liver transplantation, or death. A prognostic model was derived using multivariable Cox regression. Discrimination was assessed by Harrell's C-index and time-dependent area under the curve (tAUC), calibration by calibration slope and Brier score, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis. Competing-risk analyses accounted for liver transplantation and death. External validation was performed in 18,856 patients with cirrhosis from the Andalusian Population Health Database. Results The A3BS score (age, sex, AST, albumin, and bilirubin) demonstrated good discrimination, with C-index values ranging from 0.73 to 0.76 at 12, 24, 36, and 60 months. Patients in the high-risk group had a substantially higher 60-month cumulative incidence of HCC than those in the low-risk group (32% vs. 9%) and a fourfold increased risk of HCC (sHR 4.0, 95% CI 2.2-7.5; p Conclusions A3BS is a simple five-variable score that provides reliable HCC risk stratification across cirrhosis etiologies and identifies a large subgroup of patients at very low risk of HCC, supporting personalized surveillance strategies and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources.

items.title: PEth as a marker of alcohol consumption in relation to arterial cardiovascular risk factors.
items.abstract: Background Alcohol has well-known detrimental effects on health. Phosphatidyl ethanol 16:0/18:1 (PEth) is a highly sensitive biomarker of alcohol consumption used in primary healthcare. The relationship between PEth concentrations and cardiovascular risk factors remains unclear. Our hypothesis was that high PEth concentrations would be associated with an unfavourable cardiovascular risk factor profile. This study aimed to investigate the associations between PEth concentrations and arterial cardiovascular risk factors. Methods This cross-sectional study was based on data from the Västerbotten Intervention Programme and included 2820 individuals. Health examinations were conducted, including questionnaires collecting data on cardiovascular risk factors. PEth concentrations were analysed in packed erythrocytes from blood samples collected between 1985 and 2014 and stored at -80 °C until analysis. Participants were categorised into four groups. Logistic regression analysis was used to calculate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between PEth concentrations and arterial cardiovascular risk factors. Results The median age of participants was 50.2 years, and the median BMI was 25.9. High PEth concentrations (>0.30 μmol/L) were observed in 8.9% of participants and were associated with hypertension (OR 1.58 [95% CI 1.14-2.18]), diabetes (OR 1.89 [95% CI 1.08-3.28]), male sex (OR 2.58 [95% CI 1.90-3.50]), ever smoking (OR 5.31 [95% CI 3.75-7.52]) and lower education level (OR 2.06 [95% CI 1.32-3.22]) compared with PEth Conclusions High PEth concentrations were associated with established risk factors for arterial cardiovascular disease. These findings should encourage a broader clinical focus when managing patients with elevated PEth concentrations.

items.title: Infectious bronchitis virus exhibits pan-mucosal tropism and ascends via the cloacal hub to infect the urogenital system.
items.abstract: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a prominent respiratory pathogen of chickens that incurs substantial economic losses to the global poultry industry, exhibits extensive genetic heterogeneity. Highly virulent strains manifest broad multi-organ tropism and elicit severe renal and oviductal lesions. Nevertheless, the precise tissue tropism profiles of different IBV genotypes, as well as their in vivo dissemination routes from respiratory mucosa to distal urogenital tissues, remain incompletely characterized. Here, we systematically elucidated the actual tissue tropism and systemic dissemination routes of IBV using in situ immunofluorescence assays, in vivo fluorescence tracking of a recombinant reporter virus, and an estrogen-induced physiological oviduct model. Our findings reveal that all tested IBV strains exclusively target mucosal epithelial cells. Classical Mass-type and emerging genotype VI strains are limited to respiratory tissues and cranial glands, while virulent QX-like isolates show pan-mucosal tropism across respiratory, lower intestinal, and urogenital tracts. Multi-route challenge and spatiotemporal antigen tracking exclude hematogenous viremia as the spread mechanism. Instead, QX-like IBV colonizes the gut and cloaca, a unique avian anatomical junction, then migrates retrogradely along continuous epithelia to the kidneys and oviducts. This work clarifies tissue tropism of major IBV genotypes and identifies a cloaca-dependent ascending mucosal pathway for urogenital infection of QX-like IBV. These results advance our mechanistic understanding of IBV pathogenesis and support the design of precise disease control and mucosal vaccine strategies. Importance Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a highly contagious avian gammacoronavirus, causes huge economic losses in global poultry farming. While primarily infecting respiratory mucosa, virulent strains trigger severe renal and reproductive damage. It has long puzzled researchers how respiratory-entry IBV reaches distant urogenital organs. This work delineates IBV's in vivo spread and rules out typical hematogenous dissemination. IBV possesses inherent pan-mucosal tropism restricted to surface epithelia. Virulent strains colonize the cloaca-the avian junction of digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts-then ascend retrogradely along connected mucosa to kidneys and oviducts. Immature pullets are shielded by sealed oviduct outlets, while mature hens develop severe genital lesions. Resolving this historical dispute, our findings revise IBV pathogenic theories and highlight mucosal immunity as a key target for innovative vaccine design.

items.title: Herpes zoster vaccination in people living with HIV: from evidence to implementation - A narrative review.
items.abstract: Herpes zoster (HZ) remains a significant, preventable cause of morbidity among people living with HIV (PLWH), who face increased risks of HZ, recurrence, and complications despite effective antiretroviral therapy. The recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV), a non-live, adjuvanted vaccine, is currently the preferred strategy for HZ prevention in immunocompromised adults. This narrative review synthesizes the evidence on the burden and pathogenesis of HZ in PLWH, RZV immunogenicity and safety, present vaccination recommendations, clinical considerations, and implementation challenges, with particular emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region. Available evidence indicates that RZV induces robust humoral and cellular immune responses and has a favorable safety profile in PLWH; however, HIV-specific evidence regarding clinical effectiveness, long-term durability of protection, and optimal timing of vaccination in the setting of advanced immunosuppression remains limited. International guidelines consistently recommend a two-dose RZV series for adults with HIV, without requiring a specific CD4+ T-cell threshold or virological suppression. Nevertheless, vaccine uptake remains constrained by cost, limited availability, inadequate patient and healthcare-provider awareness, vaccine hesitancy, and fragmented vaccination services. Future research should prioritize real-world effectiveness, durability of protection, cost-effectiveness, and determinants of vaccine acceptance, including behavioral factors, such as perceived susceptibility, perceived benefits, and perceived barriers. Integrating RZV into routine HIV care and strengthening implementation strategies, particularly across the Asia-Pacific region and other resourcelimited settings, will be critical to translating guideline recommendations into equitable vaccination coverage and reducing HZ-related morbidity among PLWH.

items.title: Modulus-Graded Liquid Metal Electrochemical Fibers for Continuous and Insusceptible Monitoring of Multiple Sweat Biomarkers during Exercise.
items.abstract: Wearable electrochemical biosensors enable non-invasive monitoring of sweat biomarkers for exercise physiology and personalized health management. However, maintaining signal stability under intense body motion remains challenging, as conventional rigid or fiber-based sensors suffer from mechanical deformation-induced interfacial instability. Here, we report modulus-graded liquid metal fibers (MGLMFs) for the simultaneous, real-time monitoring of sweat pH, uric acid (UA), and lactate (LA) during various exercise modalities. By selectively coating high-modulus carbon-based sensing layers onto low-modulus, strain-insensitive liquid metal fibers, our design achieves localized mechanical reinforcement while preserving global stretchability. The resulting sensors exhibit high sensitivity (pH: 68.82 mV pH-1, UA: 39.78 nA μM-1, LA: 4.69 μA mM-1), excellent selectivity, and remarkable electrochemical stability under both static (0-100%) and dynamic (0-50%) strain with minimal signal fluctuation (<5%). After being integrated into a textile-based wireless system, the MGLMFs successfully captured dynamic biomarker changes during jogging, weightlifting, and cycling in human trials, revealing distinct metabolic patterns across aerobic, resistance, and anaerobic exercises. This modulus-graded strategy offers a robust platform for motion-artifact-free wearable electrochemical sensing.

items.title: Seeing the Heat: How a Communication Tool Transformed Experiences into Evidence for New York City's Climate Response.
items.abstract: As climate change intensifies heat, New York City faces mounting health risks. While quantitative data like temperature trends and mortality rates are essential, they cannot capture the lived experience of the climate crisis. Your Heat Story , a partnership between South Bronx Unite, Columbia University, and the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, addresses this gap by collecting and visualizing firsthand narratives from New Yorkers alongside public health data. By integrating stories with environmental health data, this project demonstrates how qualitative and quantitative approaches together strengthen climate communication. These narratives illuminate the cumulative toll of heat on physical, emotional, and mental health and community life, particularly in under-resourced neighborhoods. This initiative models a new form of government communication that uses public platforms for storytelling and relationship-building. In doing so, it advances awareness, informs policy, and offers a replicable framework for integrating narrative into climate-health resilience work.

items.title: The Persuadable Middle-A Target for Increasing Routine Childhood Vaccine Confidence Among Parents in North Carolina.
items.abstract: National childhood vaccination rates in the United States have declined in recent years, a trend exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and linked to the resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases. At the state level, North Carolina maintains strong baseline coverage but increasing numbers of religious exemptions and provisionally enrolled or non-compliant primary and secondary school students points to emerging vulnerabilities in the state's immunization framework.Against this backdrop, this study investigates how parental vaccine confidence, provider practices, and policy environments intersect to influence childhood immunization in North Carolina. It examines how parental beliefs and behaviors correspond-or conflict-with provider experiences, and how provider adaptability, school mandates, and message framing can be aligned to build confidence and improve vaccination uptake.Drawing on a statewide survey of 753 parents and a focus group of 176 immunization providers, this study identifies a "persuadable middle" of parents who are motivated by child protection, open to vaccination, but remain uncertain. Findings reveal that trust, transparent communication, and respectful engagement are essential for fostering confidence, especially when parents value both autonomy and provider guidance.The study proposes a framework for strengthening vaccine uptake by aligning provider communication with parental expectations, emphasizing shared goals, and viewing mandates as opportunities for engagement. Findings support the development of trust-based, relationship-driven strategies designed to reach and motivate persuadable parents.

items.title: Listening, Local Engagement, and Lateral Connections as the Future of Health Communication.
items.abstract: Amid a rapidly evolving health communication landscape, innovative efforts to engage communities and cultivate trusted, local sources of health information have become crucial. In this essay, we describe lessons learned from such efforts, including the importance of centering community voices, engaging a diverse range of interest holders, and strengthening social networks that support information sharing and collective action. We argue that the role of health communication professionals must expand beyond a narrow focus on recommending individual and group behavior change to a more multidisciplinary approach that actively monitors and informs popular news and entertainment media while building durable bridges across people, organizations, and sectors. This annual Society for Health Communication special issue reflects that shift in the field, highlighting communication's growing emphasis on partner- and community-engaged approaches, relationship building, and the development of learning networks among diverse groups of people and community organizations.

items.title: Beyond Automatic Reminders: Adaptive Layered Communication Strategies to Sustain Young Adult Engagement in a Longitudinal Intervention Study.
items.abstract: Digital health interventions offer promising opportunities for behavioral change among young adults, but maintaining longitudinal trial engagement is difficult. This study examined the adaptive layered communication strategies (ALCS) developed collectively through aniterative loop with community members in the Student Health Initiative for Eliminating HPV Diseases (SHIELD) study. These strategies included welcome videos, personalized messages (e.g., thank-you texts, birthday messages, exam period check-ins), and memes. Compared to the period/phase before ALCS, participants exposed to ALCS demonstrated significantly higher survey completion rates at 6 months (76.09% vs. 60.51%, p = .01) and 9 months (78.08% vs. 65.64%, p = .05). Moderation analyses revealed a phase×school type interaction ( p = .04): completion rose from 50.05% to 75.95% among public school students ( p = .03), while private school rates remained stable ( > 75.00%), suggesting a ceiling effect ( p = .41). While automated reminders remain valuable, researchers developing longitudinal digital health interventions should consider a "cocktail" approach, which combines reliable automation with authentic, timely, and culturally tuned human touches, to sustain engagement, particularly in lower-engagement contexts (e.g. public schools).

items.title: Heads Up Boston: A Youth-Led Movement That Addresses Today's Mental Health Crisis.
items.abstract: Argus created and activated a youth-led campaign, featuring a pop-up store in downtown Boston, that promotes mental wellbeing and peer support, in partnership with the Boston Public Health Commission, youth across Boston, NOBULL Apparel, and iHeartMedia. The campaign was developed based on two research insights: First, teenage participants across Boston showed an association between the term mental health and "being in trouble," rather than wellness. Second, youth saw the value in "being there" for their friends, but the stigma associated with the idea of mental health made it difficult for youth to reach out when they themselves were in distress. We needed to forge new associations with "mental health" in our audiences' minds, and after extensive discussions with youth and adult advisors, we saw an opportunity to put Boston teenagers at the forefront of a movement to redefine how all of us think about our emotional well-being. Through a series of workshops, youth put the issue in their own terms, which served as powerful inspiration for the creative process. Anchored on the core idea that "We can make things better," we launched the Heads Up movement to empower youth to listen and speak out about mental health. In a survey held at our landmark in-person activation at the Boston pop-up store, 75% of youth indicated that after attending the event, they were more likely to talk to a friend about their mental health. (We also "sold-out" of swag). Through youth partnership, we cultivated brand ambassadors to expand the reach of and trust in our message.

items.title: Never use genes: terminology effects on public acceptance and implications for agricultural biotechnology.
items.abstract: Public acceptance remains a major social bottleneck in the diffusion of agricultural biotechnologies. Following the U.S. policy of mandating the labeling of genetically modified foods as "bioengineered" rather than using gene-explicit terminology, this study examines whether alternative Chinese names for agricultural biotechnologies shape public acceptance and related evaluations. In a one-way between-subjects online experiment, 1,217 Chinese participants were randomly assigned to one of four naming conditions: biotechnology food , transgenic food , genetically modified food , or genetic engineering food . While biotechnology food elicited higher acceptance, lower perceived risk, higher perceived benefits, and higher perceived naturalness, the three gene-explicit terms did not show significant differences in these dimensions. Moderated mediation analyses showed that the association between naming and acceptance was primarily through perceived benefits and, more conditionally, through perceived risk. Stronger naturalness orientation amplified naming differences in perceived risks and benefits and strengthened the association between perceived benefits and acceptance, whereas genetics knowledge played a more limited moderating role. The findings highlight the role of terminology in public evaluations of GM foods and suggest that responses to naming are sensitive to concerns about naturalness. For food labeling governance in China, terminology choices should be evaluated for their effects on consumer understanding, informed choice and acceptance.

items.title: Comparative Harm Perceptions of Vaping Nicotine Relative to Vaping or Smoking Cannabis and Their Associations With Adolescent Use Status.
items.abstract: Objectives Comparative harm perceptions of nicotine and cannabis may influence use. We explored adolescents' comparative harm perceptions for vaping nicotine, vaping cannabis, and smoking cannabis, as well as associations with current use and susceptibility to future use. Methods From April through May 2024, 4760 Connecticut high school students reported comparative perceptions of health harms from vaping nicotine, vaping cannabis, and smoking cannabis. Electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) and cannabis use status were categorized by past-30-day use into 4 groups: no current use (86.9%), ENDS use only (3.4%), cannabis use only (3.5%), and dual use (6.2%). Among never users, susceptibility to ENDS or cannabis use was assessed (yes/no). Logistic regression assessed associations between harm perceptions and current use status and susceptibility. Results Overall, adolescents perceived vaping nicotine as equally harmful (48.8%) as vaping cannabis but more harmful (45.3%) than smoking cannabis. Those perceiving vaping nicotine as less harmful than vaping cannabis (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.80; P = .03) or smoking cannabis (AOR = 2.50; P P Conclusions Adolescents commonly perceived vaping nicotine as equally or more harmful than cannabis use. Lower harm perceptions were associated with current ENDS/cannabis use and susceptibility to future cannabis use. Prevention strategies should enhance accurate risk perceptions of nicotine and cannabis to discourage uptake or product switching based on comparative harm beliefs.

items.title: Community science uncovers environmental azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus across Norway, including a novel tandem repeat variant (TR62).
items.abstract: Azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus (AR Af ) is an emerging global health concern, mainly driven by environmental selection caused by azole fungicide use. Despite reports of environmental resistance across Europe, data from northern regions remain scarce. Here, we conducted the first nationwide investigation of environmental AR Af in Norway using a community science-based air sampling approach. Volunteers across the country collected airborne fungal spores using passive sticky-seal traps during three sampling periods between 2022 and 2023. In total, 2,332 air samples from 398 locations were analyzed, yielding 1,583 A. fumigatus isolates. Azole resistance screening identified 15 resistant isolates (0.95%) from 14 locations across four out of five Norwegian regions. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) confirmed resistance to medical azoles and elevated MICs toward azole fungicides. Whole-genome sequencing revealed known environmentally associated resistance mechanisms, including TR 34 /L98H ( n = 11) and TR 46 /Y121F/T289A ( n = 2), as well as a TR 46 /Y121F/T289A/S363P/I364V/G448S variant ( n = 1). In addition, a previously undescribed promoter tandem repeat variant (TR 62 ) was identified in one isolate that exhibited multi-azole resistance. Population genomic analyses indicated that resistant isolates were genetically diverse and not restricted to a single clonal lineage, suggesting both local expansion and recombination within a structured population. Although the observed resistance frequency was low, the presence of globally disseminated resistance mechanisms in airborne spores across Norway demonstrates that environmental azole resistance is established in the region. This study provides baseline data on the frequency and distribution of environmental AR Af in Norway and contributes to international efforts to strengthen monitoring of antifungal resistance. Importance Azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus (ARAf) is an emerging public health concern, yet data from northern Europe remain limited. This study provides the first nationwide investigation of the frequency, distribution, and genetic diversity of environmental ARAf in Norway. By combining community-based environmental sampling with whole-genome sequencing, we demonstrate that resistance-associated genotypes of international concern are established in the Norwegian environment and occur across multiple regions. These findings provide important baseline data for future surveillance and contribute to global efforts to monitor and understand the emergence and spread of antifungal resistance.

items.title: Ventilator Modes Used to Facilitate Liberation From Mechanical Ventilation: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Objectives Liberation from invasive ventilation involves gradual decrements in respiratory support, spontaneous breathing trials, or both. Although various ventilator modes have been studied to facilitate weaning, the approaches used across trials for the highest risk patients are not well summarized. We sought to summarize the different ventilator modes and liberation strategies that have been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of critically ill adults at risk for difficult or prolonged weaning from invasive ventilation. Data sources We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 2026. Study selection We conducted a scoping review of RCTs that enrolled critically ill adults (≥ 18 yr) who received invasive ventilation for greater than or equal to 24 hours and were considered to have either difficult or prolonged weaning (Weaning according to a New Definition [WIND] group "no wean," "difficult weaning," or "prolonged weaning") and compared two or more assisted ventilatory modes. We excluded trials that compared ventilatory modes for spontaneous breathing test (SBT) conduct, invasive vs. noninvasive ventilation, or tracheostomized patients at the time of randomization. Data extraction We extracted data related to eligibility criteria, outcomes, and weaning protocols and assessed risk of bias using a modified Cochrane risk of bias tool in duplicate. Data synthesis Among 38 eligible trials, the most studied ventilatory modes were pressure support ventilation (71.1%, 27 trials) and synchronized intermittent or intermittent mandatory ventilation (31.6%, 12 trials). The most frequently studied automated modes were SmartCare/pressure support (15.8%, six trials) and proportional assist ventilation (15.8%, six trials). Weaning typically used a gradual reduction in support without a mode change (52.6%, 20 trials), or with intermittent SBTs (31.6%, 12 trials). Overall risk of bias was commonly high due to a probably high risk of selective reporting. Conclusions Diverse modes and strategies have been evaluated to achieve liberation. Future research should focus on adequately powered, high-quality trials of the effect of commonly used and widely available modes and strategies on clinically important outcomes for liberation from mechanical ventilation of high-risk patients.

items.title: Incyclinide exhibits potent antibacterial and anti-biofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus.
items.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and biofilm-associated infections remain major therapeutic challenges. Here, we investigated the antibacterial activity and mechanism of Incyclinide against S. aureus . Incyclinide showed potent activity against 40 clinical isolates, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 µM for 81.25% of MSSA isolates and 91.66% of MRSA isolates. In representative MSSA and MRSA strains, 1× MIC completely inhibited planktonic growth, while time-kill assays demonstrated concentration-dependent bactericidal activity; at 8× MIC, bacterial counts decreased by 3.2 log 10 CFU/mL in NCTC 8325 and 4.3 log 10 CFU/mL in USA300 after 24 h. Incyclinide also markedly reduced the biomass of mature, pre-established biofilms. Proteomic profiling of Incyclinide-treated USA300 identified 59 differentially expressed proteins enriched in membrane-related functions. Transmission electron microscopy and fluorescence assays revealed severe cell envelope damage, increased membrane permeability, and membrane depolarization. Exogenous phospholipids antagonized antibacterial activity, with phosphatidylethanolamine and cardiolipin showing stronger effects than phosphatidylglycerol. In addition, resistance induction and whole-genome sequencing identified recurrent clpX mutations; clpX deletion increased the MIC from 2 to 8 µM, whereas complementation restored susceptibility. Molecular docking suggested favorable binding between Incyclinide and ClpX, with a predicted binding energy of -9.4 kcal/mol. Incyclinide also exhibited low hemolytic activity, negligible cytotoxicity toward BEAS-2B and human umbilical vein endothelial cell up to 128 µM, and significant protection in a Galleria mellonella infection model. Collectively, these findings identify Incyclinide as a promising anti- S . aureus agent with potent activity against MRSA and mature biofilms, acting primarily through membrane disruption, with ClpX potentially contributing to susceptibility.IMPORTANCEMethicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and biofilm-associated infections pose significant clinical challenges due to limited therapeutic options. Here, we identify Incyclinide, a tetracycline derivative, as a potent anti- S . aureus agent. It exhibits potent bactericidal activity against clinical MRSA isolates and effectively eradicates mature biofilms. Mechanistically, Incyclinide disrupts membrane integrity, causing depolarization and leakage. Notably, we identify the essential chaperone ClpX as a key molecular determinant of susceptibility through genetic and docking studies. Incyclinide demonstrates a favorable safety profile and superior efficacy compared with vancomycin in a Galleria mellonella infection model. Our findings highlight Incyclinide as a promising candidate featuring a dual membrane-targeting and intracellular mechanism, offering a strategic advantage against drug-resistant and biofilm-embedded pathogens.

items.title: Before the first complaint: first response review as a practical governance teaching method in GP speciality training.
items.abstract: Clinical governance is taught during GP training, but practical exposure is uneven. A trainee may complete learning event analyses without ever receiving a complaint or being shown what to do immediately after a serious concern is raised. This Teaching Exchange describes First Response Review, a 30- to 45-minute tutorial method developed through routine one-to-one supervision. The trainer uses one anonymised closed case or a short composite scenario and asks the trainee to work across four lanes: patient, process, record and practitioner. Each lane is considered across three clocks: now, today and next. Six steps structure the conversation: separate fact from allegation, identify continuing risk, name every relevant pathway, assign ownership, protect communication and documentation, and locate support. A Complaint-Harm Grid helps trainees understand that complaints and patient harm are related but separate dimensions of care; either may occur without the other, and responses may run in parallel. The exercise is formative, not an investigation, significant event analysis or legal rehearsal. It requires one printed page and knowledge of local routes. First Response Review offers a simple way to teach governance as actions before a trainee has to learn it during a real complaint in independent practice.

items.title: Care-Partner Support Needs During Recovery After Fecal Ostomy Surgery in Older Adults: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Background Older adults recovering after fecal ostomy surgery may require substantial care-partner support, yet the activities requiring assistance and barriers to obtaining support are poorly understood. We sought to identify care-partner contributions to recovery and opportunities to improve care-partner involvement. Study design We conducted semi-structured interviews 30-90 days after planned fecal ostomy surgery among adults aged ≥65 years at a tertiary academic medical center. Purposive sampling captured experiences across the aging spectrum and benign and malignant indications. Interviews were analyzed using hybrid inductive-deductive coding and a modified Framework method until thematic saturation was reached. Results Twenty-one participants completed interviews; median age was 73 years (IQR 68-77), 13 (61.9%) were female, 11 (52.4%) underwent surgery for benign disease, and 10 (47.6%) for colorectal malignancy. Preoperative vulnerabilities included cane/walker use in 5 (23.8%), wheelchair use in 4 (19.0%), >5% weight loss in 10 (47.6%), and polypharmacy in 14 (66.7%). Care-partners provided emotional and psychological support, ostomy-specific assistance, shopping and cooking, transportation and mobility assistance, and cleaning and housework. Participants frequently described variable care-partner availability and unanticipated support needs. Physical distance, reluctance to request assistance, and financial costs to care-partners further constrained support. Most participants supported an intervention to identify care-partners and organize anticipated recovery tasks. Conclusions Older adults recovering from fecal ostomy surgery require care-partner support across multiple domains, but support may be unavailable or unanticipated. Explicit preoperative identification of anticipated tasks and available care-partners may improve preparation for postdischarge recovery.

items.title: Boundaries Without Walls: The Ethical Challenge of Outdoor Mental Health Treatment.
items.abstract: Outdoor mental health treatment, including walk-and-talk therapy, has emerged as a novel extension of psychiatric care grounded in theories of nature's restorative effects. Despite potential clinical benefits, such practices raise ethical concerns insufficiently addressed by frameworks developed for indoor settings. Challenges arise in preserving confidentiality within public environments, maintaining professional boundaries amid increased informality, ensuring patient and provider safety, addressing inequities in access, and securing adequate liability coverage. These concerns warrant deliberate adaptation of established ethical norms to guide responsible implementation of care in outdoor contexts.

items.title: Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N.
items.abstract: Background Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear. Methods Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury-AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis-related genes after AKI. Results Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes ( FN1, COL1A1, TGF-β1 ), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N. Conclusions We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

items.title: Multiple Traumas Accelerate the Transition From Cardiovascular Disease to Depression: A Multistate Study.
items.abstract: Background Traumas are risk factors for both cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depression. However, the specific impacts of trauma on the critical transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression and mortality remain scarce. Methods Using data from the UK Biobank cohort ( N =138 036), we constructed multistate models to investigate the associations of childhood trauma, adult trauma, and lifetime trauma with the transitions between health states. Specifically, we modeled transitions from a healthy state to incident CVD, further to subsequent depression, and ultimately to death. Results Over a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 14 278 participants developed incident CVD, with 679 developed subsequent depression and 4144 dying. Trauma was positively associated with the dynamic disease progression: the transition from baseline to incident CVD showed significantly elevated hazards for multiple childhood traumas (hazard ratio [HR], 1.294 [95% CI, 1.170-1.432]), adult traumas (HR, 1.145 [95% CI, 1.071-1.225]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.632 [95% CI, 1.528-1.742]) compared with no trauma exposure. Similarly, the transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression demonstrated increased risks for multiple childhood traumas (HR, 2.260 [95% CI, 1.661-3.075]), adult traumas (HR, 1.950 [95% CI, 1.510-2.518]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.608 [95% CI, 1.245-2.078]) versus no trauma exposure. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that exposure to multiple traumas significantly increases the risk of developing depression following an incident CVD diagnosis. This underscores the urgent need for clinical and public health interventions targeting multiple traumas to mitigate the risk of CVD and depression progression, thereby improving outcomes.

items.title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
items.abstract: Background Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. Methods We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge. Results Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6. Conclusions Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

Results A total of 699 patients (mean age, 78±8 years; 56% women) were included in the analysis. Echocardiographic follow-up was performed at a median of 407 days (interquartile range, 205-801 days). items.title: Greenspace Exposure Reduces the Risk of Hypertension: A Large Prospective Cohort Study in Northwestern China.
items.abstract: Background The effects of greenspace on hypertension remain unconfirmed. This study aimed to validate this by performing a large prospective cohort study in China. Methods PEAHEN-China (Prospective Environment and Health Epidemiological Study in Northwestern China) recruited 5 484 119 adults in 2017 and followed them to 2021. Blood pressure levels and hypertension were measured and defined using recommended standards. Greenspace exposure was estimated using the normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index. Cox regression models and generalized estimating equation models were used to assess the associations of greenspace with hypertension incidence and blood pressure levels, respectively. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were also performed. Results During a median 3.21-year follow-up, 1 290 003 new hypertension cases occurred. Living in greener areas was significantly associated with a lower risk of hypertension and lower blood pressure levels. For example, in the adjusted models, compared with the first quartile of normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index within a 500-m buffer, the hazard ratios of incident hypertension in the fourth quartile of the 2 metrics were 0.871 (95% CI, 0.861-0.881) and 0.896 (95% CI, 0.885-0.906). In addition, stronger associations of greenspace exposure with hypertension risk and blood pressure levels were observed in younger, male, rural, and less educated participants than their counterparts. Conclusions Our study indicates that neighborhood greenspace may reduce residents' odds of having hypertension, offering robust evidence for developing policies and strategies to mitigate the burden of hypertension.

items.title: Age-Related Differences in Physical Activity for Primary Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease: Insights From Wearable Accelerometers.
items.abstract: Background Current physical activity recommendations suggest at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD) across ages. However, age-related disparities exist in exercise capability, engagement, and guideline adherence, and their implications for CHD prevention remain underexplored. Methods We included wrist-worn accelerometer data from 80 243 UK Biobank participants (aged 61.54±7.84 years, 57.3% women), classified as older (≥65 years; n=31 663) or middle-aged ( Results Over a median follow-up of 7.88 years, 3764 CHD events occurred. A 20% lower CHD risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.8) was observed at approximately 60 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in older adults versus 330 minutes per week in middle-aged adults ( P interaction =0.006). Guideline adherence was associated with stronger inverse associations in older than in middle-aged adults (HR, 0.72 versus 0.85; P interaction =0.029). Older weekend warriors exhibited a 28% lower CHD risk, comparable with regularly active individuals, whereas the association was weaker and nonsignificant in middle-aged adults ( P interaction =0.005). At 150 minutes per week, a 10% lower CHD risk corresponded to an acceleration threshold of 100 milligravity in middle-aged adults but approximately 55 milligravity in older adults. A possible U-shaped relationship was observed in older adults. Conclusions The findings suggest potential age-related heterogeneity in wearable-measured physical activity for CHD prevention, and may help motivate activity engagement among older adults and enhance CHD prevention.

items.title: Fabrication of Multiscale Porous Hydrogel Scaffold for Air-Liquid Interface Culture of Epithelial Cells Using Nebulized CaCl2-Assisted Three-Step Cross-Linking Three-Dimensional Printing.
items.abstract: Creating thick tissue constructs that can enable air-liquid interface (ALI) culture is of great interest for the culture of epithelial cells. This paper presents a method of using nebulized calcium chloride (CaCl2)-assisted three-dimensional printing with a sacrificial polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) porogen component for the fabrication of a thick, multiscale porous scaffold for ALI cell culture. The ink used for scaffold fabrication is composed of gelatin microgels, PVA, sodium alginate, and a continuous gelatin solution. This fabrication approach utilizes ionic in situ cross-linking of sodium alginate using nebulized CaCl2, in addition to gelatin microgel jamming-based physical cross-linking during printing and enzymatic cross-linking of gelatin-based scaffolds post-printing, to create a robust structure, incorporating three different cross-linking steps. Exposure to the nebulized CaCl2 increases the storage modulus of the gel from 150 Pa to over 700 Pa and increases printing fidelity significantly. After cross-linking, the PVA component is leached from the scaffold, creating a network of pores to enhance transport. Printed scaffolds are able to transport 10 kDa molecules, roughly analogous to standard protein sizes. For applications in cell culture, the printing approach described here is used to fabricate a thick cylindrical scaffold with multiscale porosity, with printed macropores present in all but the solid top layer and micropores throughout the entire scaffold. Cells cultured on such porous scaffolds maintain a high degree of confluence, with an 88.1% surface coverage, while being exposed to air for multiple days. To demonstrate potential use of this approach to create drug screening platforms, cells grown on the scaffolds are exposed to the cancer drug Ulixertinib, delivered via scaffold transport. These results demonstrate that the presented fabrication method can be used to make porous scaffolds for the creation of an ALI culture environment, an important step towards biomimetic ALI models for biomedical applications, including therapeutic screening.

items.title: Promoting Equitable Access to Addiction Recovery among Hispanic/Latino Men Experiencing Homelessness.
items.abstract: IntroductionHispanic and Latino men are disproportionately impacted by substance abuse and face greater barriers in accessing addiction treatment. The purpose of this manuscript is to evaluate an innovative program for Hispanic/Latino men experiencing homelessness and addiction within the context of a faith-based, 12-step, residential addiction recovery program in Baltimore City.MethodThe program design is based on a peer recovery model where bilingual peer recovery coaches, mentors, and practitioners provide coordinated addiction treatment and wrap around services. Program outcomes are tracked through a Progress to Life Transformation matrix covering five overarching domains: sobriety, spirituality, relationships, physical and emotional wellness, and community re-integration (education, employment, housing).ResultsIn its first two years, program enrollment increased by 500%. Outcome data revealed improvement in all domains from program entry to exit with a 28% improvement in overall scores. The domains with the greatest degree of improvement related to spirituality and recovery, while the least improvement was noted in the community re-integration domain.ConclusionThis program provided culturally responsive addiction treatment and comprehensive wrap around services through a coordinated continuum of care. Barriers to progress included lack of access to health care, housing, legal aid, and culturally responsive education and workforce development opportunities.

items.title: Life Expectancy After Incident Ischemic Stroke in a Bi-Ethnic Population: Estimates Over 2005 to 2022.
items.abstract: Background This study measured 5- and 10-year life expectancy after an incident ischemic stroke using a high-quality sample of Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White patients over a recent period. Methods Data were from the Brain Attack Surveillance in Corpus Christi Project. The sample included 2011 Mexican American and 1262 non-Hispanic White men and women who had an incident ischemic stroke during 2005 to 2022 and were aged 45 years or older at the time of stroke. Participants were followed up to 18 years. Primary outcome was 5- and 10-year life expectancy. Discrete-time logistic regression models were implemented. Results Mean age at incident stroke was 69 years. There was no difference in the odds of dying between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White men and women after adjustment for age at stroke and sex. Among men, an incident stroke at age 70 years was associated with a 10-year life expectancy of 6.4 years (95% CI: 6.1-6.6) in Mexican Americans and 6.5 years (95% CI: 6.2-6.9) in non-Hispanic White adults. Among women, the analogous 10-year life expectancy was 6.7 years (95% CI: 6.3-6.8) in Mexican Americans and 6.8 years (95% CI: 6.4-7.0) in non-Hispanic White adults. Comparing these estimates to life expectancy at age 70 in the general US population indicates that stroke is associated with a life shortening effect of 2.1 to 2.4 years over 10 years. Conclusions Life expectancy after an ischemic stroke did not differ between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White adults. Incident ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial life shortening effects in the recent period.
