items.title: Toxicological epidemiology and utilization patterns of Nepal's first institution-based poison information center.
items.abstract: Introduction Poisoning remains a major cause of preventable morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries, yet Nepal has historically lacked centralized toxicology surveillance and consultation services. In 2023, piloting of an institution-based poison information center was done at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital through a multi-national collaboration. We describe the epidemiology, utilization patterns, and clinical characteristics of cases managed during the pilot phase of the Nepal Poison Information Center. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of prospectively collected data from all consultations reported to the Nepal Poison Information Center between September 2023 and December 2024. Trained poison center specialists documented demographic characteristics, exposure details, toxicological agents, consultation characteristics, and clinical disposition using a secure database. Data cleaning and descriptive analyses were conducted using SAS statistical software (version 9.4; SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC). Results A total of 393 poisoning cases were managed during the pilot period (September 2023-December 2024). Most patients were aged 18-39 years (53.4%), and 53.7% were female. Suspected intentional self-harm (suicidal-intent) accounted for 55.0% of exposures. Pesticides were the most common toxicological agents (46.1%), with insecticides (50.3%) and rodenticides (26.0%) predominating. Non-pesticide exposures included mushroom poisoning (8.1%), chemical exposures (7.6%), snake envenomation (6.9%), and medication-related poisonings (3.3%). The median time from exposure to poison information center phone call was four hours (IQR 1.0-15.0 hours). International toxicology experts were consulted in 28.2% of cases. The most common initial clinical disposition was observation in the emergency department (39.2%). Discussion: First, cases were dominated by intentional exposures, with suspected suicide accounting for 55% of all consultations. Second, pesticides represented nearly half of all primary toxicological agents (46.1%), with insecticides and rodenticides as the most common subtypes. Third, nearly one in three cases required consultation with international toxicology experts (28.2%), highlighting both the complexity of poisoning presentations and the limited availability of specialized toxicology expertise within Nepal. Together, these findings demonstrate that the pilot institutional PIC successfully operationalized a 24/7 toxicology consultation and follow-up model (previously described) while generating a centralized dataset capable of informing toxicovigilance, suicide prevention strategies, and regulatory policy. The PIC's model requires a daily follow up (and earlier if clinically indicated) of the patient (via phone by calling the treating providers) to acquire patient's clinical status and disposition plan. This study highlights the essential components required for sustainable poison center operations, including dedicated staffing, reliable telecommunications infrastructure, structured training pathways, continuous quality improvement processes, and integration of poisoning management within national emergency care and public health frameworks. Anchoring the pilot at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, a government-affiliated academic institution, was a strategic decision that provided institutional credibility, access to clinical pharmacology leadership, and a platform for national advocacy. Conclusion During its pilot phase, Nepal's first institutional poison information center successfully delivered nationwide toxicology consultation and generated a centralized poisoning dataset. The predominance of intentional pesticide exposures and rising burden of other agents underscores the need for integrated suicide prevention strategies, strengthened pesticide regulation, and sustained investment in toxicology capacity and poison center infrastructure in Nepal.

items.title: Sample size estimation for pre- and post-intervention design with incomplete observations of count outcomes.
items.abstract: The pre- and post-intervention design is frequently utilized in medical and behavioral research, with each subject typically providing a pair of observations collected before and after the intervention. However, not all subjects furnish complete pairs of data. Some subjects may contribute either pre- or post-intervention information only. In this study, we proposed a sample size formula based on the generalized estimating equation (GEE) method for clinical trials where subjects are supposed to provide pre- and post-intervention measurements of a count outcome. The sample size formula is flexible to accommodate different missing patterns, magnitude of missingness and correlation. We compared it with the crude sample size adjustment approach for missing data, which is commonly used in practice and involves dividing the required sample size under complete observations by the proportion of subjects with complete data. Through simulation studies, we evaluated the empirical performance of the proposed sample size formula in preserving desired power and type I error. Furthermore, we presented a clinical trial example to demonstrate its application.

items.title: Serum vitamin D, innate immunity markers, and biofilm presence as determinants of therapeutic strategies in diabetic foot infections: A comparative cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: BackgroundSevere diabetic foot infections (DFIs) often require surgical management (SM), whereas less severe infections may be managed medically (MM). Vitamin D, its receptor (VDR), and LL-37 play key roles in innate immunity, wound healing, and antimicrobial defense.AimTo determine the association between serum vitamin D, VDR, and LL-37 levels and the prevalence of biofilm-forming bacteria in SM and MM in patients with DFIs.Methods207 patients with DFIs were recruited from the Department of General Surgery, Kasturba Hospital, Manipal, India, between September 2022 and September 2025. Treatment allocation (SM or MM) was determined by the attending surgeons based on DFI severity. At 24 h after treatment initiation, blood samples were collected for vitamin D assessment (electrochemiluminescence immunoassay) and VDR and LL-37 quantification using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Biofilm formation was analyzed using the tissue culture plate method.ResultsOf the 207 participants, 169 (81.64%) required SM and 38 (18.36%) received MM. Patients with SM had significantly lower median levels of vitamin D (12.6 vs. 24.3 ng/mL), VDR (0.69 vs. 1.34 ng/mL), and LL-37 (1.28 vs. 2.46 ng/mL) compared to those with MM (all p p = 0.004) and CRP levels ( p = 0.034) after adjusting confounders. Among the 182 biofilm-forming bacterial isolates, 87.4% were isolated from patients undergoing SM and 12.6% from those receiving MM ( p < 0.001).SummaryLower serum vitamin D, VDR, and LL-37 levels, together with a higher prevalence of biofilm-forming bacteria, were associated with greater DFI severity and an increased likelihood of SM.

items.title: Embedding the Cultural Health Navigator Model: A Health System-Integrated Approach for Refugee Care.
items.abstract: Resettled refugees and culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) populations face persistent barriers to health care, including linguistic constraints, cultural disconnects, and limited availability of system-integrated approaches responsive to their needs. This article presents the Cultural Health Navigator (CHN) model, a health system-integrated community health worker (CHW) approach developed within an Arizona Medicaid-integrated public safety-net hospital system. The model embeds trained, multilingual CHNs within clinical workflows to provide culturally and linguistically responsive navigation, health education, care coordination, medical interpretation, and linkage to clinical and community resources. We apply the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) retrospectively to describe the model's implementation features and use the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework to guide prospective evaluation. The CHN model integrates CHW certification, clinical workflows, community partnerships, electronic health record infrastructure, and Medicaid reimbursement pathways to support implementation and sustainability. Preliminary evidence from the program supports continued evaluation of its potential contributions to patient navigation, trust, health literacy, health care utilization, and maternal and newborn health. We present the CHN model as a practice-based, potentially transferable implementation approach that health systems can adapt to strengthen culturally responsive care for refugees and other CALD populations. Future evaluation should establish its effectiveness, sustainability, and transferability across diverse health care settings.

items.title: Data quality and discharge-time readmission risk in diabetes hospitalisations.
items.abstract: Background Electronic health record (EHR) and administrative data are widely reused for readmission modelling, but models may learn from documentation completeness, coding pathways and measurement availability as well as from clinical status. Objective This study assessed how documentation completeness, administrative fields and interpretable clinical predictors shaped discharge-time 30-day readmission risk stratification among hospitalised patients with diabetes. Method A retrospective secondary analysis of the public Diabetes 130-US hospitals for years 1999-2008 dataset was conducted. Encounters with death or hospice-related discharge dispositions were excluded. The outcome was 30-day readmission. Four calibrated logistic regression models compared core clinical variables, administrative fields and missingness indicators under a discharge-time prediction frame. Uncertainty was estimated using patient-level clustered bootstrap resampling. Results The cohort included 99,343 encounters from 69,990 patient identifiers; 11,314 encounters (11.4%) had 30-day readmission. Weight, maximum glucose serum, A1C result, medical specialty and payer code were missing or not recorded in 96.9%, 94.8%, 83.1%, 48.9% and 39.7% of encounters, respectively. Adding administrative fields increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from 0.640 to 0.667 (ΔAUROC 0.0266, 95% clustered bootstrap confidence interval (CI) 0.0178 to 0.0347). Missingness indicators alone produced little change (ΔAUROC 0.0019, 95% CI -0.0007 to 0.0046). The full model containing administrative fields and missingness indicators showed similar discrimination (AUROC 0.666). Conclusion The modest performance gain was driven mainly by administrative coding and discharge-pathway variables. EHR readmission studies should define prediction timing, report measurement availability and interpret model performance as a product of clinical data generation as well as clinical risk.Implications for health information management practice:Secondary-use EHR modelling should profile variable availability, establish predictor timing and provenance, test administrative-field contributions and report calibrated performance before local use.

items.title: Mind the gap: patient perspectives on missing links in access to and participation in exercise and rehabilitation of polyneuropathy.
items.abstract: Purpose The study aimed to explore how patients with polyneuropathy experience access to and participation in exercise and rehabilitation, how they perceive the provided exercise, and to understand the facilitators and barriers to engagement in exercise and rehabilitation. Materials and methods We performed a qualitative study interviewing patients with polyneuropathy. The study combined deductive and inductive approaches. While the interview guide was developed based on our clinical experience and knowledge and informed by the COM-B model, the analysis was data-driven, following Reflexive Thematic Analysis as described by Braun & Clarke. Results Thirteen participants were included. We generated three themes and eight subthemes. The themes were: (1) Exercise as a cornerstone of everyday life; (2) Navigating polyneuropathy and exercise depends on information, guidance, and support; (3) Individualized exercise: through professional expertise, adaptation, and patient experiences. Conclusions Participants perceived access to and participation in the exercise and rehabilitation provided to vary considerably, with gaps in support. Facilitators for exercise included viewing exercise as imperative to regaining physical functioning to preserve identity, as well as individualized assessments, adjustments, and goal setting. Barriers to exercise included unspecific exercises, insufficient information and guidance from physiotherapists, leading to uncertainty about exercise planning, safety, and effectiveness.

items.title: Proportion of frailty across eGFR categories and their association with patient-reported outcomes: insights from the SHARE database.
items.abstract: Background Frailty is a common condition among older adults with high prevalence within the dialysis population, but there has not been a large-scale investigation among European older adults with reduced eGFR. The objectives of this study are to describe the proportion of frailty among adults aged ≥50 years with reduced eGFR in the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) and assess the association between frailty, eGFR, and patient-reported outcomes. Methods We used cross-sectional data from Wave 6 of SHARE. Participants were categorized using CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin-based equations. Frailty was measured with the Fried's Frailty Scale. Results A total of 23,028 participants with a mean age of 68 years were included in the analysis. The proportion of pre-frailty/frailty was higher in the lower eGFR categories: 49% of those with eGFR≥60 ml/min/1.73m2, 75.0% of those with eGFR:45-59 ml/min/1.73m2 (G3a), 87.3% of eGFR:30-44 ml/min/1.73m2 (G3b), and 92.9% of eGFR≤29 ml/min/1.73m2 (G4/G5) were classified as pre-frail or frail. GFR categories were associated with frailty categories after adjustment for age and sex. Compared to subjects with eGFR≥60 ml/min/1.73m2, those in the G3a, G3b, and G4/G5 categories had 1.18, 1.28 and 2.11 times higher odds for worse self-rated health, respectively. Quality of life scores were lower in participants with reduced eGFR, while impairments in instrumental activities of daily living were more common. Conclusions Increased frailty levels are common in adults with reduced eGFR. Lower eGFR categories were consistently associated with frailty and greater IADL impairment. Geriatric assessments should be considered in this population.

items.title: Bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract alleviates insulin resistance in gestational diabetes mellitus by modulating the AKT/LRRFIP1/GLUT4 pathway in skeletal muscle.
items.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is characterized by progressive insulin resistance (IR), with skeletal muscle representing a primary site of this pathology. This study investigated the potential of anthocyanin-rich bilberry ( Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract (VME) to ameliorate skeletal muscle IR in a high-fat diet (HFD) induced rat model of GDM. We integrated proteomics and bioinformatics approaches to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.UHPLC-MS/MS analysis identified cyanidin-3- O -galactoside (C3Gal) as the principal anthocyanin constituent of VME. Daily oral administration of VME (400 mg per kg bw) during pregnancy ameliorated hyperglycemia, IR, and dyslipidemia, and improved oral glucose tolerance in GDM rats. Proteomic analysis of gastrocnemius muscle identified VME associated differentially expressed proteins as candidate targets for further investigation. Gene set enrichment analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis implicated AKT signaling and highlighted Lrrfip1 as a hub gene correlated with HOMA-IR. Cross-species comparison with human type 2 diabetes skeletal muscle transcriptomes (GSE55650, GSE7014) supported target prioritization, with LRRFIP1 showing concordant regulation at both mRNA and protein levels. Molecular docking predicted binding of C3Gal to AKT and LRRFIP1, and a cellular thermal shift assay supported cellular target engagement of C3Gal with these proteins. C3Gal restored p-AKT and GLUT4 levels both in vivo and in palmitate-induced C2C12 myotubes. siRNA mediated knockdown of Lrrfip1 attenuated these effects, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AKT abolished them. Collectively, these findings support LRRFIP1 as a downstream mediator of AKT associated GLUT4 regulation. Together, our data propose LRRFIP1 as a candidate molecular target associated with skeletal muscle IR and support further investigation of VME as a potential dietary intervention for GDM associated IR.

items.title: Prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus, risk factors, and complications in Middle East and North African region: A systematic review.
items.abstract: BackgroundType 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly growing health challenge in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, contributing to increasing morbidity and mortality.ObjectivesThis review synthesizes evidence on the prevalence of T2DM, risk factors, and complications in the MENA region.MethodsFollowing PRISMA reporting guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD420251111168), systematic searches were conducted for studies published between 2015 and 2025.ResultsAcross the 19 included studies, the prevalence and burden of T2DM varied considerably across the MENA region. Regional data indicated an 85.5% increase in diabetes prevalence between 1990 and 2019, while individual population-based studies reported T2DM prevalence of 32.0% in north-eastern Tunisia and 15.3% in southwestern Iran. In Jordan, age-standardized diabetes prevalence increased from 13.0% in 1994 to 23.7% in 2017. Older age, obesity, physical inactivity, hypertension, central adiposity, family history of diabetes, and socioeconomic factors were commonly associated with T2DM. Among individuals with established T2DM, microvascular and macrovascular complications were reported in 17.7% and 10.7%, respectively, while diabetic neuropathy affected 15.3%-23.0% in selected studies. Suboptimal glycaemic and cardiovascular risk-factor control was also frequently reported.ConclusionT2DM constitutes a substantial and heterogeneous public health challenge across the MENA region. The findings indicate a need for context-specific strategies that integrate prevention, early detection, culturally appropriate lifestyle interventions, and comprehensive long-term disease management. Strengthening multidisciplinary approaches and addressing modifiable risk factors may help reduce the future health burden associated with T2DM across the region.

items.title: Determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents in Sekondi-Takoradi, Western Region of Ghana: A community-based cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Mpox re-emerged as a global public health concern in 2022, and the Western Region of Ghana became the epicentre of the country’s largest recorded outbreak in 2025. Ahead of a sub-national vaccination campaign launched in October 2025, no study had examined the determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the region using a theoretically grounded framework. This study determined the sociodemographic and Health Belief Model-based determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Western Region, Ghana. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 580 adults in six purposively selected peri-urban areas and their surrounding communities between July and August 2025, before the vaccination campaign began. Vaccine acceptance was measured as a three-category outcome (accept, hesitant, refuse) and analysed using chi square tests and multinomial logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, Health Belief Model constructs, and peri-urban area. Overall, 75.7% of respondents were willing to accept the vaccine, 12.9% were hesitant and 11.4% would refuse. Perceived vaccine safety was the strongest determinant: respondents who considered the vaccine very safe had markedly lower adjusted odds of hesitancy (adjusted odds ratio 0.02, 95% confidence interval 0.00–0.12) and refusal (0.03, 0.01–0.13) than those who considered it unsafe. Uncertainty about vaccine effectiveness was associated with hesitancy (9.83, 1.95–49.50), and belief in its effectiveness with lower odds of refusal (0.22, 0.06–0.86). Higher educational attainment was associated with lower odds of hesitancy, being a student or employed with lower odds of refusal, and acceptance differed be 1 tween peri-urban areas (55.1% to 95.6%). Knowledge of mpox transmission was associated with acceptance in bivariate analysis (p < 0.001) but not after adjustment. Risk communication that addresses vaccine safety and effectiveness, rather than generic disease-awareness messaging alone, is likely to be most effec tive in improving mpox vaccine acceptance in this population, with unemployed and less-educated residents warranting targeting. As a pre-campaign baseline collected during an active outbreak, these findings can inform the vaccination response in the Western Region and preparedness in comparable peri-urban West African settings.

items.title: Phylogeography and transmission dynamics of the 2025-2026 Utah-Arizona measles outbreak: a retrospective genomic epidemiology study
items.abstract: Background: Measles outbreaks are increasing in frequency globally as vaccine coverage decreases. During the 2025-26 Utah-Arizona border outbreak, identifying where and between whom transmission occurred was essential for directing control measures. However, epidemiological data alone are not sufficient to infer transmission patterns. Methods: As part of the local and state-wide outbreak investigation, we conducted amplicon-based whole genome sequencing on residual diagnostic samples from confirmed measles cases collected from June 15, 2025-April 30, 2026. We reconstructed viral dispersal across Utah using Bayesian phylogeographic analyses. We evaluated genetic distance thresholds for identifying recent transmission by comparing single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based genetic clusters with known epidemiologic linkages. We then assessed pairwise exposures associated with genetically supported transmission linkage using logistic regression, accounting for network and spatial dependence between pairs. Findings: We generated 509 high-quality whole measles virus genomes from 913 patients. In 2025, most viral dispersal events (67.9%) originated in Southwest Utah and Mohave County, Arizona, where the first cases were reported. By 2026, most viral spread (60.5%) occurred outside of this area. A threshold of 0 SNPs identified epidemiologically linked pairs of individuals with a sensitivity of 77.4% and specificity of 92.3%. Household membership (odds ratio (OR): 219.10, 95% credible interval (CI): 112.66-325.53), participation in the same sport (OR: 15.19, 95% CI: 9.75-20.63), and attendance at the same school (OR: 51.5, 95% CI: 36.38-66.61) were independently associated with transmission linkage. Increasing distance between households was associated with reduced odds of linkage (OR: 0.46: 95% CI 0.44-0.48). Interpretation: Repeated introductions of measles virus from southwestern Utah seeded transmission elsewhere in Utah, with household, school, and sports exposures contributing to onward transmission. Validated genome-based linkage measures can complement contact tracing by helping public health teams identify likely transmission networks and prioritize investigation when resources are constrained.

items.title: Antifolate resistance markers and complexity of infection in children with sickle cell anaemia receiving malaria chemoprevention in Uganda: a molecular sub-study of the CHEMCHA randomised trial
items.abstract: Background: Sickle cell anaemia (SCA) is a major public health problem in Uganda. Monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) remains the standard malaria chemoprevention regimen despite widespread antifolate resistance in East Africa. We assessed Pfdhfr and Pfdhps resistance mutations and the complexity of infection (COI) among children with SCA receiving malaria chemoprevention. Methods This prospective study of antifolate resistance was nested within the CHEMCHA randomised controlled trial comparing monthly SP with weekly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP) for malaria chemoprevention. Participants were children with SCA aged 6 months to 15 years and attending Jinja and Kitgum hospitals in Uganda. Dried blood spots were collected at enrolment, study closeout, and during febrile episodes. Parasite DNA from microscopy-confirmed clinical malaria samples was genotyped by amplicon sequencing for Pfdhfr (N51I, C59R, S108N, and I164L) and Pfdhps (A437G, K540E, A581G, A613S, and A613T). COI was estimated using MOIRE. Results Complete Pfdhfr/Pfdhps haplotypes were resolved for 7-28 isolates per site and time point, and COI was estimated for 67 samples. The quintuple mutant (Pfdhfr IRN/Pfdhps GE) accounted for 85.7-100% of isolates across sites and time points; A613S and A613T were not detected. Pfdhfr I164L was detected in 2/9 isolates in Jinja at baseline and 1/8 at endline. The Pfdhps A581G mutant allele was absent at baseline (0/44 isolates) but was found in 1/8 isolates in Jinja and 3/34 in Kitgum at endline, including quintuple-plus-581G (sextuple) haplotypes in 1/8 and 2/27 isolates, respectively. Most infections were monoclonal (51/67, 76.1%). Conclusions The high prevalence of quintuple antifolate-resistant haplotypes and the detection of higher-level resistance markers, including emerging sextuple mutants carrying Pfdhfr I164L and Pfdhps A581G, call into question the continued use of SP for chemoprevention in children with SCA in Uganda and support evaluation of alternative regimens.

items.title: A Novel Extreme Weather Risk Insurance System for Kenya (NEWRISK): Encouraging preparedness, planning, community co-design, and protection of Kenya’s health system from the effects of extreme weather
items.abstract: Kenya is a frontline country for extreme weather and faces long droughts, flooding and heat waves. This study will focus on the broader, pervasive health risks associated with the reduction or catastrophic withdrawal of health services. Our aim is to determine what extreme weather hazards Kenya faces, and how resulting impacts on the population and health service can be mitigated, creating scalable tools that inform planning. This study will be carried out in four counties, selected to represent the different climatic regions of Kenya. We will conduct a mixed methods study drawing on qualitative participatory approaches, climate modelling, health facility surveys and health economic modelling. We will conduct a policy document review; non-participant observations of key county budgeting and planning events; in-depth interviews with health managers; and stakeholder dialogue workshops to co-create a framework for developing extreme weather mitigation plans. We will use the latest climate analysis techniques to provide high resolution data on heat and precipitation for the whole of Kenya. Drawing on secondary data, we will then create a population vulnerability index to spatially represent vulnerable populations. We will create a tool to assess the readiness of public health facilities across four counties. We will map this data to understand the interactions between extreme weather, population vulnerability, and the health system. We will present this information during community consultation and stakeholder workshops to get input and co-develop mitigation plans. Finally, we will use health economics methods to estimate the costs of doing nothing versus various protective strategies. We will create a set of tools and methods that can be combined to analyse the extreme weather threats posed to health systems or inform a climate risk insurance product. We expect to provide policymakers with practical approaches to protect their health systems and populations.

items.title: Cu-Doped Intercalation-Engineered 2D ZIF-8/alk-MXene Heterostructure: A High-Performance Synergistic Adsorbent for Efficient Tetracycline Removal from Wastewater
items.abstract: Abstract The safe disposal of high-concentration antibiotic wastewater from medical, livestock and aquaculture sectors is critical to ecological security and public health. Herein, a Cu-doped ZIF-8/alk-MXene heterostructure with a well-defined intercalation structure and ultrahigh adsorption capacity for tetracycline in aquaculture wastewater was rationally fabricated via in-situ growth and post-modification. This heterostructured material (Cu-ZIF-8/alk-MXene) was fabricated via in-situ growth of two-dimensional ZIF-8 nanosheets within the intercalated structure of alkalized MXene (alk-MXene) followed by Cu doping, which synergized the electron-metal-support interactions (EMSI) induced by Cu dopants and the inherent structural merits of alk-MXene. Impressively, the Cu-ZIF-8/alk-MXene adsorbent achieves a remarkably boosted TC adsorption capacity in wastewater through the synergy of electrostatic attraction, metal coordination and π-π interaction. The Pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir isotherm fitting further verify that the adsorption process is mainly controlled by chemical adsorption and follows a monolayer adsorption pattern. The composite delivers a Langmuir maximum TC adsorption capacity of 1631.1 mg·g -1 , with stable performance across pH 4-10 and initial TC concentrations of 10-200 mg·L -1 . It also shows excellent reusability: after five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, the adsorbent retains approximately 1283 mg·g -1 of TC uptake, corresponding to ~78.7% of its initial capacity, and exhibits strong anti-interference ability against coexisting ions in complex water matrices. DFT calculations further verify that the synergistic TC adsorption arises from the combined effects of metal coordination, electrostatic attraction and π-π interaction. This work demonstrates the great application potential of the as-designed heterostructure for practical tetracycline-contaminated water remediation.

items.title: knowledge–practice gap in junk food consumption among secondary school students in Nepal
items.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a period of increasing independence in food choices. During these years, dietary behaviour may be influenced by peers, media exposure, and the availability of different types of food. Junk food consumption among adolescents in Nepal has emerged as a public health concern due to its potential long-term effects on health. Frequent consumption of such foods may increase the risk of obesity and dental caries during adolescence and may also contribute to the development of chronic conditions such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease later in life. Studies in Nepal using the knowledge–attitude–practice approach have generally examined knowledge and dietary practices as separate aspects and have often assumed that greater knowledge results in healthier food choices. However, having knowledge about the health effects of junk food does not necessarily mean that students will avoid or reduce its consumption. This study therefore examined the level of knowledge and patterns of junk food consumption among secondary-level students in Pokhara. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was carried out among 290 students enrolled in grades 9 and 10 in six public schools in Pokhara Metropolitan City. Participants were selected through a multistage sampling procedure. Data were gathered using a pretested, self-administered questionnaire. Students’ knowledge of junk food was measured using 21 items for which objectively verifiable answers were available, with an overall reliability coefficient of KR-20 = 0.634. Knowledge levels were categorised using Bloom’s cut-off criteria. Practice was assessed mainly in terms of the number of times students consumed junk food during a typical week, with consumption three or more times per week considered frequent. In addition, a four-component index was developed to provide a broader assessment of dietary practices. Relationships between the study variables were examined using independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, chi-square tests with Cramér’s V, correlation analysis, and binary logistic regression. Results The mean knowledge score was 15.41 ± 2.99 out of 21, corresponding to 73.4% of the items answered correctly. Overall, 33.4% of students had high knowledge, 51.0% had moderate knowledge, and 15.5% had low knowledge. Most students correctly recognised common characteristics of junk food. However, fewer students were able to explain why processed junk food has a long shelf life (37.9%) or identify the nutrient that is generally lacking in such foods (42.4%). Junk food consumption was almost universal, with 97.2% of students reporting consumption, and 59.3% consuming it frequently. Taste was the most commonly reported reason for consumption (61.0%). Grocery stores were the main source of junk food (83.8%), while only 6.6% of students reported obtaining it from school canteens. Mother's education was the only socio-demographic factor significantly associated with knowledge (F = 3.387, p = 0.010). Daily pocket money was the only factor associated with frequent junk food consumption (χ² = 10.150, p = 0.017), indicating a threshold effect rather than a gradual increase in consumption with increasing pocket money. However, the results demonstrated that students with higher knowledge scores reported more frequent junk food consumption. The mean knowledge score was 13.12 among students who did not consume junk food and 16.01 among those who consumed it five or more times per week (F = 3.310, p = 0.021). After adjustment for other variables, knowledge remained the only independent predictor of frequent junk food consumption. For each one-standard-deviation increase in the knowledge score, the odds of frequent consumption increased by 35.9% (adjusted OR = 1.359, 95% CI: 1.057–1.746, p = 0.017). Conclusions Students at the secondary level in Pokhara demonstrated a generally good understanding of junk food; however, greater knowledge was not accompanied by lower consumption. Rather, students with higher knowledge scores reported consuming junk food more frequently. This finding suggests that knowledge about the health effects of junk food, by itself, may not be sufficient to bring about changes in adolescents’ dietary practices. Strategies aimed at reducing frequent junk food consumption should therefore address the wider factors that shape students’ food choices. The availability and affordability of these foods, their prices and portion sizes, exposure to food marketing, and the amount of pocket money available to students may all play a role in consumption patterns. Restricting or regulating the sale and availability of junk food in and around schools could also be considered as part of a broader intervention. Nutrition education should remain an important component of such efforts, but it could place greater emphasis on helping students understand food processing and acquire practical skills for reading and interpreting food labels.

items.title: Cross-border health care seeking among Somali nationals: a multi-country rapid evidence synthesis of determinants, outcome domains, economic burden and health-system implications, 2014–2026
items.abstract: Abstract Background Somali nationals travel abroad for care that the domestic health system cannot supply, yet the scale, clinical drivers, costs and outcomes of this movement have not been synthesised. We aimed to consolidate the available evidence on outbound medical travel from Somalia to India, Türkiye, Ethiopia and Egypt, to distinguish what is measured from what is not, and to draw implications for health financing and governance. Methods We conducted a rapid evidence synthesis of evidence from 2014 to 2026. Sources were Indian parliamentary and ministerial series, peer-reviewed studies, country-of-origin reports, health-financing documents and consular guidance. Synthesis was narrative because heterogeneity precluded pooling. Every statement was assigned to one of three evidence tiers: directly measured, credibly inferred or unquantifiable. Movement indicators count episodes, not unique patients, and expenditure envelopes are planning scenarios, not accounts. Results India is the only corridor with a nationality-specific public series: 13,585 medical-purpose arrivals in 2015–2017 and 47,880 medical visas in 2019–2024 (2018 unavailable), a minimum of 61,465 episodes. Medical visas peaked at 16,411 in 2023, 4.8 times the 2019 level, and fell to 12,261 in 2024. Türkiye offers a single anchor (2,742 Somali patients in 2019); Ethiopia and Egypt lack nationality-specific series. Demand concentrates in oncology, cardiovascular and renal disease, advanced diagnostics, reproductive medicine and orthopaedics. A snowball survey of 106 medical travellers in Garowe reported a mean direct cost of US$8,543 per episode. Out-of-pocket payments met 30.8% of current health expenditure in 2023. Applying published per-patient benchmarks to Indian visas gives US$88–105 million for 2024; a four-corridor central scenario gives approximately US$219 million, about 1.8% of projected gross domestic product. No pooled morbidity, complication or mortality rate can be derived, because outbound episodes are not linked to treatment or outcome. Conclusions Outbound travel functions as an unregulated, privately financed parallel tertiary-care system that is substantial in scale, financially consequential and largely unmeasured in outcome. We propose a minimum outbound-referral dataset, pooled catastrophic-illness protection linked to authorised referral, facilitator licensing, bilateral referral compacts and sequenced domestic investment in oncology diagnostics, chemotherapy, dialysis and imaging.

items.title: Narrative Inquiry on the Innovation Journeys of Biomedical and Health Technology Startup Founders in the Philippines
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Research on biomedical and health technology startups in the Philippines has documented regulatory, financial, and market barriers, but little is known about how founders themselves experience, interpret, and manage the journey from ideation to commercialization. This study examines how biomedical and health technology startup founders narrate that journey in the Philippines, a resource-constrained, lower-middle-income country. Methodology: Guided by a constructivist-interpretivist paradigm, the study used narrative inquiry with eight purposively selected founders representing medical devices, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, and digital health. The study conducted semi-structured narrative interviews, re-storied them into individual narrative profiles, member-checked them, manually coded them, and compared them through cross-narrative synthesis, retaining negative cases. Findings: The journeys were organized around five non-linear narrative thresholds: arrival or entry; building and validation under constraint; regulatory qualification; procurement and adoption; and relational reconfiguration with the systemic environment as well as, resilience and identity reconstruction. Entry was relational and often serendipitous. A problem-led orientation and commitment to identifiable beneficiaries sustained the founders. Founders validated functioning technologies through improvisation and resource combination. Regulatory qualification varied by product and venture. Founders sought clear product categorization, proportionate requirements, and predictable timelines rather than deregulation. The sharpest divergence occurred after validation, when procurement and institutional adoption enabled movement or produced delays, redirection, withdrawal, or re-entry. Financing and adoption were mutually constraining. Resilience and narrative identity formed an adaptive architecture. Resilience was characterized as individualized, team-distributed, or organizational, while identity was reconstructed in sequential, layered accumulation or continuity deepening modes. Implications: The study qualifies effectuation, resilience, narrative identity, and diffusion of innovations for resource-constrained biomedical settings. For policy, it points to aligning development funding with public procurement, proportionate regulatory pathways, pre-revenue financing, simplified administrative processes, and entrepreneurial capability building. Originality/Value: This is among the first founder-centered narrative studies of biomedical and health technology commercialization in the Philippines. It shows that the decisive challenge is not invention itself but moving viable technologies into institutional adoption and sustained public benefit. JEL codes: L26, O31, O32, I11, I18, O53.

items.title: Job satisfaction and self-efficacy as mediators of organizational support and job competency: a cross- sectional study among Shanghai community health personnel
items.abstract: Abstract Background Job competency among public health personnel is essential for delivering quality community health services. This study examined the relationships among job competency, perceived organizational support, job satisfaction, and self-efficacy among public health personnel in Shanghai. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 3,809 public health personnel from 249 community health service centers across 16 districts in Shanghai. Multiple linear regression examined demographic differences in job competency. Spearman correlation analysis assessed relationships among the four core variables. A multiple mediation model was tested using structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Harman’s single-factor test assessed common method bias. Results Job competency was associated with gender, marital status, professional title, number of professional training sessions, regular exercise, and sleep. The final mediation model showed good fit (χ² = 5.383, df = 2, p = 0.068, CFI = 0.999, TLI = 0.998, NFI = 0.999, RMSEA = 0.021, SRMR = 0.007). The total indirect effect from perceived organizational support to job competency was 0.747 (95% CI [0.662, 0.834]). The indirect effect via job satisfaction was 0.426 (95% CI [0.350, 0.511]), and the sequential indirect effect via job satisfaction and self-efficacy was 0.320 (95% CI [0.270, 0.372]). Common method bias was not a serious concern. Conclusions Perceived organizational support was associated with job competency through job satisfaction and sequentially via self-efficacy. Community health service centers should strengthen organizational support, monitor job satisfaction, and provide self-efficacy training to improve workforce competency and public health service delivery.

items.title: Factors Associated with Zero-Dose Status Among Children Aged 12–23 Months in the Mobayi-Mbongo Health Zone, North Ubangi Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, from January to December 2024: A Cross-Sectional Study

Data were collected through structured electronic questionnaires (KoboCollect), direct observation, and vaccination card review. items.title: Sequential Sampling from Memory Underlies Perceptual Decisions Unyoked from Actions.
items.abstract: Perceptual decision-making refers to the class of decisions in which sensory evidence is used to categorize percepts and guide actions. Conventionally, categorical decisions are thought to precede motor actions. However, recent studies in nonhuman primates challenge this assumption-when perceptual decisions were uncoupled from the actions they bear upon, animals postponed the decisions until relevant response options were revealed. To determine whether this postponement stems from cognitive limitations unique to nonhuman primates, we conducted a similar experiment with human participants. Naive participants viewed a random dot motion (RDM) stimulus that was difficult to categorize. After a delay period following the RDM, two choice targets were presented and participants decided which target lay closer to the perceived motion direction. Decision accuracy varied across participants, reflecting individual differences in ability to integrate motion evidence. Notably, participants with higher decision accuracy showed prolonged deliberation after choice-target presentation. Furthermore, the time they took to report their decisions depended on the strength of the motion evidence. This pattern of accuracy and decision reporting time could be accounted for by a bounded diffusion model in which participants sequentially sample stored sensory information from memory during the target selection phase. When the RDM was challenging to categorize, the subsequent appearance of the targets provided a framework to interrogate stored evidence and render a decision. Our results reveal a strategic feature of working memory of retaining information based on its future utility. This observation opens new avenues for investigating how memory and decision-making interact.

items.title: Confounds in Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Part III: Auxiliary Data.
items.abstract: In the first part of this series, we reviewed the pathways that bring about confounding nuisance signals in fMRI. Then, in the second part, we considered how human factors can modify these pathways. In this, the third and final part, we review auxiliary data that may allow researchers to identify and perhaps correct for nuisance signals and their modifiers. We consider three broad categories of data: (1) measures that can be collected synchronously with the fMRI, (2) other MRI scans that either capture trait information or attempt to define the state that exists during an fMRI scan in the same session, and (3) non-MRI measures that can be collected before or after the scan and that also capture trait or relevant state factors influencing the fMRI. We conclude with some recommendations on ways to improve fMRI experiments going forward.

items.title: Distributed Neural Dynamics Underlie the Shift from Movement Preparation to Execution.
items.abstract: Understanding how neural population activity supports the transition from movement preparation to execution remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience. Invasive recordings in nonhuman primates indicate that motor preparation and execution occupy orthogonal subspaces within the primary motor cortex (M1), yet how these neural dynamics evolve across broader networks and support skilled, memory-guided action remains poorly understood. We used source-resolved magnetoencephalography during a memory-guided finger-sequence task to track population dynamics across a cortico-hippocampal network. Manifold trajectories and decoding revealed that preparation and execution of movement sequences occupy distinct, yet not fully orthogonal, neural subspaces-a separation that generalized across all regions but was most pronounced in motor regions. Crucially, we identified a hierarchical spatio-temporal transition across the brain: The state shift originated in the hippocampus via theta-band modulations and rippled through the pre-SMA, SMA, and lateral premotor areas before culminating in M1 via broadband activity. This progression follows the functional hierarchy of descending motor pathways, with M1 shifting last, 160 msec before the first button press. Although sequence identity could be decoded from all areas during execution, only the hippocampus and M1 maintained predictive representations of upcoming sequences during preparation. These findings demonstrate that the initiation of complex motor sequences relies on a well-timed integration of hippocampal memory systems with primary motor output, rather than being a process localized to the motor cortices alone.

items.title: Biodiversity conservation and its associations with economic performance, inequality, and peace
items.abstract: Abstract Biodiversity conservation is increasingly recognized as a product of coupled social–ecological systems shaped not only by ecological processes, but also by economic capacity, social inequality, and geopolitical stability. Here, we examined whether national conservation performance is systematically associated with economic prosperity, income inequality, peace, and the importance of natural resources in the national economy across 142 countries. Conservation performance was represented using the Nature Conservation Index (NCI), a composite metric integrating biodiversity threats, land management, governance capacity, and future environmental trends. We analyzed relationships between NCI, Gross National Income per capita, the Gini coefficient, the National Peace Index, and the total nature resources rents using a generalized additive model that accounted for nonlinear relationships and income stratification. Together, these societal variables explained deviance of 52.2% for the NCI model. Economic prosperity was positively associated with NCI, although the relationship was nonlinear across income groups, suggesting that conservation capacity does not increase uniformly with development. Counter to commonly assumed relationships between inequality and biodiversity loss, income inequality showed a positive multivariate association with NCI scores. This result suggests that high national conservation performance can coexist with unequal social conditions, potentially reflecting centralized or exclusionary conservation systems that elevate institutional conservation metrics without necessarily improving equitable biodiversity outcomes. We also found that more peaceful countries consistently exhibited higher conservation performance, supporting the view that geopolitical stability provides enabling conditions for sustained conservation governance and institutional continuity. We further suggest that national conservation indices may partly capture governance capacity, reporting infrastructure, and political commitment rather than ecological condition alone, while telecoupled trade systems may allow wealthier nations to externalize environmental pressures beyond their borders. Although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, our findings highlight the need to interpret global conservation indicators cautiously and to incorporate social equity and externalized environmental impacts more explicitly into international biodiversity assessment frameworks.

items.title: Improving Parental Investments in Children: Experimental Evidence from The Gambia
items.abstract: We study two early childhood programs in The Gambia for children between 0 and 3 years of age. The basic version of the program, called Baby Friendly Community Initiative (BFCI), provides parents with child health and nutrition information delivered through home visits and community meetings. A second version, called BFCI+, is center-based and adds cognitive stimulation to the basic version of the program through activities with children. Villages were randomly assigned to one of two versions of the program or to a control group that received neither. The BFCI+ program had moderate impacts on parental investments in children in terms of resources and time. Child language development improved for well-off parents or parents in the more well-off region. Poorer parents invested more in time spent with the children, whereas those who were more materially well-off spent more financial resources on the children. The basic version of the program, the BFCI, had no detectable impacts.

items.title: The more the merrier? systematic review and meta-analysis of working memory and category learning
items.abstract: The role of working memory capacity (WMC) in category learning (CL) remains theoretically contested. While the COVIS model posits that information-integration (II) learning is WMC-independent, empirical findings are mixed. Through a systematic review and subsequent three-level meta-analysis of 21 articles (164 effect sizes), we synthesized the WMC–CL relationship. Results revealed a significant overall positive correlation (r = 0.258; trim-and-fill adjusted r = 0.118). Notably, category structure (rule-based vs. information-integration) did not significantly moderate this relationship, challenging the COVIS prediction that implicit learning is independent of WMC. However, WMC task-specific moderation revealed significantly weaker correlations for reading span compared to operation span, memory updating, and spatial storage. No moderating effects were found for age, gender, or stimulus modality. These findings suggest that performance across diverse category structures shares a common reliance on WMC.

items.title: Serotonin signaling in the rat prefrontal cortex is required for Retrieval-Induced Forgetting
items.abstract: Forgetting is a ubiquitous phenomenon actively promoted in many species. The act of remembering some experiences can cause forgetting of others in both humans and rats. We previously found that when rats retrieve a memory to guide exploration, it reduces later retention of other competing memories encoded in that environment. As with humans, this retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) relies on prefrontal control processes, is competition-dependent, and cue-independent. RIF is thought to be driven by inhibitory control signals from the prefrontal cortex that target areas where memories are stored. Serotonin plays a crucial role in behaviors requiring high cognitive demand, including memory processes, partly through its modulation of prefrontal cortex activity. However, its potential involvement in regulating active forgetting remains unexplored. Here, in male and female rats performing a task known to induce RIF, we pharmacologically manipulated serotonin 5-HT1A, 5-HT2A, and 5-HT2C receptors and their downstream effectors in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). Our findings reveal a specific role for prefrontal serotonin signaling in RIF. Whereas 5-HT2C receptor manipulation had no effect, activating 5-HT1A or blocking 5-HT2A receptors in the mPFC abolished RIF. By contrast, activating 5-HT2A receptors promotes RIF under conditions in which it is normally reduced. Further analyses identified the PI3K/AKT pathway as a downstream effector of 5-HT2A receptor signaling, suggesting a specific molecular mechanism through which serotonin modulates inhibitory control over memory. These results uncover a previously unrecognized serotonergic modulation of adaptive forgetting, identifying specific receptor subtypes that link prefrontal serotonin signaling to inhibitory control over memory competition. Significance statement Forgetting is an essential, active process that helps the brain stay flexible and focused. In both humans and animals, remembering one thing can lead to forgetting competing memories, a phenomenon called retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF). Our research shows that serotonin, a neurotransmitter best known for its role in mood, also actively regulates which memories are forgotten. In rats, we found that serotonin signaling in the prefrontal cortex regulates adaptive forgetting: 5-HT2A receptor signaling promotes RIF, whereas activation of 5-HT1A receptors disrupts it. We further identified PI3K/AKT signaling as a key downstream effector of 5-HT2A receptor activation in this process. These findings matter because the mechanisms of active forgetting remain poorly understood, and their disruption may contribute to psychopathological conditions.

items.title: Noun-adjective collocations in L2 Portuguese: Exploring the effects of proficiency and native language in a large-scale learner corpus
items.abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the development of phraseological knowledge in Portuguese second language learners, focusing on noun–adjective combinations through the lenses of phrasal frequency, association strength, and accuracy. We analysed essays from 693 learners across five proficiency levels, representing 18 typologically diverse first languages (L1). Learners’ use of noun–adjective combinations was examined using four association measures — phrase frequency, mutual information, log dice, and delta P (ΔP) — as well as the accuracy of use. Findings reveal that phraseological development is not linear; advanced learners produced less frequent and less strongly-associated combinations, suggesting a shift toward more varied or creative expressions. L1 word order typology did not influence phrase frequency or association strength, but learners from noun–adjective dominant L1s produced collocations more accurately, indicating a dissociation between accuracy and idiomaticity. Accuracy followed a U-shaped developmental trajectory. Overall, the results highlight the complex interplay of learner and input-related variables in L2 phraseological development.

items.title: A moderation examination of the effects of a mindfulness-based intervention on primary school students’ symptoms of inattention, depression, and anxiety
items.abstract: Abstract The number of mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) has proliferated in the last decade, as accessible evidence-based practices, to improve children’s mental health in school settings. However, some studies suggest that MBIs do not offer distinct advantages over other mental health promotion interventions. These inconsistent findings may be explained, at least in part, by the lack of a clear definition of what constitutes a MBI, inconsistencies in intervention length and facilitator training, and importantly, the limited examination of moderating variables––particularly dispositional mindfulness, emotional regulation, and social competence––that may influence intervention effectiveness and mental health outcomes (inattention, anxiety, and depression). The present study was therefore interested in the potential benefits associated with a case of this type of intervention and aimed to explore whether dispositional (i.e., trait) mindfulness and mental health indicators evolved over time in primary school children. A secondary objective meant to evaluate whether receiving a MBI could moderate the relationship between changes in mindfulness and changes in mental health indicators. Contrary to our hypothesis, results showed that mindfulness levels were linked with indicators of mental health. Specifically, changes in mindfulness were associated with increases in inattention, anxiety and depression using structural equation modelling. Moreover, the association between changes in mindfulness and inattention differed by intervention group, with greater increases in mindfulness associated with greater increases in inattention in the control group but not in the intervention group. Results thus lend support to exercising caution when aiming to only foster mindfulness abilities, without ensuring that children also learn the emotion regulation skills that are required to deal with the increased awareness of their difficulties. ClinicalTrials.gov trial registration number NCT06346002; trial registration date: April 3rd, 2024.

items.title: Public carry, private fear: empirical evidence on fear and avoidance responses to visible firearms
items.abstract: Introduction The Supreme Court's 2022 New York State Rifle Pistol Association v. Bruen decision recognized a constitutional right to carry firearms in public. Its 2024 United States v. Rahimi decision applied Bruen's historical approach, considering the affrighting tradition's going armed laws prohibiting carrying weapons in a manner that terrorized the public. Little experimental research has examined fear responses to visibly carried firearms in ordinary public encounters. The current preregistered between-subjects experiment examined whether firearm visibility was associated with fear, hostile intent attribution, perceived proximity, and avoidance or reporting intentions. The study also examined hostile intent attribution and perceived proximity as potential mediators of the association between firearm visibility and fear, and rural identity as a potential moderator. Methods Participants were 415 U.S. adults recruited through Prolific in February 2026 (ages 18–81; M = 41.31, SD = 12.46). Of these, 54.0% were male and 44.3% female; 71.6% identified as White, 10.4% Black, 9.2% Asian, and 4.6% Hispanic. Participants were randomly assigned to view one of two 6-second videos showing the same individual in a public setting, either carrying a visible firearm ( n = 205) or no firearm ( n = 210). Welch's t -tests compared conditions, and a bootstrapped parallel mediation model examined indirect effects on fear. Moderated regression and moderated mediation tested rural identity as a moderator. Results Participants who viewed the armed individual reported greater fear ( d = 1.15), hostile intent attribution ( d = 1.47), perceived proximity ( d = 0.87), and avoidance or reporting intentions ( d = 1.86) than those who viewed the unarmed individual. Hostile intent attribution measured judgments about the individual's intentions, while perceived proximity measured felt closeness or intrusion. Together, these variables statistically accounted for approximately 81% of the total effect of firearm visibility on fear. Gun owners and non-owners showed similar differences between conditions, with no significant moderation by firearm ownership. Rural identity did not moderate the proposed pathways in the predicted direction. Discussion The findings provide experimental evidence that viewing a visibly armed individual in the setting studied was associated with greater fear, a response relevant to the historical affrighting tradition.

items.title: Exploring the Value of Diverse LLM Explanations in Introductory Programming
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown the potential to generate code explanations that surpass those of peers in quality, offering promising opportunities for computer science education. While these explanations may not yet match the depth and clarity of instructor-provided explanations, research in computational creativity highlights that the quantity and diversity of ideas can often outweigh a singular focus on quality. Inspired by this, we explore whether combining multiple diverse explanations, each emphasizing distinct aspects (e.g., function, concept, goal), can enhance students' understanding of programming exercises compared to generic explanations that do not emphasize distinct conceptual aspects. In our study 971 first-year computing students were randomly assigned either diverse or generic LLM-generated explanations for two programming exercises. Students completed multiple-choice and open-ended questions for each exercise, followed by Likert-scale questions and open-ended reflections. Our findings outline patterns in student performance and perceived cognitive load across the two explanation conditions. These findings highlight how variation in explanation emphasis may relate to learner engagement and understanding. Across participants, open-ended response accuracy was consistently about 7.7% higher when students received diverse explanations, with no difference in perceived cognitive load.

items.title: Less Deliberate in Teams: Student LLM Use Across Individual and Collaborative Work
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become common in computing courses, we need to understand how the social setting shapes how students use them. This paper reports findings from a semester-long study of 96 undergraduate students who completed six assignments, alternating between individual homework and team project milestones. We tracked LLM usage, prompting habits, and how students verified AI-generated output across all six assignments. LLM usage dropped by 42.7 percentage points when students moved from individual work to their first team milestone, then partly recovered in later team tasks. Students also wrote fewer prompts, used fewer deliberate prompting strategies, and checked LLM output less carefully. The share of students who ran tests on AI-generated code fell by 19.4 percentage points during team assignments and never fully rebounded. A within-student analysis found that 18.9% of students who consistently used LLMs on their own stopped using them entirely in teams, while only 3.2% went the other direction. These results suggest that collaborative context is associated with reduced deliberate LLM engagement beyond what task type alone can explain. The moment students form teams appears to be a critical turning point that may benefit from more explicit instructional support.

items.title: Exploring Mindfulness in the Context of Gambling: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Future Directions
items.abstract: Abstract Background Although researchers have investigated the relationship between mindfulness and gambling, findings across observational and intervention studies remain underdeveloped and inconsistent. Objectives This scoping review synthesised existing literature on mindfulness (state and trait) and gambling by addressing two key research questions: (1) How does mindfulness (state and trait) relate to gambling ? and (2) What areas and gaps in knowledge require further investigation and clarification ?. Method Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, five electronic databases (Academic Search Elite, PsycINFO, PsycProQuest, Scopus, and PubMed Central) were searched from inception to March 2025, with an updated search in November 2025. Independent double-screening and data extraction against a priori eligibility criteria yielded 20 synthesised peer-reviewed articles. Data were synthesised using descriptive and thematic approaches. Results High levels of trait mindfulness were related to lower gambling severity. The mindfulness facets of non-judging and acting with awareness were most consistently associated with lower gambling severity and propensity. Preliminary evidence also associated mindfulness-based interventions with lower levels of gambling severity. Conclusions Lower levels of mindfulness potentially serve as a risk factor for increased gambling propensity. However, the literature surrounding mindfulness and gambling remains underdeveloped, with limited evidence regarding underlying mechanisms or potential bi-directional relationships. Future research adopting randomised controlled trials, qualitative methodologies, multidimensional measurement, and culturally diverse samples is required to address these current gaps in understanding. Preregistration This review was not preregistered.

items.title: The social cure effects of United Voices: a randomized waitlist-controlled pilot trial of an online group-singing intervention for older adults with HIV
items.abstract: Introduction Older adults with HIV experience increasing loneliness and social isolation as they age with the stigma of HIV. Group singing is a promising social identity approach but remains largely understudied among people with stigmatizing health conditions. Based on our conceptual model, we developed United Voices (UV), a group-singing intervention for older adults with HIV to mitigate the impacts of stigma on loneliness and social isolation. Methods We conducted a randomized, waitlist-controlled pilot trial of UV to evaluate its feasibility and acceptability. A total of 23 people with HIV ages 50 years and older were randomized into immediate- (n=13) or delayed-start (n=10) group of 12 weekly 90-minute group-singing sessions via Zoom during COVID-19. Psychosocial and behavioral measures were administered at baseline, 6- and 12-weeks, and semi-structured exit interviews were conducted. Results Of four a priori feasibility thresholds, only enrollment was met (6.8 per week vs. 6). Of 27 enrolled participants, 23 (85%) were randomized (threshold 100%). Of 13 randomized to the immediate-start arm, 9 (69.2%) completed baseline (threshold 80%); of these, 7 (77.8%) attended at least 10 of 12 rehearsals and 7 (77.8%) completed both follow-up assessments (thresholds 80%). Among the 7 participants who completed the acceptability survey, the 80% benchmark was met for staff support (100%), information provided, the study website, rehearsal structure, and confidence in ability to participate (86% each), but not for overall satisfaction with the choir (71%) or the research study (57%). Exit interviews from 4 of the 13 participants randomized to the immediate-start arm indicated that while participants were at first skeptical regarding online group-singing, the experience was enjoyable, providing a social outlet during shelter-in-place. Discussion Participants appreciated getting to know and supporting each other over time. The professionally rendered concert recording was a source of pride. Interviewed participants described pride, belonging, and mutual support, consistent with the social identity processes UV is designed to engage; whether these processes reduce loneliness and social isolation remains to be tested. Findings identify the procedural changes needed before a full-scale randomized controlled trial to test the efficacy of UV among older adults with HIV.

items.title: Development and feasibility of a theory-driven multidomain intervention for community-dwelling older adults with mild cognitive impairment: a quasi-experimental pilot study based on the Multi-Theory Model
items.abstract: Abstract Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a critical stage for dementia prevention, and multidomain interventions are recommended to delay cognitive decline. However, implementing these interventions in community settings remains challenging because of difficulties in initiating health behaviours and maintaining long-term adherence. Theory-based interventions can facilitate the initiation of behaviors and sustained engagement. This study aimed to develop a multidomain intervention guided by the Multi-Theory Model (MTM) for community-dwelling older adults with MCI and to evaluate its feasibility and preliminary effectiveness. Methods This study comprised two sequential phases: intervention development and feasibility evaluation. The intervention was developed through evidence synthesis, semi-structured interviews with older adults with MCI guided by the Multi-Theory Model (MTM), and multidisciplinary expert consultation. A 12-week quasi-experimental pilot study with a historical non-equivalent control group was subsequently conducted. Participants in the control group (n = 20) received a conventional multidomain intervention, whereas those in the intervention group (n = 22) received the MTM-guided multidomain intervention. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment and adherence. The primary outcome was feasibility, assessed by recruitment and adherence. Secondary outcomes included cognitive function, physical performance, frailty, depressive symptoms, instrumental activities of daily living, and social participation. Results Forty participants completed the study (intervention, n = 21; control, n = 19). Recruitment was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (73.3% vs. 40.0%, P = 0.024), and overall adherence was also significantly better (P = 0.007). Compared with the control group, participants receiving the MTM-guided intervention demonstrated significantly greater improvements in global cognitive function, physical performance, instrumental activities of daily living, and social participation (all P < 0.05), together with greater reductions in frailty and depressive symptoms (both P < 0.001). Conclusions The MTM-guided multidomain intervention was feasible and acceptable for community-dwelling older adults with MCI, with higher recruitment and adherence than a conventional programme. These findings suggest that integrating behaviour change strategies that explicitly target behaviour initiation and maintenance may facilitate the implementation of multidomain interventions in community settings. Larger multicentre randomised controlled trials with longer follow-up are warranted to confirm the intervention's effectiveness and scalability. Trial registration This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500112119; registered on 10 November 2025. https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=289572).

items.title: A scoping review of self-silencing and mental health outcomes in women across three decades
items.abstract: Silencing the Self-theory proposes that women who inhibit self-expression to preserve close relationships are at greater risk of depression. This scoping review maps the empirical literature on self-silencing and women’s mental health published since 1996. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched Scopus, Web of Science and ProQuest (1,761 records) and an AI-assisted search engine (Consensus; 108 records). After deduplication, single-reviewer title/abstract screening and quality-control checks, 184 records (1996–2026) were charted: 154 primary studies, 11 reviews and 19 non-empirical records. Two raters appraised the quantitative studies with the MMAT (κ = 0.98). Depressive symptoms were the most frequently examined outcome (111 of 184 records; 60.3%), followed by anxiety (29; 15.8%), disordered eating (27; 14.7%), self-esteem (19; 10.3%), relationship functioning (18; 9.8%), intimate partner violence (18; 9.8%), trauma/PTSD (9; 4.9%) and suicidality (2; 1.1%). Most studies were cross-sectional, and cultural context, racial identity and partner dynamics are increasingly examined as moderators. Screening and charting were done by one reviewer from abstracts, and effect directions and sizes were not charted, so counts show where research effort has gone, not the strength or consistency of associations. The review maps three decades of research across outcomes, populations, designs and theoretical frameworks, and identifies which outcome areas now have enough primary studies to justify full systematic reviews. Many women learn to quiet their own thoughts, feelings and needs to keep the peace in close relationships. This review looks at “self-silencing” and how it connects to women’s mental health. We searched three academic databases and a supplementary citation-search tool, then screened the results against explicit criteria and cross-checked them against a keyword-network analysis, arriving at 184 records published between 1996 and 2026 that map what is already known about self-silencing and women’s mental health. Of these, 154 were primary empirical studies (original research reporting new data), 11 were reviews of the existing literature, and 19 were commentaries, conceptual papers or book chapters without new data. Most of these studies look at depression; fewer look at eating problems, self-esteem and relationships, and a growing number ask whether the picture differs by culture or racial identity. Most of this evidence comes from single-survey, cross-sectional studies, so they can show that self-silencing and poorer mental health tend to occur together, but not that one causes the other. The review is intended to help clinicians and researchers see which populations and mechanisms have been studied most, and to help researchers identify where more rigorous, longer-term, and more diverse research is still needed.

items.title: Processing speed accounts for the discriminative power of a brief smartphone Go/No-Go task among individuals with multiple sclerosis
items.abstract: Background Identifying and longitudinally measuring cognitive decline remains challenging because traditional assessments rely largely on episodic, in-person administration of analog scales by trained examiners. Smartphone technology offers a scalable alternative for extracting distinct digital biomarkers from continuous sensor and event streams. Following the integration of several cognitive modules into the self-administered Neurological Functions Test Suite (NeuFun-TS), this study evaluates the clinical utility and incremental validity of a final candidate module: a brief (30 s per hand) equiprobable (50/50) Go/No-Go (50/50GNG) choice-reaction task. Methods We analyzed 3,270 quality-controlled 30-s runs from 303 participants, with primary analyses focused on the first run per hand (488 observations; 18,650 stimuli) across 34 healthy donors (HDs) and 213 multiple sclerosis (MS) participants. From the raw event stream, we screened 16 candidate metrics and retained 10 based on their psychometric properties. Using these 10 metrics, we evaluated diagnostic group separation, test–retest reliability, correlations with clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) benchmarks, and incremental validity over existing digital modules: the randomized Symbol Digit Modalities Test (rSDMT) and the Motor Sequencing Test (MST), using paired observations. Results Although nine of the 10 outcomes significantly separated HD from MS and seven separated relapsing–remitting from progressive MS subtypes (all adjusted p < 0.05), discriminative power was driven almost entirely by response latency rather than by commission errors or inhibitory metrics. Response latency accounted for the majority of its full-run separation within the first 12 s. Multi-predictor composite scores offered no diagnostic advantage over reaction time alone. Furthermore, the Go/No-Go task showed poor-to-moderate longitudinal test–retest reliability and did not provide incremental clinical value over existing modules. Conclusion In this brief implementation, the smartphone Go/No-Go task served as a choice-reaction-time measure reflecting processing-speed impairment in MS; however, its discriminative capability was redundant with reaction-time metrics already implemented on the platform, so the module was excluded from NeuFun-TS. These findings do not generalize to longer continuous performance tests, whose error-based measures require many more stimuli than a 30-s run provides.
