items.title: Impacts of ultra-processed food warning labels on product perceptions and behavioral intentions among Latino adults: A randomized trial.
items.abstract: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs), defined as foods in group 4 of the NOVA classification system, are a key contributor to chronic disease in the United States. Front-of-package warning labels ("warnings") offer a promising strategy to help Americans identify UPFs, increase awareness of their negative health effects, and reduce consumption. However, the effects of UPF warnings, including among Latino adults, remain largely unknown. Online randomized trial conducted in 2024. 4,107 Latino adults (49% limited English proficiency) in the US. Participants viewed one of three labels: a control label displaying a barcode; an intervention identity warning label stating "WARNING: Ultra-processed food"; or an intervention health warning label stating "WARNING: Consuming ultra-processed food and drinks can cause weight gain, which increases the risk of obesity and type 2 diabetes". Participants viewed four UPF products each displaying their randomly assigned label. Participants indicated whether the product was UPF (primary outcome) and rated perceived healthfulness of the product, intentions to purchase the product, and perceived message effectiveness (secondary outcomes). Identity warnings (70% correct) and health warnings (67% correct) led to higher correct identification of UPF than control labels (54%, p<.001), with the identity warning having a larger impact than the health warning (p=.007). Compared to the control label, the identity warning and health warning both elicited lower healthfulness perceptions and purchase intentions (p<.001 for all outcomes) and higher perceived message effectiveness with no significant differences between UPF labels. The impact of the health warning label (vs. the control label) on correct identification of UPF was greater for participants with high education (p=0.012) compared to those with low education, and for participants with limited English proficiency compared to high proficiency (p=0.001). UPF warnings may help consumers identify UPFs and influence product perceptions and intentions. NCT06296355.

items.title: How prenatal residential greenness links to congenital heart defects: The role of multi-pollutant mediating pathways and non-linear exposure-response.
items.abstract: Background Rapid urbanization has intensified cardiovascular burdens, particularly congenital heart defects (CHDs), a leading cause of neonatal mortality globally. The first trimester is the critical exposure window, which results in the cardiac septation and outflow tract formation. The vegetation may affect air pollutants through processes such as purification, dust retention, and temperature regulation. These pollutants have been linked to disrupted embryonic cardiogenesis. Methods We conducted a case-control study using Xiamen birth records for January 2016 to June 2019, comprising 1785 infants with CHDs and 1848 without. After applying 1:1 propensity score matching, 890 pairs (1780 neonates) were retained. Exposure was quantified as NDVI in 250, 500 and 1000 m buffers and as 23 landscape indices. Multi-pollutant mediation models were fitted for NO 2 , PM 2.5 , SO 2 and O 3 . Results Maternal first-trimester exposure was associated with lower CHD odds. At 1 km, large core patches and high connectivity were associated with lower odds, whereas fragmentation and high edge density were associated with higher odds. Indirect associations appeared through NO 2 and PM 2.5 , largest for NO 2 . The SO 2 pathway was shared with these two and did not persist when all four pollutants were modelled together. The NDVI-NO 2 relation was non-linear, with a population-specific turning point at an NDVI of about 0.46. The inverse association was stronger off-island, during high-temperature periods, and among mothers with shorter gestational periods. The O 3 indirect estimate was positive at 1 km. Conclusions Planning should shift from quantity-based expansion to morphology-oriented strategies prioritising connectivity and vulnerable groups.

items.title: Trade-offs between greenhouse gas mitigation and nutrient enrichment during tropical composting.
items.abstract: Composting provides an opportunity to recycle organic residues into valuable soil amendments; however, amendment selection can create trade-offs between nutrient enrichment and greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation. Our study evaluated the effects of different organic amendment combinations on GHG emissions and nutrient dynamics during tropical composting. Six cattle manure-based treatments were assessed: cattle manure alone (CM), cattle manure with Tithonia diversifolia (CMT), Tithonia with biochar (CMTB), Tithonia with citric acid (CMTCA), Tithonia with maize stover (CMTM), and Tithonia, maize stover, and citric acid (CMTMCA). We monitored composting for 84 days, measuring CO 2 , CH 4 , and N 2 O emissions alongside changes in temperature, moisture, pH, and carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus fractions. Greenhouse gas emissions concentrated during the thermophilic phase, the period of greatest emission intensity due to enhanced substrate availability, rapid carbon mineralization, and active microbial transformation. During this phase, cumulative CH 4 emissions ranged from 299 to 1284 g CH 4 -C m -2 , with CMTCA producing 180% higher emissions than CM, while cumulative CO 2 emissions ranged from 10.8 to 14.1 kg CO 2 -C m -2 , with CMTMCA and CMTCA producing 23% and 13% higher emissions than CM, respectively. CMTCA produced the greatest cumulative CH 4 emissions, exceeding CM by 165%. This response reflects the combined influence of Tithonia diversifolia and citric acid addition, where enhanced carbon solubilization increased substrate availability and microbial oxygen demand, potentially promoting transient anaerobic microsites favorable for methane production. Across the composting period, CMTM generated the highest cumulative CO 2 emissions, 18.5% higher than CM, reflecting enhanced carbon turnover from readily degradable substrates in Tithonia diversifolia and maize stover. Biochar amendment (CMTB) increased cumulative N 2 O emissions by 41% compared with CM, suggesting that biochar effects were dependent on interactions with nitrogen-rich Tithonia and compost nitrogen transformation pathways. Conversely, Tithonia-based amendments improved nitrogen enrichment but increased emission risks. Overall, the findings demonstrate that climate-smart composting requires balancing nutrient recovery and GHG mitigation rather than optimising either outcome in isolation. For smallholder farmers in tropical regions, the findings demonstrate that locally available organic amendments can improve compost nutrient characteristics. However, amendment selection should consider potential trade-offs between nutrient enrichment and greenhouse gas emissions.

items.title: Diagnosing urban ecosystem service flow dynamics under supply-demand mismatch: A coupled social-ecological network and gravity modeling approach with evidence from Wuhan.
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization intensifies spatial mismatches between ecosystem service supply and demand (ESSD), yet existing studies rarely quantify supply-demand relationships, extract spatial pathways, and estimate flow volumes for multiple services within a single analytical architecture. To address this gap, we coupled social-ecological networks with the gravity model to construct an integrated analytical framework that simultaneously characterizes ESSD patterns, service-specific transmission pathways, and distance-decay flow allocation. Using Wuhan (2005-2025) as a case study, we examined five ecosystem services: crop production (CP), water yield (WY), carbon storage (CS), biodiversity support (BS), and recreation (RE). Three findings emerge. First, all five ESSD patterns exhibit a persistent "central deficits versus peripheral surpluses" spatial configuration, with deficit zones expanding outward over time except for CS. Second, network metrics varied by service type without consistent structural reorganization. CP had the highest connectivity, whereas WY had the lowest (mean 1.44%). Among infrastructure-dependent services, weighted degree was higher for CP and RE than for WY, while CS and BS showed uniformly low values because their edge weights were set to 1. CS and BS had the highest clustering coefficients (0.265 and 0.263), while WY had the lowest (0.056) and the shortest average path length (2.13). Average path length did not decline consistently: it decreased slightly for CP and BS, increased for RE, and remained nearly stable for CS. Core nodes contributed disproportionately to network connectivity relative to peripheral nodes. As supply-demand deficit zones expanded outward from the urban core, virtual flow pathways increased accordingly, whereas actual pathways for CP, WY, BS, and RE shifted from inner suburb-core to outer suburb-inner suburb configurations; those for CS remained stable. Third, flow volumes declined for CP (-68.9%) and CS (-21.3%) but increased for RE (+11.6%), with WY showing the largest interannual fluctuations. These trends were associated with intensifying ESSD mismatches and heterogeneous transmission media. The framework is subject to uncertainties from closed-boundary constraints, neighborhood-priority matching, and isotropic distance decay, which may bias cross-boundary and omnidirectional flows. By enabling unified characterization of ESSD relationships, spatial pathways, and flow processes, the proposed framework provides a replicable toolkit for urban-scale ESF quantification and spatial network analysis. Our findings highlight a sustainability dilemma in rapidly urbanizing regions, characterized by ecological supply contraction, escalating anthropogenic demand, and persistent spatial mismatches, and provide a scientific foundation for ecological space optimization and trans-regional compensation design.

items.title: Enhanced chlorobenzene degradation by sodium alginate-stabilized nanoscale zero-valent iron coupled with aerobic microbial consortium: Synergistic mechanisms and transformation pathways.
items.abstract: Chlorobenzene (CB), a highly toxic, recalcitrant halogenated aromatic contaminant, poses hazards to aquatic ecosystems and human health. Aerobic bioremediation is limited by CB biotoxicity. Although nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI) exhibits outstanding dechlorination capacity, it suffers from magnetic aggregation and triggers irreversible oxidative injury to pollutant-degrading consortia. In this work, sodium alginate-stabilized nZVI (SA-nZVI) was synthesized and coupled with an acclimated aerobic CB-degrading consortium to build a synergistic groundwater remediation system. Characterization techniques including SEM, XRD, FTIR, XPS and zeta potential measurements verified that the alginate coating inhibited particle agglomeration and retarded the oxidation of metallic Fe⁰ without altering its intrinsic crystalline phase. Under optimized conditions, the composite system achieved 89% CB removal, far exceeding the 35% achieved by the microbe-only group. Mechanistic studies revealed three synergistic pathways. First, sustained and controlled Fe²⁺ release prevented ROS surges and pH/ORP oscillations and maintained antioxidant enzyme and DHA activities. Second, biodegradable SA supplied labile carbon substrates and promoted soluble microbial byproduct (SMP) generation. Third, Fe⁰-mediated reductive dechlorination and microbial aerobic hydroxylation likely occur in parallel, with intermediates possibly entering the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle for transformation. This work supports the field application of SA-nZVI bioaugmentation for remediating groundwater polluted by halogenated aromatic hydrocarbons.

items.title: From deterministic selection to stochastic drift: Salinity-associated patterns of bacterial community assembly and predicted functional potential in the Pearl River estuarine sediments.
items.abstract: Salinity gradients in estuaries strongly shape microbial communities and biogeochemical processes, but the links between salinity-driven shifts in bacterial diversity, community assembly, ecological networks, and functional potential remain to be incompletely understood. Here, we investigated bacterial community dynamics across a natural salinity gradient in surface sediments of the Pearl River Estuary, using 16S rRNA gene sequencing combined with neutral community modeling (NCM), β-nearest taxon index (βNTI), infer Community Assembly Mechanisms by Phylogenetic-bin-based null model (iCAMP), co-occurrence network analysis, and functional prediction. Bacterial richness followed a unimodal pattern, peaking at intermediate salinity. Salinity was the primary driver of community variation, explaining 35.9% of the variation, followed by NH 4 + at 13.4%. Community assembly shifted from stronger deterministic selection under low and intermediate salinity to increased stochasticity under high salinity, supported by higher neutral model fits and enhanced ecological drift detected by iCAMP. High-salinity communities formed simpler networks, mainly characterized by weakened taxon associations rather than reduced taxonomic participation. Predicted functional profiles showed greater representation of heterotrophic carbon processing and denitrification at low salinity and sulfur-related respiration at high salinity. Overall, our findings indicate that salinity gradients regulate estuarine sediment bacterial communities through coordinated effects on species turnover, community assembly, network structure, and functional differentiation, offering a baseline perspective that may help inform potential microbial community responses under future hydrological variability and seawater intrusion.

items.title: Comparison of components and processes among river catchment systems using interaction matrices prepared for different climate conditions using Fukushima case as a benchmark.
items.abstract: Conducting radiological impact assessments for environmental systems such as river catchments requires the identification of radionuclide mobility and transfer processes across multiple interlinked components. These linkages can be effectively described using Interaction Matrices (IMs), which define key environmental components (e.g., air, soil, water, and biota) and the associated radionuclide transfer processes within the connected system. IMs provide a structured framework for organizing the data and parameters required for the modelling of radionuclide transfer in the environment and the assessment of radiation doses to human and non-human biota. Despite these advantages, IMs have not yet been widely applied in radiological impact assessments, particularly for river catchments, where they are especially needed due to the diversity and large number of components and processes involved. Radionuclide transfer processes following the accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant have been extensively studied for more than a decade. In this study, the Fukushima river catchment system including its transfer pathways and processes is presented as a case study for the development and application of IMs. Building on the 'Fukushima' IMs, scientists from countries with a range of climatic and landscape conditions have developed fit-for-purpose IMs to support dose assessments for nuclear facilities and sites worldwide. By comparing these IMs with those developed for the Fukushima river catchment, key components and processes have been identified that need to be considered under different climatic conditions. This work has helped clarify common elements for the modelling and assessment of doses in river catchments which, in turn, supports the development of international best practice. Overall, this study demonstrated the key features and the benefits of applying IMs in radiological impact assessments across diverse global environmental systems.

items.title: From consent forms to social media: a proposed framework for digital nocebo responses in chronic pain management with emphasis on headache.
items.abstract: Negative treatment expectations can contribute to pain and adverse-event reporting, but online symptom narratives alone do not establish a nocebo effect. This narrative, hypothesis-generating synthesis examines communication in chronic pain management, with emphasis on headache. It examines mechanisms, trial evidence, and digital exposure pathways. Prioritized literature from 2015 to May 2026 was identified by targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and the Cochrane Library. Experimental and neurobiological studies show that verbal suggestion, conditioning, anxiety, social observation, and heightened symptom vigilance can amplify pain and adverse-event reporting through expectancy-mediated mechanisms. Placebo-controlled headache trials demonstrate substantial adverse-event reporting and discontinuation among placebo-treated participants, supporting the clinical relevance of nocebo responses. Digital content may provide decontextualized side-effect lists, emotionally salient peer experiences, difficult-to-read information, and algorithmically amplified treatment-failure narratives. However, descriptive social-media listening, video audits, and topic-modeling studies document exposure ecology. Therefore, the available evidence supports a plausible, testable pathway from digital risk exposure to negative expectations, symptom misattribution, non-adherence, treatment avoidance, and worse pain outcomes.

items.title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms.
items.abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

items.title: The ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis-silking synchrony in maize.
items.abstract: The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of SPL29 for reproductive transition, BA1 for female inflorescence initiation, and EXPA5 for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of ZmMYC2a/b or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.

items.title: Genetic diversity of bacterial endophytes associated with Crotalaria (Rattlepods).
items.abstract: Crotalaria is a diverse legume genus valued for its ecological and agronomic roles. However, its associated endophytic microbiome remains minimally characterized. This study examined the genetic diversity and community structure of bacterial endophytes inhabiting domesticated and wild Crotalaria species. Twenty-nine healthy Crotalaria plant samples were analyzed using the culture-independent 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing approach. Genomic DNA was extracted using the Phenol-Chloroform method from both domesticated and wild samples. Sequencing of 16S ribosomal RNA gene was performed using Illumina MiSeq to profile endophytic bacterial communities. The sequence data was imported into R and processed using Divisive Amplicon Denoising Algorithm 2 (DADA2) pipeline. In total, 1,546,153 high-quality sequence reads were obtained and grouped into 611 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) at 97% sequence similarity threshold. Domesticated samples exhibited higher observed species richness (median of 39 ASVs) than wild samples (median of 36 ASVs), while wild samples showed greater microbial community evenness (median ~1.08) compared to domesticated samples (median ~0.93). Beta diversity analyses showed clear separation between domesticated and wild endophytic bacterial communities, with domestication status explaining most of the observed variations (PERMANOVA: Bray-Curtis R2 = 0.826; Jaccard R2 = 0.846), but PERMANOVA detected no statistically significant difference (Bray-Curtis and Jaccard; p = 0.067). Overall, five bacteria phyla were detected in the Crotalaria samples. Pseudomonadota was the dominant phylum (64.27%) followed by Cyanobacteriota (35.5%). Enterobacteriaceae was the most abundant family (81.06%) with Enterobacter emerging as the most abundant genus in both domesticated (38.3%) and wild (89.4%) accessions. Notably, Pseudomonas was relatively enriched in domesticated plants while several bacterial genera were restricted to either wild or cultivated hosts, indicating habitat-associated endophytic specialization. This study provides the first comprehensive assessment of endophytic bacterial diversity in Kenyan Crotalaria species and highlights wild germplasm as an important reservoir of microbial diversity with potential biotechnological value.

items.title: AquaMamba: Selective state space modeling for underwater scene segmentation in marine robotics.
items.abstract: Underwater scene segmentation is challenging because image degradation and domain shift vary greatly in marine environments, and the behavior of selective state-space models (SSMs) in this environment remains insufficiently characterized. We propose AquaMamba, a ResNet34-UNet segmentation framework that replaces the bottleneck operator with stacked Mamba layers, and compare it with five established CNN-based methods and a constructed Transformer-bottleneck baseline in the SUIM benchmark. AquaMamba achieves an mIoU of 0.669, 1.9 percentage points higher than the controlled Trans-UNet baseline (0.650), while using fewer parameters (29.5M vs. 33.9M). DeepLabV3 + remains the strongest overall model, reaching 0.712 mIoU. On the unlabeled UIEB dataset, AquaMamba shows the highest confidence retention among four representative models, retaining 93.5% of its source-domain prediction confidence. Due to the lack of semantic annotation in UIEB, this result reflects prediction confidence rather than target-domain segmentation accuracy. Scale- and boundary-specific diagnostics within the selected representative subset further show complementary behavior among AquaMamba, Trans-UNet and DeepLabV3 + : AquaMamba is competitive in several large object categories and obtains the lowest boundary error point estimate, while DeepLabV3 + remains stronger for human divers and plant/seagrass, and AquaMamba is limited on the reported small-RO subset. These findings position AquaMamba as a controlled SSM baseline for underwater semantic segmentation and emphasize the need for future SSM designs to better integrate multi-scale and high-resolution features.

items.title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub-grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs.
items.abstract: Ecosystems are complex adaptive systems in which local interactions among individuals shape macroscopic phenomena such as pattern formation, multistability, and critical transitions. However, how such bottom-up interactions govern emergent behaviors and system-level complexity remains a central challenge in ecology. Phase transition theory, a classic paradigm in physics, links local interaction rules to emergent changes in macroscopic system states, offering a formal language for understanding cross-scale dynamics. Here we unite this theory with empirical evidence from dryland shrub-grass ecosystems and show that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions. First, abrupt shifts separate different phases of deserts, shrublands, and grasslands. Second, shrublands and grasslands self-organize into Turing-like phase patterns, contrasting with homogeneous deserts. Third, special phenomena emerge near-transition threshold, including patch enlargement and abrupt decline at desert-vegetation interface, and fairy circles within the shrub-grass transition zone. Using a cellular automaton model built on a fundamental trade-off between extensive and intensive resource foraging strategies (EI trade-off), we show how kernels encoding local trade-offs integrate these seemingly disparate phenomena within a unified phase transition framework. Moreover, this EI trade-off was empirically validated through analyses of plant functional traits and spatial patterns of plant patches. These findings illustrate that dryland ecosystem dynamics reflect universal self-organization principles. Our work establishes phase-transition theory as a powerful framework for understanding, predicting, and managing complexity in dryland ecosystems, which advances the integration of complexity science with ecology, offering a pathway toward bottom-up ecosystem understanding.

items.title: Characterising the longer-term impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks prior to 2020 on wild bird populations.
items.abstract: Since 2020, there has been a global escalation of the impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) on wild bird species. However, the population-level consequences of this disease remain poorly understood, despite repeated outbreaks affecting wild birds over the past two decades. To address this, we collated population counts and mortality data from 40 historical cases where HPAI mass-mortality occurred in wild bird populations prior to 2020. We characterised local impacts of these outbreaks based on i) initial change in population count from the last count pre-outbreak to the first count post-outbreak, ii) longer-term change in average population counts, iii) change in population trend, and iv) time taken to recover to the pre-outbreak baseline. Following outbreaks, initial population count declines were observed in most cases, with a median decrease of 17% (Inter-quartile range -35% to 5%). Yet in the longer-term, significant reductions in average population counts were detected in only eight of the 40 cases, and a significant decrease in population trend in only two cases. Overall, in the majority of local populations, outbreaks resulted in either limited impacts on population counts or short-term reductions followed by recovery. However, in 25% of cases (10/40) initial declines were not recovered within the monitoring period (4-17 years after the initial outbreak). Initial declines were more apparent in gulls and terns; however, impacts were seen in local populations across a range of taxa. Given that the scale of impacts of HPAI has changed dramatically since 2020, our findings support the need for disease surveillance to be combined with effective population monitoring in order to identify species impacted from the ongoing outbreaks. Further research is also needed to identify strategies for minimising impacts of HPAI, and to understand factors limiting recovery in affected populations.

items.title: Alternaria leaf spot-induced phyllosphere microbiota and metabolite interact to combat leaf spot disease.
items.abstract: Pathogen-mediated induced resistance (IR) and beneficial microbe-mediated IR are key for plant survival during pathogen attack, yet how these two forms of IR interact remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that foliar pathogen-triggered induced resistance (IR) orchestrates the assembly of a specific phyllosphere microbiota that can activate IR. Pathogen-triggered IR caused plant flavonol accumulation, which in turn enriched Aureimonas spp., especially the native A. phyllosphaerae Leaf1, in the phyllosphere endophytic microbiota near infection sites. Genetically impairing the capacity of Leaf1 to utilize flavonols reduced its proliferation during pathogen infection. Moreover, Leaf1 protected plants against leaf disease by activating IR and extended the protective range of pathogen-mediated IR. Importantly, pathogen-mediated IR-induced mobilization of native microbiota represented a common yet underrated component of plant resistance to foliar disease. These findings reveal a plant defense "relay" mechanism, whereby pathogen-mediated IR reassembles a specific microbiota that in turn activates IR to jointly combat further pathogen infection.

items.title: Systematic analysis of hydrophobin genes and heterologous characterization of a key hydrophobin Hyd15 in the culinary-medicinal mushroom Pleurotus tuber-regium.
items.abstract: Hydrophobins are small, surface-active proteins that play essential roles in fungal development and have attracted industrial interest due to their self-assembly. Pleurotus tuber-regium (Fr.) Singer is a rare, thermotolerant, edible and medicinal macrofungus capable of forming sclerotia. Both its fruiting bodies and sclerotia are edible. However, the hydrophobins of this species remain largely uncharacterized. In this study, 32 hydrophobin genes were identified and the DNA an​d coding sequence (CDS) of 31 hydrophobin genes were successfully cloned from P. tuber-regium. Their gene structures, conserved domains, subcellular localization, signal peptides, amino acid properties, and phylogenetic relationships were predicted. The transcriptional profile of 31 hydrophobin genes in the entire growth cycle of P. tuber-regium was analyzed based on transcriptomics. In addition, the physiological roles of these hydrophobins were inferred. A key hydrophobin gene evm.model.contig_18_pilon.15 (hyd15), which is potentially involved in growth and development of P. tuber-regium, was selected for heterologous expression in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3). The recombinant Hyd15 protein could deposit on the silicon wafer surface and alter the hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity of an interface, as confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and water contact angle measurements. Furthermore, recombinant Hyd15 exhibited emulsifying property superior to that of sodium caseinate. This study expands our understanding of the physiological functions of hydrophobins from mushrooms and provides a basis for their applications as natural surface-modifying and emulsifying agents.

items.title: New occurrence and distributional records of hard ticks (Acari: Ixodidae) from Bolivia.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to report new occurrence records of hard tick (Acari: Ixodidae) from the Bolivian-Peruvian Yungas ecoregion in Bolivia. Free-living ticks were collected at two sites of Suapi (La Paz department) and in Villa Independencia (Cochabamba department). Host-associated specimens were obtained from the avian collection of the Colección Boliviana de Fauna and from a puma (Puma concolor) captured in La Paz. A total of 34 ticks (three larvae, 27 nymphs, one male and three females) were collected. Of these, 32 were collected from vegetation: Amblyomma naponense (one male and one female) from Suapi 1, Ixodes pararicinus from Villa Independencia (one female) and Suapi (two larvae), and Amblyomma sp. cf. A. brasiliense (26 nymphs and one larva) from two sites of Suapi. Two nymphs of Amblyomma sp. cf. A. brasiliense were subjected to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays targeting the 16S rRNA and COI genes, whereas one larva was analyzed for 16S rRNA. Phylogenetic analyses recovered the Bolivian specimens as a distinct taxon closely related to A. brasiliense, suggested the possibility of an undescribed taxon. In addition, a nymph collected from Troglodytes musculus in Irupana was identified as Ixodes silvanus. Finally, one female of I. pararicinus was recorded parasitizing Puma concolor, representing the first reported association between this tick species and the host. These findings increase the known hard tick species richness in Bolivia through the first confirmed records of I. pararicinus and I. silvanus, Amblyomma sp. cf. A. brasiliense as potencial new taxon, and provide an additional locality record for A. naponense, providing information for future studies on tick ecology and potential risks of tick-borne pathogens.

items.title: The LAMp-LC Study: Unveiling the lung microbiome in Australians with early- and late-stage lung cancer using shotgun metagenomics
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer‑related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. Here, we characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n =106, healthy n =10) using shotgun metagenomics and semi‑quantitative culture to evaluate site-specific microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across early‑ and late‑stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culture‑based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking pack‑years, sex, and tumour characteristics. Cumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive core commensal depletion ( Neisseria subflava , Gemella sanguinis , Rothia mucilaginosa ), alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. β diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst Shannon diversity (α diversity) was significantly reduced in early-stage compared with late-stage BWs. The early‑stage TME also demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched ( Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted ( Streptococcus parasanguinis , Streptococcus cristatus , R. mucilaginosa ) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only lung adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral β‑diversity restructuring. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiome‑based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Integrating the concept of acoustic diversity into the functional ecology framework
items.abstract: The ecological relevance of sounds in ecosystems has gained increasing attention in the recent decade. While ecoacoustics seeks to study these roles, a majority of studies to date have focused on using Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) for species monitoring or calculating integrative ecoacoustic indices as rapid proxies for biological diversity. This paper proposes an ecological perspective on acoustic diversity that distinguishes three core interconnected dimensions: (i) compositional acoustic diversity, reflecting the acoustic assemblage present; (ii) structural acoustic diversity, describing the spatial and temporal organisation of acoustic activity; and (iii) functional acoustic diversity, relating to variation in acoustic traits involved in information exchange. We aim to provide a clearer conceptualisation of what different approaches to acoustic diversity represent ecologically and how they can be related to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning. We present a conceptual framework for acoustic diversity, building on existing research and linking it to Noss's (1990) hierarchical classification of biodiversity. We define and distinguish compositional, structural, and functional acoustic diversity across spatial scales ranging from the individual to the soundscape, and consider variation in alpha, beta, and gamma diversity within these dimensions. We propose methods for quantifying these different aspects of acoustic diversity and provide application examples and exemplary hypotheses to illustrate how the framework could be operationalised.

items.title: The social ecology of trustworthiness inferences: Cultural gradients in emotion overgeneralization
items.abstract: Judgments of trustworthiness from faces guide critical social decisions. It remains debated whether these judgments reflect shared features of human perception or are shaped by cultural experience. One prominent explanation is emotion overgeneralization: faces that structurally resemble emotional expressions elicit corresponding impressions, even when no emotion is displayed. Although often treated as universal, emotion overgeneralization may reflect ecological learning shaped by culture-specific norms. We propose a cultural gradient: where emotional expressions are more informative, the link between happiness resemblance and perceived trustworthiness should be stronger. Participants from 32 countries (N ≈ 6,400) will evaluate the trustworthiness of unfamiliar individuals from standardized resting facial photographs and complete a measure of emotional expressivity, with each face’s resemblance to happiness quantified computationally. We will test whether emotional expressivity is associated with greater emotion overgeneralization at both country and individual levels. Null results would favor perceptual invariance, whereas positive associations would support ecological calibration.

items.title: TerraLingua: Open-ended Emergence of Societies in an LLM Ecology
items.abstract: Abstract Artifacts that persist across generations---such as monuments, technologies, and texts---catalyze major developments in human societies. Can artifacts have a similar impact in AI-based societies? This paper introduces (1) TerraLingua, a many-agent world where agents have limited lifespans and resources, but can build artifacts that outlive their creators; and (2) an AI Anthropologist that characterizes the rich societal dynamics that emerge. With these tools, it is possible to answer a well-known conjecture in open-ended AI: artifacts are critical to sustained complex development. Blocking artifacts produces shallow cultural lineages and more frequent aggression, whereas instructions to maximize artifacts may lead to population collapse. The findings establish a path towards understanding AI societies whose impact scales far beyond individual agents. Such an understanding in turn is critical to the design and governance of real-world agents, and ultimately, to the effective and safe integration of AI into human societies.

items.title: Automated 3D Reconstruction of Mycorrhizal Fungal Structures from Bright-Field Microscopy Using Oriented Bounding Boxes and Focus Modeling
items.abstract: Abstract Background Fungal networks play a fundamental role in soil ecology and plant symbiosis, yet their three-dimensional characterization remains challenging due to their complex filamentous morphology and the limitations of conventional microscopy image analysis. This work presents a data-driven framework for three-dimensional reconstruction of fungal structures from bright-field microscopy, combining YOLO-based oriented bounding box (OBB) detection with continuous focus modeling for depth estimation. Addressing a problem explored by relatively few existing microscopy-based reconstruction approaches, the framework was developed using images of the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus Rhizophagus irregularis , with additional qualitative applications to other biological structures exhibiting similar filamentous morphologies. Results The OBB detector achieved an mAP50 of 0.60 ± 0.03, with instance-level and spatial-coverage F1-scores of 0.67 ± 0.02 and 0.78 ± 0.02, respectively. To account for the continuous nature of filamentous structures, a composite score combining both evaluation criteria was proposed, yielding S = 0.72 ± 0.01. Focus was modeled using complementary directional, spectral, and intensity descriptors integrated through PCA, achieving an F1-score of 0.90 on the ×10 validation dataset. The complete framework was applied to a 25-hour time-lapse experiment, enabling repeated three-dimensional reconstruction of the evolving fungal structure. Quantitative spatial evaluation yielded a global pixel-wise recall of 0.93. Furthermore, 75.75% of the focused OBBs overlapped the manual segmentation by at least 20% of their area within an axial tolerance of ± 35 µm, as measured by the axial-tolerant overlap rate (ATOR), substantially exceeding spatially randomized controls. Conclusions These results support the feasibility of combining orientation-aware detection and focus modeling for automated three-dimensional characterization of fungal structures, providing a foundation for future investigations of fungal network architecture and growth dynamics.

items.title: Species-specific ontogenetic isotopic niche dynamics in Amazon River turtles
items.abstract: Abstract The partitioning of the available resources is a key to species’ coexistence. Ontogenetic changes in resource use can alter ecological roles within species, yet such trajectories remain poorly resolved for Amazonian freshwater turtles. We used stable carbon and nitrogen isotope ratios (δ 13 C and δ 15 N) to evaluate ontogenetic and spatial variation in the isotopic niches of Podocnemis expansa and P. sextuberculata in floodplain lakes of the Middle Juruá River, Brazilian Amazon. P. expansa showed substantial isotopic niche overlap among ontogenetic classes (57.1–70.8%) and little evidence of size-related change in δ 13 C or δ 15 N. In contrast, P. sextuberculata showed lower overlap between sampled age classes (49.1%) and a size-related shift in δ 13 C, indicating stronger ontogenetic differentiation in assimilated resource pathways. P. sextuberculata also exhibited higher δ 15 N values than P. expansa . These results indicate that trophic ecology in Podocnemis emerges from the interaction among species identity, ontogenetic stage, and the spatial and temporal structure of floodplain resource landscapes. Moreover, the conservation of Amazonian turtles is centred on ontogenetic resource landscapes with its unique habitats, hydrological and ecological processes and resource pathways that support individuals as they grow.

items.title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation-compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry-specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod-shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L -1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L -1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state-of-the-art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

items.title: The bird-like complexity of hadrosauroid beaks.
items.abstract: Duck-billed dinosaurs evolved complex cornified oral structures whose soft-tissue biology remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the rostral anatomy of the hadrosauroid Tethyshadros insularis using gross morphology and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) data, focusing on the premaxillae and predentary. Structures previously interpreted as anomalous 'spiked' beak ornamentation are reinterpreted as osteological correlates of an extensive neurovascular network. Circumflex vessels, palatine and narial circulation and a median premaxillary sinus supplied a hypertrophied keratinous rhamphotheca that probably exceeded the extent of the underlying bone in both size and morphological complexity. Comparative evidence indicates that marginal denticulations reflect vascular excavation and/or ossified dermal papillary structures, implying vascular and somato-sensory functions analogous to avian beaks. Mesowear marks and functional correlates support a major role in cropping abrasive, grit-laden vegetation, while the dense vascularization suggests an additional thermoregulatory function via beak-nares heat exchange. These findings re-evaluate the hadrosauroid beak as a multifunctional sensory, mechanical and thermal organ, representing a key innovation that may have underpinned the ecological expansion and gigantism of later diverging hadrosaurids.

items.title: Prophylaxis in ant societies: a social response to pathogen vulnerability?
items.abstract: Social insects rely on multiple defence mechanisms to limit pathogen transmission within colonies. Prophylactic sanitary behaviours are performed in the absence of immediate pathogenic threats and contribute to routine disease prevention. Among these behaviours, grooming and necrophoresis help manage potentially harmful biological material, but how their expression relates to variation in pathogen susceptibility among colonies remains poorly understood. We investigated the relationship between susceptibility to the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana and the expression of prophylactic grooming and necrophoresis in the ant Lasius flavus . We found strong and consistent intercolonial differences in pathogen susceptibility, as well as marked variation in the expression of prophylactic sanitary behaviours. None of the grooming behaviours examined were associated with pathogen susceptibility. However, more pathogen-susceptible colonies tended to remove corpses more rapidly during the early phase of necrophoresis. This pattern is consistent with a possible compensatory relationship among defence components, but may also arise from demographic and organizational differences among colonies, as worker age structure and task allocation can influence both susceptibility to infection and corpse removal behaviour. Overall, our results reveal substantial intercolonial variation in multiple components of disease defence but provide little support for a compensatory relationship between pathogen susceptibility and prophylactic sanitary behaviour.

items.title: The evolutionary structure of acoustic learnability: a deep learning approach to neotropical birdsong.
items.abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring offers a scalable solution for biodiversity assessment in the Neotropics, although classifying hundreds of sympatric species in complex soundscapes remains challenging. We developed a deep learning framework for large-scale avian classification by training convolutional neural networks on recordings from 667 Neotropical bird species across northern South America. EfficientNetV2L performed best, achieving 94.48% accuracy, 94.30% macro F1-score and 0.998 macro ROC-AUC. After training, we conducted a post hoc analysis of species-level F1-scores using phylogenetically informed models (phylogenetically generalized least squares (PGLS) and phylogenetic generalized linear mixed models (PGLMM)) to test morphological, ecological and geographic predictors under phylogenetic control. Broad traits explained little interspecific variation: the best-supported PGLS accounted for approximately 2.2% of the variance, whereas the null model received the strongest support among PGLMM candidates. Geographic range size showed the most consistent negative association with F1-score, while morphological and ecological predictors added little explanatory power. Performance nevertheless showed weak but significant phylogenetic signal, and frequent confusions tended to involve more closely related species. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping and Monte Carlo Dropout provided complementary descriptions of saliency and predictive uncertainty. Overall, deep learning performed effectively for regional biodiversity monitoring and provided a comparative framework for assessing how much of the variation in acoustic classification performance could be explained by broad biological predictors.

items.title: Beyond point estimates. A comment on: 'The environmental cost of welfare-driven policy changes in UK egg production' (2026), by Martinic et al.
items.abstract: A recent study comparing UK egg production systems concluded that the current ('business-as-usual') UK egg production system consisting of a mix of cage and non-cage systems minimizes environmental impacts, requires fewer laying hens and results in lower mortality than alternative cage-free scenarios. While the objective of evaluating environmental and welfare consequences of production system changes is important, I argue that these conclusions are not sufficiently supported by the methodology employed. The analysis relies on life cycle inventory and mortality data generated around 2010 to represent the UK industry in 2022, despite substantial advances in genetics, nutrition, housing, flock health and management over the intervening period. More importantly, it disregards the uncertainty associated with the original environmental and production datasets, treating inherently variable biological systems as deterministic. This omission is compounded by scaling farm-level point estimates to national production, thereby magnifying apparent differences between scenarios without quantifying their statistical significance. I contend that robust policy recommendations regarding transitions between egg production systems require analyses based on contemporary production data, explicit propagation of uncertainty and integrated evaluation of environmental sustainability and animal welfare.

items.title: Optimizing voyages for biodiversity: rerouting vessels around ocean giants can have minimal impact on shipping.
items.abstract: Vessel strikes are a significant and growing threat to marine megafauna, yet few mitigation measures are implemented at scale owing to perceived economic costs to shipping. Here, we present a proof of concept for integrating biodiversity considerations into commercial voyage optimization, using critical aggregation sites for the endangered whale shark ( Rhincodon typus ) as a case study. We simulated eight port-to-port voyages for two vessel classes-a crude oil tanker and a container ship-under three routing scenarios: baseline optimization, speed reduction to 10 kts within core habitats and complete avoidance of these areas. Across routes, fuel-use changes ranged from -0.13% to 9.65%, with minimal impacts (less than 1%) for most long-distance voyages. Results indicate that speed reduction is the more efficient mitigation for short voyages, while area avoidance is preferable for longer voyages, with impacts varying by vessel type and operational constraints. Incorporating dynamic, species-specific habitat layers into voyage planning could enable targeted vessel strike mitigation with negligible disruption to global trade. Adoption of such measures, supported by improved data pipelines, dynamic forecasting and integration into regulatory and incentive frameworks, offers a scalable pathway to align biodiversity conservation with decarbonization goals in the maritime sector.

items.title: Anemonefish prioritize mutualistic partner over social group during a marine heatwave.
items.abstract: Changing their behaviour is animals' first line of defence in response to environmental disturbance. However, changes in behaviour towards social group members and mutualistic partners can also lead to reduced fitness and resilience. Here, we use clown anemonefish, Amphiprion percula , to understand how disturbances alter social and mutualistic behaviours directly and indirectly via degraded mutualistic partners. We measured fish behaviour from video recordings made during a marine heatwave in Kimbe Bay, Papua New Guinea. Since some of the hosting anemones bleached, lost symbiotic algae, and others did not, we were able to estimate the effects of heat stress separate from the indirect effects through stressed mutualistic partners. Neither stressor significantly impacted activity levels or interactions with the mutualistic partner, which made up a high proportion of behaviours throughout. However, bleaching did increase aggression between group members and defensive behaviours. Our results provide an example of behavioural plasticity in response to environmental disturbance where different behaviours were adjusted to the stressor itself or to the changing habitat. We show that some species will prioritize interactions with mutualistic partners, while their social cohesion is weakened.

items.title: Everyone knows what science is…until you ask.
items.abstract: What is science? Scientists often assume that we share a general understanding of what science is, yet this assumption has rarely been empirically assessed. We examined scientists' and members of the public's agreement with a range of common conceptualizations of science, including science as a search for truth, a mirror of nature, a free marketplace of competing ideas and others. We found substantial heterogeneity in responses to these conceptualizations, with scientists disagreeing with each other more than the public does. We also found systematic differences in how the public and scientists understand science. Members of the public tended to endorse an idealized view of science, portraying it as a reliable machine for discovering objective truths through well-defined procedures. Scientists, in contrast, were more reserved in their endorsements, often emphasizing the limitations of the scientific method, contingency of scientific results and the roles of improvisation and creativity in scientific practice. This suggests that shared understanding of science cannot be taken for granted. Differences in how we understand science have implications for science practice, education and communication.

items.title: Analysis of biofilm complexity in 3D: an open-source framework for quantitative fractal, textural and statistical analysis of colony biofilm morphology in three dimensions.
items.abstract: Quantitative image analysis is central to understanding microbial growth, morphology and spatial organization. However, conventional metrics such as mean intensity or object count often do not capture the complex structural heterogeneity and patterning characteristic of microbial colonies and biofilms. To address this limitation, analysis of biofilm complexity in 3D (ABC3D), an open-source Python framework for automated extraction of fractal, textural and statistical descriptors from volumetric microscopy images, is reported. ABC3D computes a set of parameters including fractal dimension, lacunarity, entropy, grey-level co-occurrence matrix features and relative wavelet sub-band energies from three-dimensional image datasets. ABC3D is demonstrated in Escherichia coli macrocolony biofilms, where the first two principal components captured 75.5% of architectural variance. Nutrient environment, genetic background and their interaction significantly influenced biofilm architecture, indicating that structural responses to nutrient conditions are strain-dependent. Analysis of individual parameters revealed coordinated changes in fractal, textural and spatial-frequency features rather than uniform changes in a single measure of complexity. ABC3D provides researchers with an accessible, quantitative approach to assessing biofilm morphology in microscopy datasets.

items.title: A viral mimic increases body temperature but does not affect mass or inflammation in a wild frugivorous bat.
items.abstract: The acute phase response is a component of innate immunity that helps fight infections. Understanding variation in this response could be critical in bats, which can be asymptomatic hosts of pathogens that cause disease in other animals. Although bats are most famously tolerant of some viruses, research on the bat acute phase response has focused predominantly on bacterial antigens. To improve understanding of bat viral responses, we challenged wild Seba's short-tailed bats ( Carollia perspicillata ) with a viral mimic (polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid (polyI:C)). We injected nine bats subcutaneously with 2 mg kg -1 of polyI:C ( n = 3), 5 mg kg -1 of polyI:C ( n = 3) or phosphate buffered saline ( n = 3). Over the next 24 hours, we measured body temperature hourly and collected body mass and blood smears for leucocyte counts every 4 hours. Regardless of dose, polyI:C-challenged bats had higher body temperatures compared to control bats but did not exhibit leucocytosis or reduced body mass. These preliminary findings improve understanding of how wild bats physiologically respond to viral challenges. Moreover, in showing that as little as 2 mg kg -1 of polyI:C can induce a febrile response, our study provides a framework to facilitate future investigations into causes and consequences of wild bat viral responses.

items.title: Contrasting pre- and post-COVID changes in within-host gp60 diversity among human-infecting Cryptosporidium species.
items.abstract: Population connectivity influences genetic diversity by facilitating exchange among populations. For enteric parasites, connectivity depends on host contact and environmentally mediated transmission, suggesting that disruptions to human movement could reduce diversity within infections. The COVID-19 pandemic provided a natural experiment to test this prediction. We used high-throughput gp60 metabarcoding to compare within-host amplicon sequence variant (ASVs) richness, diversity and composition before and after the pandemic in three human-infecting Cryptosporidium species with contrasting transmission ecologies: anthroponotic Cryptosporidium hominis , zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum and wildlife-associated Cryptosporidium cuniculus . Primary analyses excluded 26 epidemiologically linked C. hominis infections from a 2023 outbreak; sensitivity analyses included these samples. Post-COVID, C. hominis showed significantly lower Shannon, Simpson and inverse-Simpson diversity, 63% fewer detectable ASVs and altered ASV composition. Cryptosporidium parvum showed compositional differences but no significant reduction in diversity or richness, whereas C. cuniculus showed no clear temporal change. Including outbreak-associated C. hominis samples attenuated diversity reductions but retained significant declines in Shannon diversity, Simpson diversity, ASV richness and composition. These findings are consistent with reduced parasite connectivity following disruption of predominantly human-associated transmission and indicate that major changes in transmission conditions can rapidly reshape the genetic diversity maintained within parasite infections.

items.title: Ex situ population dynamics of Brazilian parrots based on zoo, trade and conservation data.
items.abstract: Zoos contribute to ex situ conservation of taxa affected by habitat loss and wildlife trade, including parrots, but their success in maintaining viable populations remains unclear. This study assessed the role of zoos in the ex situ maintenance and reproduction of Brazilian parrot species over 2004-2024 using Zoological Information Management System demographic records, Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) trade data and International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List categories. Generalized linear mixed models, generalized additive models and generalized additive mixed models tested effects of population growth, threat status, sex ratio and extinction risk in relation to trade intensity. Ex situ populations showed no consistent demographic growth. Hatching rates declined over time, and per capita net population change was near zero or negative for most species, with populations often sustained by acquisitions rather than reproduction. More threatened species did not show higher reproductive success under captive management. Sex ratio was associated with population dynamics, with more favourable outcomes near balanced ratios. International trade was positively associated with extinction risk, with species at higher threat levels appearing more frequently in trade records. These findings show that captive population growth is uneven across species and highlight the need for integrated demographic, welfare, genetic and trade management to improve conservation outcomes.

items.title: Distinct space-use patterns are associated with alternative reproductive tactics in lekking ruffs Calidris pugnax.
items.abstract: Territoriality is a key strategy through which animals secure access to reproductive opportunities, yet in many lekking species, males differ in their investment in defending space. Breeding aggregations often include territorial residents and non-territorial floaters, raising questions about the flexibility and endocrine regulation of alternative spatial tactics. The ruff ( Calidris pugnax ) provides a powerful model to address these questions because males occur as three genetically determined reproductive morphs: territorial independents and two non-territorial floater morphs, satellites and faeders. Using artificial intelligence-assisted tracking in a captive colony, we quantified fine-scale space-use patterns within experimental and control leks. Our aim was to test whether male morphs adjust spatial behaviour when social opportunities arise. Independents exhibited smaller and more segregated activity areas, whereas satellites and faeders showed larger, overlapping activity areas, consistent with a floater strategy. Despite experimentally manipulating lek composition to create single-morph social environments, neither satellites nor faeders adopted territorial-like spatial behaviour. In addition, circulating concentrations of testosterone were higher in independents than faeders and satellites, but short-term variation in testosterone was not linked to changes in spatial behaviour and experimental treatment. These findings support the view that space-use tactics in ruffs represent fixed specializations rather than flexible responses to social opportunities.

items.title: Beyond short delays: one-week recall and recognition Italian norms for the Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to establish Italian normative data for the Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test (ROCFT), extending the standard protocol to include a recognition trial and a one-week delayed recall. Additionally, the study evaluated the clinical utility of these extended memory measures for detecting accelerated long-term forgetting (ALF) and for differentiating impairments in encoding, storage, and retrieval processes. A total of 413 cognitively healthy Italian adults completed the ROCFT. The protocol included a copy trial, delayed recall at 10 minutes and 1 week, and recognition trials at both delays. Recognition hits and false positives were recorded, and composite indices were computed, including Recognition Accuracy Index (RAI) and ALF indices for recall and recognition. Multiple regression analyses were conducted to adjust scores for demographic variables, and Equivalent Scores (ES) were derived using outer tolerance limits to classify performance. An automated Excel-based tool was developed to facilitate score adjustment. Normative data demonstrated significant effects of age, education, and, to a lesser extent, sex across ROCFT indices, supporting the need for demographic correction. Equivalent Score cutoffs based on outer tolerance limits provided a robust framework for classifying performance. This study provides the first Italian normative framework for the ROCFT including Recognition and one-week delayed recall and recognition trials. The extended protocol improves the test' sensitivity to subtle memory impairments and ALF, while enabling a more precise characterization of underlying cognitive mechanisms. These findings support the use of the ROCFT as a multidimensional tool for assessing visuoconstructive abilities and long-term memory processes in both clinical and research settings.

items.title: Do you know what you're looking for? Guiding templates are imprecise for both simple and real-world stimuli.
items.abstract: Recent research has found evidence that a highly veridical representation of the target is not used to guide attention. Rather, the template is broadly tuned to guide attention to a wider range of feature values than characterized by the target. In three experiments, we investigated whether a veridical representation of target features is used to guide attention when the target is a real-world object. In Experiment 1, we examined the imprecision of the guiding template when searching for real-world objects. We compared the coarseness of the guiding template across colored circles and real-world objects in Experiment 2. In Experiment 3, we evaluated if the accuracy of the encoded target item affected the coarseness of the guiding template. We found evidence across all three experiments that the guiding template does not represent the target veridically and that the coarseness of the template is affected by the initial precision of the target representation. The results support prior research suggesting that a coarser template may be inherent to efficient guidance regardless of stimulus type. OPEN PRACTICES STATEMENT: The data for all three experiments are available in the Open Science Framework (OSF) repository ( https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/PBG4U ). All three experiments were preregistered and can be found in the same repository.

items.title: Trends in mental health and behavioural outcomes in UK 10-15 year olds from 2009 to 2024.
items.abstract: This is a longitudinal observational study aiming to describe recent trends in mental health and behavioural outcomes among UK adolescents 10-15 years-old and examine differences by socio-demographic characteristics. We used self-reported data from a household-based UK survey; 2009-2024to examine trends the prevalence of emotional problems, hyperactivity, and conduct problems (Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire); health behaviours (diet, physical activity, social media use); parent-child relationships (conflict, communication); risk behaviours (alcohol, tobacco, vaping, staying out late); and antisocial behaviours (violence, vandalism, shoplifting). Overall, 16,356 participants provided 46,218 observations. Between 2009 and 2024, emotional problems more than doubled (from 11.4% to 27.1%), with acceleration after 2014 and again after 2019. Increases were greatest among girls (38.9% in 2024 vs. 15.8% in boys) and white British adolescents. Hyperactivity symptoms were stable up to 2017 (~ 16.1%) but rose to 27.4% by 2024, mainly in girls. Conduct problems declined steadily from 13.6% in 2009 to 11.4% in 2024, driven by reductions among boys. Peer problems rose (particularly among girls), and vaping increased sharply after 2020. In contrast, alcohol and tobacco use, staying out late, and conflict with parents all declined. CONCLUSION: These findings align with previous reports indicating that emotional problems in early adolescence have risen at an epidemic scale while many externalising and risk behaviours have declined. The divergence of trends, and concentration of poor outcomes among girls and white British adolescents, points to specific mechanisms of risk and resilience. These findings, alongside current service demand, support urgent investment in prevention of the drivers of the increases in adolescent emotional problems.

items.title: Examination of Performance Anxiety Theories in Sport Psychology Textbooks and a Proposed Framework for Organizing These Theories.
items.abstract: What are the major theories of performance anxiety, and what key variable sets do they share? Although many sport psychologists utilize specific performance anxiety theories to guide client treatments, we doubt many are familiar with the full spectrum of available theories and their associated variables. This knowledge gap may lead to the selection of suboptimal treatment plans. We examined sport psychology textbooks to assess which theories are commonly presented, evaluated the accuracy of their presentation, and developed a categorization system based on common key variables. We analyzed 16 unique sport psychology textbooks, with independent coders reviewing each textbook. Twenty-five unique theories were identified, 10 of which appeared in five or more textbooks. We were surprised by the frequency of incomplete or inaccurate presentations of the theories and by the absence of a coherent framework for organizing these theories. We discuss applied implications for educators, practitioners, and textbook authors, introduce a proposed categorization system for organizing theories by key variables, and offer recommendations for future research.

items.title: Effects of resistance training on neuronal response to visual food cues in adults with overweight/obesity.
items.abstract: Individuals with overweight/obesity show altered neuronal response to food cues, but how exercise affects this response remains unclear. This study examined resistance training (RT) effects on neuronal response to visual food cues and eating behaviors in adults with overweight/obesity. We hypothesized RT would be associated with decreased response in brain regions involved in regulating energy intake and decreased ad libitum intake, with brain and behavioral changes correlated. Exploratory analyses evaluated RT effects on eating behaviors and whole-brain response and compared RT with a 12-week diet intervention. Participants (N = 19) completed a visual food cues task during functional magnetic resonance imaging in fasted and fed states, before and after a 12-week RT program. Paired t-tests examined RT effects on response to high-calorie foods versus non-food objects in regions of interest (ROIs; dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, insula, nucleus accumbens), energy intake, Three Factor Eating Questionnaire, and whole-brain response. Repeated measures correlations examined associations between changes in ROIs and energy intake. Linear mixed models compared RT and diet (N = 17). RT was associated with decreased dietary disinhibition (p = 0.009) and increased restraint (p = 0.023). No significant within-group effects were observed on neuronal response, energy intake, or associations between the two. Between-group analyses demonstrated (1) increased restraint across groups (p = 0.017), with a stronger effect for diet, and (2) a significant group*time interaction in right posterior insula and left primary somatosensory cortex (p < 0.001), with decreased response following RT and increased response following diet. Despite an absence of observed changes in predefined ROIs or energy intake, RT may promote self-regulatory eating behaviors in adults with overweight/obesity. Exploratory analyses suggest RT and diet may have distinct effects on neuronal response to food cues, with RT decreasing and diet increasing response in interoceptive and sensory processing regions. Findings should be interpreted with caution, however, given the small, non-randomized sample. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT02047721 and NCT03985787.

items.title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation And Psychometric Validation of Screen11: A Screening Instrument for Voice Disorders in Persian-Speaking Adults in Iran.
items.abstract: This study aimed to translate, cross-culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Screen11 voice disorder screening instrument for Persian-speaking Iranian adults, which is designed to identify individuals with potential voice disorders. Non-experimental, cross-sectional psychometric study. A total of 119 Persian-speaking adults, including 64 individuals with a confirmed voice disorder and 55 with a normal voice, were recruited from the otolaryngology clinic of Amir-A´lam Hospital in Tehran. The translation and cultural adaptation followed established World Health Organization (WHO) and cross-cultural adaptation guidelines, incorporating forward translation, expert panel review, back-translation, and cognitive debriefing. Additionally, the psychometric properties were evaluated in accordance with the Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) (reference). The psychometric evaluation included face validity; content validity, assessed using the Content Validity Ratio (CVR) and Content Validity Index (CVI); internal consistency, assessed using Cronbach's alpha; test-retest reliability, assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); and construct validity, including structural validity assessed using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and hypothesis testing through known-groups comparisons and correlations with the Persian Voice Handicap Index and the Consensus Auditory-Perceptual Evaluation of Voice (CAPE-V). Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Face validity was confirmed by the panel of experts, and all items met the accepted thresholds for CVR and CVI, confirming satisfactory content validity. Internal consistency was excellent (α = 0.91), and test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.89). Structural validity was confirmed through EFA, with all Screen11 items loading onto a single common factor. Additionally, hypothesis testing demonstrated construct validity through significant known-groups differences between the two groups (P < 0.001) and a very high correlation between Screen11 and VHI total scores (ρ = 0.908), and with CAPE-V severity ratings (ρ = 0.82). ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.98, with an optimal cutoff of 5.5, sensitivity of 93.8%, and specificity of 90.9%. The Persian version of Screen11 is a valid, reliable, and diagnostically accurate instrument for screening voice disorders in Persian-speaking Iranian adults. Its brevity and ease of administration support its integration into clinical and research settings.

items.title: Incentive-driven instrumental actions depend on intact astrocytic signalling in nucleus accumbens core.
items.abstract: Astrocytes in the nucleus accumbens (NAC) core have been observed to undergo phenotypic changes associated with drug-seeking behaviour in both humans and animals. However, the role of NAC core astrocytes in non-drug-related instrumental behaviour remains poorly understood. To address this, we chemogenetically activated hM4Di receptors selectively expressed on NAC core astrocytes in male and female rats during food-motivated decision-making tasks. In Experiment 1, rats were first trained to associate two auditory stimuli with two distinct food outcomes (pellets and sucrose), then to press left and right levers for those same outcomes. All training was conducted drug-free, and rats then received intraperitoneal (i.p) injections of either vehicle or Deschloroclozapine (DCZ) prior to test. Disrupting astrocytic signalling left instrumental choice intact when it was guided by cues signalling the sensory-specific properties of each outcome, as tested in specific Pavlovian instrumental transfer and outcome-selective reinstatement, but suppressed responding in an outcome devaluation test. In Experiment 2, a single stimulus and single lever were separately paired with distinct food outcomes, then presented together on test. Control animals demonstrated a general PIT effect, elevating responding during stimulus presentations, and this was prevented by Gi activation on NAC core astrocytes. Immunohistochemistry revealed increased neuronal activity following hM4Di activation in astrocytes. Together, these findings suggest that intact signalling in NAC core astrocytes is necessary for instrumental actions that depend on general arousal or affective processes, but not for actions guided by sensory-specific outcome expectations. Significance Statement Astrocyte dysfunction in the nucleus accumbens (NAC) has been implicated in several forms of compulsion in humans, yet preclinical work has focussed almost exclusively on drug-taking and seeking. The role of NAC core astrocytes on responding for non-drug outcomes is therefore unclear. Here, using food outcomes, we show that agonising Gi receptors on astrocytes in NAC core selectively impairs actions driven by general motivational states but spares those guided by specific outcome expectations. These findings suggest that NAC core astrocytes play a critical role in invigorating behaviour, extending their involvement beyond drug-seeking in animals and highlighting their potential relevance to compulsive behaviour more generally.
