items.title: The open-source computerized Trail Making Test in PEBL: Preserved task structure, practice effects, and limited agreement with paper-based testing.
items.abstract: This pilot study examined preliminary evidence regarding the measurement properties of the computerized Trail Making Test implemented in PEBL. Thirty-seven Brazilian adults completed the paper TMT and four administrations of three PEBL conditions: number sequencing, alternating number and letter sequencing, and letter sequencing. We evaluated short-term practice effects, task hierarchy, relative switching cost, and correspondence between formats using nonparametric tests, correlations, intraclass correlations, and Bland-Altman analyses. Completion times decreased significantly across administrations for all conditions, with the largest improvements occurring after the first administration. The expected hierarchy of difficulty remained stable. Relative switching cost decreased gradually, with a significant difference only between the first and fourth administrations after correction for multiple comparisons. PEBL and paper completion times were positively associated for TMT-A and TMT-B. However, intraclass correlations indicated limited consistency, while Bland-Altman analyses showed systematic bias and wide limits of agreement, with longer completion times on paper. Age was associated with performance only during the first administration, and no mood associations remained significant after correction. These findings indicate that the PEBL implementation preserves expected task ordering and short-term performance patterns, but provide limited evidence of cross-format correspondence; scores from the two formats should not be considered interchangeable.

items.title: Prenatal Fluoride Exposure in Relation to Cognitive and Motor Outcomes in Preschool-Aged Children: The New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background Evidence linking prenatal fluoride exposure to child neurodevelopment has focused on global cognition, with less attention to specific domains or effect modification by sex and exposure timing. Objectives To examine associations between maternal fluoride and children's cognitive and motor outcomes, and interactions by sex and exposure window. Methods Mother-child dyads from the New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study used private, unregulated water. Fluoride was measured in maternal toenails at approximately 28 weeks' gestation (early pregnancy) and 6 weeks' postpartum (mid-late pregnancy), and in tap water (24-28 weeks). Cognitive and motor outcomes were assessed at 5 years using the WPPSI-IV and BOT-2. Covariate-adjusted generalized estimating equations tested sex and exposure-window interactions. Restricted cubic splines were used to examine the shape of exposure-outcome relationships. Results Complete-case models included 409 dyads for toenail and 432 for water fluoride; imputation models included 543 dyads. Neither exposure measure was associated with global cognitive or motor outcomes. Higher early pregnancy toenail fluoride was associated with lower Working Memory in girls (unstandardized B=-1.24; 95% CI: -2.40, -0.09) but not boys (B = 0.77; 95% CI: -0.14, 1.68; Pint=.007), which attenuated after imputation (B = -0.27; 95% CI: -1.30, 0.77 in girls). For Fine Motor Precision, higher water fluoride was associated with poorer scores in boys (B=-0.59; 95% CI: -1.10, -0.09) but not girls (B = 0.41; 95% CI: -0.16, 0.99; Pint=.010), and this persisted under imputation (B=-0.58; 95% CI: -1.09, -0.09 in boys); mid-late pregnancy toenail fluoride showed the same direction in boys (B=-0.35; 95% CI: -0.70, 0.01; Pint=.032) but attenuated under imputation (B = -0.23; 95% CI: -0.60, 0.14). Spline curves for toenail fluoride were largely consistent with linear associations; for water fluoride, scores tended to decrease with increasing fluoride below approximately 1 mg/L, but the shape at higher concentrations could not be reliably characterized because data were sparse. Conclusions In this U.S. cohort, we found some evidence of sex-specific associations between prenatal fluoride exposure and specific neurodevelopmental domains (i.e., working memory and fine motor precision), depending on exposure timing and fluoride exposure measure. Fluoride was not strongly associated with global cognitive and motor scores.

items.title: Orthographic repetition elicits enhancement without suppression at both the word- and character-levels in Chinese.
items.abstract: In Chinese, orthographic repetition (e.g., ""-"") modulates neural activity associated with orthographic processing around 200 ms after target onset, as indexed by the N200 enhancement effect. The present study combined time-frequency analysis with priming paradigms in two EEG experiments to determine whether orthographic repetition is accompanied by oscillatory power enhancement or suppression. In Experiment 1, complete repetition priming of two-character words elicited both a significant N200 enhancement effect and significant theta power enhancement relative to the control condition, whereas no significant N200 or theta-power enhancement was detected for semantic or phonological priming. To separate orthographic overlap from the concomitant phonological and semantic repetition inherent in complete repetition, Experiment 2 used partial orthographic repetition with single-character prime-target pairs that differed in phonology and semantics and replicated both effects. Exploratory participant-level correlations between the N200 and total theta effects were positive but nonsignificant in both experiments. A positive correlation between N200 enhancement and evoked theta enhancement reached the unadjusted significance threshold only in Experiment 2. These findings indicate that orthographic repetition is associated with enhancement rather than suppression of theta-band activity and that this pattern extends across word and character levels.

items.title: Individual characteristics interacting with processing level and hyperpalatability are associated with food addictiveness: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Some people experience symptoms of food addiction and evidence indicates certain foods, particularly ultra-processed foods and those high in refined carbohydrates and fats, have addictive properties. The study explores whether specific phenotypic characteristics were associated with perceived food addictiveness ratings and whether food processing and hyperpalatability interact with these characteristics in their association with perception of addictiveness of foods. In a nationally representative cross-sectional survey (n=1,664), participants reported demographics, height, and weight; and completed the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire Short (EDE-QS) and Modified Yale Food Addiction Scale Questionnaire 2.0 (mYFAS 2.0). Participants rated the addictiveness of 99 randomly chosen food items from a set of 297 on a 100-point Visual Analog Scale, anchored by "Not at all" and "Very", from the question "How PROBLEMATIC is this food for you?", which referenced the Problematic foods in the mYFAS 2.0. The food items were categorized according to the Nova classification system and standardized Hyperpalatable foods (HPF) definitions. Individuals living in the U.S., over 18 years, and members of the research survey platform, Prolific were included in this 2024 study. The main outcome was rated perceived addictiveness of food items associated with participant phenotypic characteristics, food characteristics, and the interaction between the two. Linear mixed effects models were used to evaluate participant phenotypic characteristics associated with perceived addictiveness ratings of foods. Two interaction models for food classifications were fit, in which all phenotypic characteristics, the food classification system, and their interactions were included. All models included food item and participant as random intercepts. In the interaction model examining Nova classification, a statistically significant interaction was observed between processing categories and both EDE-QS (χ2(2) = 222.8, p<.001) and mYFAS 2.0 (χ2 (2) = 54.7, p < .001) scores on addictiveness rating, where there was a highest slope for both independent variables in the Nova 4 foods. In the interaction model with HPF classification, a statistically significant interaction between HPF and both EDE-QS (χ2(2)=210.3, p<.001) and mYFAS 2.0 (χ2(2)=22.8, p<.001) scores was observed. Phenotypic differences in eating behaviors, but not BMI, interact with degree of food processing and hyperpalatability in their association with a food's rated addictiveness. This provides evidence for a framework in which ultra-processed and hyperpalatable foods are perceived as substantially more addictive than minimally processed and non-hyperpalatable options in people with food addiction and eating disorder symptoms.

items.title: Neural signatures of impulsivity in adolescence: A multivariate pattern analysis of reward and loss processing.
items.abstract: Adolescence is characterized by increased mood disturbances and impulsivity linked to maladaptive risk-taking. However, the frontostriatal circuitry underlying these phenotypes remains poorly understood in adolescents, particularly given its rapid maturation in this developmental period. Thus, the current pre-registered study sought to develop models predicting adolescent anhedonic, sad, and manic mood, as well as impulsivity, from multivariate frontostriatal neural responses during incentive (i.e., reward and loss) processing. Participants were 12-18 years old (n = 153, 104 assigned female at birth) and were drawn from a larger study on depression and mixed manic symptoms. They underwent functional neuroimaging during a monetary incentive delay task and completed self-report questionnaires on mood and impulsivity. Multivariate pattern voxel analysis (MVPA) was employed, which can detect distributed patterns of neural activity during incentive processing, compared with traditional univariate approaches. MVPA models demonstrated statistically significant, albeit very small, predictive performance for impulsivity (R 2 = 0.01-0.02). Models predicting depression-residualized impulsivity (to account for shared variance with depressive symptoms) performed modestly better (R 2 = 0.03-0.04). Across models, signal in cognitive and motor-related frontostriatal circuits, particularly during loss anticipation followed by reward receipt and reward anticipation, contributed most to predictive performance. No models successfully predicted anhedonic, sad, or manic mood. These findings suggest that multivariate neural activity within cognitive- and motor-related frontostriatal circuits during incentive processing may underlie impulsivity in adolescents. Given low predictive performance, these models are not appropriate for clinical prediction at this time.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between PTSD symptoms, suicide exposure, and suicidal ideation among U.S. military personnel.
items.abstract: Military personnel are at an elevated risk of both posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms and suicidal ideation (SI). Suicide exposure-knowing one who has died by suicide-is associated with PTSD symptoms and SI. However, few studies have explored longitudinal relationships between suicide bereavement, PTSD symptoms from a military experience, and SI within a military sample. Using longitudinal data from N = 771 U.S. military personnel, linear mixed-effects models examined how military-related PTSD symptoms and SI severity differ across timepoints based on suicide exposure. Lagged linear mixed-effects models further examined how PTSD symptoms and suicide exposure were associated with subsequent SI severity. Among individuals who experienced suicide exposure, linear mixed-effects models examined how closeness to the decedent and perceived impact of the loss were associated with PTSD symptoms and SI severity. Lagged linear mixed-effects models further examined how closeness to the decedent and perceived impact of the loss were related to subsequent SI severity. Findings indicated that military-related PTSD symptoms predicted subsequent SI, regardless of suicide exposure status. Among suicide-exposed individuals, greater closeness to the decedent was not associated with PTSD symptoms but was associated with decreased SI severity across timepoints and lower future SI severity. Greater perceived impact of the loss was associated with greater military-related PTSD symptom severity, greater SI severity across timepoints, and greater future SI severity. Findings underscore the importance of assessing military-related PTSD symptoms in conjunction with SI and suicide exposure, and considering suicide exposure characteristics among military personnel who have experienced suicide loss.

items.title: Lateral orbitofrontal cortex enables new learning to overwrite previously acquired information.
items.abstract: Responding that has been reduced through experience can recover over time or following re-exposure to a biologically relevant outcome; these phenomena are known as spontaneous recovery and reinstatement, respectively. First described by Pavlov in 1927, 1 these effects are most commonly (but not exclusively 2 , 3 , 4 ) documented following extinction 5 , 6 and are thought to contribute to relapse following behavioral treatments for anxiety, addiction, and related disorders. 7 , 8 Therefore, extinction is generally considered to suppress rather than erase prior learning. 5 , 6 In contrast, contingency degradation has been suggested to weaken initial response-outcome learning. 9 Although previous studies of recovery following degradation have produced mixed results, 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 each of these studies combined degradation with extinction, making it unclear whether degradation itself produces persistent reductions in responding. Here, rats learned two action-outcome contingencies (e.g., left lever, pellets; right lever, sucrose), one of which was subsequently degraded by unsignaled, non-contingent delivery of its outcome. Responding to the degraded action was reduced and did not recover following a 2-week interval or unexpected outcome delivery. This indicates that degradation, unlike extinction, produces persistent changes in behavior. We next examined the role of the lateral orbitofrontal cortex (lOFC), a region implicated in resolving interference between competing contingencies. Chemogenetic inactivation of lOFC impaired acquisition but not retrieval of degradation, consistent with the existence of competition between original and degraded contingencies during learning but not at test. These findings indicate that contingency degradation overwrites initial action-outcome learning and identify a potential framework for developing behavioral interventions that are resistant to relapse.

items.title: Volatile emission dynamics are temporally associated with neighbor-modulated movement in climbing plants.
items.abstract: Climbing plants use circumnutation, a rhythmic exploratory movement of the shoot apex, to locate supports. 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 Although neighboring plants can alter this movement before physical contact, the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 Here, we combined three-dimensional kinematic tracking and real-time volatilomic profiling in Pisum sativum to investigate the temporal association between volatile emissions and circumnutation. Seven volatile-associated m/z features showed transient increases before peak circumnutation velocity in plants growing with a conspecific, a pattern absent in isolated plants. Neighbor presence also increased apex velocity, acceleration, path length, and explored area. Wavelet coherence analysis revealed stronger temporal coordination between real neighboring pairs than between randomly paired individuals. Neighboring plants additionally exhibited faster shoot growth and increased chlorophyll content in upper leaves. Together, these findings link volatile emission dynamics with exploratory movement and reveal coordinated behavioral and physiological responses to neighboring plants. This work establishes a framework for investigating the temporal organization of plant-plant interactions while highlighting the need for experiments to determine whether volatile cues causally influence movement.

items.title: How animals are used in education shapes public perceptions of their minds and moral concern for them.
items.abstract: Aims To examine how framing of an animal's use in educational teaching influences people's perceptions of the animal's mind and the moral concern given to it. Methods Members of the New Zealand and Australian public (n = 439 after exclusions) were recruited through an online platform and randomly assigned to read one of three vignettes describing a rabbit: a naturalistic vignette depicting the rabbit in its wild habitat (control; n = 146), an observational teaching vignette (n = 147), or an intervention teaching vignette describing a surgical procedure (n = 146). All three vignettes were portrayed as occurring within an established ethical framework. Participants rated their perceptions of the rabbit's mental capabilities (two dimensions of mind perception: affective sociality and cognitive autonomy) and their moral concern for the rabbit, each on a scale from 0 to 7. Results There was no evidence that perceptions of the rabbit's affective sociality differed across vignettes (proportion of variance explained (η 2 : min 0, max 1) = 0.007, 90% CI = 0.000-0.022). Scores for perceptions of its cognitive autonomy were slightly lower in the teaching vignettes than in the naturalistic vignette (naturalistic versus observational mean difference 0.45, 95% CI = 0.06-0.84): a small effect (η 2 = 0.019, 90% CI = 0.002-0.042). Contrary to a mind-denial prediction, moral concern score was higher in both teaching vignettes than in the naturalistic vignette (observational: 0.58 (95% CI = 0.29-0.88) points higher; intervention: 0.50 (95% CI = 0.20-0.79) points higher, statistically adjusting for mind perception). Moral concern was associated with perceptions of the rabbit's affective sociality (0.30 (95% CI = 0.21-0.38) points per scale point) but not its cognitive autonomy. Conclusions Framing a rabbit's use within a teaching context did not produce the mind denial seen when people consider animals used for meat or testing; moral concern was not diminished and was higher than for a naturalistic portrayal. Moral concern was driven by perceptions of the animal's capacity for emotional experience, which teaching-use did not reduce, leaving little basis for the withdrawal of mind and moral concern that characterises moral disengagement. Because all scenarios were ethically framed, these effects cannot be attributed to the ethical framing itself. Clinical relevance Among members of the New Zealand and Australian public, presenting an animal's use in education as ethically regulated was associated with greater, not lesser, moral concern for the animal. Whether this holds for veterinary students, and whether ethical framing is an operative factor, remains for future research.

items.title: Modular signaling architecture of Meteorin-like protein (METRNL): From acute tissue repair to chronic tumor immune evasion.
items.abstract: Meteorin-like protein (METRNL) is a stress-responsive homeokine that coordinates tissue repair through three context-dependent signaling modules: signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3)-driven immune reprogramming, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-centered metabolic resilience, and KIT-PI3K-AKT-eNOS architectural renewal. These modules are engaged selectively rather than uniformly across organ systems. KIT is the only receptor with functional validation, and it operates in KIT-expressing cells; the receptors that transduce METRNL signals in KIT-negative immune and metabolic tissues are unidentified, and the co-receptor models proposed for them are hypotheses. Transient, pulsatile exposure is associated with repair, whereas sustained exposure of CD8 + T cells to METRNL disrupts mitochondrial function through an E2F-PPARδ program and, in preclinical tumor models, impairs anti-tumor immunity. A three-variable switch model, defined by exposure pattern, co-signal milieu, and receptor availability, is proposed as a testable framework for this duality; its temporal parameters have not been quantified for METRNL. Receptor deorphanization in KIT-negative tissues is the gating step for rational therapeutic development. Delivery strategies that reproduce transient, physiological METRNL kinetics are a reasonable working principle, particularly where tumor-like co-signals prevail, but the principle remains to be tested, and a tiered roadmap with explicit entry criteria is provided.

items.title: The interaction between polygenic risk scores for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder is associated in healthy subjects with resting-state prefrontal activity linked with depressive symptoms in patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders.
items.abstract: Mood symptoms often characterize schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD). However, their biological underpinnings remain poorly defined. Given that these symptoms are a core feature of bipolar disorders (BD), and that BD-related genetic liability is also present in schizophrenia (SCZ), genetic variation for each disorder may jointly interact to modulate brain phenotypes relevant for mood symptoms in SSD. To test this interaction, we computed Polygenic Risk Scores (PRS) for SCZ and BD in 263 healthy participants (HP) using diagnosis-associated variants at the genome-wide level significance (PRS_SCZ_GWA, PRS_BD_GWA) or at p < 0.05 (PRS_SCZ_05, PRS_BD_05) with the clumping and thresholding method. We also calculated further PRSs using the Bayesian continuous shrinkage method (PRS_CS_SCZ, PRS_CS_BD) to verify our results using a different approach. Spontaneous brain activity was estimated using the fractional Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations (fALFF). Finally, the relationship between fALFF and mood symptoms was investigated on an independent sample of 40 SSD. In HP, multiple regression indicated a PRS_SCZ_05 by PRS_BD_05 interaction on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) and angular gyrus (AG) fALFF, such that lower PRS_SCZ_05 and higher PRS_BD_05 was associated with lower DLPFC fALFF, whereas higher scores of both PRSs were associated with greater AG fALFF. PRS_CS analysis yielded convergent results in left DLPFC. In SSD, DLPFC fALFF negatively correlated with depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that genetic risk for SCZ and BD jointly modulates spontaneous brain activity in HP in areas that may be relevant to depressive symptoms in SSD. Clinical heterogeneity of SCZ may thus reflect the cross-talk between SCZ- and BD-related genetic pathways.

items.title: How do US children and adults make sense of unequal compensation in division of labor?
items.abstract: Division of labor is a ubiquitous feature of social life, as it allows people to specialize and reach desired outcomes efficiently. However, it also creates pay disparities, as some roles are compensated more than others. Here we examined how U.S. children (105 6-12-year-olds [52 girls, 52 boys, 1 other; 37 Asian, 51 other, 17 race unknown]) and adults (N = 108 [Mage = 43.39; 70 women, 36 men, 2 other; 91 White, 17 other]) make sense of why some roles receive higher pay. Children, like adults, are more likely to perceive unequal compensation as fair in division of labor compared to cooperative arrangements where all participants perform the same tasks (i.e., "parallel cooperation"). Also, while older children are more likely to see unequal pay as unfair in parallel cooperation, they continue to see unequal compensation as fair in division-of-labor cases. Participant explanations provide a potential explanation: a circular meritocratic logic, in which participants assume that higher pay signals greater difficulty, and then use perceived difficulty to justify those same wage disparities. This tendency does not depend on actual job characteristics, and increases with age in the child sample. We discuss how this may help rationalize lower pay for certain occupations-such as assuming female-coded roles like caregiving are easy simply because they offer lower pay.

items.title: A variability-based account of motor coordination in joint action: the co-adaptability perspective.
items.abstract: Over the last decade, research on joint action has expanded considerably, and multiple theoretical frameworks have been proposed to explain how agents achieve motor coordination while pursuing a shared goal. Early accounts focused on minimal building blocks, such as shared goal representations, whereas more recent perspectives have given greater emphasis to internal predictive mechanisms, including the idea that co-agents rely on shared motor plans. Although these studies provide insights into describing the population-level processes underlying interpersonal coordination, they overlook how each agent's motor variability may contribute to these shared dynamics. The present paper aims at addressing this gap by integrating current joint action theories with the construct of "space of variability". We claim that the initial similarity between co-agents' spaces of variability and the ability of each co-agent to flexibly reshape their own spaces during the interaction constitute important processes driving between-agents co-adaptation. Thus, we propose the theory-driven co-adaptability framework and articulate it at three complementary levels: a theoretical reformulation, a computational formalization, and an empirically testable research proposal. This framework is presented as a theoretical scaffold specifically applicable to alignment-based joint action tasks, rather than as a comprehensive account of joint action in its full complexity. The shift from population-level explanations to the individual-centered account proposed within this paper moves the understanding of interpersonal coordination in alignment-based tasks to a variability-based level and generates testable predictions, with the aim of enriching current co-representational frameworks and advancing conceptual and translational avenues for joint action research.

items.title: Forecasting Next-Day Alcohol Craving in Individuals With Problematic Alcohol Use With Multimodal Data and a Tiny Recurrent Neural Network: Prospective Longitudinal Study.
items.abstract: Background Alcohol craving is associated with drinking behaviors despite negative consequences and relapse following periods of abstinence or treatment. Accurately forecasting alcohol craving is crucial for preventing alcohol consumption and relapse, thereby mitigating alcohol-related problems. Previous studies have assessed alcohol craving using diverse modalities such as psychological assessments, neurophysiological measures including electroencephalography (EEG) or heart rate variability (HRV) at a single time point, and digital phenotypes collected longitudinally via smartphone apps. However, alcohol craving is inherently heterogeneous and multidimensional across individuals and over time, making it difficult to capture using any single modality alone. In contrast, multimodal AI enables the prediction of alcohol craving by integrating complementary behavioral and neurophysiological features. Objective This study aimed to develop and evaluate AI models to forecast next-day alcohol craving in individuals with problematic alcohol use with multimodal datasets. Methods We analyzed multimodal datasets comprising smartphone-based digital phenotypes collected over 28 days, along with baseline EEG, HRV, and psychological measures in a prospective longitudinal study of 60 participants with problematic alcohol use. A tiny multimodal recurrent neural network (RNN) was implemented, in which representations of static baseline features were encoded into a latent representation and used to initialize the hidden state of the RNN. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, weighted F 1 -score, macro F 1 -score, and mean absolute error (MAE). Results The multimodal model consistently outperformed the unimodal model based on digital phenotypes alone, achieving higher accuracy (0.56 vs 0.45), weighted F 1 -score (0.51 vs 0.38), and macro F 1 -score (0.37 vs 0.24), along with lower MAE (0.68 vs 0.90). At the individual level, 72% (43/60) of participants showed improved prediction accuracy with the multimodal model. These improvements were statistically significant (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P t test, P Conclusions Integrating digital phenotypes with neurophysiological and psychological features enhances the prediction of short-term alcohol craving dynamics. This approach may enable more precise and timely personalized interventions for individuals at risk of relapse.

items.title: 'So… What Do You Do?': How Gender-(In)Congruence and Occupational Prestige Affect First Impressions.
items.abstract: People commonly ask potential romantic partners, "what do you do for a living?", yet little is known about how answers to this question affect first impressions. Building on research showing that first impressions can be linked to both the target's adherence to traditional social roles and/or their job's occupational status, the current research is the first to distinguish between the gender congruency and prestige of people's occupations to examine their effect on person perception, including romantic attraction. Participants ( N = 245) were randomly assigned to read a vignette describing a potential partner in a male- or female-dominated occupation of high or low prestige and then offer their impressions. Results showed that targets in female-dominated (versus male-dominated) occupations were seen as warmer but less agentic; targets in high- (versus low-) prestige jobs were judged as less warm but more competent and more agentic. In addition, women (versus men) were viewed as less agentic but not significantly different on warmth or competence. Both men and women preferred long-term partners in female-dominated fields. Future directions and implications (e.g., leveraging job characteristics on the dating market) are discussed.

items.title: Construct Overlap Between Two Widely Used Self-Report Measures of Dispositional Mindfulness: Evidence from Stress and Anxiety Control Outcomes.
items.abstract: Researchers commonly conceptualise dispositional mindfulness as a multidimensional construct comprising attentional awareness, present-moment focus, and acceptance. However, widely used measures differ considerably in the dimensions they assess, raising questions regarding the extent to which they demonstrate construct overlap and can be considered interchangeable. The present study evaluated the psychometric functioning, construct overlap, and associations of the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS) and the Freiburg Mindfulness Inventory (FMI) with stress and anxiety control outcomes. A community sample of 1,498 UK adults completed the MAAS, FMI, Perceived Stress Scale, and Anxiety Control Questionnaire. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), exploratory structural equation modelling (ESEM), Rasch analysis, and structural equation modelling (SEM) evaluated measurement properties and examined associations with stress and anxiety control outcomes. ESEM provided superior fit relative to CFA for multidimensional measures, while Rasch analyses indicated satisfactory measurement functioning across mindfulness measures. Contrary to expectations, despite satisfactory psychometric performance, the MAAS demonstrated near-zero correlations with the FMI total score and its Presence and Acceptance facets, indicating that these measures were essentially independent in this sample rather than showing substantial dimensional overlap. Structural models further revealed distinct patterns of association, with acceptance showing the strongest relationships with coping and emotion control, whereas mindfulness awareness displayed the strongest associations with threat control and stress control. Findings are consistent with multidimensional conceptualisations of mindfulness and demonstrate negligible convergence between the MAAS and FMI, indicating that researchers should not assume that these instruments are interchangeable. More broadly, the findings highlight the importance of empirically evaluating construct overlap when selecting scales intended to assess the same psychological construct.

items.title: Potential Impact of Breathing Practice on Brain and Mental Health in Rural Adolescents With Psychiatric Symptoms: Protocol for a Single-Arm Pilot Feasibility Trial.
items.abstract: Mental health conditions (MHC), particularly depression and anxiety, are the leading contributors to youth disability globally. In the United States, there has been a steep increase in diagnosed MHC cases over the last decade. Adolescents in rural areas are disproportionately affected by the combination of limited access to mental health professionals and stigma around seeking care. Current treatment options, mainly psychotherapy and psychopharmacology, have shown modest effects. Prior research suggests associations between slow-paced deep breathing and autonomic function, cerebral perfusion, and stress regulation, supporting further investigation of structured breathing as a potential adjunctive approach for MHC management. This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, implementation appropriateness, and participant satisfaction of a digitally supported, breathing-based intervention for adolescents with mild-to-moderate anxiety and depressive symptoms. The study will assess recruitment, retention, intervention engagement, usability, and the feasibility of collecting physiological and patient-reported outcome data to inform the design of a future efficacy trial. We aim to recruit approximately 40 adolescent patients receiving care through the Mayo Clinic Health System from rural communities in northwestern Wisconsin and southeastern Minnesota. Participants will complete a 4-month structured breathing program delivered entirely online, supported by a mobile app for guided instruction and practice tracking. All participants will attend 2 in-person visits (baseline and 4 mo) for functional near-infrared spectroscopy, as participants will already be on-site, the baseline and final study assessments will be completed at these same visits. A subsample (n=10) will additionally undergo magnetic resonance imaging at these visits. This study was funded in October 2025, and data collection began in February 2026, with completion anticipated in late 2026. As of July 2026, 14 of the 40 (35%) planned participants have been enrolled. Analysis will follow completion of data collection, with results expected to be reported in early 2027. Adolescents with anxiety and depression are a particularly vulnerable group, often undertreated due to limited access to mental health care. The proposed breathing intervention is designed as an accessible and scalable approach that warrants feasibility evaluation in rural youth populations.

items.title: Depression Management: Daily Practice in Dutch and Flemish Nursing Homes.
items.abstract: BackgroundDespite the numerous guidelines and training programs, depression remains highly prevalent among nursing home residents.ObjectiveExploring depression care strategies currently applied in nursing homes.MethodsA cross-sectional observational study.Results204 residents from 46 care units (21 Dutch and 25 Flemish) participated. Approximately one in five participating residents had an official depression diagnosis. Regular screening and monitoring procedures were reported in 17 (37%) care units and established in one in five participants. Depression management was organized in multidisciplinary teams. Non-pharmacological interventions, such as restructuring daily schedules and offering pleasant/meaningful activities, were frequently employed. Evaluation procedures were conducted in 26 (56%) of the care units and established in one in five participants. Clinical and statistical relevant regional differences in depression care strategies were found at the nursing homes' unit level.ConclusionDepression remains prevalent among nursing home residents. Areas for improving depression care included monitoring, screening, and evaluating procedures.

items.title: Classroom Integration of AI-Simulated Patients and Automated Feedback in Doctoral Psychotherapy Training: Longitudinal Mixed Methods Study.
items.abstract: Psychotherapy education increasingly emphasizes technology-assisted methods that extend deliberate practice beyond human supervision. AI has enabled automated skill assessment and patient simulations, yet few studies have examined how students experience such tools in real-world settings alongside established practice modalities. We aimed to evaluate students' experiences with AI-augmented deliberate practice embedded in an existing psychotherapy course sequence. Secondary aims included identifying implementation barriers, ethical and pedagogical considerations, and factors influencing students' acceptance of AI-assisted learning. Participants were 29 first-year clinical psychology doctoral students in a 2-quarter psychotherapy sequence at an American Psychological Association-accredited program. In the fall course, students completed weekly peer role-plays and could optionally submit transcripts to CARE for AI feedback to supplement peer feedback. In the winter course, students completed required weekly deliberate practice through Skillsetter video vignettes and could optionally practice with CARE's voice-based AI-simulated patients, receiving AI and instructor feedback afterward. Surveys with Likert-type and free-response items were voluntary in the fall and required in the winter; 9 and 25 students completed them, respectively. Analyses included descriptive statistics, matched-pairs testing, and thematic analysis. In the fall course (n=9), where privacy concerns and survey nonresponse limited data on AI feedback, students rated peer feedback higher than AI feedback on being constructive and helpful (median 3, IQR 3-3 vs median 2, IQR 2-2; P=.02) and recognizing areas to improve (mean 5.22, SD 0.83 vs mean 4.33, SD 0.87; P=.046), citing transcription errors and a narrow focus on empathy while valuing AI's alternative phrasing. In the winter course (n=25), Skillsetter was rated higher than CARE only for learning from mistakes (mean 4.52, SD 2.00 vs mean 3.20, SD 2.04; P=.03); immersion, spontaneous responding, communication beyond words, and alliance building did not differ significantly. Students valued CARE for interactive practice not possible with vignettes but reported undetected vocal pauses (20/25, 80%), insufficient realism (14/25, 56%), and limited emotional expression (13/25, 52%), and raised concerns about AI replacing peer support (22/25, 88%) and peer interaction (20/25, 80%). Asked about AI broadly, students expressed mixed views, citing concerns about supplanted relational dynamics, nonconsensual data use, and generative AI's environmental impacts. Embedding AI-augmented deliberate practice into an existing course sequence was feasible, but students' experiences favored established methods: they preferred human over AI feedback and described video vignettes as more realistic than voice-based AI interactions, while valuing AI-simulated patients for interactive practice other modalities could not provide. Implementation barriers included feedback quality, transcription accuracy, and instructor time required to supplement AI feedback. Perceptions of AI's instructional utility appeared contingent on students' trust in the technology, suggesting future deployments should weigh a sample's attitudes toward AI and its value relative to existing training resources.

items.title: An Online Cross-Sectional Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) Positive Valence Assessment Study With Patients With a Severe Mental Illness: Methodological Evaluation.
items.abstract: Abnormal reward processing is considered a core feature of severe mental illness (SMI). Deficits in this domain can have severe implications for daily functioning. The Online Positive Valence Study aimed to assess reward processing in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia using the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) Positive Valence Systems (PVS) framework in an online task-based study. Recruitment and study adherence fell short of expectations. This paper critically evaluates the methodology used and shares the lessons learned from conducting an online task-based study of reward processing in a sample of patients with SMI. Using a cross-sectional design, the Online Positive Valence Study measured reward processing using 3 reward tasks, the monetary incentive delay task (MID), effort expenditure of rewards task (EEfRT), and a social and coin version of the Bandit task. Participants were eligible if they were 18 years or older. They were recruited mainly via email from 2 completed prospective cohorts. From 2023, the initial recruitment goal was no longer followed. Recruitment strategies and task performance are evaluated. The sample consisted of 319 participants: 186 patients (58.3%), 81 first-degree relatives (25.4%), and 52 controls (16.3%). Multinomial logistic regression analyses revealed participants who were additionally called were more than 4 times more likely to respond "no" (odds ratio [OR] 4.57, 95% CI 3.12 to 6.70, P<.001) and more than twice as likely to respond "yes" (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.93 to 3.92, P<.001) versus no response compared with those who received only emails. Personal salutations in invitation mails reduced the likelihood of participation compared to nonpersonal salutations (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.47, P<.001). Analyses of covariance (ANCOVAs) and linear mixed effects models (LLMs) revealed task performance was comparable between in-lab and online groups. Online participants showed longer reaction times on the MID task (β=20.43, SE=2.55, t309.10=8.02, P<.001) and lower win-stay rates on both Bandits (Bandit Coin: β=-0.55, 95% CI -0.68 to -0.42, SE=0.06, t306.0=-8.73, P<.001, η² P=.14; Bandit Social: β=-0.65, 95% CI -0.80 to -0.49, SE=0.08, t307.2=-8.54, P<.001, η² P=.14). For the first time, we performed a remote online task-based assessment of the PVS domain in patients with SMI, and we learned important lessons along the way. Future studies should carefully consider recruiting from existing cohorts; hire full-time dedicated personnel; and use personal approaches to recruitment, like phone calls, adjusting recruitment to the target population(s), and making participation technically as simple as possible. Attrition may be reduced by shortening the duration of participation and/or adding gamification. This study offers guidance for future research in online cognitive assessment in patients with SMI.

items.title: Evaluating Wearable Electrodermal Activity as a Candidate Digital Biomarker of Occupational Well-Being: Longitudinal Real-World Study.
items.abstract: Wearable physiological sensing and mobile self-report methods offer new opportunities for monitoring occupational well-being in real-world settings. However, interpreting continuous physiological signals in relation to psychological states such as job burnout and work engagement remains challenging, particularly when using deployable systems that rely on proprietary signal processing. This study examined a proprietary electrodermal activity (EDA)-derived arousal index as a candidate digital biomarker for research on occupational well-being. We examined associations between job burnout, work engagement, and sympathetic activation indexed by a device-derived EDA metric, and assessed whether combining physiological data with mobile-based ecological momentary assessment (mEMA) of valence provides complementary information. A total of 75 knowledge workers participated, with sufficient paired physiological and mEMA data obtained from 57 participants in wave 1 and 51 in wave 2 (total observations=108). Participants were monitored continuously over 14 consecutive days at 2 time points 6 months apart. Autonomic arousal was operationalized using the device-derived double normalized electrodermal activity (DNE) index obtained from wearable EDA recordings. Valence was assessed using mEMA. Associations between physiological activation, valence, and occupational well-being outcomes were analyzed using generalized least squares models with a compound-symmetry covariance structure to account for repeated observations within participants. The wearable-derived DNE index showed a clear diurnal pattern, with higher values during daytime and lower values during nighttime. Greater within-nighttime DNE variability was associated with higher burnout (estimate=0.02, 95% CI 0.01-0.03; P<.001) and lower engagement (estimate=-0.03, 95% CI -0.05 to -0.01; P=.009). The daily DNE × valence interaction was also associated with engagement (estimate=-0.35, 95% CI -0.69 to -0.00; P=.047). Removing all DNE and valence variables significantly worsened model fit for both burnout (χ²₁₀=28.5; P=.002) and engagement (χ²₁₀=23.7; P=.009), supporting their combined explanatory value. Model-based profiles further showed that negative valence was associated with higher predicted burnout and lower predicted engagement than positive valence across both high- and low-arousal scenarios, although prediction intervals were wide and partially overlapping. Model comparisons showed that including physiological and mEMA-based variables improved explanatory power. These findings provide practical evidence that continuous wearable EDA monitoring can be combined with mEMA in naturalistic occupational settings. Associations between the proprietary DNE index, valence, burnout, and work engagement provide preliminary convergent evidence supporting further evaluation of DNE as a candidate digital biomarker in occupational well-being research. Interpretation remains constrained by the proprietary signal-processing pipeline, and this study does not establish construct-specific validity, prospective predictive performance, screening or diagnostic validity, sensitivity to change, or individual-level monitoring usage.

items.title: Suppressing autobiographical memories in adolescents: evidence from a think/no-think task.
items.abstract: Retrieval stopping, the intentional suppression of unwanted memories, plays a critical role in emotion regulation and cognitive control, yet little is known about its function in adolescence. Using an autobiographical Think/No-Think (TNT) paradigm, we investigated whether adolescents could control the retrieval of personal memories. 49 adolescent participants aged 13.2-17.8 years generated positive and negative autobiographical memories for retrieval or suppression in a TNT task. Participants rated vividness before and after suppression training, and researchers assessed memory recall after the training. Adolescents showed suppression-induced forgetting, recalling suppressed memories less accurately than negative baseline memories. Vividness ratings declined for suppressed memories, but not significantly more than unsuppressed negative memories, providing no clear evidence of a suppression-specific vividness reduction. Overall, the results provide evidence that adolescents can intentionally suppress autobiographical memories, extending to adolescence findings previously established in adults. The flexibility of the autobiographical TNT task paradigm provides a useful experimental framework for investigating goal-directed control over unwanted autobiographical memories and its development across adolescence. Future research should examine how retrieval stopping operates across development and how individual differences in cognitive control and emotional functioning influence its effectiveness.

items.title: "It pushes me, but it also drains me": A qualitative study of perfectionism and well-being among doctoral students in India.
items.abstract: Although perfectionism has been linked to academic achievement and psychological functioning, less is known about how doctoral students experience, interpret, and negotiate perfectionism in their academic lives, particularly within Indian higher education. This qualitative exploratory study examined how doctoral students in India experience perfectionism. The study was conducted between October 2024 and March 2026 following institutional ethics approval (Ref: IEC2: 177/2025). Thirteen doctoral students were recruited purposively after screening for sociodemographic variation and scores on the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Five themes were identified: Making sense of perfectionism, Expressions of perfectionistic tendencies, Influences on perfectionism, The double-edged experience, and Managing perfectionism. Findings suggest that perfectionism was experienced as both rewarding and exhausting, dynamically shaped by personal standards, academic cultures, supervisory relationships, familial expectations, and broader socio-cultural ideals of achievement. By situating perfectionism within the Indian doctoral context, this study contributes to the literature on mental health and well-being in higher education. Findings may inform doctoral supervision, institutional support systems, and interventions aimed at addressing maladaptive perfectionism while supporting students' well-being.

items.title: Use of psychotropic medication among adolescents with borderline personality disorder: a 6-year descriptive follow-up study.
items.abstract: Psychotropic medications are widely used in the treatment of borderline personality disorder (BPD), despite limited supporting evidence. Characterizing the use of psychotropic medications in adolescents with BPD is a prerequisite for understanding the underlying factors that contribute to prescribing patterns, as well as for critically evaluating the clinical indications for such treatments. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to longitudinally assess psychotropic medication use in a sample of adolescents with BPD or BPD features over a six-year period. Medication data were obtained from 110 adolescents with BPD or BPD features from medical records at baseline and at follow-ups after one, two, and six years. Descriptive analyses were conducted to characterize prescription patterns over time. Over the six-year follow-up period, the proportion of participants prescribed psychotropic medication remained high, increasing from 47% at baseline to 77% at the six-year follow-up, and polypharmacy was prevalent. Sertraline and quetiapine were most frequently prescribed, with quetiapine often used as pro re nata (PRN) medication. Our results indicate that treatment with psychotropic medication for BPD is initiated during adolescence and sustained over time, with high prescription rates and polypharmacy. High levels of psychiatric comorbidity and variable courses of BPD may, among other factors, influence the observed prescribing patterns. Considering the limited evidence supporting their effectiveness, and the potential adverse effects, our findings emphasize the need for research into the factors driving the excessive use of psychotropic medications in BPD.

items.title: Dual-task interference in the drop jump: Frequentist, Bayesian, and waveform analysis of vertical ground reaction force.
items.abstract: To ensure standardization, reliability, and maximal performance, physical performance tests are usually performed with little to no cognitive load. However, during training and competition, athletes usually perform physical actions while under the demands of a concurrent cognitive task (CT). This study examined the effect of a concurrent CT on the force-time metrics of the drop jump (DJ) and their reliability under single-task (DJ without a CT) and dual-task conditions (DJ with a CT based on simple arithmetic calculations). Thirty-five healthy young participants performed single-task and dual-task DJ trials in a randomized order. Nineteen force-time metrics covering the braking, propulsion, and landing phases of the DJ were compared between conditions using paired t-tests with Holm adjustment and Hedges' gz, Bayesian paired t-tests, and statistical parametric mapping (SPM) of vertical ground reaction force (VGRF) waveforms. For three-trial mean scores, 17 of the 19 metrics had within-session intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.812-0.930 across both conditions. Under the dual-task condition, jump height (p < 0.001, gz=1.40, Bayes factor BF10 = 1.76×107) and reactive strength index (p < 0.001, gz=1.04, BF10 = 45,943) were lower, while ground contact time was longer (p = 0.025, gz=-0.57, BF10 = 20.57). SPM showed that VGRF was significantly lower under the dual-task condition during 29.2-34.3% (within braking) and 52.0-79.1% (within propulsion) of ground contact. In the landing phase, VGRF was significantly lower under the dual-task condition during 1.3-6.3% (initial force rise) and significantly higher during 15.5-19.6% (attenuation of the impact force). The spring-like correlation (p = 0.462, gz=0.20, BF01 = 2.79) and the vertical time to stabilization (p = 0.462, gz=0.15, BF01 = 3.74) showed no significant difference between conditions, with weak and moderate evidence for the absence of an effect. These findings suggest that a concurrent CT reduces force production within both the braking and propulsion phases of the DJ and alters the VGRF waveform during the subsequent landing phase in healthy young participants.

items.title: Poor sleep quality and anxiety in patients with diabetes mellitus and its association with glycemic control: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Sleep is crucial for maintaining physical and mental health, and poor sleep quality is associated with an increased risk of metabolic, cognitive, and cardiovascular diseases. This study aimed to assess sleep quality and factors associated with poor sleep quality, such as mental disorders, especially anxiety, in adult patients with type 2 diabetes in Morocco. A cross-sectional study was conducted on patients with type 2 diabetes, using random selection, aged 39-85, in the clinical neurophysiology and internal medicine department of the Mohammed V Military Instruction Hospital, between 30/09/2024 and 30/12/2024. The questionnaire comprised demographic data, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7). Descriptive tests, independent two-sample t-tests, chi-square tests, and logistic regressions were performed using Jamovi version 2.6.2. Out of the 120 participants, the mean age of our patients was 65.4 ± 9.32 years, of whom 66.67% were women. The mean PSQI score was 9.18 ± 3.73, and the mean GAD-7 score was 8.0 ± 6.11. Poor sleep quality was reported in 84.2% of participants, while a binary logistic regression analysis revealed that poor sleep quality was not significantly associated with high HbA1c, but rather was highly significant with age and GAD-7. The study reveals that poor sleep quality is common among type 2 diabetic patients in Morocco, and is strongly associated with generalized anxiety disorders. These findings underscore the crucial role of psychological factors in diabetes management. They highlight the need for a comprehensive and integrated approach that takes into account not only biomedical aspects but also the psychological and behavioral dimensions of patients.

items.title: Trajectories of random walks on Markov sources reveal the structure of complex sequences.
items.abstract: We highlight a hierarchical property that is found in many sequences, the property of subunit structure, in which sequence symbols are joined together in tightly knit groups to create new subunits at higher levels of organization. Many sequences have strong connections both between the subunits and within the subunits. We propose an information-theoretic method that reveals hierarchical subunit structure in sequences. We use the probability flow of random walks on the Markov source encompassing transitions from subunit to subunit as a proxy for information flow in the sequence. We decompose the sequence into subunits by compressing the description of the information flow within the Markov source that generates the sequence. We illustrate the method by partitioning several real-world sequences whose subunit structure is already known and find that the method detects this known structure with high sensitivity and reliability. We show the relative complexity of different types of sequences in terms of bits per transition step. Finally, we show relative information flow between levels of the sequence within a revealed hierarchy.

items.title: EMPOWER-cancer-grief: An open trial with bereaved cancer caregivers.
items.abstract: Informal cancer caregivers often experience significant psychological distress and risk for Prolonged Grief (PG), yet interventions addressing their bereavement needs remain limited. In Cyprus, no culturally adapted grief‑focused intervention currently exists in Greek. We adapted the EMPOWER-Cancer-Grief intervention to the Cypriot sociocultural setting and present a single-arm, pre-post open feasibility trial implemented with 10 bereaved cancer caregivers who were at risk for PG. The intervention includes cognitive-behavioral, psychoeducation, acceptance-based, and meaning-centred techniques, delivered through weekly individual face-to-face sessions over six weeks. PG, depression, anxiety, resilience, post-traumatic growth, and psychological flexibility, were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, one-and three-month follow-ups. Open-ended questions explored suggestions for improvement. The intervention showed high retention rates (100%) and consistent improvement across all outcomes [PG‑13R: F(3, 27) = 32.94, p < .001; TRIG:F(3, 27) = 25.71, p < .001], with participants recommending extending its duration and incorporating group sessions. These preliminary findings suggest that EMPOWER-Cancer-Grief is a promising culturally adapted intervention for bereaved cancer caregivers.

items.title: Beyond Gender Identity: Clinicians' Perspectives on Comorbidity, Traumatic Events, and Diagnostic Complexity in Children and Adolescents with Gender Dysphoria.
items.abstract: This qualitative study maps the features of care for children and adolescents with gender dysphoria (GD) from the perspective of Czech clinicians. Given the high identity plasticity in adolescence and scarce data on minor populations, it explores expert conceptualisations of anamnestic data, developmental contexts, and social influences to define needs for informed clinical decision-making. Data were collected via interviews (n = 26) and focus groups (n = 2) with 35 clinicians (psychologists, sexologists, specialist physicians) reflecting on care for 75 clients, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings reveal tension between depathologisation ideals and high clinical complexity marked by comorbidities, unresolved trauma, or attachment disorders. Diagnostic overshadowing indicates that gender fixation may displace deeper etiopathogenetic factors. Furthermore, digital socialization fosters "scripted case histories," while assigned female at birth (AFAB) populations exhibit "somatic panic" as a defence against puberty. The study calls for clinical caution and redefines psychotherapy as an integral component of affirmative care rather than a gatekeeping tool. Serving as a secure base for identity exploration, the therapeutic relationship respects developmental plasticity and utilizes a psychological moratorium to prevent hasty medicalization and the risk of detransition.

items.title: Small events, big impact: Can rural sports event IP generate county-level tourism dividends? Evidence from "Village BA" in Taijiang County, China.
items.abstract: Small-scale rural sports events are increasingly used as tools for regional regeneration, yet counterfactual evidence on whether they generate sustained tourism benefits at the county level remains limited. This study examines the rapid rise of "Village BA" in Taijing County, Guizhou, China, as a quasi-experimental setting. Using county-level panel data from 2015 to 2024, we estimate tourism responses associated with the post-2022 Village BA-centered expansion by combining the synthetic control method, synthetic difference-in-differences, and a matching-weighted two-way fixed-effects model. Across the baseline specifications, the estimated effects are positive for both outcomes, although their inferential profiles differ across estimators and robustness settings. First, the estimated effects in 2023-2024 are generally larger than those in the 2022 breakout stage, indicating a sustained post-breakout tourism response. Second, tourist-visitor estimates are comparatively more directionally stable across estimators and sensitivity specifications, whereas baseline tourism-revenue effects become more pronounced and more precisely estimated during the later institutional-expansion stage, a pattern broadly consistent with a relative "flows first, returns later" interpretation. SCM placebo rankings do not reach conventional significance levels, while SDID and matching-weighted TWFE provide alternative assessments of statistical precision. Sensitivity analyses further show that tourism-revenue estimates are more sensitive to estimator choice and the treatment of the COVID-affected pre-treatment years. These findings provide counterfactual evidence of county-level tourism gains associated with the Village BA-centered expansion, while the underlying mechanisms remain theory-grounded rather than directly identified.

items.title: HeteroGrad-DT: Gradient Flow Transformer for heterogeneous multi-task offline reinforcement learning.
items.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning enables policy learning from static datasets without online exploration, making it particularly suitable for robotic control under safety and data constraints. Decision Transformer recasts offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling. Extending it to heterogeneous multi-task settings is challenging because task representations and dynamics differ, while joint training can suffer from destructive gradient interference. To address these challenges, we present HeteroGrad-DT, an integrated framework that employs task-specific tokenizers and decoupled prediction heads to retain task-native input and output dimensionality at the model interfaces while learning a shared sequence backbone. It further introduces a Gradient Flow Transformer that periodically coordinates cross-task updates using fixed-dimensional task statistics, compact summaries of shared-backbone gradients accumulated within the current synchronization interval, and an alignment-based coordination objective, rather than relying only on stepwise projection or static regularization. Experiments on the DeepMind Control Suite with up to 30 tasks show that HeteroGrad-DT improves average normalized return over representative multi-task methods. In the 30-task setting, it achieves a 32.3% relative improvement over standard training with a shared backbone and an 8.6% gain over a representative gradient-conflict mitigation baseline using the same task-aware interfaces. Ablation, mechanism, and sensitivity analyses further support complementary benefits from task-aware interfaces and gradient coordination in the evaluated settings.

items.title: Protocol for measuring the effects of cortical scotoma on visual space perception.
items.abstract: We aim to investigate the spatial experience of patients with chronic scotomas caused by lesion to early visual cortex, including primary visual cortex (V1) and adjacent extrastriate visual areas. These experiments are conducted as part of an adversarial collaboration testing contrasting theories of consciousness: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and two Predictive Processing accounts, Active Inference (AI) and Neurorepresentationalism (NREP). The central question is whether lesions to early visual cortex alter the experienced extent of visual space itself, or instead primarily disrupt stimulus content within an otherwise preserved visual space. To address this, we use paradigms in which patients estimate distances or spatial extents that either span a scotomatous region or fall entirely within intact visual field locations. Psychometric functions relating perceived and physical extent are modeled to estimate shifts in the point of subjective equality (PSE). According to IIT, lesions to early visual cortex, including V1 and occipital extrastriate cortex, should lead to systematic reductions in perceived spatial extent across the scotoma (negative PSE shifts), reflecting a contraction of experienced space. In contrast, Predictive Processing accounts posit that higher-level predictive mechanisms preserve spatial structure despite loss of early input, predicting little or no systematic contraction (with NREP allowing limited context-dependent effects). By quantifying distortions in perceived spatial extent, this protocol aims to distinguish between these competing theoretical predictions.

items.title: Sexual behavioural risk, partnership contexts, and correlates of condomless sexual intercourse among men newly diagnosed with HIV in Shanghai, China.
items.abstract: Given low HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and treatment as prevention uptake, understanding patterns of condomless sexual intercourse is critical for developing HIV prevention strategies in China, where HIV disproportionately affects men through sexual transmission. We quantified condom use and identified correlates of condomless sexual intercourse among men in Shanghai, China. We recruited 151 cisgender men ≥ 18 years within 60 days of their HIV diagnosis from Shanghai's sole HIV treatment center (05/2021-03/2022). Participants were surveyed about their sexual behavioural risks within six months before survey completion. Condom use was categorized into mutually exclusive groups: low-risk (always used condoms), moderate-risk (condomless with one primary partner only), or high-risk (condomless with ≥1 non-primary partner or >1 primary partner). We used sequential Firth logistic regression to identify correlates of condomless sexual intercourse. Of 151 participants, 4.6% ever used HIV PrEP; at survey completion, 39.7% initiated antiretroviral therapy (ART) and 1.3% achieved viral suppression. Of 129 participants who engaged in sexual intercourse within six months before survey completion, 69.5% only had sex with men and 55.6% reported concurrent sex partners. One-fifth (21.7%) always used condoms (range: male partners: 11.6%-25.9%; female partners: 0%-50%). Among the 129 participants, older age (aOR per 5-year increase = 1.68;95%CI:1.20,2.51;p = 0.0018), lifetime sexually transmitted infections (aOR=3.17;95%CI:1.08-10.02;p = 0.0357), and multiple sex partners (2-3 partners: aOR=10.3;95%CI:3.45-37.48;p < 0.0001; ≥ 4 partners: aOR=17.17;95%CI:5.08-71.94;p < 0.0001) were associated with increased odds of high-risk intercourse (compared with low-/moderate-risk). In contrast, restricting to participants reporting low-/moderate-risk intercourse, ≥ 4 partners (aOR=0.10;95%CI:0.01-0.48;p = 0.0112) reduced the odds of moderate-risk intercourse. Overall, condomless sexual intercourse was common among men newly diagnosed with HIV in Shanghai, who often had multiple and concurrent partners. These findings, alongside suboptimal PrEP uptake, ART initiation, and viral suppression, underscore the need for comprehensive HIV prevention strategies integrating drivers of concurrent partnerships, publicly funded condom distribution, expanded PrEP use, and timely ART initiation among men with large sexual networks.

items.title: Navigating healthcare access and utilization in rural and Northern Ontario: Immigrants' experiences amid regionalization and dispersal policies.
items.abstract: Immigration to Canada has historically concentrated in major metropolitan areas, with over half of newcomers settling in Ontario's urban centres in 2019. However, recent government initiatives seek to address labour shortages and stimulate regional development by encouraging immigrant settlement in five rural Northern communities. As policies increasingly direct newcomers to these regions, it becomes essential to understand their unique settlement experiences and ensure that local services effectively meet their needs, especially healthcare needs. Yet, the limited research focusing on immigration in rural and northern contexts constrains the development of evidence‑based programs and supports. To explore the experiences of immigrants in accessing and utilizing healthcare services in rural and northern Ontario in the context of post-government regionalization and dispersal policies. This qualitative descriptive study was conducted in North Bay, Ontario. Purposive sampling was employed to recruit 20 immigrants who had settled in North Bay through the Rural Community Immigration Pilot, along with four key informants who work with immigrant populations, to participate in virtual interviews. Data were analyzed thematically. Ethical approval was obtained from the Nipissing University Research Ethics Board (File No. 103946) on April 17, 2025. Findings indicate that healthcare access for immigrants is not a single encounter, but an ongoing, complex care journey shaped by barriers before, during, and after contact with services. Four interrelated themes characterized this journey: Getting In, which reflected challenges initiating care due to information gaps, limited primary care attachment, transportation and distance barriers, language readiness, and fear of discrimination; Getting Through, which captured participants' struggles to obtain timely, understandable, respectful, and culturally safe care amid language barriers, long waits, fragmented referrals, and rushed encounters; Getting On, which described the post-visit consequences of unclear follow-up, diminished trust, and constrained self-management; and Getting the System Better, which highlighted participants' recommendations for improving immigrant healthcare access through earlier orientation, peer navigation, transportation and financial supports, targeted immigrants services, reliable language access, multilingual resources, cultural competence training, and stronger follow-up systems. This study underscores the need to move beyond narrow definitions of healthcare access and toward a more holistic, immigrant-responsive model of care. Improving access requires proactive, coordinated, and culturally safe health system supports that build trust, strengthen continuity, and ensure that immigrants are not only able to reach services but are also meaningfully supported throughout their care journey.

items.title: Sleep starts: Phenomenology and associations with sleep, psychological, and demographic characteristics.
items.abstract: Sleep starts (SS) are transient phenomena during sleep onset. Although traditionally characterized by sudden muscle jerks, they may also involve sensory, cognitive, emotional, and autonomic experiences. Despite their high prevalence, empirical data on phenomenology and associated characteristics remain limited. This online survey examined SS phenomenology and exploratory associations with demographic, sleep-related, and psychological variables in 194 adults. Participants with self-reported sleep-related movement disorders or relevant medical conditions were excluded. Individuals reporting abrupt awakenings ≥1/week and ≥1 additional symptom formed the SS group (SS frequency ≥1, n = 96); all others the comparison group (SS frequency <1, n = 98). Because SS were operationalized using self-reported symptoms, they could not be distinguished from related sleep-onset phenomena (e.g., exploding head syndrome, hypnagogic hallucinations). Standardized questionnaires (PSQI, ISI, ESS, MZS, HADS) assessed sleep quality, insomnia severity, daytime sleepiness, dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and anxiety/depression symptoms. Participants described diverse experiences including motor jerks, falling sensations, dream-like experiences, somatosensory symptoms, autonomic arousal, and emotional reactions, accompanied by alarm, anxiety, and confusion. Compared with controls, the SS group reported poorer sleep quality, greater insomnia severity, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety/depressive symptoms (all p < .05). Exploratory regression analyses indicated that poorer sleep quality, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety symptoms were associated with higher SS frequency, whereas depressive symptoms were not. The final model explained 26.9% of variance (R2 = .269, adjusted R2 = .245). More frequent SS were retrospectively reported during emotional stress, whereas sleep deprivation was perceived as less influential. Although many described SS as manageable, a substantial subgroup reported distress and sleep disruption. This suggests that SS represent heterogeneous sleep-onset experiences associated with subjective sleep disturbance and cognitive-emotional arousal. Although causality cannot be inferred from cross-sectional self-report data, the results highlight potentially relevant links between SS and sleep-related cognitive-emotional processes.

items.title: ID-SCAN: a functional MRI protocol for neurophenomenological phenotyping of dissociative identity disorder without trauma provocation.
items.abstract: Background: Dissociative identity disorder (DID) is a trauma-related dissociative disorder in which two or more identity-agents recur within one person, each experiencing and evaluating itself and its surroundings. Most existing neuroimaging paradigms rely on symptom provocation using trauma-related autobiographical material. Identity-agent effects that are independent of symptom provocation need to be disentangled from emotional responses to trauma-related material and from the co-consciousness of other identity-agents.Objective: To introduce ID-SCAN (Identity-agent State Characterisation and Analysis), a functional MRI protocol without trauma provocation for within-person neurophenomenological characterisation of identity-agent expression and switching, and to test its feasibility in a co-conscious case.Method: A woman with DID living with persistent co-consciousness between two identity-agents (Adu and Ado) completed two fMRI tasks: identity-cued evaluation of identical insect photographs the agents made sense of in opposite ways, and trait judgments about self, the other agent and a shared intimate other. Within-person analyses combined Bayesian general linear modelling, generalised psychophysiological interaction, representational similarity analysis and a pooled identity-cue switching analysis, with cross-task overlap providing a task-general baseline.Results: Adu and Ado made sense of the same insect photographs differently. Ado showed greater activation in striato-thalamic regions, whereas Adu showed greater activation in the amygdala and in the orbitofrontal and medial prefrontal cortex; the two also differed in task-evoked connectivity. Adu-as-self and Ado-as-self occupied separable positions within self-referential regions. Cue-locked activity differed by switch direction, with greater reconfiguration when switching to the less-foregrounded Adu. Cross-task overlap localised to posterior visual and dorsal parietal cortex.Conclusions: Two co-conscious identity-agents showed distinct, convergent neurophenomeno-logical signatures of expression and switching in this single case without trauma provocation. ID-SCAN suits single-case and groupwise, simulator-controlled designs and provides a candidate framework for future longitudinal and treatment-related research whose test-retest reliability and clinical sensitivity remain to be established.

items.title: Measurement invariance of the Clinician Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 between trauma-exposed non-Western refugee patients and Dutch patients seeking treatment for PTSD.
items.abstract: Background: The Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) is the gold standard to assess post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Although the CAPS-5 was developed and validated primarily in Western samples, it is often used to assess PTSD in non-Western refugees.Objective: This study investigated whether PTSD as assessed with the CAPS-5 has the same factor structure, item-factor relationships and symptom severity scores across trauma-exposed, treatment-seeking individuals with either a Dutch (i.e. Western) background or a non-Western refugee background.Methods: We evaluated four DSM-5 PTSD models and tested different levels of measurement invariance in non-Western refugee (nWr) patients (N = 710) and Dutch patients (N = 1162) using confirmatory factor analyses (CFA).Results: CFAs showed that the Hybrid model of PTSD fit the data best in the nWr group, the Dutch group, and in the combined sample, indicating that configural invariance was met. The model representing scalar invariance showed a worse fit compared to the model representing configural invariance, indicating that item-factor relationships and/or thresholds (representing the value above which an individual endorses the next symptom severity category) differed between the subsamples. Further exploration showed that this result could likely be attributed to nWr patients generally receiving higher symptom severity ratings on the CAPS-5 items than Dutch patients with similar underlying symptom severity levels.Conclusions: NWr patients showed a similar factor structure of DSM-5 PTSD symptoms as Dutch patients. Furthermore, the relative contribution of the majority of symptoms to its belonging symptom cluster was similar between nWr patients and Dutch patients, indicating that item-factor relationships were similar across groups. However, nWr patients generally received higher symptom severity ratings than Dutch patients.
