items.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
items.abstract: Most frameworks for teams of large language model (LLM) agents fix the team's shape inside the software: who talks to whom, how much is passed along, and what a human can do once a run has started. Human-team research has long asked those questions: where team phenomena live (in members or in their interaction), how team-level properties arise, and what separates what a team does from how a team is. I propose using that theory as the organizing lens for configuring, observing and intervening in LLM-agent teams, without assuming its findings transfer. I introduce teamknitt, a framework and open reference implementation in which a user configures a team of 1-16 AI agents for task completion, solution generation, achieving a goal or a research mission; selects one of fourteen deterministic routing topologies or a custom directed graph; chooses a sharing profile that limits what may travel along permitted routes; and binds sources, representations, work dependencies, handoffs and an expertise directory. The recorded process can be observed through non-system views (member reports and behavior) and system views (distributed problem-solving, differentiated transactive memory, interactive coordination, team dynamics). Interventions are explicit and human-led: reviewed reconfiguration between runs, planned disturbances, and private feedback, pause, resume or stop applied at dependency-wave boundaries, with "queued", "applied", "assembled", "understood" and "improved" kept as separate claims. Emergent states such as trust and shared understanding are declared unmeasured. This is an idea and system-description paper with falsifiable hypotheses on topology, information flow and intervention timing, including whether the fractal scaling of communication output between members, and between members on different models, relates to task and team performance. No comparative result is reported.

items.title: Kinematic Signatures of Stellar Flybys in Protoplanetary Discs
items.abstract: Recent high-resolution molecular line observations of protoplanetary discs have revealed large-scale non-Keplerian features in the gas kinematics of several systems, which can be interpreted as signatures of warps in the disc. Warps can arise from a range of physical mechanisms, and it remains unclear whether the observed kinematic residuals can be uniquely attributed to warping, or to different competing effects. Stellar flybys are one such mechanism capable of both warping a disc and directly perturbing its kinematics. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we study the evolution of protoplanetary discs perturbed by inclined and coplanar stellar flybys, focusing on timescales of several thousand years after periastron rather than the immediate aftermath of the encounter. We find that inclined stellar flybys initially induce warping and twisting in the disc, but that this geometric perturbation is damped on a timescale set by the disc viscosity. Despite this geometric damping, synthetic ALMA observations of the CO kinematics show that complex non-Keplerian spiral features persist in the velocity residuals long after the warped morphology has relaxed, including in coplanar encounters where no warp is ever induced. Fitting these residuals with a simple warped-disc model, the degree of warping in the disc is systematically overestimated. We therefore conclude that kinematic residuals alone are insufficient to establish that a disc is warped, as flybys induce kinematic complexity independently of warps. We further show that scattered light observations provide an independent diagnostic, showing spiral arms and lateral asymmetries.

items.title: Long-term average collision frequencies between two bodies undergoing Lidov-Kozai evolution
items.abstract: The existing {Ö}pik-type collision frequency framework that accounts for the projectile's Lidov-Kozai (LK) secular evolution holds the target's semimajor axis, eccentricity, and inclination fixed and prescribes uniform precession of its longitude of the ascending node and argument of periapsis. This treatment is not readily applicable when the target's eccentricity, inclination, or orbital precession rates undergo appreciable secular variations. Here, we extend the framework of Liang and Liu (2026, arXiv:2608.30972) to address one such case, in which both the projectile and target undergo LK evolution. Using a doubly averaged quadrupole model to describe the secular dynamics of both bodies, we include the target's orbital evolution when evaluating the collision contribution of each orbital intersection configuration. In the numerical example considered, the projectile survival curve predicted using the calculated collision frequency shows an overall decay trend close to that obtained from direct N-body simulations using REBOUND. In addition, we examine whether the long-term mean collision frequency depends on initial states while holding both bodies' semimajor axes, Kozai constants and closed Hamiltonian level curves fixed. Our theoretical analysis indicates that this frequency is independent of initial states when the parameters describing their relative state are jointly equidistributed at the start of successive projectile LK cycles. Numerical cases with different initial states support this conclusion.

items.title: ALMA detection of continuum emission from GQ Lup B
items.abstract: GQ Lup B is a massive (10-40 M$_{\text{Jup}}$) companion orbiting the young T-Tauri star GQ Lup A at a projected distance of $\sim$110 au (0.7''). It is outside the circumprimary disk in the submm continuum, but its ${\sim}\,63^\circ$ inclined orbit intersects the primary's gas disk twice per period. We report a 5.8$σ$ detection of continuum emission at the location of GQ Lup B, obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.89 mm (band 7). We associate this emission with a dusty disk around the companion, already detected by VLT/NACO and JWST/MIRI in the mid-Infrared. To date, this is the third disk observed at mm wavelengths around a companion spanning the brown dwarf and planetary mass regimes, following PDS 70 c, a gas giant embedded in the parent circumstellar disk, and SR 12 c, a planetary-mass companion at 1200 au from the primary. We retrieve a point source with peak intensity $54.5\pm9.4\,μ\rm Jy\, beam^{-1}$, co-spatial with GRAVITY astrometry. The emission is spatially unresolved, placing an upper limit on the source radius of 2.3 au (from a synthesized beam of $\sim\,29\times25$ mas). For comparison, this is smaller than 1/3 of the Hill's radius (3-5 au for GQ Lup B, depending on the assumed mass), the theoretical upper limit for circum-planetary disks. Assuming optically thin thermal emission from mm-size grains in a disk-like structure, we infer a mass of 0.0032 M$_\oplus$, while the optically thick limit yields an emission radius of 0.2 au. Assuming a gas to dust ratio of 100, our results indicate a very low disk mass to accretion rate ratio, of the order of $\sim10^4$ years, analogously to the highest accretors in the stellar mass regime. In the case of GQ Lup B, this can be explained by its periodic crossings of the circumprimary disk, which could deliver a substantial amount of gas to the companion's disk over a long timescale.

items.title: Retweeting patterns reveal partisan asymmetries in information sharing and signal state-level electoral outcomes in the 2020 US presidential election
items.abstract: As social media has become a primary source of political information, concerns are growing that online information consumption may intensify political polarization and reshape democratic processes. Yet how large-scale online information consumption organizes polarized political ecosystems and relates to offline voting remains unclear. Here we reconstruct partisan information ecosystems from more than 500 million tweets generated during the 2020 US presidential election, integrating information diffusion across media outlets, influencers, and social peers. Contrary to the conventional expectation that broader information exposure promotes moderation, we find that retweeting a wider range of political information is associated with stronger political polarization. We further show systematic asymmetries in political information ecosystems: the Republican ecosystem is highly concentrated and ideologically biased, whereas the Democratic ecosystem is more dispersed and primarily organized around relatively moderate left-leaning sources. Finally, we demonstrate that several shared retweeting signatures robustly map onto state-level electoral outcomes despite cross-state heterogeneity. Our findings reveal asymmetric political information ecosystems as a key organizing principle of online political communication and identify collective retweeting patterns as a scalable signal of real-world voting behaviours.

items.title: The role of administrative costs in policies to improve cooperation
items.abstract: We use an agent-based model for studying policies of an abstract government to increase the level of cooperation. In situations where defection is the rational choice, agents receive a bonus if they choose to cooperate. The government taxes agents' payoffs from a repeated prisoner's dilemma game to establish a budget that covers the payment of bonuses, but also the administrative costs involved. We consider costs to identify cooperators, and costs to mitigate the consequences of defective behavior. Governmental interventions are fallible, i.e. cooperators and defectors are correctly identified only with a certain accuracy. Hence, the critical bonus needed to let agents cooperate depends on the accuracy, but also on the current level of cooperation. We analyze the cost constraints for the government to pay the critical bonus and different policies to adjust the accuracy dependent on the level of cooperation. We find that perfect cooperation becomes impossible. Instead, high levels of cooperation can be achieved with optimal adjustment policies.

items.title: Hidden Distances: How Likert-Scale Spacing Shapes Algorithmic Voting Advice
items.abstract: Voting Advice Applications (VAAs) are algorithmic recommenders that match voters with political candidates on policy preferences. They are widely adopted across many multi-party democracies; in Denmark, 62\% of eligible voters used a VAA ahead of the 2022 general election, and 45\% of VAA users reported following its advice. VAAs typically ask voters and candidates to respond to policy statements on a Likert scale, from ``strongly disagree'' to ``strongly agree'', and recommend candidates whose responses are closest to the voter's. Computing these distances requires assigning numbers to response options, a design choice without an empirical basis, since it is unknown how people perceive the distances between options. Here we show that this seemingly technical choice substantially changes whom voters are matched with. We parameterize the distance between ``(dis)agree'' and ``strongly (dis)agree'' relative to the distance between ``neutral'' and ``(dis)agree'' as $α$, and quantify how it changes recommendations for a popular Danish VAA. We find that moving from equidistant options to doubling this distance can change $37.7\%$ of top candidate matches and $21.9\%$ of top party matches, although no answers change. Low $α$-values favor candidates with strong positions, with some parties receiving up to $ 19.6\%$ more recommendations, while high $α$-values favor moderates. Similarly, female candidates receive fewer recommendations at low $α$ and more at high $α$-values. Our findings demonstrate that undisclosed quantification choices in algorithmic recommenders can carry considerable electoral consequences, and they call for transparency and sensitivity analysis in VAA design. As Likert-based matching also underpins dating platforms and roommate allocation systems, these implications extend well beyond elections.

items.title: Modelling socio-economic effects of the pandemic in a metropolitan area
items.abstract: One of the most notorious measures taken by authorities in every country trying to prevent the uncontrollable spread of the Covid 19 pandemic was to impose severe measures to diminish the mobility of people. In recent publications we proposed a mathematical model to address the consequences of these measures and to predict the infections under different scenarios, for various different countries. In this paper we extend the model, called the BTH--SEIRS-model, to deal with the reduction of mobility in an urban area. The chosen region was the densely-populated metropolitan area around Helsinki, the capital of Finland. This choice obeyed to the fact that there are precise data related to mobility from a mobile telephone company, and that this region was completely isolated from the rest of the country for a short period during the pandemic. We also used public transport data from railways and the accommodation occupation rates in the area of interest. We show that the BTH--SEIRS model is capable of simulating the real infection data as well as the mobility-related economic activity, exhibiting the main trends present in the three indicators used for comparison. Our calculations allow us to highlight the difference of the behaviour of the pandemic in a totally different spatial scale, and to discover the hidden factors that govern the behaviour of people who are forced to commute every day from home to work.

items.title: Predictability of Collective Behavior in Networks of LLM Agents
items.abstract: As AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly interact at scale, anticipating their collective behavior becomes necessary. Unlike humans, individual LLM agents can be probed in {controlled scenarios}; however, the predictability of their collective outcomes hinges on what such measurements capture. We study information cascades on networks of LLM agents that decide whether to share a post given how many of their contacts have shared it. At the same fraction of sharing contacts, an agent's response depends on how many contacts it has and on the post. Responses that ignore the number of contacts mispredict the cascades, increasingly on heterogeneous networks, by an error we derive analytically and that network topology alone cannot reveal. Measured in context, the response predicts, through mean-field theory, the cascades of full LLM simulations, tipping points included. Anticipating the collective behavior of AI agents thus requires evaluating them in their local network context.

items.title: Detecting space objects with Earth-observation radar satellites
items.abstract: Millimetre-to-centimetre orbital debris poses a hazard to spacecraft, but its abundance remains difficult to measure. Spaceborne radars offer a substantial sensitivity advantage at close range: received echo power decreases with the fourth power of distance, so an otherwise identical object ten times closer produces a 10,000 times stronger echo. We investigate this opportunity using openly available Sentinel-1 radar voltages recorded on six calendar days. Catalogue-assisted processing identifies a manually validated sample of 76 objects at ranges of 41.7--492.9 km, including satellites, rocket bodies and debris fragments. A blind search recovers two selected debris transits without using their orbital predictions during detection. A short debris encounter also demonstrates how precise range and Doppler measurements can refine a catalogue orbit. Ground scatter increases the effective background and is the principal sensitivity limitation in Earth-looking observations. An ideal receiver-noise sensitivity comparison predicts detectable conducting-sphere diameters of approximately 3.4 mm for Sentinel-1 and 0.6 mm for EarthCARE at 10 km range, assuming coherent integration limited by beam transit time and a 10 ms cap. These results establish the feasibility of space-object detection using existing Earth-observation radars and motivate statistical debris surveys and targeted orbit refinement following collision warnings. Observations directed away from Earth and receive windows adapted to nearby objects could improve sensitivity to small debris.

items.title: Spatial effects of Kuramoto modeling on the power-grid frequencies
items.abstract: Spatial coupling and heterogeneity can generate complex power-grid frequency dynamics. We investigate the contributions of spatial structure, intrinsic nonlinear dynamics, and external driving using the Kuramoto model (KM), with and without uncorrelated noise, and compare its predictions with real-grid measurements. We analyse one month of 100 ms frequency measurements from 16 Hungarian transmission-grid sites and simulate the KM on a 387-node transmission network and two-dimensional lattices. The measured power spectra exhibit two scaling regimes, with exponents of approximately 1.63 and 2.23. One-second frequency increments decorrelate rapidly, while correlations of their local inverse variance decay slowly, initially as a power law, $τ^{-0.26(2)}$, up to 15 minutes. A superstatistical Gaussian mixture based on measured local variances captures much of the non-Gaussian increment distribution, but not the rare extreme events. We also estimate the non-stationary long-time frequency autocorrelation exponent. KM simulations on low-dimensional networks exhibit algebraically decaying autocorrelations and power spectra, consistent with the measurements and the Wiener-Khinchin relation in the steady state. On the heterogeneous transmission network, partial synchronization and frequency locking produce persistent spatial patterns and multi-peaked frequency distributions. However, neither deterministic KM dynamics nor independent Gaussian driving reproduces the measured spectra and increment statistics simultaneously. Moreover, empirical frequency fluctuations are largely shared across substations, whereas simulated fluctuations mainly reflect relative node motion. These findings suggest that spatially coupled nonlinear dynamics contribute to observed frequency fluctuations alongside external driving, including 15-minute power dispatches.

items.title: Ejecta fate and deposition in the Didymos-Dimorphos system after the DART impact
items.abstract: Kinetic impact is a promising technique for asteroid deflection in planetary defense. The NASA Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft collided with Dimorphos, the satellite of the binary asteroid (65803) Didymos, at 6.1449 km s^{-1} in 2022. Observations revealed changes in both the orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos and the heliocentric orbit of the Didymos-Dimorphos system. The ESA Hera spacecraft will arrive at the system at the end of 2026 to investigate the post-impact surfaces. Here, we present an analytical model, based on Maxwell's Z model, to predict ejecta behavior following the DART impact. The model provides the relationships among ejection velocity, ejection angle, and ejecta mass, allowing the momentum enhancement factor beta to be estimated for both Dimorphos and the Didymos-Dimorphos system. We show that the observed beta can be reproduced when 0.3-1% of the impact kinetic energy is converted into ejecta kinetic energy and the effective strength of the target is less than 100 Pa. The escaping mass is estimated to be 0.3-3.0% of the mass of Dimorphos. The globally averaged and minimum ejecta thicknesses on Dimorphos are estimated to be 2.0 m and 0.5 m, respectively, indicating that the entire surface was resurfaced by ejecta deposition, although boulders larger than 1 m were only partially buried. The model also predicts the momentum partition parameter kappa_p to be as low as 0.6, suggesting that the mass and the bulk density of Dimorphos may be revised upward. These predictions provide quantitative constraints for interpreting forthcoming Hera observations.

items.title: Competing Influence in LLM Populations: Budget Timing and Baseline Drift
items.abstract: When competing campaigns target a population of large language model (LLM) agents, observed opinion changes may reflect both campaign influence and changes that would occur without intervention. We study how the timing of campaign expenditure and the population's own evolution shape outcomes in a network of persona-conditioned LLM agents that exchange and revise opinions in natural language. A proponent and a challenger are tasked with generating opposing messages under equal delivery budgets, while a separate stance probe measures opinions without influencing the simulation. Across eight claims, we compare single-campaign and competitive conditions against matched no-campaign runs, and evaluate all nine combinations of early, sustained, and late spending on a reference topic. Baseline stance drift varies substantially across claims and, on some, accounts for a sizeable fraction of apparent campaign effects. After accounting for this drift, the direction of observed campaign-associated changes aligns more closely with the claim's epistemic standing than with the campaigner's assigned role. Uninfluenced populations also consistently lose stance diversity, demonstrating that directional opinion change and convergence are distinct phenomena. In networks with two opinion-segregated communities, campaigns primarily reduce differences between communities rather than diversity within them. LLM campaign agents do not always argue for their assigned positions, particularly when these conflict with established evidence. Finally, campaign outcomes depend on the opponent's expenditure schedule: unlike a matched numerical bounded-confidence population receiving interventions at the same times and locations, the LLM population exhibits a payoff structure with no pure-strategy equilibrium.

items.title: Inhabiting a wounded world: a qualitative phenomenology of ecological anxiety
items.abstract: Introduction Ecological anxiety is defined as distress caused by awareness of the ongoing climate crisis. This qualitative phenomenological study aimed to describe how lived experience is altered in ecological anxiety. Methods We conducted 58 interviews with 30 participants who identified themselves as experiencing ecological anxiety. Interviews combined lifeworld analysis with a micro-phenomenological approach to explore specific experiential episodes. Transcripts were analyzed using constructivist grounded theory, with participant validation and intercoder verification. Results Participants reported fatigue, rumination, bodily symptoms, and sleep difficulties, alongside feelings of guilt, shame, and anger and heightened empathy toward humans and non-human entities. We identified two forms of ecological anxiety: informational, involving distress associated with information about the climate crisis, and experiential, arising from witnessing its consequences. A central phenomenological characteristic was a marked attitude toward information, including a perceived obligation to remain informed despite the associated distress. Participants also described altered temporality, feeling alienated from the future and rushed in the present. These temporal disturbances were intertwined with a pervasive loss of agency. Discussion Our findings suggest that ecological anxiety extends beyond discrete episodes of worry to broader alterations in participants’ lifeworlds, which we conceptualized as a prereflective sense of inhabiting a wounded world. Within this predominantly European, highly educated sample, ecological anxiety also provided a framework for interpreting wider personal and societal concerns. These findings highlight the importance of considering informational, temporal, and social dimensions when understanding and addressing ecological anxiety.

items.title: Subliminal beauty engages the brain’s valuation circuits
items.abstract: Abstract Neuroeconomic models propose that the anterior ventral striatum (aVS) and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) are key regions for computing subjective value (SV) signals that guide choice. However, the role of conscious awareness in this process remains debated. Here we examined whether SV can be automatically computed in these regions without conscious awareness. In an fMRI experiment, participants viewed faces that varied in attractiveness under three conditions: (i) suppressed from awareness via continuous flash suppression (CFS), (ii) clearly visible without suppression, or (iii) absent (background only) with CFS. Participants reported trial-wise facial identity (objective) and visibility (subjective) measures of facial awareness. In a post-fMRI session, they rated the attractiveness of each face as a measure of SV. When faces were seen, task performance (d’) exceeded chance and responses were faster than in absent trials. When faces were unseen, performance was at chance but responses were slower than absent trials. Neurally, seen and unseen faces elicited greater neural signal than absent trials and showed similar neural patterns in the fusiform face area (FFA). Critically, neural signal in vmPFC correlated with SV for both seen and unseen faces, with similar neural patterns. In aVS, SV-related signal was only observed for unseen faces. Furthermore, mean face-related signal in FFA correlated with SV-related signals in aVS and vmPFC for unseen faces. These findings demonstrate that SV can be automatically computed in aVS and vmPFC without conscious awareness, suggesting a neural pathway by which subliminal information can influence value-based choice.

items.title: THE MISERABLE EMPATH. ABOUT THE DARK SIDE OF EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: This paper makes a short incursion into emotional intelligence and its potential implications with regard to mental health issues and other negative effects. It was initially assumed that emotional intelligence would have a good impact on health, overall wellbeing, interpersonal relations and would be a predictor of success at the workplace. However, more recent studies have also explored the darker sides of emotional intelligence and have shown that it might have downsides for the individual as well. Aspects such as increased sensitivity, heightened affective states and overemphasis on emotions can represent drawbacks for emotionally intelligent people, making them more vulnerable, hindering their judgment, or impairing their social and professional performance. Empathy is one of the core dimensions of emotional intelligence and we can argue that it is the most likely to have destructive influence, to be emotionally draining and overwhelming for the person who exhibits an empathetic mindset and behavior. The present paper includes a small experiment that investigates the relationship between empathy and sadness, or depressive tendencies. The results indicate that individuals who display a predisposition to depression or report a history of depression score higher in several components of emotional intelligence, particularly in empathy. Differences between men and women are also taken into consideration and prove to be relevant in the analysis.

items.title: Perceptual versus memory-guided affordances: training-related adaptations in a spatial computer game
items.abstract: Traditional sequence learning research relies on discrete button-press paradigms where pauses segment responses. We developed a continuous game-based adaptation of the Serial Reaction Time task and tracked neural changes in 25 participants using fMRI before and after 1–3 weeks of training. Participants learned to control an avatar’s position and follow fixed and random sequences in the game. Behaviourally, fixed sequences showed robust learning with shorter response times and increased number of perfect playthroughs between Scan1 and Scan2. Random sequence performance unexpectedly declined, with fewer perfect playthroughs, consistent with negative transfer from consolidated sequence representations. For fixed sequences at Scan2 relative to Scan1, we identified the expected cerebellar and occipital decreases alongside unexpected increases in bilateral superior temporal regions. Random sequences showed increased insular activity, consistent with conflict monitoring when consolidated predictions fail. The temporal recruitment suggests continuous sequences consolidated through integrative mechanisms, potentially grammatical encoding, verbal mediation, or spatiotemporal binding, not typically reported in discrete tasks. Critically, training produced no premotor or superior parietal decrease within the fixed sequence, the automatisation signature discrete paradigms report. Our results suggest that discrete sequence learning principles may not fully generalise to continuous environments and highlight the need for paradigms that capture the spatiotemporal demands of real-world skill acquisition.

items.title: Composting mathematics: cascading processes of composition and decomposition in an era of climate crisis
items.abstract: Abstract This autoethnographic assemblage traces composting as a site of mathematical and socio-ecological sensemaking. I proceed from the conviction that understanding mathematics as practice is inseparable from the project of living. If I want to understand whether and when mathematics is formatting separability or enabling multispecies flourishing, I must first examine my own mathematical practices. Three questions guide this project: Where does emergent mathematical sensemaking support a commitment to living well—in a body, with a community, on the planet? When do rigorous commitments to precision and abstraction fall short of or subsume other ways of knowing? What role does mathematics play in socio-ecological sensemaking at scale? Sustainable futures grow from our habits of attention, action, and relation. The socio-ecological turn entails a reexamination of the ways of knowing and doing which structure mathematics and our relationships with the living world. Enactivism provides an overarching framework for understanding how patterns of action format ways of knowing. My central contribution is a sequence of explorations in and through composting. Drawing on ethnomathematics, metabolic literacies, and radical artifactualism, I position the compost box as a tool which instantiates a cascading process of coming to know. Finally, I explore an abstraction of these enacted practices through an agent-based model built to simulate socio-ecological relationships scaled across place and time. I call for a mathematics education rooted in sustained participation in practices that matter. This text is part of the article collection entitled “Mathematics Education for Sustainable Futures” (available at https://link.springer.com/collections/acebaagbha ).

items.title: The microstructure-weighted human connectome: network properties and structure-function correlations across spatial scales
items.abstract: Abstract Conventional connectome edge weights, such as number of streamlines (NOS) or diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics, lack specificity to microstructural details which may hold relevance for macroscale brain organisation. Since biophysical diffusion modelling offers greater specificity to microstructure, we investigated whether parameters from the Standard Model of white matter diffusion provide informative alternatives for connectome weights – namely the intra-axonal signal fraction (f) and perpendicular extra-axonal diffusivity (De⟂). Using diffusion MRI data from healthy adults, we constructed structural networks at four parcellation scales, weighted by f, De⟂, NOS, fractional anisotropy (FA) and radial diffusivity (RD). While all weights reproduced expected small-world properties and hub structure, only De⟂ and normalised NOS captured non-random properties of local organisation at all spatial scales. We then correlated each weighted connectome with resting-state fMRI functional connectivity and intracranial measurements of conduction velocity. At both the whole-brain and regional level, NOS gave strong coupling with fMRI functional connectivity. Connectomes weighted by De⟂, FA and RD gave weak but significant coupling with fMRI functional connectivity and conduction velocity. Notably, De⟂ and RD gave highest consistency in regional structure-function coupling across spatial scales. Thus, connectome weights derived from De⟂ capture meaningful aspects of brain network organisation with functional relevance.

items.title: Sexual trauma relates to central sensitization severity in fibromyalgia: A community-based cohort study of women
items.abstract: Background Central sensitization (CS) is a core feature of fibromyalgia, but the relative contribution of pain distribution, sleep disturbance, cognitive symptoms, and trauma-related factors to its severity remains unclear. Objective To identify independent determinants of CS severity in fibromyalgia, focusing on sexual abuse as a primary exposure, and to explore indirect pathways using mediation analyses. Methods In this cross-sectional community-based study, 2099 women with fibromyalgia completed validated measures of central sensitization (CSI), pain distribution, sleep disturbance, cognitive symptoms, psychological factors, medication use, and lifetime adversity. We applied a theoretically driven hierarchical regression model, followed by mediation analyses with 10,000 bootstrap resamples. Results are reported as regression coefficients (β) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results The fully adjusted model explained 52.8% of CSI variance (adjusted R 2 = 0.523). Sexual abuse was independently associated with higher CSI scores (β = 1.26; 95% CI 0.13–2.39). Widespread Pain Index (WPI) (β = 0.14; 95% CI 0.03–0.25), cognitive symptoms (β = 1.81; 95% CI 1.24–2.38), and non-restorative sleep (β = 1.49; 95% CI 0.77-2.22) were also independent correlates. Non-restorative sleep showed an indirect association between WPI and CSI (effect = 0.105; 95% CI 0.068–0.144), whereas cognition did not (effect = 0.037; 95% CI −0.004–0.080). WPI did not mediate the sexual abuse–CSI association (indirect effect = 0.124; 95% CI −0.101–0.356). Conclusion CS-related symptom burden was associated with pain distribution, sleep, cognition, and trauma. Sexual abuse retained a small independent association not statistically explained by WPI. These cross-sectional findings support a multidimensional, trauma-informed framework but do not establish causality.

items.title: Building evolutionary resilience as a framework for managing safe haven populations
items.abstract: Safe havens are widely used to mitigate the impacts of invasive predators on threatened species, yet their isolation often disrupts evolutionary processes and can leave these species vulnerable to environmental change and stochastic events. Effective approaches to overcome these limitations and promote adaptive capacity in safe haven populations are lacking in conservation biology. Thus, we developed a pragmatic, heuristic management framework for integrating evolutionary principles into safe haven management with a focus on establishing a metapopulation of individuals distributed across geographically separated safe havens spanning environmental gradients. We used genetic simulations to demonstrate how this approach can enhance adaptive potential and persistence and to explore the optimal configuration of safe havens and number of individuals in each haven. Using demographic simulations for two threatened Australian mammals, we illustrated how this approach can be practically implemented. Based on spatially explicit population models, we predicted that many existing safe havens for these species are at risk of collapse within decades. However, our simulations showed that selection based on standing genetic variation can drive fitness gains within tens of generations, improving population resilience to novel conditions. Integrating these processes revealed that safe haven networks can promote adaptation and resilience, substantially improving long-term persistence and providing robust sources for reintroductions.

items.title: Contrasting patterns of herb-layer diversity and their environmental correlates in evergreen coniferous and deciduous broadleaf forests: evidence from Mount Lao, China
items.abstract: Abstract Key Message Evergreen coniferous forests (ECF) and deciduous broadleaf forests (DBF) exhibit fundamentally distinct mechanisms driving understory herbaceous diversity across α- and β-diversity dimensions. Canopy cover dominates α-diversity in ECF (peaking at 0.6–0.7), while soil organic matter governs richness in DBF. Forest-type-specific management strategies are required to maintain biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality. Context Understory herbaceous layers harbor over 80% of vascular plant diversity in temperate forests and serve as early indicators of ecosystem dynamics. While ECF and DBF differ fundamentally in microenvironmental conditions (light availability, litter dynamics, and soil properties), few studies have systematically compared how these contrasting systems shape herbaceous diversity mechanisms within homogeneous climatic regions. Aims This study aims to quantify the divergent drivers of α- and β-diversity in understory herbaceous communities between warm-temperate ECF and DBF, and to identify forest-type-specific management implications for biodiversity conservation. Methods Using vegetation surveys, soil sampling, and advanced modeling (GAMM, GDM, JSDM) across 69 forest plots on Mount Lao, China, we assessed how forest type modifies ecological filters governing herbaceous community assembly across multiple diversity dimensions. Results The two forest types harbored distinct compositions (15 species exclusive to ECF, 23 to DBF). In ECF, species richness followed a significant unimodal response to canopy cover (optimal at 0.6–0.7), whereas DBF richness declined with increasing soil organic matter. Overstory diversity positively influenced herbaceous richness in both systems, consistent with the resource heterogeneity–diversity hypothesis. For β-diversity, soil pH served as the primary driver in ECF, while available potassium heterogeneity dominated in DBF. Both forest types displayed significant distance–decay relationships strongest within 0–15 km, indicating joint effects of environmental filtering and dispersal limitation. Conclusion Divergent canopy-soil interaction mechanisms necessitate differentiated management approaches: ECF requires optimized canopy cover (0.6–0.7) to maximize richness while maintaining spatial connectivity, whereas DBF management should emphasize nitrogen mitigation and soil carbon regulation through mixed-species plantations to prevent competitive exclusion and maintain abundance equitability.

items.title: Quantitative eDNA abundances for multispecies monitoring along the US West Coast
items.abstract: Abstract Molecular data from environmental samples can reflect the abundance of species’ DNA, an index immediately relevant to natural-resources management at a broad geographic scale. These data commonly derive from assays designed and targeted for individual species (e.g., using qPCR or ddPCR), or from metabarcoding that use more general PCR primers to amplify many species simultaneously. Multispecies analyses make efficient use of field samples and laboratory time, and speak to inherently multispecies questions of management and ecological interest. However, unlike single-species techniques, metabarcoding alone generally reflects only the environmental DNA (eDNA) proportions of target-species DNA present, not their absolute quantities. Here, we combine qPCR and metabarcoding data derived from the same samples to estimate quantities of eDNA from many fish species along the US West Coast in three dimensions, demonstrating a technique of practical relevance for both management and ecology. We derive spatially explicit maps of eDNA abundances for 12 common species of ecological and management importance and point the way to quantitative surveys of wild species using molecules alone. We find that species distribution maps derived from eDNA largely mirror known species niches and known spatial distributions. Notably, our analyses indentify biodiversity hotspots that align with previously documented regions of ecological significance, such as the Columbia River plume and the Heceta Bank.

items.title: Quantifying the geographic mosaic of coevolutionary temperature: from coldspots to hotspots
items.abstract: Abstract The Geographic Mosaic Theory of Coevolution (GMTC) predicts that reciprocal evolutionary effects vary across landscapes, generating hotspots and coldspots. Traditionally, these states are treated as discrete categories, even though the intensity of coevolutionary selection can vary continuously. To capture this variation, we introduce a concept of coevolutionary temperature, ranging from coldspot to hotspot. We propose two complementary metrics to quantify it: reciprocity and strength of pairwise evolutionary effects. We also extend the GMTC framework beyond its traditional focus on pairwise systems to species-rich communities. Applying this approach to empirical plant-pollinator networks in a fragmented landscape, we find pronounced geographic mosaics in coevolutionary temperature. Smaller habitat patches support small, highly connected, and weakly nested communities with high reciprocity and strength, suggesting that they act as coevolutionary hotspots. In contrast, larger patches host species-rich, poorly connected, and highly nested communities with low reciprocity and strength, consistent with coldspots. At the interaction scale, reciprocity depends on degree similarity, with interactions between species that have similar numbers of partners exhibiting higher reciprocity. Together, these results highlight the strong dependence of coevolutionary effects on spatial variation in community structure and show how extending the geographic mosaic framework to species-rich communities can deepen our understanding of coevolution in complex systems.

items.title: Climate‐driven compositional shifts across a temperate–subtropical island ecotone
items.abstract: Climate change is expected to drive substantial shifts in species distributions, yet ecological responses are often delayed under disequilibrium dynamics, limiting the effectiveness of range‐based indicators for detecting ongoing change. Compositional approaches have been proposed as an alternative; however, conventional comparisons based on gradient shape or pointwise differences may fail to detect change when the overall gradient structure is conserved, because small and spatially heterogeneous differences cancel out across the gradient. Here, we address this limitation by presenting a direction‐sensitive analytical framework that integrates signed differences along environmental gradients. Using a comprehensive dataset of island floras across a temperate–subtropical transition in South Korea, we quantify temporal changes in the relative representation of warm‐temperate and subtropical plant (WTSP) assemblages. By emphasizing proportional changes along latitudinal gradients, we detect directional redistribution within communities even in the absence of pronounced changes in gradient shape. Our results reveal patterns consistent with northward redistribution of WTSP composition across survey periods, despite minimal changes in overall gradient form, indicating that community‐level redistribution can occur prior to detectable range shifts or richness changes. These findings highlight the sensitivity of cumulative, direction‐sensitive compositional metrics for detecting early ecological responses to climate warming. More broadly, this study provides a generalizable framework for detecting compositional redistribution through cumulative inference, even when conventional approaches may have limited sensitivity under some conditions, and for identifying early signals of climate‐driven change across gradient‐structured ecological systems. Transitional systems may therefore serve as particularly sensitive contexts for detecting incipient biogeographical change under ongoing warming.

items.title: Tools for the computation of acoustic parameters of narrow band high frequency clicks of odontocetes
items.abstract: Acoustic recording can be a very interesting way of monitoring cetaceans for conservation purposes. However, some sympatric species produce very similar sounds and are thus difficult to study specifically. In this work, we are interested in characterizing the narrow band high frequency (NBHF) clicks emitted by several species of odontocetes, among which all porpoises and some species of dolphins. The traditional acoustic parameters (durations, frequencies, bandwidths) of NBHF clicks show several drawbacks, such as redundancy, lack of precise definition, and poor robustness to noise. In this study, we propose a new method of characterizing NBHF clicks by fitting a Gabor wavelet to the signal and thus extracting two specific metrics, the Gabor frequency and the Gabor duration. We first assess the theoretical usefulness of this mathematical model, and then test it against traditional measurements in numerical examples with varying levels of noise. Our method is then applied to two empirical datasets recorded in South America, a place were many sympatric species are found to emit NBHF clicks. Two large sets of signals are thus analyzed and compared : one of clicks of Peale’s dolphins (Cephalorhynchus australis) from Chaihuin bay, Chile, and the other of clicks of Franciscana dolphins (Pontoporia blainvillei) from San Clemente del Tuyu, Argentina. Our metrics allow a good characterization of each species’ clicks with quick and efficient computation, with good reproducibility across different recording devices, and a clear separation of the two species. We suggest it could be applied to more datasets from different species, and possibly be used to classify NBHF of sympatric species.

items.title: Fate of legacy ammonium in the coastal Baltic Sea
items.abstract: Abstract. Eutrophication has enriched coastal sediments globally with organic matter (OM), fuelling internal nutrient loading once benthic hypoxia occurs. Internal ammonium (NH4+) loading may be particularly prominent in the coastal Baltic Sea due to the existence of a substantial NH4+ pool in its sediments, accumulated via OM burial and mineralization over long-term eutrophication. However, despite its potential to exacerbate eutrophication, internal NH4+ loading has so far received little attention in the coastal Baltic Sea. It remains poorly understood for how long the benthic legacy OM may affect both the benthic NH4+ pool and the internal NH4+ loading via sediment-water NH4+ effluxes, especially under varying oxygen availabilities. To reconstruct past and predict future NH4+ effluxes in response to different OM loading and bottom water oxygen conditions, we developed a reactive transport model for muddy, organic-rich sediments of the coastal Baltic Sea. Our model results suggest that the legacy OM in the coastal sediments is the key driver sustaining benthic NH4+ pools and effluxes both today and well into the future. As today’s OM loading is constantly adding new OM to the already existing legacy loading, the benthic NH4+ pool will continuously grow and result in persistently elevated NH4+ effluxes in the future, even under oxic conditions. If external measures strongly reduce OM loading to eventually pre-industrial levels, the NH4+ pool still continues to grow for at least 80 years due to the continued mineralization of legacy OM, which keeps NH4+ effluxes elevated for at least 180 years before eventually returning to pre-industrial levels in the year 2300. These model results highlight the persistence of eutrophication legacy effects and their importance for ecosystem management of the coastal Baltic Sea. The knowledge obtained is beneficial also for other anthropogenically impacted coastal seas with similar geomorphology as the Baltic Sea.

items.title: Impact of climate extremes on socio-economic characteristics of peri-urban mountain settlements
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanisation and a changing climate are transforming the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR), driving profound socio-economic and environmental changes. Himachal Pradesh, located in the western IHR, exemplifies these transformations. As climate change undermines the viability of traditional livelihoods such as agriculture and pastoralism, rural households are increasingly shifting towards secondary and tertiary occupations through livelihood diversification within villages or migration to urban peripheries. This trend is particularly visible in settlements located near major infrastructure, such as highways and hydropower plants, and urban centres where economic opportunities are concentrated. However, such peri-urbanisation often unfolds in an unregulated and unplanned manner, straining the fragile mountain ecosystems and amplifying vulnerabilities to extreme climate events. Despite this, peri-urban mountain settlements remain largely overlooked in policy and research. Fragmented governance structures and overlapping rural and urban jurisdictions result in administrative neglect, exposing these areas to cascading social, environmental, and economic pressures. This study investigates the developmental and climate-induced challenges faced by peri-urban settlements in Himachal Pradesh. Drawing on policy reviews, secondary literature, and primary research, it examines the interlinked risks of climate change and unregulated peri-urban growth, their impacts on livelihoods and infrastructure, and the associated gendered vulnerabilities. A review of the Indian policy landscape highlights critical gaps in existing plans, frameworks, and governance approaches for addressing these compounding challenges. Building on field-based and policy best practices, the study proposes context-sensitive recommendations to strengthen adaptation planning and support climate-resilient development across the peri-urban regions of the IHR.

items.title: Evolutionary history suggests nymphal origin of antennal expansions in adult leaf‐footed bugs
items.abstract: Abstract Insect antennae morphology is highly conserved in many insect families, yet in some clades, elaborations of antennae form are more common. Leaf‐footed bugs (Hemiptera: Coreidae) are one case where there is considerable variation in antennal morphology. Antennae can be rectilinear, with cylindrical antennomeres, or have laterally flattened expansions that differ in which antennomeres they occur. Strikingly, such variation is also found across development, where nymphs and adults can also display different antennal shapes. Thus, Coreidae presents a unique opportunity to study how much shared ancestry and development influence antennal variation. We characterized the antennal expansion across a recent Coreidae phylogeny using research‐grade iNaturalist photos and primary taxonomic descriptions of adults (species) and nymphs (genus). We then performed ancestral reconstructions to estimate how many transitions between antennal states occurred across the phylogeny and compared these patterns between adults and nymphs. We found that adult antennal expansions are rare and restricted to Coreinae. The reconstructed history is consistent with repeated transitions to expanded adult antennae across Coreinae, with expansion most commonly confined to the third antennomere and concentrated in a few genera. In contrast, nymphal data reveal that antennal expansions are more widespread and often occur in genera whose adults lack expansions, suggesting that conspicuous antennal morphologies can be developmentally transient and frequently lost before adulthood. Together, our results indicate that adult antennal expansion is associated with nymphal expansion in the sampled genera and may reflect repeated retention or prolongation of a morphology expressed during development. Additionally, we provide a comparative framework for future work on the functional and developmental bases of exaggerated antennal forms.

items.title: Suspected white shark (Carcharodon carcharias) predation on an adult Atlantic sturgeon (Acipenser oxyrinchus) from the Gulf of Maine
items.abstract: Abstract Atlantic sturgeon ( Acipenser oxyrinchus ) are threatened under the United States Endangered Species Act in the Gulf of Maine (GoM), where natural sources of adult mortality remain poorly documented. We report a stranded adult female Atlantic Sturgeon (224-cm total length) recovered in Scarborough, Maine, USA, with injury consistent with predation by a juvenile white shark ( Carcharodon carcharias ) and inconsistent with vessel strike. Bite-mark analysis indicated a shark of at least 2.6 m total length, matching juveniles increasingly documented in nearby Saco Bay. The stranding coincided with peak seasonal white shark activity within known sturgeon foraging area, supporting predation as the most parsimonious cause of death. Predation on adult Atlantic sturgeon has only been known via tooth-mark injuries on surviving individuals in Canadian weir fisheries making this the first direct evidence of the interaction in the GoM. As white sharks expand into warming GoM waters, such encounters may become more frequent, highlighting the need for continued monitoring of shifting predator-prey dynamics.

items.title: Динамика роста и половые различия длиннотных размеров верхней конечности и ее звеньев обследуемых детско-юношеского возраста (обзор литературы)
items.abstract: Роль верхней конечности в жизни человека зачастую недооценивают, в то время как она является сложноустроенным и высоко координированным органом труда, выполняющим разнообразные двигательные функции. Цель исследования: изучить особенности возрастной изменчивости продольных размеров верхней конечности и ее звеньев (плеча, предплечья и кисти) обследуемых детско-юношеского возраста мужского и женского пола. Материалы и методы. В работе использованы теоретические методы исследования: анализ и сравнение данных литературы. Методология исследования включала сопоставление результатов за период с середины XX века по настоящее время. Общий объем изученных рукописей составил 39 штук. Выполнена критическая оценка анализируемого материала авторов, занимающихся изучением особенностей развертки, интенсивности роста и сроков достижения зрелости продольных размеров верхней конечности и ее звеньев у лиц мужского и женского пола. Результаты и обсуждение. Выполненный анализ показал отсутствие единых критериев оценки динамики роста верхней конечности и ее звеньев. Рассогласованность выявлена при сравнительной оценке таких ключевых параметров как: количество и сроки начала и окончания перекреста кривых роста длины верхней конечности ее звеньев у лиц разного пола, возраст начала проявления выраженных половых различий и сроки их завершения, которые могли варьировать в широких пределах. Установленные различия связаны с изучением лиц разных регионов проживания, влиянием на них различных климатогеографических и социально-экономических условий, приводящих к рассогласованности в проявлении эпохальных тенденций. Выявленная фрагментарность исследований затрудняет использование антропометрических параметров в прогностическом отборе в видах спорта и клинической диагностике. Однако их схожесть определена при оценке общей тенденции роста верхней конечности: опережение девочек в скорости созревания, большие абсолютные размеры у мальчиков. Однако сравнительная оценка роста сегментов: плеча, предплечья и кисти у разных авторов позволяет выделить существенный разрыв в полученных результатах. Заключение. Следовательно, несмотря на существенные различия в данных исследователей, показатели длины верхней конечности и ее сегментов остаются высоко информативными, требующим дальнейшего изучения с целью создания актуальных региональных стандартов у лиц разного пола и возраста.

items.title: From Jiangnan water land to Greater Shanghai: exploring ‘nature-culture holistic conservation’ in an international metropolis
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, through a policy and planning analysis of nature-culture integration, a ‘nature-culture holistic conservation’ paradigm is proposed to address the disconnection between nature and culture in the development of Chinese metropolises. Drawing on the historic urban landscape (HUL) approach and integrating the Eastern philosophy of ‘harmony between heaven and humans’, this study takes Shanghai as a case to construct a theoretical framework for the holistic conservation of 'nature-culture ecosystems' tailored to megacities. The research reveals that Shanghai’s urban genetic code is deeply embedded in a nature-culture foundation characterised by the organic integration of ‘mountains, waters, settlements, and fields’, which has shaped the city's distinctive urban character and value. However, owing to factors such as the megacity’s vast spatial scale and fragmented administrative governance structures, the existing conservation system suffers from significant fragmentation at the planning, governance, and practice levels, which constrains the realisation of holistic value. The paper argues that Shanghai should transcend the single-element conservation model by incorporating the recognition and interpretation of ‘nature-culture’ relationships into planning frameworks across different scales and by considering the natural foundations and cultural genes of the Jiangnan water system as core strategic resources for sustainable development. Strategies include the following: at the cognitive level, constructing a ‘nature-culture system’ framework; at the planning level, integrating holistic conservation into territorial spatial planning (TSP) and identifying high-composite-value areas; and at the governance level, establishing multiscalar coordination mechanisms. This study provides theoretical support for shaping Shanghai into an ‘international metropolis with Jiangnan characteristics’ and offers a reference for the sustainable development of comparable metropolises.

items.title: Dynamic Natural-Capital Accounting under Tipping Risk and Spatial Contagion: A Regenerative Forest Network Model
items.abstract: Abstract Classical renewable-resource models value the biological stock that remains after current extraction, whereas ecological resilience theory emphasizes the possibility of alternative regimes separated by tipping boundaries. This paper combines these perspectives in a networked forest-management problem with two continuous ecological states---harvestable biomass and resilience---and a discrete ecological regime for each patch. Harvesting lowers biomass and resilience and increases the endogenous intensity of a harmful regime shift; regenerative effort rebuilds ecological capital and reduces that intensity. The hazard also rises with exposure to degraded neighboring patches, generating spatial contagion. The planner solves an infinite-horizon controlled piecewise-deterministic Markov decision problem. Rather than assuming positive ecological shadow values, we derive them from primitive order conditions by monotone dynamic programming. Six structural results follow. The model nests Clark's classical target-stock problem; sufficiently large expected tipping losses generate \emph{regenerative inactivity}, with zero harvest and positive restoration; the optimal harvest rule contains a direct tipping-risk precautionary wedge; degraded neighbors can induce preventive closure before local collapse; a next-generation matrix yields a spectral threshold for early-stage landscape cascades; and Perron--Frobenius sensitivity identifies the patches at which restoration most effectively reduces systemic ecological risk. A stylized numerical illustration shows how restoration can move a connected forest from a supercritical to a subcritical cascade regime. The framework extends the economics of endogenous regime shifts by making resilience a managed state and by adding network contagion and systemic restoration targeting. JEL codes: C61; Q23; Q28; Q57. items.title: An escalation toward risk: climate change impacts on the distribution, genetic diversity, and conservation of Neesiochloa barbata (Poaceae: Chloridoideae: Pappophorinae)
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change represents a primary threat to global biodiversity, particularly in seasonally dry tropical forests (SDTF), affecting species distribution, genetic diversity, and ecosystem conservation. Neesiochloa barbata (Poaceae: Chloridoideae: Pappophorinae) is a grass species belonging to a monotypic genus endemic to the Caatinga, the largest SDTF in South America. In this study, we addressed conservation issues related to the impacts of the climate crisis (2080–2100) on the potential distribution, genetic diversity, and structure of N. barbata populations to: (a) assess extinction risk; (b) estimate the future distribution overlap with protected areas (PA); and (c) identify priority areas for conservation. We assessed the current conservation status from Not Evaluated (NE) to Least Concern (LC), however, under future climate scenarios, suitable habitat for N. barbata will be reduced, elevating the threat level to Near Threatened (NT) and finally to Endangered (EN). This severe contraction of climatically suitable areas results in a progressive escalation in extinction risk: LC > NT > EN. Despite the overall loss of suitable habitat, the remaining future niche shows a slight spatial shift toward the boundaries of existing PA (increasing from 39% to 43%). The haplotype network (nrDNA and cpDNA) showed distinct polymorphism rates between the genomes, consistent with the DAPC clustering (best K = 2 and Northern and Southern haplogroups). This genetic structure highlights lineages with distinct evolutionary histories that must be preserved. The reduction in suitable areas and the rising extinction risk underscore the urgent need for targeted conservation in the Caatinga. While the current PA system is crucial for protecting climatic refugia, the expansion and connection of these areas are essential to ensure the long-term persistence and genetic heritage of N. barbata against the climate crisis.

items.title: Carbon balance, canopy spatial structure and renovation benchmarks in old cocoa agroforestry systems of the Dominican Republic
items.abstract: Abstract Rehabilitation and renovation (Rh/Re) are essential elements in the cocoa cultivation cycle. Cocoa farmers must decide on whether to rehabilitate (Rh) or to renovate (Re) a cocoa orchard when its productivity declines due to ageing, disease outbreaks or other causes. Cocoa Rh/Re interventions alter standing biomass while retaining variable amounts of old canopy, roots and soil carbon. We quantified carbon stocks and structural attributes across a 52-farm project frame in in two growing regions in the Dominican Republic using 40 vegetation inventories, 50 soil records, 26 preparation-site intervention records and 25 matched inventory–intervention pairs. Above-ground biomass was estimated with diameter-compatible allometry; woody roots and 0–15 cm soil carbon was accounted for separately. Mean live-biomass stock was 192.63 ± 34.21 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ (n = 40) and mean live-plus-soil stock was 306.60 ± 36.45 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ for 38 farms with linked soil data. In matched farms, estimated preparation-site above-ground removal averaged 93.72 ± 11.44 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹, which is almost half of the above-carbon stocks. Group-specific Clark–Evans spatial indices, vertical structure and soil latent factors were integrated at farm level. Across all farms, 21 total-stem arrangements (cacao + companion trees) were classified as aggregated, 16 as approximately random and 3 as regular. Finally, a fixed 35-year renovation scenario produced 73.94 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ of new cocoa and boundary-tree stock, 19.78 Mg CO₂e ha⁻¹ below the mean removal proxy suggesting that Rh/Re interventions do not compensate for the above-ground carbon removed from target cacao orchards. This study provides a reproducible plot-level accounting framework for Rh/Re implementation while distinguishing measured stocks, removed above-ground stocks, residual below-ground reserves and future regrowth and carbon sequestration scenarios.

items.title: Aquatic subsidies increase the resilience of riparian spider communities after pulse disturbance
items.abstract: Climatic events such as intense winds and rainfall act as strong pulse disturbances in many ecosystems. Although these disturbances can abruptly alter community structure and dynamics, recovery depends on community resilience, which may be enhanced by resource availability. Cross-ecosystem subsidies can increase prey availability for generalist predators, potentially buffering communities against the effects of disturbance. In this study, we tested whether aquatic subsidies (i.e., emergence of aquatic insects) enhance the resilience of spider communities following unpredictable climatic pulse disturbances. We conducted a field experiment in four Atlantic Rainforest streams, simulating pulse disturbances in riparian and inland plots. We surveyed vegetation-dwelling spiders one day before and four times after disturbance simulations to estimate changes in abundance and community resilience, while stable isotope analyses assessed the contribution of aquatic insects to spider diets. Riparian spiders consumed more aquatic insects than inland spiders, and spider abundance was 24% higher in riparian plots. Disturbance effects were also 43% stronger in riparian communities. Despite this stronger immediate impact, recovery models indicated greater resilience in riparian spider communities, highlighting the role of emergent aquatic insect subsidies in post-disturbance recovery. Our findings demonstrate that cross-ecosystem resource linkages can enhance the resilience of terrestrial predator communities to climatic pulse disturbance.

items.title: Above-ground biomass recovery after fire in a West African semi-deciduous forest invaded by Cedrela odorata L.
items.abstract: Abstract Key message Invasion by Cedrela odorata L. can substantially contribute to above-ground biomass recovery after fire while simultaneously altering forest composition. Context Tropical forests are increasingly exposed to successive disturbances that can alter forest dynamics and ecosystem functioning. Understanding long-term responses to disturbances offers a solution for sustainable ecosystem services management. Aims This study assessed the long-term aboveground biomass recovery in a tropical semi-deciduous forest that has undergone silvicultural treatments, devastating fire, and invasion by Cedrela odorata L . We also aimed to quantify the contributions of three species groups: local commercial species (Com), C. odorata (Ced), and non-commercial species (Sec), i.e., all other species. Methods First, we used tree inventory data (diameter at breast height ≥ 10 cm) collected over 42 years from 25 permanent plots covering 100 ha. Then, we used a Bayesian framework to infer the aboveground biomass recovery trajectory. Finally, we analyzed the respective effects of fire severity and silvicultural treatment intensity on above-ground biomass recovery. Results Following invasion by C. odorata, 90% of the biomass lost after the fire will be recovered in less than 50 years. Fire severity affects biomass recovery more than silvicultural treatments. Predictions at the end of recovery indicate a biomass composed of 33% C. odorata , 50% commercial species, and 17% non-commercial species. Conclusion Invasion by C. odorata has advantages and inconveniences for the recovery of forest attributes. These results highlight the importance of adapting forest management strategies to balance ecological resilience and timber production in West Africa, where forest resources are threatened.

items.title: Diversity of Cladocera and Cyclestherida (Crustacea, Branchiopoda, Diplostraca) in continental waterbodies of southern Vietnam
items.abstract: Microscopic crustaceans, particularly Branchiopoda, often dominate the zooplankton and microzoobenthos of continental waterbodies and are widely utilised in aquaculture as a vital food source for fish and invertebrates. Despite their ecological and economic importance, the knowledge of their diversity and distribution remains highly uneven across the globe. Tropical Southeast Asia, in particular, harbours a rich but, still inadequately documented cladoceran and branchiopod fauna, with many regions remaining largely unexplored or represented only by few historical records. The Republic of Vietnam represents an example of territoty with such knowledge gap: the last comprehensive, systematic survey of its branchiopod fauna was conducted as early as 1980 and, since that time, only fragmented and localised contributions have been added. Consequently, our current understanding of the species richness, biogeographical patterns and environmental drivers in this biodiversity hotspot is severely outdated and incomplete, hampering both fundamental research and applied conservation efforts.To address this gap in current knowledge, we present a new, extensive dataset on samples collected during 2023–2025 in southern Vietnam within the framework of the Joint Vietnam–Russia Tropical Science and Technology Research Center. In total, 476 samples from 360 distinct localities were investigated, covering a wide range of permanent and temporary waterbodies of various types (e.g. ponds, lakes, reservoirs, rice paddies and temporary pools). Sampling was performed using plankton nets and all material was processed at the A.N. Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution following standard hydrobiological protocols. Species identification was based on both recent taxonomic monographs and the extensive expertise of our team, which is internationally recognised as a leader in Southeast Asian Cladocera research. The resulting dataset is published as a Darwin Core Archive in the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and includes, for each sampling event, precise geographic coordinates, date of collection and collector information. This comprehensive, georeferenced resource not only fills a critical geographic and temporal gap in branchiopod biodiversity data, but also provides a solid baseline for future monitoring, biogeographic analyses and assessments of environmental change in the rapidly developing landscapes of southern Vietnam. The dataset contains information on branchiopod zooplankton and microzoobenthos (Branchiopoda, Diplostraca, Cladocera and Cyclestherida) from many permanent and temporary waterbodies in southern Vietnam. The branchiopod communities of the region were poorly known as taxonomy of the group has changed a lot since the latest revision of the local fauna (Thang et al. 1980). Our core data table contains 2415 records belonging to 80 presumptive (76 recognised) species and 45 genera of Cladocera and Cyclestherida from 360 locations. The families Chydoridae with 45 (42 recognised) species from 27 genera and Sididae (nine species from five genera) are the most diverse. No invasive species were found. Results of the current study increase our knowledge about microplankton and microzoobenthos of Vietnam and SE Asia in general.

items.title: Same Void, Different Spatial Logics: Rethinking Natah through Asian Courtyard Traditions
items.abstract: The morphological similarity of courtyards across cultures leaves a fundamental question: are seemingly similar empty spaces also understood, shaped, and valued in the same way? This study examines the Balinese natah, with traditional Chinese and Indian courtyards as conceptual comparisons, through a structured literature review and comparative document analysis. The data were analyzed through ontological, epistemological, and axiological dimensions. The results show that all three regard emptiness as a meaningful space, but through different mechanisms. The natah functions as a relational center that orients building masses and is shaped through spatial knowledge and socio-ritual practices; the Chinese courtyard emphasizes axiality, hierarchy, and privacy; whereas the Indian courtyard demonstrates diverse relationships among central space, Vastu, ritual, and social order. These findings question the adequacy of the courtyard as a cross-cultural morphological category. This study offers an ontological-epistemological-axiological framework for interpreting empty space and emphasizes that the conservation of the natah needs to preserve the relationships, knowledge, and practices that make it meaningful.

items.title: Integrating ecohydrological modelling and participatory processes to co-design multifunctional forest management
items.abstract: Mediterranean forests are becoming denser, drier, and more combustible because of natural and human-driven factors. Forest managers report that managing them is increasingly costly relative to its economic returns and requires informed decision-making supported by appropriate tools and dialogue. This study couples the Decision Support System (DSS) CAFE (Carbon, Aqua, Fire and Eco-resilience) with structured participatory processes across four Living Labs in Spain, Morocco, and Italy, representing distinct Mediterranean socioecological systems: semiarid Aleppo pine forests, traditional argan woodlands with goat grazing, and cork-oak silvopastoral systems. The aim was to evaluate whether management co-designed in this way is resilient to climate disturbance while improving ecosystem services (ES). In three rounds of co-design workshops, stakeholders identified priority ES, agreed on the management actions to enhance them, and evaluated alternatives generated by the DSS. Their priorities were remarkably consistent across sites, focusing on wildfire risk, water availability, and biomass extraction. Preferred interventions were ecologically sound and consistent with field evidence. To this end, CAFE was expanded to quantify locally relevant ES that had not previously been modelled, including argan fruit production, cork extraction, fodder availability, and bark regeneration. Model outputs agreed well with published data at all sites. However, in none of the four sites did stakeholders select the most resilient options available, and their selections were statistically indistinguishable from random choice. These findings highlight that resilience to climate disturbance remains difficult to perceive without appropriate metrics. Making resilience an explicit objective of participatory planning is a necessary contribution of decision-support tools for Mediterranean forests facing increasing uncertainty.

items.title: Salinity filtering and hydrological stage transitions drive the community reassembly of eukaryotes and particle-attached bacteria in Yuncheng Salt Lake
items.abstract: Extreme salt lakes represent natural model systems for investigating microbial community assembly under strong environmental filtering. However, cross-kingdom associations between eukaryotes and particle-attached bacteria, as well as the combined effects of salinity and hydrological phase transitions on community structure, remain poorly unresolved. We conducted a field survey in Yuncheng Salt Lake, comparing eukaryotic and particle-attached bacterial communities across high-salinity and low-salinity habitats during crystallization and stabilization phases. Salinity served as the dominant environmental filter and exerted stronger filtering effects on eukaryotes than on particle-attached bacteria, whereas phase effects were more pronounced under low-salinity, particularly for eukaryotes. Within deterministic processes, the relative contribution of variable selection for eukaryotes increased from 13.33% to 24.44%, while particle-attached bacteria became increasingly dominated by stochastic processes from crystallization to stabilization. The high-salinity network exhibited greater connectivity than the low-salinity network and was characterized by bacterial connectors as topologically central nodes. Functional potential of particle-attached bacteria was phase-dependent: crystallization was associated with carbon and energy metabolism pathways, whereas stabilization shifted toward heterotrophic carbon utilization and motility. In the high-salinity network, connector taxa were additionally associated with predicted functional potential related to attachment, nutrient acquisition, stress tolerance, and sulfur/methane metabolism. These findings elucidate the assembly and adaptive strategies of microbial communities in salt lakes, underscoring the critical roles of both salinity and hydrological phase in driving cross-kingdom community reorganization. This study provides novel insights into the ecology of extreme saline environments and the dynamics of aquatic microbial communities under environmental stress.

items.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
items.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.
