items.title: Rights of Nature and the Rights of Wild Animals: Guiding Principles for Resolving Human–Wildlife Conflicts
items.abstract: Abstract Rights of Nature (RoN) is increasingly used to challenge conventional legal frameworks, restructure governance over ecosystems and living beings, and rethink human–nature relations; however, its role in addressing human–wildlife conflict remains undertheorized and insufficiently defined. Using the case of the Andean (spectacled) bear ( Tremarctos ornatus ) in Ecuador’s Andean Bear Corridor, and the emerging conflict between individual bears and local farmers, this article presents an innovative RoN framework for conflict governance. The research employs a socio-legal approach – doctrinal analysis, qualitative interdisciplinary fieldwork (2022–2025) across five local communities in the Ecuadorian Andes and informal expert interviews – to compile a set of rights at multiple scales (ecosystem, species, individual animal) and identifies relevant principles of human–wildlife conflicts based on jurisprudence. Practical tests for consideration by courts and regulators are proposed: (i) an interspecies capabilities assessment outlining parameters for individual animal well-being and flourishing; (ii) a precautionary and eco-proportionality framework to balance the interests of humans, animals, and ecosystems; and (iii) adherence to principles that prioritize nature in decision-making (including for individual wild animals). Applied to the Andean bear case study, the proposed RoN framework could shift practice from conflict and killing to coexistence. The article argues that the RoN framework, including rights for wild animals, is more than solely a legal instrument, but a catalyst for reshaping human–nature relationships. The RoN framework presented provides a model to implement and operationalize RoN approaches in the wider Andean Bear Corridor and transnationally for other species in other countries accounting for individual animal rights.

items.title: First Integrated Ecological Assessment of a Marginal Golden Eagle Population in the Moroccan Atlantic Sahara
items.abstract: Las poblaciones marginales de Aquila chrysaetos que habitan el Sahara se encuentran entre las menos estudiadas y más aisladas de la especie. Realizamos la primera evaluación ecológica integrada de la población de A. chrysaetos del Sahara Atlántico marroquí, combinando datos reproductivos, de dieta, climáticos, morfométricos y de movimiento. En abril de 2026, muestreamos seis territorios históricos y confirmamos la reproducción en tres, con cuatro pollos registrados en tres nidos activos. Estimamos en aproximadamente 2500 ha (25 km2) el área defendida por una pareja reproductora. La dieta estuvo dominada por Uromastyx y Lepus, que conjuntamente representaron 51 de las 56 presas identificadas. Equipamos tres pollos con transmisores GPS-GSM, pero solo uno proporcionó datos de movimiento. El juvenil permaneció cerca de su territorio natal durante aproximadamente 40 días después de abandonar el nido e inició la dispersión natal a los 115 días de edad. Recorrió aproximadamente 460 km en 3 días y alcanzó un punto artificial de abastecimiento de agua para ganado en Mauritania, a unos 100 km del territorio natal. La temperatura máxima diaria alcanzó 48°C. El juvenil entró en un depósito elevado de agua para ganado el 27 de mayo y no pudo salir; la actividad del acelerómetro cesó el 29 de mayo y el cadáver fue localizado durante una inspección de campo el 30 de mayo. El ahogamiento fue la causa de muerte más probable. Aunque un único evento de mortalidad no permite establecer efectos a escala poblacional, identifica un riesgo antropogénico potencialmente prevenible en un paisaje hiperárido. Estos resultados aportan información ecológica de referencia para esta población marginal y ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de continuar los censos reproductivos, ampliar el seguimiento mediante GPS-GSM, evaluar la variabilidad de las presas y las precipitaciones y analizar las infraestructuras de abastecimiento de agua para ganado como posible fuente de mortalidad. [Traducción de Jesús Bautista-Rodríguez]

items.title: Constraints on cosmology and baryonic feedback with a joint analysis of Dark Energy Survey Year 3 lensing data and ACT DR6 thermal Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effect observations
items.abstract: We present a joint analysis of weak gravitational lensing (shear) data obtained from the first three years of observations by the Dark Energy Survey and thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect measurements from a combination of Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and Planck data. A combined analysis of shear (which traces the projected mass) with the tSZ effect (which traces the projected gas pressure) can jointly probe both the distribution of matter and the thermodynamic state of the gas, accounting for the correlated effects of baryonic feedback on both observables. We detect the shear$~\times~$tSZ cross-correlation at a 21$σ$ significance, the highest to date, after minimizing the bias from cosmic infrared background leakage in the tSZ map. By jointly modeling the small-scale shear auto-correlation and the shear$~\times~$tSZ cross-correlation, we obtain $S_8 = 0.811^{+0.015}_{-0.012}$ and $Ω_{\rm m} = 0.263^{+0.023}_{-0.030}$, results consistent with primary CMB analyses from Planck and P-ACT. We find evidence for reduced thermal gas pressure in dark matter halos with masses $M < 10^{14} \, M_{\odot}/h$, supporting predictions of enhanced feedback from active galactic nuclei on gas thermodynamics. A comparison of the inferred matter power suppression reveals a $2-4σ$ tension with hydrodynamical simulations that implement mild baryonic feedback, as our constraints prefer a stronger suppression. Finally, we investigate biases from cosmic infrared background leakage in the tSZ-shear cross-correlation measurements, employing mitigation techniques to ensure a robust inference. Our code is publicly available on GitHub.

items.title: How well can we forecast local magnetic ground perturbations with existing space weather monitoring resources?
items.abstract: Abstract. In this study we examine how a deep-learning based forecast of local, ground-based geomagnetic field variations trained on solar wind parameters available in real time might be improved by including information contained in an accurate forecast of solar wind conditions. This is accomplished using a long short-term memory (LSTM) model together with magnetic field measurements made at the Rørvik magnetometer station in Mid-Norway. We use Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) satellite measurements of solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) conditions at the first Sun-Earth Lagrange point, and historical lists of coronal mass ejection (CME) impacts at Earth to train and validate the LSTM model. We find that accurate information about the IMF Bz component and solar wind speed are important for obtaining a reasonably accurate (r² ≥ 0.5) forecast of local geomagnetic activity over forecasting horizons beyond ~ 3 h. Information about CME arrival time is only important when simultaneously accompanied by accurate, relatively high-resolution information about IMF Bz. In the absence of the latter, CME arrival time information does not contribute to model performance. This empirical result amounts to a quantitative demonstration of the widely recognized impact of IMF orientation on CME geoeffectiveness. This result also highlights that new innovations, probably in the form of new prediction capabilities of conditions in interplanetary space, will be required to produce accurate forecasts of local geomagnetic disturbances beyond a forecast horizon of 1 h.

items.title: On sub-sevenfold symmetries in LH2 stacked ring scaffolds: A quantum optical perspective
items.abstract: Abstract For highly efficient light-harvesting, purple photosynthetic bacteria rely on light-harvesting 2 (LH2) complexes featuring ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold rotational symmetries; however, sub-sevenfold scaffolds have not yet been observed in nature. To investigate this absence, we utilize a closed coupled-dipole model that neglects dissipative effects, which remains valid for a temporal window shorter than the interlayer excitation energy transfer time (on the picosecond scale) in an LH2 scaffold. We examine collective eigenmodes across $C_n$ stacked model ring geometries for $n=9,8,7,6$. Our results demonstrate that the minimum energy separation between specific collective bands occurs at the angular-momentum modes $m=\pm 1$ for known geometries, effectively predicting the photoactive absorption wavelengths of the lower bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) ring. Specifically, we predict peaks at 851, 848, and 825 nm for ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold symmetries, respectively, which agree well with experimental observations. Applying this analysis to a hypothetical sixfold geometry, we predict a significant blue shift in the photoactive wavelength of the lower BChl ring, suggesting inefficient harvesting of the available solar spectrum and offering a quantum optical perspective on the evolutionary absence of sub-sevenfold scaffolds in LH2 complexes. Our study demonstrates that quantum cooperative models can elucidate specific aspects of biological LH systems.

items.title: Radial dependency of ICME-associated particle acceleration processes: Statistical multipoint observations from 2016-2023
items.abstract: During the propagation of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs), evolution of the ICME-driven shock along with interactions with other solar wind structures, planetary bodies, and general changes to their morphology can alter particle acceleration efficiency and transport effects at their associated shocks. While the underlying mechanisms for these processes have been studied, the connection between the radial evolution of the ICME-driven shock during propagation and the resulting gradual solar energetic particle and energetic storm particle (ESP) intensities, composition, and acceleration has yet to be fully understood. The current distributed array of spacecraft at varying heliocentric distances provides a welcome opportunity to statistically analyze the radial dependency of particle populations and acceleration mechanisms present at ICME-driven shocks. We compiled a database of multipoint ICME events from 2016--2023, focusing our analysis on 23 events that were observed in situ by at least two of the following spacecraft: Parker Solar Probe (PSP), Solar Orbiter, ACE, Wind, and STEREO-A. Using the magnetic field, plasma, and ion compositional data provided by these spacecraft, we derived both local shock and ESP spectral shape parameters. By comparing the changes in these parameters at different stages of ICME propagation, we analyzed the connection between the evolution of the local shock conditions and the spectral shape. We find evidence to suggest a consistent increase in shock acceleration efficiency with heliocentric distance while the parent ICME is within 0.7 au, followed by a reduction in shock efficiency at further distances.

items.title: Can Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo with Broken Symmetry Trials Describe Iron–Sulfur Clusters?
items.abstract: Abstract Phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) has in several cases been found to perform well on strongly correlated systems, including compounds containing transition-metal elements. Here, we benchmark the method for three iron–sulfur clusters ([2Fe-2S], [4Fe-4S], and the FeMo cofactor) using a hierarchy of systematically improved trial states derived from coupled cluster (CC) theory, including up to quadruple excitations relative to the Hartree–Fock (HF) reference, as well as multi-Slater trial states derived from unrestricted density matrix renormalization group wave functions. Our results reveal for these systems that, as the symmetry-broken trial is improved beyond the mean-field level, the phaseless AFQMC energy can become less accurate, and in some cases even less accurate than the underlying trial projected energy itself, displaying an inverted energy pattern that is only corrected once the trial fidelity is sufficiently high. For [2Fe-2S], we show that a decreased accuracy in the AFQMC energy can coincide with a simultaneous improvement in the trial state and the walker ensemble, as measured by their fidelity relative to the exact ground state, a behavior which is allowed by the nonvariational nature of the phaseless AFQMC energy estimator. We further find that this is not solely due to the use of spin-unrestricted trial states, as the inversion persists in [2Fe-2S] when we explicitly break the symmetry of the Hamiltonian by applying a fictitious local spin-Zeeman field. Instead, we find that the energy inversion is related to the choice of measurement trial in the estimator, where using a high-order CC trial state for measurements may introduce errors that are suppressed when the measurement wave function is restricted to lower excitation subspaces. In particular, measuring the energy with the mean-field reference while guiding the walkers with a CC trial removes the inverted pattern and improves the overall accuracy across the iron–sulfur clusters, with a possible exception for [4Fe-4S] where energies with a CCSDT guide may be less accurate than those guided by CCSD for some broken-symmetry families. Taken together, our findings suggest that the relatively accurate energies obtained with an HF trial state in these systems arise from favorable error cancellation, warranting significant caution about the reliability of phaseless AFQMC with such trials for strongly correlated transition-metal systems of this kind.

items.title: The first 3D magnetohydrodynamic core-collapse progenitors. I. General properties, convection, and nuclear burning
items.abstract: The most energetic core-collapse supernovae are thought to arise from rapidly rotating, magnetised progenitors, yet the 3D structure of their pre-collapse interior remains poorly constrained, and realistic distributions of magnetic fields, angular momentum, and convective asphericities are still lacking. We constructed physically consistent 3D pre-supernova progenitors, from the stellar core to the helium shell, including rotation and magnetic fields. In this first paper, we focus on the behaviour of turbulence and nuclear burning in the shells surrounding the stellar core. We assess their deviations from 1D stellar-evolution models. The magnetorotational properties of the progenitors are discussed in the second paper of this series. We used to perform 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of two compact Wolf--Rayet progenitors obtained from the stellar evolution codes and The models were mapped onto the multidimensional domain several minutes before collapse and evolved until the onset of core collapse. We find that in extended oxygen-burning shells, turbulent velocities exceed the standard mixing-length-theory (MLT) predictions by approximately a factor of 2. In contrast, a thin silicon-burning shell is poorly described by MLT: mixing is reduced near both shell boundaries, and the inferred effective diffusion profile departs significantly from the standard 1D prescription. These differences directly affect the spatial extent and efficiency of nuclear burning. In one of our models, a late shell merger present in the 1D stellar-evolution calculation does not occur in the 3D MHD evolution, indicating that such events may be sensitive to the specific modelling framework adopted. We present the first 3D MHD pre-supernova progenitors of this kind, suitable for subsequent collapse and explosion calculations. We show that multidimensional effects can significantly modify turbulent mixing and shell burning during the final stages of massive-star evolution. We propose prescriptions to account for these effects in the advanced phases of stellar evolution.

items.title: Alternative origins of polarity in compressively strained SrTiO3-RENiO3 capacitors
items.abstract: Since its original prediction 25 years ago, room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity in compressively strained SrTiO3 remains an ongoing pursuit. In this work, we investigate the structural, electrical, and electromechanical properties of highly strained epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors with rare earth nickelate electrodes. The SrTiO3 layers experience compressive strains up to −3% and exhibit pronounced tetragonality, comparable to that of bulk PbTiO3. Variable-temperature electrical measurements and room-temperature piezoresponse force microscopy reveal butterfly-shaped capacitance–voltage hysteresis and domain-like electromechanical response typical of ferroelectric materials. However, the overall behavior is inconsistent with a stable ferroelectric state. We therefore propose an alternative mechanism for the observed polarity in our samples based on spatially inhomogeneous internal fields. Our first-principles calculations show that such fields may arise from charge discontinuities between the formally charged NdNiO3 layers and charge-neutral SrTiO3 layers.

items.title: Probing $$\varvec{\Lambda }$$CDM-mimicking $$\varvec{f(Q)}$$ gravity model using gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences
items.abstract: Abstract The direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) is a very significant achievement in the history of physics and has opened a new window to probe the possible deviations of physics from that of general relativity (GR). In this work, we forecast constraints on the free parameter of an f ( Q ) gravity model that mimics a $$\Lambda $$ Λ CDM background at the level of cosmic expansion. We consider modified gravitational wave signals from inspiraling of compact binary systems such as binary black holes (BBH), binary neutron stars (BNS) and black hole neutron star binary (BBHNS) systems in the context of the f ( Q ) gravity model and perform parameter estimation for two future third-generation ground-based GW detectors, namely Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic explorer (CE), respectively. Our results show that both detectors can give tight constraints on the model parameter up to a significantly high redshift. These results show the potential of future GW observations to probe the deviations of the nature of GWs from that of GR within the framework of f ( Q ) gravity.

items.title: Density-wave order enhances the phonon thermal Hall effect in a trilayer nickelate
items.abstract: Ruddlesden--Popper nickelates have emerged as a promising platform for high-temperature superconductivity, yet the role of lattice degrees of freedom in their correlated normal state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the observation of a finite phonon thermal Hall effect in the trilayer nickelate La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$ at ambient pressure. Remarkably, the thermal Hall response is strongly enhanced below the density-wave transition at $T^*\approx140$ K, exhibiting two distinct plateaus in the thermal Hall resistivity. The characteristic energy scale extracted from the thermal Hall response ($\sim4.1$ meV) closely matches the magnon--phonon crossing span energy ($\sim3.2$ meV), pointing to magnon--phonon hybridization as the primary mechanism enhancing the thermal Hall effect. These results provide new insight into the interplay between lattice and spin excitations in nickelates, with implications for understanding both their superconductivity and the multiple possible origins of insulating thermal Hall signals.

items.title: Spin–torsion interaction and geodesic bending
items.abstract: Abstract The intrinsic spin of fermions induces torsion in spacetime, leading to an effective four-fermion interaction. This affects the bending of null and timelike geodesics inside a star with a spherically symmetric distribution of gravitationally dense fermionic matter of constant density. Our analysis shows an additional torsional contribution to the geodesic deflection, alongside the conventional curvature-induced effect. This change depends on the fermion number density, coupling constants of the different species of fermions with different chiralities, and the temperature of the matter distribution. We have shown that the torsion-induced corrections to null geodesic bending remains very small for both low- and high-mass white dwarfs, whereas significantly larger effects may arise in more compact astrophysical objects such as neutron stars.

items.title: Attosecond delay metrology beyond the photon coherence time with spectrally resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry
items.abstract: Abstract Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) interferometry enables delay estimation at the quantum precision limit but is traditionally constrained to path differences within the coherence time of the interfering photons. Here, we demonstrate single-shot path-delay sensing using spectrally resolved HOM interference, achieving a precision near the measurement Cramér–Rao bound over an operating range of approximately ±300 μm, removing the conventional dynamic-range limitation imposed by the photon coherence window. By extracting delay information from the spectral interference fringes of spectrally entangled photon pairs, we retain near-optimal sensitivity over an operational range exceeding the photon coherence time by over two orders of magnitude. Using one million detected photon pairs, we achieve a time-delay precision of 13 attosecond (4 nm), while real-time operation (at 1 Hz) with 2000 detected photons yields 330 attosecond (100 nm) precision. Because the estimator relies on fringe periodicity rather than absolute coincidence rates, the method is intrinsically robust to variations in interference visibility, eliminating the need for recalibration. As a practical demonstration, we measure the thickness of a nominally 300 μm transmissive target with nanometer-scale precision. These results mark a significant step towards deploying quantum-enhanced HOM interferometry for high-precision displacement sensing in real-world applications.

items.title: Evidence for the Moon and Sun shadows with cosmic rays at an average energy of 7 × 10 17 eV
items.abstract: Interactions of cosmic rays with the Moon and the Sun produce deficits in their arrival-direction distributions relative to an isotropic flux. Such shadows have been observed previously at energies between $10^{12}\,$eV and $10^{16}\,$eV. We report the first observation of the Moon and Sun shadows at cosmic-ray energies larger than about $10^{16}\,$eV (average energy of $7\times10^{17}\,$eV), using data collected by the Pierre Auger Observatory. We employ data from three detector arrays covering $3000\,\text{km}^2$, $27\,\text{km}^2$, and $2\,\text{km}^2$, with spacings of $1500\,\text{m}$, $750\,\text{m}$, and $433\,\text{m}$, respectively. The data amount to over 10.6 million events. The Moon and Sun shadows are detected with a combined significance of approximately $3σ$. These observations confirm the pointing accuracy of the Surface Detector of the Pierre Auger Observatory using celestial bodies. From the combined Sun and Moon shadows, we infer an overall angular resolution of $(0.59^{+0.15}_{-0.11})^\circ$.

items.title: Electrical control of valley hybridization in moiré quantum dots
items.abstract: The search for scalable, electrically controlled qubits remains a central challenge in quantum technology. We introduce gate-defined moiré quantum dots as a promising platform for valley-based qubits. Moiré engineering resolves the central conflict of valley physics: momentum-space separation protects the states, while the enlarged moiré length scale allows smooth gates to mix them controllably. Dot geometry and confinement strength program valley hybridization, while a displacement field controls detuning, providing two noncommuting electrostatic axes for qubit control.

items.title: Density-induced dark baryon conversion in Δ − admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
items.abstract: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $χ$ in cold, charge-neutral, $β$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $Δ(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $χ$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $Δ$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $χ$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_χ=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+Δ+χ$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$, and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_χ=1400$ MeV, $χ$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.

items.title: AT 2016blu: Accretion-powered Outbursts in a Luminous Blue Variable and Compact Object Binary
items.abstract: Abstract We present the first X-ray detection of the supernova (SN) impostor AT 2016blu in NGC 4559. AT 2016blu exhibited 27 detected quasiperiodic (∼113 day) outbursts between 2012 and 2026 June, presumably triggered by periastron passages in an eccentric binary system in which the primary is a ≳33 M ⊙ luminous blue variable (LBV). AT 2016blu was serendipitously observed by Chandra in 2001–2002, prior to its first documented outburst in 2012, but the stacked archival data show no X-ray detection. We monitored the source’s visual-wavelength variability around its predicted outburst time and triggered a Chandra Target of Opportunity (ToO) program in 2026 March, obtaining observations with detections over five closely spaced epochs. These data indicate an X-ray luminosity of log L X ≈ 38.64 ± 0.11 erg s −1 and an accretion rate of M ̇ ≳ 8 × 1 0 − 8 M ⊙ yr − 1 , consistent with the presence of a compact companion. We therefore conclude that AT 2016blu is the first known case of an LBV SN impostor where X-ray observations clearly favor intermittent accretion onto a compact object as the cause of the outbursts. Given that the system consists of a massive star and a compact companion, AT 2016blu is a high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB), similar to SN 2010da, although the donor star in SN 2010da is a red supergiant (RSG).

items.title: Frequency-domain extended-effective-source gravitational self-force for eccentric Schwarzschild orbits
items.abstract: Effective-source formulations provide a practical route to gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations when singular retarded fields cannot be handled directly mode by mode. Up to now, only frequency-domain first-order GSF for circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime was obtained with the effective-source method. We construct and implement a frequency-domain extended effective-source (EES) formulation for first-order Lorenz-gauge GSF on eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime. The central obstacle is that radial libration forces the physical puncture and effective source to switch between interior and exterior branches, limiting their differentiability and producing slow spectral convergence. We overcome this obstruction by analytically extending both branches across the libration region and solving the coupled Lorenz-gauge perturbation equations for the resulting smooth extended sources. This provides an end-to-end gravitational EES implementation for eccentric motion and validates a computational ingredient needed for extending frequency-domain effective-source calculations toward second order.

items.title: Composition gradients in sub-Neptunes: K2-18 b and TOI-270 d as case studies
items.abstract: Structure models of sub-Neptunes commonly assume purely adiabatic interiors with distinct layers of homogeneous composition. We assess how allowing for more complex interiors with composition gradients affects the inferred internal structure and bulk compositions of the sub-Neptunes K2-18,b and TOI-270,d. We compare purely adiabatic models with distinct layers against models that include composition gradients and stable non-convective regions. We present solutions that are consistent with the observed masses, radii, and atmospheric boundary conditions. Generally, interior degeneracy remains substantial even at a fixed mass and radius. We further find that composition gradients significantly increase the range of viable interior structures. For example, the maximum hydrogen--helium (H--He) mass fraction can increase significantly, by a factor of about three at a 1,bar temperature of 300,K and by a factor of about 10 at 600,K for K2-18,b. For TOI-270,d, the increase is generally more than an order of magnitude. Composition gradients additionally weaken parameter correlations. For K2-18,b and TOI-270,d, the Spearman rank correlation between the H--He and iron abundances drops from sim0.7 to sim0.3, with a similar weakening between the H--He abundance and the rock-to-iron mass ratio. However, other correlations, such as that between the H--He abundance and the water-to-rock mass ratio, persist or even strengthen and remain non-negligible. Purely adiabatic models underestimate the range of plausible compositions and overestimate the impact of more precise measurements, atmosphere models, and host-star constraints on a more accurate characterisation. We suggest that interior models of sub-Neptunes should by default include more complex interiors, such as composition gradients and non-convective regions, when using data for interpreting the planetary structure, formation, and evolution.

items.title: Nova shells in 3D. I. A catalog of integral field spectroscopic observations
items.abstract: Classical novae eject material during thermonuclear eruptions on the surface of accreting white dwarfs, forming expanding shells (the so-called nova remnants or nova shells). The physical structure and kinematics of nova shells shed light onto the eruption mechanism and binary interaction. Nova shells are typically characterized using direct imaging and spectroscopy, but their intrinsic 3D structure remains poorly constrained. The aim of this work is to present the first 3D catalog of nova shells based on integral field spectroscopic observations, allowing us to investigate the diversity of their physical structures beyond projection effects. We compiled integral-field spectroscopic observations of 19 nova shells obtained with MUSE at the VLT, complemented by new observations obtained with MEGARA at the GTC and WEAVE at the WHT. We constructed 3D visualizations of the emission lines of interest. The 3D visualizations of nova shells reveal a wide variety of structures, including ellipsoidal or spherical (round) shells, ring-like and bipolar features, and clumpy or irregular components. Many of these structures are not evident in two2D projections alone. Approximately 60% of the sample exhibits predominantly ellipsoidal or spherical shapes, while about 30% shows ring-like structures or is bipolar. Several objects show strong line-dependent morphological differences, with the iii or N ii emission lines tracing distinct kinematic components distinct from those in Hα. Compared with imaging studies, integral field spectroscopic observations reveal a larger fraction of bipolar or toroidal nova shells. Their physical structures differ considerably among different emission lines, highlighting distinct excitation mechanisms and physical properties within the ejecta. The comparison of the expansion velocities of nova shells on the plane of the sky and along the line of sight implies that their intrinsic aspect ratios are low, consistent with the conclusions derived from their projected aspect ratios.

items.title: Tracking a solar energetic eruption and associated energetic particles from the Sun to spacecraft
items.abstract: Solar energetic particles (SEPs) in the heliosphere are produced by flaring processes on the Sun or shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Electrons in particular are regularly detected remotely as electromagnetic radiation (X-rays or radio emission) --- which they generate through various processes --- as well as in situ by spacecraft monitoring the Sun and the heliosphere. We aim to combine remote-sensing and in situ observations of an energetic solar eruption to link energetic processes in the solar corona to energetic particles observed in situ in the heliosphere. This will be done using the tools developed in the Horizon Europe SOLER project. We investigated a solar energetic eruption at the Sun together with its associated signatures of accelerated electrons observed at radio and X-ray wavelengths and combined these remote observations to in situ particles observed by spacecraft on 10 March 2024. These observations were combined with a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) model of the solar corona in order to make the remote to in situ connections. We observe a high-energy SEP event at multiple spacecraft (>25 MeV protons and 1 MeV electrons), despite the event being associated with a slow white-light CME. Remote observations of the Sun show that the event was associated with a fast, large-scale coronal wave (1400 km/s) and multiple regions where electrons are accelerated around this large-scale wave observed as type II radio bursts. In addition, we observe a strong coronal dimming away from the main flaring region, providing evidence of field lines being opened onto interplanetary space and dislocated from the flare site. Although we observe a slow, co-temporal CME in white light, we show that an expanding extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) dome corresponding to the upper portions of the large-scale coronal wave is likely to steepen into a shock, as shown by the presence of multiple type II radio bursts on the surface of the dome. The EUV dome, and thus a coronal shock, is a likely source of energetic particles since it is the main feature intersecting magnetic field lines connecting to spacecraft. The SEPs observed in this study also have consistently hard spectral indices at two different locations.

items.title: Breaking the symmetry: X-ray polarization from a spreading layer on a tilted weakly magnetized neutron star
items.abstract: When modeling the emission from an X-ray binary system, we often assume that the rotational axis of the compact object is aligned with that of the binary system. While often considered irrelevant for spectroscopic observations, the orientation of the binary system is crucial for polarimetric properties. With the recent advent of X-ray polarimetric observations enabled by the ( Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer indications of a possible misalignment of the neutron star's rotational axis with respect to the binary axis have been reported. Following these indications, we present an analytical model for the polarimetric properties of emission arising from a spreading layer on an inclined weakly magnetized neutron star (WMNS). We discuss the expected polarimetric properties and study the impact of the geometrical parameters of the system on the polarization of WMNS emission. We compare our results with those for aligned systems. Finally, we discuss applications of the model to recent and upcoming X-ray polarimetric observations with and mention the suggestions for further development of the model.

items.title: A neural-network model for finding correlations in astrochemical space
items.abstract: The detection of new interstellar molecules is a central objective of astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field over the past decade has been the dramatic increase in both the number and diversity of detected species. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing models, we developed a machine-learning pipeline, in line with recent approaches reported in the literature, to establish relationships between molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in the prototypical dark cloud TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. In this work, these representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17 and 0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29 and 0.59, all expressed in logarithmic units of the column density, together with coefficients of determination of 0.88 and 0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets, respectively. The latent vectors learned by the model represent a rich mathematical object that captures not only the underlying chemical relations but also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory allowed us to identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. Furthermore, by training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond the accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.

items.title: Faint companions to hot stars. Spectroscopic detection sensitivity and implications for survey design
items.abstract: Searches for black holes in binaries must distinguish genuinely dark companions from faint luminous stars. This is particularly challenging for massive hot stars. Their masses can exceed those of typical stellar black holes, while their spectra contain only a few broad lines. We developed a Fourier-domain method that converts isolated, broadened spectral lines into calibrated constraints on faint companions. In Fourier space, Doppler shifts are encoded in the phase, while the line profile defines a smooth amplitude envelope. A faint secondary introduces an oscillatory perturbation to the otherwise smooth log-amplitude. Expanding this perturbation to first order in the secondary-to-primary line-depth ratio, α, allows it to be profiled against the smooth baseline in a likelihood-ratio test with the single-star model. Because the model is analytic and nearly linear, its sensitivity can be evaluated transparently for individual spectra and at survey scale. It can be applied to single or multiple epochs without requiring full spectral disentangling. At small velocity separation v, the companion signal becomes degenerate with the smooth single-star profile. For the Fourier log-amplitude, the fractional uncertainty scales as Δα/α ∝ v^ -4 . If the primary velocity is known, the Fourier phase provides a more favorable detection channel whose sensitivity scales as v^-1. We demonstrated the method on archival FEROS spectra of the massive binary CPD-41^̧irc7742. We detected the known secondary in He,I 6678 Å and obtained a stringent nondetection in He,II 5411 Å, where its contribution is expected to be negligible. The same framework yields local detection efficiencies as functions of line-depth ratio, velocity separation, noise, and instrumental setup. These can be combined across lines, epochs, and targets to construct survey selection functions for spectroscopic black-hole searches, including those enabled by SDSS-V and Gaia.

items.title: J-PAS: Exploring the connection between local environment and the triggering of bursty star formation in extreme emission line galaxies
items.abstract: Extreme emission line galaxies (EELGs) are typically compact low-mass systems undergoing intense bursts of star formation whose spectra are dominated by very strong nebular emission lines. Their physical conditions resemble those of galaxies in the early Universe, making them ideal analogues for investigating the processes that regulate star formation, feedback, and chemical enrichment at low redshift. Our objective was to characterise the local environment of a sample of EELGs identified in the J-PAS survey in order to determine whether their extreme properties are associated with the presence of nearby companions, as expected if galaxy–galaxy interactions were the main trigger of the burst. Using the J-PAS internal data release, we analysed a sample of 917 EELGs in the redshift range of 0.03łesssim złesssim0.9, previously selected using photometric and machine-learning methods over an area of ∼30 deg2$. We employed the pair probability function formalism, which combines the full photometric redshift probability distributions of galaxy pairs, to statistically identify companions within projected separations up to 200, and velocity differences up to $500, . Stellar masses, star formation rates, dust attenuation, and metallicity estimates were derived for the EELGs and their companions through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting using , and Monte Carlo simulations were performed to correct for projection and completeness effects. -1 CIGALE The derived average pair fraction of the EELGs is f_ = 0.162^ pair +0.048 _ -0.033 , indicating that only ∼16% of the sample has detectable companions, a value lower than the observed average for other star-forming galaxies within the adopted limits. When companions are identified within the sensitivity and stellar-mass completeness limits of J-PAS, they tend to be more massive and to show higher SED-based metallicity estimates than the EELGs, suggesting that the latter are typically low-mass components in asymmetric pairs. However, lower-mass companions below these limits may remain undetected. Finally, no statistically significant correlation was found between the equivalent widths of the O III $,łambda5007$, Hβ, and Hα emission lines and the projected separation to the detected companions within the limits of the J-PAS data.

items.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of the binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
items.abstract: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. As it produces radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed most likely to be an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital-inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of -(6.8-9.6) -13 -1 when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD (1.4 M_⊙). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than 1.4 M_⊙ if the measured period derivative exceeds -9.6 ̊m s,s^ -13 -1 . However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a 1.0-1.6 M_⊙ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of -(4.9-13.5) ̊m s,s^ -13 -1 . In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of 1.35-1.5 M_⊙. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be 0.006 when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

items.title: On-chip multimode vibrational strong coupling of polar dielectrics within hybrid metal–dielectric nanocavities
items.abstract: Abstract Vibrational strong coupling (VSC) provides a powerful route to manipulate energy exchange and polaritonic energy landscapes through the hybridization of vibrational modes with optical resonances, offering significant potential for ultrasensitive infrared spectroscopy, biochemical sensing, and the control of chemical reactivity. Plasmonic nanocavities can achieve strong confinement, but their substantial ohmic losses often broaden the optical resonance and obscure the intrinsic evolution of hybrid branches. In contrast, low-loss dielectric platforms generally suffer from insufficient field overlap with the vibrational medium. Moreover, in dual-channel or mode-selective architectures, coupling behavior is highly sensitive to localized hotspots and the precise placement of the active layer. Consequently, achieving simultaneous and robust access to both transverse-optical (TO) and longitudinal-optical (LO) channels remains challenging, especially within systems that require continuous tunability and fabrication simplicity. Here, we experimentally demonstrate multimode VSC in a hybrid metal–dielectric nanocavity, where the optical field is strongly confined inside the SiO 2 layer. Owing to the coexistence of in-plane and out-of-plane electric field components in the vibrational layer, the same photonic mode can simultaneously couple to both the TO and LO phonon responses of SiO 2 . The measured Fourier transform infrared spectra agree well with full-wave simulations and are quantitatively reproduced by an effective three-oscillator model. By varying the thickness of SiO 2 , we further reveal the relationship between the coupling strength, the polar molecular layer thickness, and the effective mode volume. The proposed architecture also shows good robustness against the fabrication distortions, establishing a low-loss and experimentally feasible platform for multimode VSC in polar dielectrics.

items.title: THE ”BIG G” CRISIS: The relationship between the magnitude of the discrepancy in the ‘Big G’ values and the critical acceleration of the MOND.
items.abstract: Measurements of the gravitational constant G conducted at the world’s leading laboratories contradict one another and diverge in an unexplained manner. We solved the inverse problem: based on the known experimental “Big G” discrepancies, we calculated the magnitude of the hidden acceleration. The hidden acceleration coincided in order of magnitude with the critical acceleration of MOND, which is driven by the gravity of the entire universe. This fact refutes the seemingly chaotic spread of G values and calls into question the very possibility of using Newton’s local equation without accounting for the gravity of the entire universe. Is this an intriguing coincidence, or a direct consequence of the fact that all research groups calculated “Big G” from the local gravity equation without accounting for the acceleration caused by the gravity of the universe? Discrepancies were not caused by instrument errors, but by the omnipresent gravity of the universe, which was not accounted for in the calculations. Paradoxically, it was precisely the discrepancies that became the most valuable result of all the G measurements. In their pursuit of “Big G,” the experimenters missed a scientific discovery. A new law of nature was right within their grasp, yet they mistook it for equipment malfunction. Dear metrologists! Hidden within your vast archives lies the most monumental discovery in the field of gravity since Newton! Don’t let it slip away! Remember: the number of fundamental laws of nature is limited—there aren’t enough to go around!

items.title: The idea of innovation in Restoration science and medicine
items.abstract: This article traces the language of innovation through mid-seventeenth-century science and medicine, focusing on controversies surrounding the Royal Society and the proposed Society of Chymical Physicians. 'Innovation' in early modern England was primarily a term of abuse directed against the alleged enemies of the church or state. Following the Civil Wars, defenders of Aristotelian and Galenic learning used the term to implicate the new philosophers and chymical physicians in the radicalism of the previous decades. In response, such thinkers as Walter Charleton, Robert Boyle, John Evelyn, Thomas Sprat and Marchamont Nedham sought to rehabilitate the concept. They aligned innovation with the new experimental philosophy and, crucially, distinguished innovation in philosophy from innovation in divinity. Freed from the stigma of heresy and sedition, the concept could serve rather than undermine the restored church. Innovation, then, was secularized for religious ends: to reconcile the new philosophy with ecclesiastical authority and Christian doctrine. But the alliance between philosophical innovation and religious orthodoxy remained precarious, not least because the boundaries of orthodoxy were far from settled. The debates over innovation reflect competing efforts to define the cultural politics of the new philosophy at a moment of profound religious, political and intellectual contestation.

items.title: Early Martian Habitability and Directional Lithopanspermia Across the Solar System
items.abstract: Abstract Whether life arose independently on habitable worlds or dispersed through interplanetary exchange remains unresolved. Here we investigate early Mars as a potential biological nursery by integrating comparative planetary thermal evolution, subsurface aqueous habitability, impact-driven ejecta transport and probabilistic biological survival. Models spanning 4.4 billion years indicate potentially habitable pore-water environments on both Mars and Earth at 4.4 Ga, with mean eligible water temperatures of 35.84 °C and 42.34 °C, respectively, at 4.2 Ga. Simulated 10-Myr material-transfer fractions are 2.588% for Mars→Earth, 1.523% for Mars→Venus and 0.182% for Earth→Mars, yielding an inward-to-reverse transfer ratio of 14.23 (95% interval: 11.41–17.99). Conditional biological-establishment simulations yield a mean Mars→Earth probability of 0.2465%, although outcomes remain strongly dependent on uncertain survival parameters. Exploratory outward-transfer simulations identify rare Mars→Jovian-orbit encounters (0.07% within 0.05 AU), without establishing delivery to individual moons. A prior-dependent Bayesian comparison does not presently favor Martian biological ancestry over independent terrestrial origins. These findings identify directional asymmetries in modeled material exchange while demonstrating that successful biological dispersal remains unverified. Early Mars therefore represents a testable, rather than established, source of potential biological exchange across the Solar System.

items.title: A probabilistic model of visual segmentation explains early visual cortical dynamics
items.abstract: Neural dynamics are a central feature of biological neural systems. In the visual cortex, the functional role of neural dynamics is poorly understood, particularly for static stimuli. The statistics of still natural images have long been used by models that successfully predict firing in early visual cortex; those models assume that neurons represent inferences about latent image features, but often ignore the dynamics of said inference. Here, we test if inferential dynamics in images explain visual-cortical dynamics. To do so, we present a biologically plausible model of cortical computation which assumes that the inference of features is coupled with inference about how those features are organized into meaningful parts, a function also known as segmentation. Given an input image, our model iterates between inferring the features and the segments, through recurrence and feedback, thus inducing dynamics in the neural representation of features. For these neural dynamics, we derive theoretical and exact predictions. Our model predicts both gain and variability in evoked responses to natural images, and we show that it captures classical single-neuron experimental findings such as gain dynamics and variability decay during stimulus presentation. The model also predicts that those dynamics are organized around inferred segment structure and more heterogeneous than previously thought, reflecting the complexity of inference for natural scenes. Finally, our analytical formulation provides a clear interpretation of our results. Insights from our normative model could generalize to segmentation problems in other experimental modalities, and help address the cost of inference in artificial networks with iterative computation.

items.title: IC-GNN: Modeling Individualized Brain Community Organization for Disease Prediction
items.abstract: Brain networks exhibit modular organization, where community structures vary substantially across individuals and diseases. Understanding these individual differences is crucial for advancing both basic neuroscience research and precision medicine. However, widely used predefined group-level brain atlases often overlook this heterogeneity. While individualized functional parcellations capture subject-specific variability in community boundaries, they often require lengthy scan times to achieve fine-grained resolution and complicate cross-subject comparisons. To address this trade-off and investigate how individualized community organization captures disease-associated changes across individuals, we propose IC-GNN, an atlas-anchored model that forms distinct, individualized functional communities directly over atlas-defined brain regions. IC-GNN derives discrete, individualized multiscale communities from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data, refines community-guided connections, and adapts shared regional weights to each subject's community context to enable both individualized modeling and group-level comparisons. Across more than 30,000 participants from ABIDE (autism spectrum disorder), ADNI (Alzheimer's disease), and the UK Biobank (depression), IC-GNN achieves the highest performance compared with 15 baseline methods. We further demonstrate that these individualized communities are reproducible within scans and across sessions, and carry predictive power on their own. Furthermore, IC-GNN identifies disease-related shifts in community organization that align with established literature, highlighting a promising approach for modeling individualized community structure for disease prediction and biomarker discovery.

items.title: A TESS Disappearing Act: The Vanishing Transits of TOI-2535 b
items.abstract: Planetary transits require a fortuitous alignment between a planet's orbit and our line of sight, but dynamical interactions can render this geometric coincidence only temporary. We report the discovery of the hot Jupiter TOI-2535 b, the first confirmed planet orbiting a single star whose transits have been directly observed to disappear. Over seven years of photometry from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), the planet's transit chord traversed and eventually moved off the stellar disk entirely, with an impact parameter changing at the rate of $\dot{b} = 0.16\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The transit mid-times also show significant departures of $\pm 6$ hours from a linear ephemeris. Joint modeling of the transit timing and duration variations (TTVs and TDVs) and NEID radial-velocity data indicates the presence of a nearby, mutually inclined ($i_\mathrm{mut} \gtrsim 5^\circ$) planetary perturber, with the TDV being primarily due to precession of the planets' orbital planes. Our dynamical modeling reveals that the perturber is likely of Saturn-mass or greater and in a mean-motion resonance with TOI-2535 b, making this an unusual system that contains two short-period giant planets. The TDVs measured for TOI-2535 b represent one of the most extreme examples of planet-planet interactions driving orbital evolution on human timescales.

items.title: The climate and potential habitability of a warm and oxygenated Mars
items.abstract: We present the first 3-D Global Climate Model simulations of an oxygen-rich, terraformed Mars. Assuming an O2-CO2 atmosphere, with additional warming from a well-mixed grey gas, we study (1) how surface temperatures change with atmospheric pressure and grey gas opacity, and (2) how temperature, pressure, and other effects limit life as oxygen builds up. We neglect the climate effects of dust and the water cycle, as well as possible soil-chemistry and nutrient limits to life. We find that (1) increasing grey gas opacity and increasing atmospheric pressure both moderate day-night temperature swings, but only slightly reduce seasonal temperature swings. Climate remains harsher in the Southern mid-latitudes relative to the Northern hemisphere. (2) For an atmospheric pressure of 30 hPa (5 times its present-day value), temperatures on Mars would be consistent with lichen and moss, followed at 60 hPa by forests (initially in the Hellas Basin). However, creating a human-breathable atmosphere through photosynthesis alone, at the oxygen production rates of biomes on Earth today, would take at least thousands of years, and require more oxygen than can be made via photosynthesis of known CO2 reserves on Mars alone (unless CO2 is recycled).

items.title: Cryohydrologic Flow and Pingo Formation Within Freezing Impact Melts in Occator Crater, Ceres
items.abstract: Ceres is a volatile-rich dwarf planet in the asteroid belt and a potential relict ocean world. It exhibits surface features indicative of subsurface brine activity, particularly within Occator Crater. High-resolution imagery from NASA's Dawn Mission reveals landslides, gullies, carbonate faculae, and mound-like features resembling terrestrial pingos on the floor of Occator Crater. Some of these landforms have been hypothesized to form from water, either from the ascent of deep crustal brines or from the freezeout of impact melt. Here, we test the hypothesis that pingo-like features can be formed via the freezing of shallow impact melts. We simulate the heat transfer and groundwater flow dynamics of a freezing impact melt deposit on the floor of Occator Crater. We test a comprehensive parameter space of regolith physical and material properties relevant to the cerean environment. We find that impact melt freezinf produces pressure gradients sufficient to drive hydrologic flow within the melt matrix and could transport fluids to the near surface through hydraulic fracturing. For most of the parameter space tested, water volumes delivered to pingo candidates on the surface meet or exceed those likely required for pingo formation. Analogous hydrologic processes may be important in the shallow subsurface of other regions of Occator Crater and Ceres at large as well as other ice-rich planetary bodies.

items.title: Beyond the Fast Rotators: A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Substellar Weather
items.abstract: Atmospheric variability provides a unique window into the three-dimensional structure, dynamics, and evolution of brown dwarf and giant exoplanet atmospheres. Recent JWST time-resolved spectroscopic observations have revealed complex wavelength-dependent variability, offering unprecedented insights into cloud structures, thermal perturbations, and atmospheric chemistry. However, existing programs have focused primarily on individual benchmarks and specific scientific questions, resulting in heterogeneous spectral and temporal coverage and leaving important regions of the substellar population underexplored, particularly across a broad range of rotation periods, spectral types, and viewing geometries. A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury program could systematically investigate substellar weather across a diverse, well-characterized population. By combining broad infrared spectroscopic coverage with observations spanning multiple rotations and strategically selected epochs, this program would constrain the contributions of different physical mechanisms while investigating how atmospheric structures depend on rotation, viewing geometry, and fundamental physical properties. Extended monitoring would also improve rotational-period determinations and reveal how atmospheric features evolve from rotation to rotation and over longer timescales. This coordinated effort would provide a consistently designed and uniformly processed dataset of time-resolved spectra and variability diagnostics, enabling population-level comparisons, testing predictions from three-dimensional circulation models, and establishing a framework for interpreting the atmospheric diversity and evolution of brown dwarfs and directly imaged giant exoplanets.

items.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
items.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation, effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation. Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation. Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories. Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2-15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b at 4.3 $μ$m. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

items.title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head
items.abstract: Attention, the core of language models, is a digital calculation over tokens: an exponential selects them, a division normalizes and a positional code sets the order. We show that attention can instead emerge from the synchronization of a receiver with its context tokens. Each past token is an oscillator whose state carries its content and whose frequency drifts with its age. The present token selects them by content, aligning an antenna with its query, and by position, setting the frequency of a receiver with its dial. Solving Kuramoto's problem for this receiver yields an attention layer in closed form with two phases: above a critical coupling set by the context, the receiver locks and its weights normalize; below it, it stays silent and its weights sum to less than one. Trained networks use both phases to select, abstain and count, fail where the theory predicts and keep reading far beyond the training length. Each part of attention finds its place in one device, a radio head: it tunes in to what to hear and when, and stays silent when nothing relevant is on air.

items.title: Near-Ultraviolet and Optical Observations of the White Dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 Reveal Variable Periodicity in its Transiting Debris System
items.abstract: We observed the transiting debris disk system around the white dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 using the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) in 2025 October, obtaining near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectroscopy with STIS over five consecutive HST orbits. Our abundance analysis supports the accretion of a chondritic body. We complemented our HST program with 16 days of optical time-series photometry beginning in 2025 October, which reveal variable periodicity and rapidly evolving transit morphology. Previous monitoring by TESS during Sectors 4 and 31 confirmed a predominant, stable transit orbital period, $P_{\rm A} = 9.937$ hr, along with a second, transient period, $P_{\rm B} = 11.2$ hr. Our 2025 autumn light curves show transits are dominated by $P_{\rm B} = 11.17$ hr with $P_{\rm A}$ initially appearing as a weaker, secondary feature and eventually returning to predominance. We also identify a candidate transit period of 7.64 hr during the final days of the 2025 autumn campaign, although its significance and persistence remain uncertain. We add simultaneous $ugr$ light curves collected with ULTRACAM in 2024 November that are dominated by $P_{\rm A}$ and show no significant color term. We further compare the transit depths in optical photometry concurrent with our NUV observations, again measuring a lack of transit-dependent extinction except during the fifth HST orbit where a reddening term may arise. The observed variable periodicity and potentially changing color behavior illuminate ongoing dynamical processes, namely collisions, and demonstrate the opportunity for studying dust physics in real time at white dwarf debris disks.

items.title: Searching for Planets around Altair with JWST/NIRcam
items.abstract: Altair (alpha Aql) is one of the nearest stars to the Sun at 5.13 pc and its age has recently been revised to 88+/-10 Myr, making it one of the youngest stars in the Solar neighborhood. This makes Altair a compelling target for high-contrast direct imaging searches for giant planets. We present two epochs of simultaneous F444W and F200W MASK430R JWST/NIRCam coronagraphic imaging observations. After post-processing, these data achieve F444W contrast levels of 2 x 10^-6 at 1" (5.1 au), 1.5 x 10^-7 at 2" (10.3 au), and a few x 10^-8 beyond 4"(20 au). Using the Sonora Flame Skimmer models, this corresponds to sub-Jupiter mass sensitivity beyond 5 au and sub-Saturn mass sensitivity beyond 10 au. We identified several candidate point sources in the field in the first epoch data. Second epoch observations confirmed that none of the candidates were co-moving with Altair and their colors are consistent with background stars. Altair has no known companions, no detected debris disk, and is not associated with any stellar association. Despite this, its youth and proximity ensure it will remain a high-priority target for future high-contrast imaging observations. We additionally discuss Altair as a potential reference star for future observations, presenting measurements of background sources in the field and showing that Altair will remain at least a few arcsec from background stars over the next 10-20 years, making it a reliable reference target for upcoming imaging campaigns including the Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument.

items.title: Planetary material is a major source of hydrogen in helium-atmosphere white dwarfs
items.abstract: Many white dwarfs with helium-dominated atmospheres show traces of hydrogen in their spectra. On average, the total mass of hydrogen within their convective envelopes increases with age, but there is no consensus on the origin of such hydrogen. Hypotheses include upward diffusion from hidden reservoirs deep within the envelope, or accretion, alongside heavier elements, of planetary material. We construct a simple model that includes both pathways, and test it using two independent samples of helium-atmosphere DB white dwarfs from the DESI and SDSS spectroscopic surveys, selected to have Gaia colours BP-RP > -0.25, corresponding roughly to 10000 < $T_{\rm eff}$ < 19000K. We find that at least $22 \pm 2$ per cent of the helium-atmosphere white dwarfs with detectable hydrogen must have accreted some of it from their planetary systems, via ices, hydrated minerals or atmospheres. We thus demonstrate that planetary hydrogen is a necessary ingredient to explain the spectral evolution of white dwarfs as a population, rather than only extreme hydrogen-enriched cases.

items.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
items.abstract: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded. Furthermore, we find a positive trend in occurrence with metallicity below the mass-ratio desert, but a negative trend above. The desert therefore separates two distinct populations, plausibly two formation channels, that each scale with stellar mass: the lightest stellar-like companions of K stars ($\sim13 \, M_{jup}$) are less massive than the heaviest planet-like companions of B stars ($\sim27, M_{jup}$), which continue well beyond the deuterium-burning limit. Mass-ratio, not mass, is therefore the physically meaningful boundary between planets and their stellar-like counterparts.

items.title: Mars Seed: A Reference Architecture for Biomanufacturing Habitats from Martian Resources
items.abstract: Human exploration of Mars will require enormous quantities of materials for the first crewed missions and substantially more for permanent habitation, making flexible and scalable technologies for in situ resource utilization (ISRU), including biological ISRU, of significant interest. However, no existing mission architecture quantitatively evaluates whether in situ biomanufacturing can realistically deliver materials at the scales required for human settlement. Here, we present Mars Seed, an end-to-end reference architecture for using biomanufacturing to produce bioplastics at scale entirely from in situ resources on Mars. We provide a complete analysis of a space bioprocess in which feedstocks are generated entirely from Martian resources, converted biologically into polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) bioplastic, and purified to produce material suitable for constructing human habitats. We show that the upfront power and upmass costs of deploying the equipment required for this bioprocess are recovered within two synodic periods relative to Earth-shipped alternatives. Further, because the process relies entirely on feedstocks sourced from Martian materials, production can continue until equipment failure without requiring additional materials from Earth, enabling scalable conversion of local resources into useful materials. Mars Seed demonstrates that biological ISRU can be mass- and power-competitive with Earth-shipped alternatives, establishing biomanufacturing as a practical component of Mars mission architecture rather than an aspirational capability.

items.title: Kinematic Signatures of Stellar Flybys in Protoplanetary Discs
items.abstract: Recent high-resolution molecular line observations of protoplanetary discs have revealed large-scale non-Keplerian features in the gas kinematics of several systems, which can be interpreted as signatures of warps in the disc. Warps can arise from a range of physical mechanisms, and it remains unclear whether the observed kinematic residuals can be uniquely attributed to warping, or to different competing effects. Stellar flybys are one such mechanism capable of both warping a disc and directly perturbing its kinematics. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we study the evolution of protoplanetary discs perturbed by inclined and coplanar stellar flybys, focusing on timescales of several thousand years after periastron rather than the immediate aftermath of the encounter. We find that inclined stellar flybys initially induce warping and twisting in the disc, but that this geometric perturbation is damped on a timescale set by the disc viscosity. Despite this geometric damping, synthetic ALMA observations of the CO kinematics show that complex non-Keplerian spiral features persist in the velocity residuals long after the warped morphology has relaxed, including in coplanar encounters where no warp is ever induced. Fitting these residuals with a simple warped-disc model, the degree of warping in the disc is systematically overestimated. We therefore conclude that kinematic residuals alone are insufficient to establish that a disc is warped, as flybys induce kinematic complexity independently of warps. We further show that scattered light observations provide an independent diagnostic, showing spiral arms and lateral asymmetries.

items.title: A two-phase model of galaxy formation: IV. Seeding and growing supermassive black holes in dark matter halos
items.abstract: Abstract We present a theoretical framework for seeding and growing supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in dark matter halos along their assembly histories. Seeds are bred out of Pop-III stars formed during the first collapse of pristine gas in mini-halos that have reached the H2-cooling limit, modulated by UV radiation from star formation and dynamical heating from fast halo assembly. Such breeding persists until the enrichment of the intergalactic medium (IGM) enables Pop-II stars to form. Post-seeding growth of black holes (BHs) is driven by distinct channels, starting with episodic super-Eddington accretion associated with nuclear bursts induced by global disturbances of galaxies, followed by sustained sub-Eddington accretion via capturing sub-clouds formed in self-gravitating gas clouds (SGCs) in halos of fast assembly, and ending with merger-dominated, quiescent growth. We implement the model in subhalo merger trees to build a coherent framework to follow SMBH-galaxy-halo co-evolution across the whole history and structural hierarchy. BH seeds are bred with a broad mass spectrum of $M_{\rm \scriptscriptstyle BH}= 10$–105 M⊙ at z ≈ 20–30 in mini-halos with masses of 105–108 M⊙. Nuclear bursts provide the key condition for seeds to grow into SMBHs. The $M_{\rm \scriptscriptstyle BH}$-M* relation is a multi-piece, redshift-dependent function shaped by the interplay among different growth channels. Our model predictions are broadly consistent with existing observations; in particular, a population of BHs reminiscent of ‘little red dots’ (LRDs) discovered by JWST naturally results from the seeding and growing processes. Potential future tests of the model are discussed.
