items.title: Dark monopoles, bounds on hidden sectors, and cosmological implications
items.abstract: Hidden sectors are a generic prediction of string theory compactifications and result in a promising landscape for dark matter model building. We consider the case of hidden sector magnetic monopoles produced via a thermal phase transition in the early Universe and subsequently diluted by pair annihilation. We show that for symmetry-breaking scales $\gtrsim 100\, \text{PeV}$, the monopole abundance is unacceptably high, overclosing the Universe. Our bounds are robust against variations in the initial fraction of energy density deposited in the hidden sector, exhibiting only a weak power-law dependence on this quantity. The bound is substantially tightened in the case of multiple hidden sectors. The standard cosmology may only be recovered if one of the following is true: the hidden sector(s) are non-existent, the hidden sectors have no monopoles with symmetry-breaking scale above 100 PeV, the maximum temperature of each monopole-producing hidden sector after reheating is below its symmetry-breaking scale, or the monopole abundance is diluted during a period of early matter domination.

items.title: Signatures of Lorentz violation in the bright ring for Sgr A* images from radiatively inefficient accretion flows
items.abstract: Abstract We have investigated the effects of Lorentz violation (LV) on the bright ring in Sgr A* images illuminated by the 230 GHz thermal synchrotron emission from radiatively inefficient accretion flows around a rotating LV black hole within the low-energy Hořava gravity framework. Our results reveal that the LV parameter reduces the bright ring diameter yet increases its width, luminosity, azimuthal asymmetry and orientation angle. A higher spin parameter strengthens the LV-induced effects on the bright ring properties. Increasing disk thickness reduces the ring diameter and enhances the LV parameter’s effects on this diameter. The ring width shows no systematic dependence on the disk thickness. These quantities of the bright ring display similar trends against the black hole spin and the LV parameter for the rotating LV black hole. Using EHT observational data of Sgr A*, we find that, at fixed disk thickness, the parameter-space map illustrates that the bounded range of the LV parameter first broadens and then contracts with the growing black hole spin, and shifts toward smaller LV parameter values. In addition, the LV parameter narrows the bounded range of black hole spin: negative LV parameter values shift this range to a higher spin, while positive values shift it to a lower spin. Finally, we probe effects of the LV parameter on the peak position value and the width of the primary image and the $$n=1$$ n = 1 photon ring for the rotating LV black hole. The peak positions and their widths nearly always decrease with the LV parameter. The peak position differences for various LV parameters are more pronounced for a purely Keplerian accretion flow. In addition, the primary image and the $$n=1$$ n = 1 photon ring produced by purely radially free-falling flows are broader than their counterparts generated by purely Keplerian flows.

items.title: Long-term 3+1 simulations of primordial black hole formation during radiation domination
items.abstract: We develop an efficient three-dimensional numerical-relativity framework for primordial black-hole (PBH) formation from superhorizon curvature perturbations in a radiation-dominated Universe. We implement flux-conservative relativistic hydrodynamics in the adaptive-mesh-refinement code \textsc{GRChombo} and introduce a cosmologically scaled Gamma-driver that allows the cosmic-time step to grow in proportion to the scale factor. For a representative long-term simulation, the scaled driver preserves the apparent-horizon mass evolution and constraint behavior while reducing the number of coarse-level advances by a factor of approximately $94$ relative to the standard driver. We also construct a conformal-time version of the moving-puncture gauge as an independent check. Applying the framework to a spherical Gaussian curvature profile, we find a collapse threshold $0.79578 < μ_c < 0.79580$ and a critical exponent $γ\simeq 0.3559$, consistent with previous spherically symmetric results. We further fit the late-time PBH mass growth to the Zel'dovich--Novikov accretion law, demonstrating that the code can follow both near-critical collapse and long-term post-formation evolution in three dimensions. The framework provides a foundation for future studies of PBH formation beyond spherical symmetry.

items.title: Perturbative solutions for the bumblebee field in a Schwarzschild background
items.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of a vector field subject to a Lorentz-violating quartic potential on a fixed Schwarzschild background. We analyze the equilibrium configuration of the field and its linear perturbations. We show that the equilibrium solution and spherically symmetric perturbations are governed by a quadratic function whose properties determine their qualitative behavior. By requiring the background field to be real and finite, we derive bounds on the allowed parameters and identify critical cases in which the monopole perturbations become enhanced. We further derive asymptotic expressions for multipole perturbations near the event horizon and at spatial infinity.

items.title: Sustained macroscopic coherence in a superradiant diamond maser under ambient conditions
items.abstract: Abstract Superradiant laser or maser provides a route to sustain macroscopic coherence of many photons and a large ensemble of emitters. Its realization, however, is mostly in gaseous atomic systems, where the number of emitters is relatively small. Solids can accommodate a large number of emitters, but the complex environments can rapidly break the macroscopic coherence and therefore stringent conditions like extremely low temperature are usually required. Here we realize a superradiant diamond maser under ambient conditions, in which optical pumping sustains long-lived coherence among about 10^14 nitrogen-vacancy centre spins with coherence time (2.1 ms) much longer than the spin dephasing time (5.7 us) and the cavity photon lifetime (0.66 us). Continuous-wave emission reaches an output power of -52.3 dBm, corresponding to an intracavity occupation of approximately 10^9 microwave photons.By tuning the pump and cavity conditions, we observe continuous-wave masing, periodic amplitude modulation and sequences of superradiant bursts, which are attributed, correspondingly, to macroscopic spin coherence synchronized at a fixed frequency, a synchronized limit cycle with a frequency comb, and unsynchronized superradiant transients. This work establishes a new platform for exploring macroscopic quantum coherence, with potential applications in quantum metrology and bright quantum light sources.

items.title: Updated upper limits on the isotropic gravitational-wave background from the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA fourth observing run through April 2025
items.abstract: We report results from a search for an isotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background using data collected by the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA Collaboration. The analysis uses data from the first observing run through April 1, 2025, during the fourth observing run. New frequency-domain cuts are implemented to address a class of non-stationary spectral noise features that were not effectively identified and mitigated by existing data-quality checks in past analyses. Consequently, previously analyzed data from the fourth observing run are re-processed with the updated cuts. We find no evidence for a stochastic background signal and place upper limits on the gravitational-wave energy density. In particular, for a background following a power law with spectral index 2/3 as predicted by inspiralling compact binaries, we find $Ω_\mathrm{GW}(25\,\mathrm{Hz}) \leq 2.0 \times 10^{-9}$, while scale-invariant backgrounds are constrained to $Ω_\mathrm{GW}(25\,\mathrm{Hz}) \leq 2.8 \times 10^{-9}$, both at the 95\% credible level for a log-uniform prior on $Ω_\mathrm{GW}$. Relative to the constraints from previous data recomputed with the new frequency-domain cuts, these limits improve by a factor of 1.4. We also update bounds on alternative gravity scenarios predicting non-standard polarization modes, and we verify that correlated magnetic noise sources remain below the sensitivity of this search. Combining these observational constraints with population models of compact binary coalescences informed by the latest gravitational-wave transient catalog, GWTC-5.0, we predict the amplitude of the compact binary background to be $Ω_\mathrm{CBC}(25\,\mathrm{Hz}) = 6.3^{+5.0}_{-2.2} \times 10^{-10}$ at the 90\% credible level.

items.title: Impact of gaps on noise and signal parameter inference
items.abstract: Gravitational-wave data is never analysed without some conditioning: filtering and tapering act multiplicatively on the noise, destroying the stationarity on which the Whittle likelihood --- the backbone of nearly all gravitational-wave inference --- rests. The problem is particularly evident for LISA, where gaps are expected to overlap almost all signals and the noise must be estimated jointly with those astrophysical signals. We provide an analytical and numerical framework to assess the impact of noise mis-modelling when signal and noise parameters are inferred jointly in the presence of gaps. From a Fisher-matrix formalism verified against Bayesian inference, we obtain closed forms for the model uncertainties, their maximum-likelihood estimates and the true scatter in the latter, for various approximations to the likelihood. The Fisher-based linear formalism is extended through the Godambe--White curvature to the non-linear regime that severe mis-modelling produces. We survey gap families from long, well-tapered interruptions to short, high-rate ones, injecting massive black-hole binaries. Except in the case of frequent gaps, we show that the windowed covariance is well approximated by its leading diagonal --- the window convolved with the power spectral density --- for the estimation of both signal and noise parameters. By omitting the convolution, the signal sector remains unbiased but the noise parameters, in particular the optical-metrology noise which is dominant at high frequency, is displaced by over an order of magnitude in power. At the highest glitch rates the diagonal approximation stays accurate yet loses an order of magnitude in precision. To remedy this, we propose an exact time-domain likelihood of the surviving samples which can be efficiently (and accurately solved) via preconditioned conjugate gradient methods.

items.title: Discovery of a 62 minute Long-period Transient with Near-orthogonal Rotator Geometry
items.abstract: Abstract We report the serendipitous discovery of the radio long-period transient (LPT) J155543.7−563102 (hereafter LPT J1555−5631) with a period of 62.2 minutes in MeerKAT and ASKAP survey data. The source emitted bright (10–30 mJy), steep-spectrum ( α ∼ −1.5), highly polarized radio pulses during a 15 hr active window in 2022 May, with no other quiescent or pulsed emission detected before or after over ∼5 yr. The mean light curve exhibits two alternating pulses per cycle. A main pulse (MP) and an interpulse (IP) separated by Δ ϕ = 165 . ° 4, with similar amplitudes but different polarization properties: the wider MP (3.9%) is partially linearly and circularly polarized and shows a constant polarization position angle, while the narrow IP (1.1%) is ∼100% circularly polarized. We classify LPT J1555−5631 as a near-orthogonal rotator, for which emission from both magnetic poles is visible during one rotation and the magnetic and rotation axes are almost perpendicular. The 14 . ° 6 deviation from an antipodal separation and the nearly constant polarization position angle suggest that the emission does not arise from the standard dipolar polar-cap geometry of ordinary pulsars, but instead originates within a broader, more complex magnetosphere. The observed properties of LPT J1555−5631 can be accommodated by extended emission regions, and favor coherent emission mechanisms such as the electron cyclotron maser instability, although they do not uniquely determine the progenitor or emission physics. If these inferences apply more broadly to the LPT population, they could account for why their beam widths are decoupled from rotation periods, the prevalence of flat polarization position angles, and may favor an elevated incidence of orthogonal rotators.

items.title: Diverse Metallicities in Protoclusters at z ~ 3.4 detected by Deep Learning
items.abstract: Abstract We present spectroscopic follow-up observations with Subaru/MOIRCS of four protocluster candidate regions identified by the deep-learning model PCFNet. In three candidate regions, we confirm four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, exhibiting galaxy density peaks over five times the uniform distribution. The detection rate of confirmed members aligns with PCFNet’s predictions, underscoring its effectiveness. Analysis of spectral energy distributions (SEDs), incorporating up to ten photometric bands (uu*grizyJHK), reveals that protocluster members lie on the star-formation main sequence. The masses of the most massive halos in the protoclusters are estimated from the most massive stellar mass of the member galaxies, yielding log Mhalo/M⊙ = 12.4–12.8, which are consistent with those at this redshift predicted by cosmological simulations and are comparable to those of the progenitors of typical local clusters ($M_\mathrm{halo}^{z=0}\sim 10^{14}M_\odot$). Using the Voronoi Tessellation Monte Carlo technique based on the probability of protocluster membership from PCFNet, we find that our protoclusters exhibit a significantly higher SFRD than the cosmic SFRD at z ~ 3.4. Based on the [O iii]/Hβ emission line ratio, two protoclusters show marginally (1.4–2σ) higher average metallicities than the field, while the other protoclusters are statistically consistent with the field. These diverse metallicities highlight the environmental impact within protoclusters detected by PCFNet, likely reflecting the complex opposing interplay between metal-rich gas recycling and metal-poor gas inflow, which may depend on the surrounding environment of each protocluster. This work demonstrates PCFNet’s capability to unveil diverse samples of high-redshift protoclusters, paving the way for a more comprehensive understanding of their role in galaxy evolution.

items.title: The 2015–2017 Large EVPA Rotation in OJ 287: Dominant Propagating Component in a Helical Magnetic Field with Time-dependent Viewing Geometry
items.abstract: Abstract We present high-cadence, multifrequency monitoring of the blazar OJ 287 using Korean VLBI Network (KVN; 22–129 GHz), Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA; 91.5–343.5 GHz), and Metsähovi (37 GHz), covering 2012–2023, together with published optical polarimetry. Within this decade-long dataset, an exceptionally large and smooth electric vector position angle (EVPA) rotation is observed only during 2015–2017. The millimeter-band EVPA rotates by more than ∼300 ∘ over ∼1.5 yr, with a comparably large and more rapidly evolving rotation observed at optical wavelengths, while remaining comparatively stable at other epochs. The rotation coincides with a sequence of strong radio flares from 37 to 343 GHz whose peak amplitudes increase toward 2017 March, when the rotation ends. Modeling the ALMA 91.5 GHz light curve yields variability Doppler factors of δ var ∼ 8–11 during the EVPA-rotation interval, with no systematic increase across the flare sequence. The absence of a monotonic change in δ var indicates that progressively enhanced relativistic beaming is unlikely to be the primary driver of the rising flare envelope. The confinement of the large EVPA rotation to this interval, together with the nearly constant δ var , indicates that the 2015–2017 event occurred when a single newly ejected disturbance temporarily dominated the polarized emission while propagating through structured inner-jet regions threaded by a helical magnetic field under modest jet-direction changes. Large EVPA rotations therefore arise intermittently as the jet orientation evolves, and are realized only when emission dominance and viewing geometry align favorably.

items.title: “Mega-Earths” are Likely an Artifact of Stellar Activity
items.abstract: Abstract Empirical relations and planet formation simulations suggest an upper mass limit for rocky planets of ∼10 M ⊕ , as cores above this will almost certainly undergo runaway gas accretion. Nevertheless, a small number of planets appear to have densities consistent with rocky Earth-like compositions above this threshold, indicating that unusual formation and evolutionary scenarios are capable of producing extremely massive rocky planets. However, all of these planets orbit active stars with log R HK ′ > −4.75. We find a <1% probability that all literature ultramassive rocky planets would coincidentally orbit such active stars, and find no astrophysical reason to expect mega-Earths to preferentially form around active stars. We therefore conclude that mega-Earths are artifacts of stellar activity, and we question the reliability of Gaussian processes to enable mass measurements for rocky planets around active stars.

items.title: Constraints on the r -process Delay Time from Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxies
items.abstract: Abstract The ancient stellar populations and simple structure of the local dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) make them excellent laboratories for studying the chemical evolution of the early Universe. In this paper, we fit one-zone galactic chemical evolution models to C, Mg, Si, Ca, Fe, Sr, Y, Ba, and Eu abundances in the dSphs Sculptor and Draco. By including the s - and r -processes in our model, we are able to place constraints on the timescale of r -process enrichment in these dSphs. We find that neutron star mergers cannot be the only source of the r -process in Sculptor and Draco, and that a prompt r -process source is required to explain the observed stellar abundances. When neutron star mergers are the only source of the r -process in our models, their minimum delay time must be just 14–16 Myr. The neutron-capture abundances in Sculptor and Draco can also be fit by models with a longer neutron star merger minimum delay time combined with a prompt r -process source that operates on the same timescale as massive star evolution, such as magnetorotational supernovae. Additionally, the Sr and Y abundances in the dSphs set limits on the Sr and Y yields per r -process event. We find that theoretical r -process yields overestimate Sr and Y production by a factor of up to 100.

items.title: What Does 2D Coronal Seismology Measure?
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) coronal seismology based on coronagraphic imaging spectroscopy has emerged as a promising method for mapping the coronal magnetic field, but the physical meaning of its inferred quantities under optically thin line-of-sight (LOS) integration remains uncertain. We investigate this problem by synthesizing coronagraphic observables from a global wave-driven magnetohydrodynamic model with a long LOS extent and a structured corona and by applying the same analysis procedures used for observations. We compare the diagnosed density, wave propagation direction, phase speed, and magnetic-field strength with different LOS-weighted reference quantities from the model. We find that the measured density and the wave propagation direction are both well represented by LOS emissivity-weighted quantities. In contrast, the phase speed is not controlled by emissivity weighting alone: the LOS distribution of wave velocity amplitude also plays an important role. As a result, the inferred magnetic field is better represented by combining the emissivity-weighted density with an amplitude-dependent effective speed. Emissivity weighting nevertheless remains a reasonable approximation, and a useful baseline, over much of the field of view, especially where the LOS does not cross strongly structured plasma-sheet-like regions. These results clarify the physical interpretation of 2D coronal seismology and provide guidance for future coronal magnetic-field tomography and model-constrained applications.

items.title: NGC 3227 Blinks: An Extreme Changing-look Event in a Seyfert Galaxy
items.abstract: Abstract We report a rapid optical changing-look event in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 3227: the optical continuum faded by ∼70%, and broad H β emission nearly disappeared within weeks before recovering within 2 months. Damped random walk simulations calibrated to the source’s normal variability show that such a decline is unlikely for stochastic accretion fluctuations. The optical decline coincides with an X-ray spectral hardening event detected by Swift, indicating additional line-of-sight absorption. During the dim state, reverberation mapping yields a clear 6–8 day lag between the continuum and broad H β , placing the obscurer interior to the broad-line region. Photoionization calculations require a fully ionized Compton-thick column with N H ≈ 1.5 × 10 24 cm −2 to reproduce the optical continuum suppression. Together, these observations demonstrate that compact, high-column-density obscurers interior to the broad-line region can produce extreme optical changing-look behavior on timescales of weeks.

items.title: DZ White Dwarfs from HETDEX: New Identifications and Reclassifications
items.abstract: Abstract We present 18 DZ white dwarfs, identified by metal absorption features, most prominently the Ca ii H and K lines, from spectroscopic observations in the Hobby–Eberly Telescope Dark Energy Experiment (HETDEX). Of these objects, 11 are newly spectroscopically confirmed through the detection of Ca ii H and K absorption in the HETDEX spectra ( R ∼ 750). The presence of Ca ii H and K absorption provides a direct spectroscopic signature of atmospheric metal pollution, which is generally interpreted as evidence for the accretion of planetary debris. By crossmatching the continuum-selected objects in the HETDEX Source Catalog with the Gaia eDR3 white dwarf catalog, we recovered 759 white dwarf candidates. Of these, all were visually inspected to account for potential metal-polluted white dwarfs that may fall below the high probability threshold ( P WD ≥ 0.75), resulting in 18 objects showing clear Ca ii H and K absorption. We determine their atmospheric parameters using an iterative fitting procedure that combines HETDEX spectroscopy with multiband photometry from the Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX), Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), and Pan-STARRS, together with Gaia parallaxes. All 18 objects were misclassified by the automated spectral classifier, demonstrating that visual inspection remains essential for recovering cool, metal-polluted white dwarfs in large spectroscopic surveys. These results highlight the power of combining low-resolution spectroscopy with Gaia astrometry to expand the census of metal-polluted white dwarfs and identify systems for future follow-up studies of planetary debris around evolved stars.

items.title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from stand-alone models towards systems of interacting agents. These systems do not merely classify, predict or generate: they plan, exchange messages, call tools, divide labour, adapt and coordinate action across tasks and time. This shift has made agentic AI one of the dominant frames for the next phase of the field. Understanding how these agents interact will therefore be as important as improving what each agent can do alone. Here, the authors argue that agentic AI requires a shift from evaluating individual agents alone to analyzing interaction architectures, proposing a framework that links agent interactions, collective configurations and time-dependent outcomes.

items.title: Three-dimensional Model Fitting to Magnetic Clouds for Multiple In Situ Spacecraft Measurements
items.abstract: Abstract We have performed an optimal model fitting analysis to a magnetic cloud (MC) event on December 1-3, 2023, when Wind and STA spacecraft crossed the same structure along closely separated paths. The Solar Orbiter (Sol) spacecraft, with a relatively larger separation distance from Earth (Wind), also appeared to have crossed the same structure at an earlier time. The analytic model employed for the optimal fitting to the magnetic field data is based on a linear force-free field formulation, possessing three-dimensional (3D) spatial variations, and is dubbed Friedberg solution (FS). By employing both Wind and STA in-situ measurements along their separate paths across the same MC structure, we obtain the set of parameters characterizing the FS model fit with an optimal reduced $\chi^2$ value of 3.60. We then compare the FS model output along the STA spacecraft path with the actual magnetic field measurements and obtain a correlation coefficient, $cc_1=$0.94 - 0.96. By examining the magnetic field line configuration more closely, we also find that the Sol spacecraft may have crossed the same MC body along its path at a relatively larger distance away from the Wind spacecraft path and over a shorter time interval. A similar comparison between the FS model output and the Sol data yields a correlation coefficient $cc_2=$0.81 - 0.90. For completeness, we also perform the two-dimensional (2D) Grad-Shafranov (GS) reconstruction of the MC structure by using the Wind spacecraft data only. A similar analysis yields $cc_1=$0.93 - 0.96, and $cc_2= -0.37$ - 0.11 for the GS reconstruction result. Hence our interpretation is that the analysis results based on three spacecraft datasets are consistent with the 3D spatial magnetic field configuration of the FS model output for this MC event to the degree indicated by the aforementioned quantitative metrics.

items.title: Constraining anisotropic f(R) cosmologies through observational data analysis
items.abstract: Abstract The present study explores the cosmological dynamics of an LRS Bianchi Type-I universe in the context of f ( R ) gravity, focusing on vacuum solutions. Two anisotropic models are constructed by considering different functional forms of f ( R ), where plane-symmetric LRSBI metrics incorporate anisotropy in the expansion rates, maintaining directional differences among Hubble parameters and scale factors throughout cosmic evolution. While such anisotropic assumptions in general relativity typically lead to a decelerating universe, functional forms of f ( R ) can support both accelerating and decelerating expansion branches, depending on the corresponding model parameters. To constrain the model parameters, we perform a comprehensive statistical analysis using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods with Hubble, BAO, and Pantheon datasets. The resulting observational constraints are interpreted at the level of the effective mean-background expansion. Model I and II constraints are illustrated through posterior contour and error bar plot, and the corresponding statistical values are summarized in tables.

items.title: Validation of Habitable Zone Limits with a New Radiative–Convective Equilibrium Climate Model
items.abstract: Abstract The habitable zone (HZ) boundaries calculated with the Clima one-dimensional radiative–convective equilibrium (RCE) model have served as a standard reference for exoplanet target selection for three decades, but they have never been independently validated with a comparable model. We present ExoColumn , a new one-dimensional RCE model that couples an independently developed atmospheric column physics package to the ExoRT correlated- k radiative transfer core that is also used by the three-dimensional ExoCAM model. We calibrate ExoColumn to present-day conditions, which matches other RCE models to within a few kelvin through the troposphere. Line-by-line benchmarks show that the ExoRT and Clima radiation cores each reproduce the outgoing longwave flux to within a few percent, with the differences due to the spectral line databases used by each model. We follow the same inverse climate modeling method as previous studies have done to find inner edge moist- and runaway-greenhouse limits of 0.970 au and 0.966 au, and an outer-edge maximum-greenhouse limit of 1.611 au at a CO 2 partial pressure of 8.7 bar. We extend these calculations to 12 host stars spanning 2000–7200 K and to planets of 0.1, 1, and 5 Earth mass, and we provide updated HZ boundary coefficients for community use. The ExoColumn limits systematically fall closer to the host star than those of Clima but agree to within a few percent in orbital distance, which validates the robustness of the published Clima HZ boundaries.

items.title: From Whole Number Bias to Gap Thinking: University Students’ Strategy Choices in Fraction Comparison and Relations to Math and Cognitive Abilities
items.abstract: Abstract Fractions pose a significant challenge for many students. Several flawed strategies have been identified in elementary and secondary students when selecting the larger of two fractions: the whole number strategy (choosing the larger numerals), the reverse strategy (choosing the smaller numerals), and the gap strategy (choosing the smaller difference between numerator and denominator). The prevalence of these strategies among university students is unknown. In the present study, we used specially designed stimuli and cluster analysis to identify fraction comparison strategy use among 90 university students. We assessed potential contributing factors to fraction understanding: general math achievement, inhibitory control, and visuospatial working memory. The results revealed three clusters: a Whole-Number-Strategy group (14%), who primarily used the whole number strategy; a Partial-Reverse-Strategy group (30%), who used the reverse strategy for challenging fractions; and a Gap-Tendency group (56%), who showed high accuracy when the gap strategy succeeds, and lower but above chance accuracy when the gap strategy fails. Regarding the contributing factors, the Gap-Tendency group performed better than the Whole-Number-Strategy group, but did not differ from the Partial-Reverse-Strategy group, on all measures. These findings extend prior research on strategies by showing that many university students have overcome whole number bias but have not yet achieved a complete understanding of fraction magnitude. Moreover, the lack of differences in math and cognitive factors between the better-performing groups shows that strong math and cognitive abilities are necessary but not sufficient for full fraction understanding among university students.

items.title: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the ma ize r hizosphere s ynthetic c ommunity (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. This community is built around Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a model maize rhizosphere colonist and synthetic biology chassis. We characterized microbe-microbe interactions and biofilm formation of MARSc members in a variety of environmental contexts, finding that both behaviors are broadly controlled by nutrient levels. Genomic analysis and microbiome profiling of these organisms revealed that annotated biofilm genes (such as surface attachment and exopolysaccharide production) were significantly correlated with rhizosphere abundance, but neither trait correlated to in vitro biofilm formation. In vitro interaction assay findings were surprisingly consistent with co-correlations of rhizosphere abundance among MARSc members on roots. Finally, we found that when applied to the roots, MARSc can increase maize biomass (dry weight) by up to 40%–50% under varying nitrogen fertilization levels. Altogether, MARSc is a useful tool for identifying some of the factors influencing rhizosphere microbiome assembly and will be a strong foundation for further work in this area. IMPORTANCE The microbiome surrounding the roots of plants can play an integral role in plant health and growth, and it is composed of thousands of species of microbes that are specific to the plant and environment it is grown in. However, due to this complexity, little is known about the means by which microbiomes form. In this study, we developed the maize rhizosphere synthetic community (MARSc) to gain a better understanding of the formation and function of microbiomes on the roots of plants. This consortium consists of 30 bacterial isolates plus Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a model maize root colonist. In this study, we investigated the interactions between these organisms, their genomes, cultural characteristics, and growth on the roots of maize. We show that MARSc increases maize growth under low nitrogen fertilizer, suggesting it will be a useful tool for identifying the mechanisms behind microbiome formation and plant growth promotion.

items.title: Farmers’ knowledge of date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) agrobiodiversity in a Saharan oasis: Folk nomenclature, fruit morphometrics and varietal turnover over four decades at Taghit, south-western Algeria
items.abstract: Abstract Background Date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.) sustains oasis livelihoods through farming systems in which clonal propagation coexists with the retention of seed-derived palms. Documenting this diversity requires attention to how farmers name, distinguish and manage their palms. In south-western Algeria, long exposed to Bayoud disease, no inventory of the local varietal repertoire has been published for Taghit since 1985, to our knowledge. This study examined date palm diversity and farmers’ knowledge and practices in the Taghit oasis system, characterised fruit and seed variation among locally recognised varieties, and assessed changes in the repertoire over four decades. Methods Semi-structured interviews with 70 farmers across 39 palm groves in six localities documented varietal names, cultivation practices, knowledge transmission, uses and perceived constraints, including resistance to Bayoud. We analysed varietal frequency, salience and spatial distribution, and compared the repertoire with a 1985 inventory. Ten quantitative fruit and seed traits were measured on 600 fruits from 75 palms representing 30 varieties to assess variation within and among varieties. Results Farmers reported diverse uses of date palm products, regular grove management and continuing intergenerational knowledge transmission. They collectively listed 30 varieties, comprising a widely shared core and numerous less frequent ones, twelve of which were recorded in only one grove. Richness and composition differed among localities. Varietal lists excluded males and collective seedling categories, while ḫalṭ served both as a varietal name and as a collective designation for seed-derived palms. Fruit and seed traits clearly differentiated varieties, with variety accounting for 96.7% of the variance among palm means. After harmonisation, the 1985 and current inventories each comprised 30 varieties, but only fourteen were shared, and historically common varieties were more often recovered. Perceived Bayoud resistance may have contributed to changes in the repertoire, as illustrated by tākarbūš, introduced for its reputed resistance, still uncommon in 1985 but now established. Conclusions Our study highlights smallholders’ role in maintaining perennial crop diversity through clonal propagation, retention of seed-derived palms and local knowledge. Conservation should support the practices and knowledge transmission that sustain this diversity, household livelihoods and oasis landscapes.

items.title: The Transformation of the Namblong Indigenous Movement Against Deforestation Practices in the Grime Nawa Valley, Papua
items.abstract: This study analyzes the transformation of the Namblong Indigenous movement against deforestation driven by PT Permata Nusa Mandiri's oil palm expansion in the Grime Nawa Valley, Jayapura Regency, Papua. The study explores why and how the movement changed, maps its stages, and identifies key actors. The intrinsic case study draws on three evidentiary layers: in-depth interviews with six key actors on 9 June 2026; participant observation; and a coded documentary corpus of seventeen items carrying fourteen named speakers, nine of whom were not part of the leadership. The customary boundaries, the revoked concession, and patrol posts were verified in QGIS. When analyzed through the lens of New Social Movement theory, the findings reveal four non-linear phases: traditional protest (2011–2020); multi-scalar advocacy alliances (2021–2022); a partial, contested victory (2022–2025), in which central-government revocations were never matched by district-level cancellation; and institutionalization through Indonesia's first Indigenous-owned corporation (2024), owned by 44 clans across roughly 52,765 hectares. This study argues that the incompleteness of the legal victory, rather than its success, drove the shift from rejection to development. The study also documents the accompanying internal friction. The present study extends New Social Movement theory by proposing the Indigenous corporation as a new repertoire of resistance in the Global South. This is offered as an analytical, precondition-dependent generalization.Keywords: Agrarian conflict, Deforestation, Indigenous corporation, Indigenous movement, New Social Movement

items.title: Genomic selection to enhance disease resilience in an endangered species
items.abstract: Abstract Chytridiomycosis caused by the amphibian chytrid fungus ( Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis , Bd) is one of the most devastating wildlife diseases of our time 1,2 . With no effective methods to control its spread, captive breeding programs have become essential to prevent frog extinctions 3 , but serve only as a temporary safeguard until threats can be mitigated 4 . Although some species have shown partial recovery through evolving resistance 5 , this is unlikely to occur for small remnant populations and those confined to captivity. Here, we showcase the utility of genomic selection to enhance disease resilience in the southern corroboree frog ( Pseudophryne corroboree ), a species highly susceptible to Bd and now functionally extinct in the wild 6 . By analysing disease phenotypes and genomic datasets, we found that P. corroboree survival traits following Bd exposure are polygenic with low-moderate heritability. Response to selection models predict that genomic selection could increase mean survival time by approximately 9% in the next generation. Importantly, selective breeding incorporating genomic information can help maintain genetic diversity and more effectively reduce inbreeding. These findings demonstrate a viable pathway to shift captive assurance colonies from passive repositories to proactive conservation tools, offering a sustainable strategy to improve disease resilience and support long-term recovery of wildlife threatened by emerging pathogens.

items.title: Extreme Hard X-ray Variability in the TeV Blazar Mrk 421: Insights from NuSTAR Observations
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the hard X-ray variability of the TeV blazar Mrk 421 over both long-term and intra-day timescales to gain insights into the particle acceleration and cooling mechanisms driving its emission. Using 27 NuSTAR observations spanning 2012 to 2024, we conduct detailed spectral and timing analyses. Our findings reveal pronounced flux variability, with changes by up to a factor of 200 over the decade and a 10-fold increase within a period of 15 days during a flaring episode. The flux distribution exhibits a lognormal profile, and a linear root-mean-square (RMS)–flux relation suggests a multiplicative variability process. Spectral analysis indicates that a log-parabolic model best describes most observations, with a strong linear anti-correlation between the photon index and curvature parameter. We also identify a positive correlation between the synchrotron peak energy and flux, accompanied by a subtle “harder-when-brighter” trend. These results align with standard blazar emission models, supporting particle acceleration via shock fronts or magnetic reconnection in the relativistic jet.

items.title: Clustering redshift distribution calibration of weak lensing surveys using the DESI-DR1 spectroscopic dataset
items.abstract: We estimate the source redshift distribution of current weak lensing surveys by applying the clustering-based redshift calibration technique, using the galaxy redshift sample provided by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI-DR1). We cross-correlate the Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS), Luminous Red Galaxies (LRGs) and Emission Line Galaxies (ELGs) from DESI, within the redshift range 0.1 < z < 1.6 , with overlapping tomographic source samples from the Dark Energy Survey (DES), Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS), and Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) survey. Using realistic mock catalogues, we test the stability of the clustering redshift signal to fitting scale, reference-sample choice, and the evolution of source galaxy bias. We calibrate a source galaxy bias correction from simulations with conservative (factor-of-two inflated) priors to account for modelling uncertainties, and we explicitly model and marginalise over magnification contributions, which become non-negligible at z ≳ 1 due to the depth of the DESI ELG sample. We then compare the resulting bias-weighted redshift distributions to previously calibrated redshift distributions from the literature, based on self-organising map (SOM) techniques, finding agreement within uncertainties for all surveys and tomographic bins. Our results demonstrate that clustering redshifts enabled by DESI’s unprecedented spectroscopic sample provide a robust, complementary, and independent constraint capable of reducing one of the dominant systematic uncertainties in weak lensing cosmology.

items.title: Relativistic effects in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals within scalar clouds: Eccentric and inclined orbits
items.abstract: We study extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) evolving in a scalar cloud environment that may form through superradiant instabilities, using a fully relativistic perturbative framework that allows for eccentric and inclined orbits. EMRIs, consisting of a stellar-mass compact object inspiraling into a supermassive black hole, are key sources for space-based gravitational-wave detectors such as LISA. Previous relativistic studies of EMRIs in scalar clouds have been restricted to circular, equatorial motion. Here, instead, we focus on a Schwarzschild black hole background to incorporate eccentricity and orbital inclination. By computing the scalar energy and angular momentum scattered off to spatial infinity and absorbed at the event horizon, we show that orbital eccentricity can induce a dense spectrum of resonances near the last stable orbit, associated with strong relativistic apsidal precession. We further find that orbital inclination can significantly modify the orbital energy and angular momentum losses. In particular, we identify a critical inclination angle below which, at sufficiently small orbital radii, there is a net transfer of energy from the scalar cloud to the orbit. Moreover, for sufficiently large eccentricities, resonances associated with relativistic apsidal precession persist across the full range of inclinations, although their structure changes significantly between prograde and retrograde orbits. These results provide a foundation for future studies of EMRIs in scalar cloud environments on fully generic orbits around spinning black holes.

items.title: Enhanced electron-beam lithography to reduce the frequency scatter of 200–400 GHz superconducting microstrip resonators for on-chip filterbank spectrometers
items.abstract: Integrated superconducting spectrometers provide the instantaneous bandwidth, sensitivity, and scalable architecture required for large-scale spectroscopic surveys in submillimeter-wave astronomy and cosmology. However, the accuracy with which the resonant frequencies of superconducting microstrip bandpass filters can be spaced has limited the spectral resolution of these spectrometers with continuous spectral coverage to F/ΔF < 500. The origin of this frequency scatter has been largely unknown. In this work, we demonstrate a fourfold improvement in the frequency spacing of superconducting microstrip resonators by optimizing electron-beam lithography. We find that reducing the electron-beam step size also reduces the random frequency scatter and that avoiding main-field stitching across filter patterns can eliminate a systematic frequency shift between groups of resonators, indicating the different origins of these two modes of frequency deviation. These findings demonstrate that nanometer-scale control of lithographic processes is imperative for the realization of next-generation integrated superconducting spectrometers with higher spectral resolution.

items.title: Can distance duality violation save late-time solutions to the Hubble tension?
items.abstract: The discrepancy between early- and late-Universe determinations of the Hubble constant may point to physics beyond $Λ$CDM or to unaccounted-for systematics. Numerous late-time modifications to the expansion history have been proposed to alleviate this discrepancy, with limited success. Recent works have shown that, when the sound-horizon and supernova calibrations are held fixed, any purely late-time resolution requires a violation of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR). Recasting the tension in the $r_d$-$M_B$ plane, we show explicitly that distance duality, together with BAO and uncalibrated supernova data and a fixed sound-horizon calibration, determines $H_0$ independently of the late-time expansion history. We then test the viability of the required CDDR violation by separately constraining reciprocity violation and photon number non-conservation, deriving a new constraint on reciprocity-violating distortions of angular-diameter distances from BAO and cosmic-chronometer data. Combining this result with existing photon-number-conservation constraints, we find that the level of distance-duality violation needed to resolve the tension is strongly disfavoured by current data. We therefore conclude that, for fixed sound-horizon and supernova calibrations, no modification confined to the late-time expansion history -- even one violating distance duality -- can resolve the Hubble tension, pointing instead toward early-Universe physics or unresolved local systematics.

items.title: Magnetic pressure anisotropy in ultra-dense white dwarfs: Landau quantization and neutronization effects
items.abstract: Abstract Strong magnetic fields modify the thermodynamics of white dwarf (WD) matter by quantizing the transverse motion of degenerate electrons into Landau levels and splitting the pressure into components parallel and perpendicular to the magnetic field. We investigate how this microscopic pressure anisotropy affects ultra-dense WD sequences when Coulomb lattice contributions, electron capture thresholds, neutron drip limits, and nuclear composition are treated consistently in the equation of state (EoS). The stellar equilibrium structure is obtained by solving an anisotropic extension of the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff (TOV) equations, where $$P_r = P_\parallel $$ P r = P ‖ and $$P_t = P_\perp $$ P t = P ⊥ denote the radial and tangential pressures, respectively. We compare the post-electron-capture branches with their corresponding pre-capture sequences for pure $$^{12}\textrm{C}$$ 12 C , $$^{16}\textrm{O}$$ 16 O , $$^{20}\textrm{Ne}$$ 20 Ne , and $$^{24}\textrm{Mg}$$ 24 Mg compositions, as well as for fixed 50/50 C/O, Ne/O, and Mg/Ne mixtures. The EoS predicts $$P_\perp < P_\parallel $$ P ⊥ < P ‖ in density ranges where only a few Landau levels are occupied. Consequently, pressure anisotropy shifts the stellar sequences toward smaller radii, with only minor changes in the maximum masses. We also find that post-capture configurations cannot be interpreted from the mass–radius plane alone, since the corresponding $$M(\rho _c)$$ M ( ρ c ) curves reveal portions with $$dM/d\rho _c<0$$ d M / d ρ c < 0 that are flagged by the turning-point diagnostic after the maximum mass is reached. Our results show that strong magnetic fields significantly reduce the radii of low-mass WDs, placing the calculated branches in the same broad mass–radius domain as a selected observational sample, without constituting a specific observational identification or statistical validation, and suggesting that future high-precision observations of massive magnetic WDs could help assess the role of magnetic pressure anisotropy in determining their masses and radii.

items.title: Pulsar J1909+0749 and supernova remnant G42.1-0.2. A case of a pulsar that has exited the shell of its associated supernova remnant
items.abstract: The ATNF pulsar catalogue currently features over 4300 Milky Way pulsars, but only 63 of them are possibly associated with a supernova remnant (SNR) arising from the same progenitor supernova explosion. Even rarer is the scenario in which the pulsar has escaped the physical extent of its corresponding SNR. We aim to identify the serendipitously discovered shell-type object G42.1-0.2 as an SNR. The known pulsar (PSR) J1909+0749 lies well outside the shell of SNR G42.1-0.2, but it has a cometary tail pointing towards the centre of the SNR; because of this positional coincidence, we propose that the SNR and the pulsar originated from the same supernova explosion. By measuring the flux densities of the shell G42.1-0.2 from ∼200 MHz to ∼6 GHz, we established the non-thermal nature of its emission. With the characteristic age of the pulsar, its distance from the Sun estimated from the dispersion measure (DM), and the angular separation between the pulsar and the centre of the shell, we inferred the evolutionary state of the SNR and the transverse velocity of the pulsar. Using proper motion measurements, we compared the SNR--pulsar direction with the velocity of the pulsar. The radio spectral index of the shell is -0.36 ± 0.08, confirming that the emission is primarily non-thermal synchrotron. The proper-motion measurements are not well constrained, but the amplitude and the direction are consistent with the interpretation that the SNR and the pulsar are associated. If the characteristic age and the DM-based distance represent the true age and the true distance of the pulsar and the SNR, the standard evolution equations suggest that the SNR must still be in the Sedov--Taylor phase and evolving in a medium with a density of about 1.5 cm -3 $. In addition, as a result of the PSR--SNR association, the transverse velocity of the pulsar PSR,J1909+0749 is estimated to be $∼1460 ^ km,s -1 , ranking it among the highest transverse velocities observed for pulsars in the Milky Way.

items.title: Dynamical plausibility of triple-assisted interaction in Be-star multiple systems
items.abstract: Classical Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars surrounded by gaseous circumstellar disks. The origin of the angular momentum required to sustain their near-critical rotation remains uncertain. Binary interaction is a promising spin-up channel, and in hierarchical multiple systems a tertiary companion may drive the secular evolution of an unresolved inner binary. We investigated whether observed Be-star multiple systems are dynamically compatible with a triple-assisted interaction scenario, in which a resolved tertiary companion excites the eccentricity of an unresolved inner binary through the Kozai--Lidov mechanism and brings it closer to an interaction regime. We combined speckle-interferometric detections, reported inner periods, and proper-motion anomalies (PMas) to construct synthetic populations of hierarchical triples. Accepted configurations were required to be dynamically stable, to evolve in the secular regime, to have a Kozai--Lidov timescale shorter than the adopted main-sequence lifetime scale, and to reach an inner-periastron interaction proxy. For the best-constrained systems, we performed refined target-specific simulations using the adopted stellar masses, distances, periods, PMa scales, and speckle separations. HD 35079 and HD 55606 provide the cleanest period-plus-speckle dynamical matches: their observed inner periods and speckle separations are simultaneously reproduced by stable, secularly active triples. HD 205329 remains dynamically plausible, but its interpretation is astrometrically cautionary because it depends on the PMa constraint. HD 41335 is a diagnostic case: the period-plus-speckle and PMa-plus-speckle constraints are viable separately, whereas the simultaneous period, PMa, and speckle constraints yield no accepted configurations under the adopted tolerances. Several PMa-plus-speckle systems, including HD 37330, HD 41600, HD 205329, and HD 71510, are observationally promising hierarchical-triple candidates, but their interpretation is more dependent on the astrometric PMa constraint. As an independent consistency check, we estimated the angular-momentum budget required to spin up the Be star and found a median fractional requirement of Δ M_ ̊m req /M under the adopted assumptions. Several observed Be-star multiple systems admit dynamically plausible Kozai--Lidov-active configurations in which a resolved tertiary companion can drive an unresolved inner binary towards interaction. These systems are therefore prime targets for continued speckle, spectroscopic, and astrometric monitoring, as well as for future binary-evolution modelling of triple-assisted Be-star spin-up.

items.title: A compact NH_2D source without an NH_3 counterpart in the S187 high-mass star-forming region
items.abstract: Our goal is to investigate a so far only tentatively detected compact NH_2D source devoid of a notable NH_3 counterpart located rather close to the luminous IRAS 01202+6133 source (the projected distance is łesssim0.3 pc) in the S187 high-mass star-forming region. A high ammonia deuteration in such an environment is unusual. We performed observations of this area with the 20 m radio telescope of the Onsala Space Observatory (OSO) in several frequency ranges from ∼72 to ∼112 GHz. The area was mapped at the lower frequencies. At the higher frequencies, only the position of the NH_2D emission peak was observed. The data were analyzed using non-LTE modeling. The data confirm a compact NH_2D source with a size of łesssim0.2 pc. In addition, emission from about 20 molecules was detected, but only the DCO+$(1--0) peak coincides with the NH_2D clump. The clump is not associated with any known astronomical source or an NH$_3 emission peak, but the dust continuum map shows a local peak at approximately the same position. The gas kinetic temperature derived from various indicators is ∼20--30 K, which is possibly the temperature of the surrounding material. The intrinsic NH_2D line width (∼0.4̨ms) implies a clump with subsonic or transonic turbulence. The ortho/para NH_2D line intensity ratio is consistent with an abundance ratio of 3, which is in line with what is expected based on the spin statistics. The NH_2D/NH_3 abundance ratio may be ∼1. In general, the data hint at a compact cold gravitationally stable dense core within the warm environment, which may comprise pristine material. However, a verification with observations at a higher angular resolution is needed for confirmation.

items.title: Microbiome structure, function, and drivers across different soil groups in an agricultural region of Serbia
items.abstract: Abstract. Soil is the largest reservoir of biodiversity, with distinct physical, chemical, and biological properties. Microorganisms play essential roles in soil formation and fertility. This study aimed to analyze the microbiomes of three selected soil groups in an important agricultural region of Vojvodina (Serbia) by 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding and explore their association with soil properties. Soil samples from a total of 26 field plots (in 5 replicates) were analyzed using Illumina MiSeq paired-end sequencing and processed through the QIIME2 pipeline. The obtained results indicate that the analyzed soils generally exhibit physicochemical properties typical for the respective soil groups. Alpha diversity indices revealed the highest microbiome diversity in Chernozem, consistent with its favourable physicochemical characteristics. Based on beta diversity, clear separation of soil groups according to their properties was determined. Proteobacteria, Acidobacteriota, and Actinobacteriota dominate the microbial community composition at the phylum level. Redundancy analysis revealed that soil properties account for 53.8 % of the variation in community composition, with pH value, iron availability, and CaCO3 content having the strongest influence, pH being particularly significant. The functional potential of microbial communities showed dominance of functions related to metabolism, with significant representation of functions belonging to the following groups: genetic information processing, environmental information processing, and cellular processes. The analysis of genes involved in nitrogen cycling using Kruskal-Wallis test showed no statistically significant differences in their abundances across different soil groups (p-value > 0.05). This study provides the first detailed analysis of soil microbial communities across Serbia and highlights factors shaping them. These findings underscore the importance of microbial diversity for ecosystem functioning and offer a framework for soil health monitoring, while providing insights relevant for sustainable agriculture.

items.title: A Closer Look at Statistical Uncertainty in Forest Ecosystem Surveys Using Remotely Sensed Data and Model-Based Inference
items.abstract: Many forest ecosystem surveys use remotely sensed data and model-based inference. Assessing uncertainties in connec­tion with such surveys is far from trivial. Focusing on continuous study variables, such as biomass, we first motivate why the mean square error (MSE) of predictors of population quantities of interest is a relevant measure of overall uncertainty. Secondly, we separate the MSE into four components involving (i) the variance of the predictor, (ii) the model-bias of the predictor, (iii) the variance of the true value of the quantity predicted, and (iv) the cova­riance between the predictor and the true value, and show how the different compo­nents can be estimated. Thirdly, based on simulations mimicking conditions in Eastern Africa and Western USA, we assess which components are influential in different survey contexts. Our findings show that using the variance of a predictor, alone, as a measure of uncertainty is a fair approxi­mation if the study area is large and if the model linking remotely sensed data with reference data is adequately specified and estimated. However, we identify substantial risks of underestimating the MSE if models are extrapolated beyond conditions for which they were calibrated, in which case predictors were found to be severely model-biased. The remaining terms contributed differently in large-area surveys compared to small-area surveys. In small-area surveys, the MSE compo­nent (iii) is the dominating part. An interesting observation was that the MSE of a predictor is sometimes smaller than the variance of the predictor, due to the negative contribution from term (iv).

items.title: Evaluating the effect of a commercial video game on pro-environmental behaviour and its determinants: a pre-post survey study
items.abstract: Abstract Commercial video games reach billions of people worldwide and may offer a scalable opportunity to engage players in climate and environmental action. However, little empirical research has assessed whether these games can influence the pro-environmental behavioural determinants or actions they aim to promote. To address this gap, we evaluated a 21-day “green activation” embedded in Love & Pies, a popular mobile game participating in the 2024 Green Game Jam. The activation encouraged players to adopt pro-environmental behaviours in food consumption, waste management, and habitat restoration through techniques like educational messaging and stories from activists and players. Using a pre–post survey design (N = 33,910), we assessed players’ self-reported pro-environmental behaviours and key behavioural determinants (e.g., knowledge), linking responses to objective gameplay data. At baseline, players reported moderate levels of subjective knowledge, perceived capability, and outcome efficacy across all three environmental issues. However, one in five players showed low levels of capability and knowledge, suggesting potential targets for intervention. Engagement with the activation, measured by milestones completed, was associated with small increases in subjective knowledge and, to a lesser extent, perceived capability. No consistent associations were observed for other determinants or self-reported behaviours. These findings align with prior research suggesting that games may more readily influence behavioural determinants than actual behaviours. However, commercial games may be a useful tool for engaging broad audiences with climate issues, particularly when grounded in behavioural theory and designed for repeated exposure to messaging. This study also highlights several design and evaluation challenges in commercial game environments, as well as future opportunities for collaborative research at the intersection of behavioural science, climate communication, and interactive media.

items.title: Drivers of ecological environment resilience in China’s coastal areas
items.abstract: Scientifically measuring the ecological environment resilience and identifying its drivers is essential for advancing ecological protection and governance. This paper employs the Resistance-Adaptability-Recovery-Transformation (RART) framework to construct an index system of ecological environment resilience. The Entropy Weight–Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method is applied to analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of ecological environment resilience in China’s coastal areas. TWFE (Two-Way Fixed Effect) and Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) methods are used to investigate the drivers of ecological environment resilience. The findings reveal that: (1) Ecological environment resilience in China’s coastal areas has shown an overall upward trend, though regional development remains unbalanced. Resilience in southern coastal areas is generally higher than in the north. (2) PA and II exhibit significant negative effects in the two-way fixed-effects model, while OU exhibits a marginally significant negative effect at the 10% level. ED, IS, and SEI are not statistically significant in the two-way fixed-effects model. (3) ED and IS show opposite directional trends between the southern and northern coastal regions of China, while the differences in the other four driving factors (PA, OU, II, SEI) are reflected in their magnitudes. These insights offer valuable policy implications for strengthening ecological environment resilience and guiding sustainable development in coastal regions worldwide.

items.title: Higher intensity, lower frequency precipitation more effectively alleviates the negative impacts of nitrogen addition on ecosystem stability in a temperate grassland
items.abstract: Abstract Changes in nitrogen (N) deposition and precipitation regime are widely recognized as key drivers of the structure and functioning of terrestrial ecosystems. Precipitation in semi-arid regions show a trend toward increasing precipitation intensity, however, how ecosystem stability responds to the combined changes in precipitation regime (specifically its intensity and frequency) and N addition, as well as the underlying mechanisms, remains poorly understood. This study focused on a temperate grassland in Inner Mongolia, using 8-year data from a field experiment to investigate the effects of N addition (0, 10, and 40 g N m−2 yr−1) and changes in precipitation regime (addition of 80 mm with two different regime: 10 mm × 8 events and 20 mm × 4 events) on ecosystem stability. The results showed that N addition reduced ecosystem stability by decreasing forb abundance and species asynchrony, mediated by alterations in soil pH. In contrast, increased precipitation alleviated the negative impact of N addition on ecosystem stability. This mitigating effect was more pronounced under higher precipitation intensity (i.e., lower precipitation frequency), mainly driven by precipitation-induced increases in soil moisture and soil pH. Improved soil moisture and pH supported stability through species richness and asynchrony, whereas the stabilizing role of forb abundance was precipitation-regime dependent. Our findings emphasize that shifts in precipitation regimes are indispensable for accurately predicting the responses of grassland ecosystem stability to N deposition.

items.title: Multi-feature fusion for grassland information extraction and temporal change monitoring
items.abstract: Grasslands play a vital role in maintaining ecological security and supporting sustainable development, yet accurate extraction and dynamic monitoring remain challenging in complex mountainous regions. This study takes Chengbu Miao Autonomous County, Hunan Province, as the study area and develops a multi-feature fusion framework on the Google Earth Engine platform by integrating optical imagery, Sentinel-1 SAR data, vegetation indices, texture features, topographic factors, and time-series characteristics. A Random Forest model was employed for high-accuracy grassland extraction, while multi-temporal remote sensing observations from selected cloud-free years between 2000 and 2025 were used to analyze long-term spatial distribution and temporal dynamics. Fractional vegetation cover (FVC) was introduced to assess grassland ecological conditions, and Nanshan Pasture was selected to investigate the impacts of topography, human activities, and climatic factors on grassland variation. The results show that multi-feature fusion significantly improves classification accuracy, achieving an overall accuracy (OA) of 93.79% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.7165 in the optimal feature combination scheme, with optical and SAR data exhibiting strong complementarity under complex terrain conditions. Grassland area in Chengbu County remained relatively stable from 2000 to 2025, with annual variations ranging from 47.32 to 52.15 km² and no significant long-term change trend. The mean FVC exhibited relatively stable interannual fluctuations, with values generally ranging from 0.59 to 0.72 during most years. However, spatial analysis of FVC trends revealed considerable heterogeneity, with significant decreasing trends observed in localized areas, particularly in the southwestern part of Nanshan Pasture, indicating potential vegetation degradation risks. In Nanshan Pasture, FVC showed a significant negative correlation with DEM (r = −0.2839) and precipitation (r = −0.589), while correlations with human activities and land surface temperature were relatively weak. Overall, grassland dynamics in the study area may reflect the combined effects of environmental conditions and human activities, although the relationships identified in this study mainly represent statistical associations rather than causal mechanisms. The proposed framework provides an effective methodological reference for grassland monitoring, ecological assessment, and sustainable management in subtropical mountainous grassland environments.

items.title: Biobanking Media Affects the Microbiome Diversity of Kelp Gametophytes
items.abstract: Abstract Kelp canopy resilience is partly influenced by their microbial partners, yet the stability of these associations in biobank-stored germplasm is unknown. We investigated how storage duration and media composition drive changes in the microbiome of Macrocystis pyrifera gametophytes. Our data suggest a shift in microbiome composition, characterized by a decline in overall microbial biodiversity. Media type significantly modulated this effect, with L1 formulation better preserving a diverse community structure than F/2 formulation. Our work here indicates that biobanking practices inadvertently select for specific microbial consortia, with implications for the viability and physiological function of preserved kelp germplasm.

items.title: Compensator stress-energy from finite-domain localization: remnant formation and horizon tests
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitational boundary constructions as diverse as Israel junction conditions, the black-hole membrane paradigm, stochastic inflation, and vacuum bubble dynamics all require boundary compensating stress-energy where a localized stress-energy source transitions to zero. This paper identifies the common structure behind them: a Bianchi-required compensator, forced when smooth finite-domain localization makes the stress-energy divergence, by the Leibniz rule of covariant differentiation, pick up a boundary term. The need for a completion is therefore not an added ingredient or model choice, but a structural consequence of restricting matter to a finite spacetime domain. A Vanishing Lemma shows that, for phase-incoherent boundary layers with integrable renormalized connected stress correlations, bounded local stress, and the minimal-retarded prescription, the compensator disappears under coarse-graining far beyond the boundary thickness, recovering general relativity (GR). A macroscopic remnant survives only when localization density invalidates independent-event suppression, the boundary remains causally inaccessible throughout the decoherence interval, and the aggregate boundary source has nonzero connected content. These requirements form a Compensator Remnant Formation Theorem. Inflationary Hubble crossing provides the cosmological realization: the horizon window generates the boundary source. The moving-window source is derived for a light spectator scalar, and the Bunch-Davies two-point calculation gives finite connected Hubble-shell power after adiabatic subtraction. The scalar transfer yields ρ_Rem(a_end) = ζH_inf⁴, with central ζ = 1/(8π²) and a factor-three prescription band; matter-like preheating gives H_inf²T_reh = (8.13 ± 0.08) × 10²⁹ GeV³. Current bounds leave a viable locus for tensor-reheating tests. Black-hole event horizons provide the geometric test: the source is regular in horizon-penetrating coordinates, and its non-extremal profile scales with surface gravity and vanishes at extremality. In the remnant-forming regime, the surviving sector is covariantly conserved, approximately pressureless, and gravitationally consistent with a cold dark component.

items.title: An (in)complete NIRSpec census of Balmer absorption in Type 1 AGN – radiation-driven outflows in little red dots, quasars and variable stars
items.abstract: Abstract A notable achievement of the first generation of JWST surveys was the discovery of an abundance of faint high-redshift (z > 4) broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the Lbol < 1045 erg s−1 regime, previously only accessible at z < 1. The high prevalence of absorption features in their broad hydrogen lines is one of the peculiarities of a significant fraction of this new population. In this paper, we conduct a broad census of Balmer absorption in a sample of 47 Type-1 AGN spanning 2 < z < 7. Accounting for incompleteness of JWST spectroscopic data, we estimate that $44_{-6}^{+21}$ % of Little Red Dots (LRDs) have absorption in Hα while the incidence rate is <25 % (at 2σ) in Little Blue Dots (LBDs). Additionally, R1000 JWST/NIRSpec data is strongly resolution limited, implying an inability to disentangle Doppler broadening in the absorption from optical depth effects. This is alleviated with R2700 observations, although some degeneracies remain. We find a significant correlation between the velocity of the Balmer absorption and the [OIII]5007 narrow line luminosity, suggesting a common driving mechanism. We do not find any other significant correlations (and do not confirm previously claimed correlations) between Balmer absorption and other spectral properties of LRDs (except for the expected correlation between Hα and Hβ absorption velocities). Comparing LRDs, quasars and stellar Hα absorbers, we establish that absorption in both LRDs and broad absorption line quasars is consistent with radiatively driven outflows, echoing the physics of variable stars yet occurring at vastly different scales.

items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.abstract: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. Because population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, we focus on mitigating the downstream effects of finite-rollout variation. We propose \emph{Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO)}, which conditions within-prompt robust reweighting on observed vote reliability to make updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative. We further introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce self-supervised forgetting during online adaptation. Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.

items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.abstract: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge. Methods: We propose GRAC (Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning), a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomical structures. Given an input scene graph, GRAC learns to retrieve relevant graph-caption pairs from training data. It compares instrument-tissue interactions between retrieved examples and the input scene, using comparison features to condition retrieved-caption representations during generation. Results: On the EndoVis-18 benchmark, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.88, compared with 4.23 for SGT and 3.36 for the strongest conventional Transformer baseline. Exact instrument-action-target triplet-set accuracy reached 52.6%, compared with 32.7% for SGT and 26.2% for the strongest conventional baseline. These results demonstrate improvements in language quality and factual agreement. On TORS, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.06, compared with 3.80 for the strongest baseline. Conclusion: GRAC demonstrates that combining structured surgical scene representations with retrieved examples improves surgical scene captioning and produces more contextually meaningful descriptions.
