items.title: Current knowledge, key gaps, and opportunities for future research on high-impact, modifiable lifestyle behaviors to promote healthy aging in adults with cystic fibrosis in the era of modulator therapy.
items.abstract: Aging in cystic fibrosis (CF), once a hopeful possibility, is now a celebrated reality for many and attributable to expert multidisciplinary care, persistent research efforts, and fervent advocacy. The median age of survival of people with CF (PWCF) increased dramatically with the advent of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapies, particularly elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor in 2019. However, as PWCF live longer, healthy aging is susceptible to the compound impact of residual CFTR dysfunction, chronic inflammation, emerging comorbidities, complexities of chronic disease management, and psychosocial burdens. We define healthy aging as maintaining physical and mental health in adults so they can remain autonomous and independent as long as possible, while also adapting lifestyle habits to support well-being and improve overall quality of life. Lifestyle factors, such as stress, nutrition, physical activity, sleep, and treatment adherence, are known to impact health outcomes in the general population. Identifying, testing, and implementing behavioral interventions addressing these factors has the potential to augment medical advances in CF care. Although the aging population of PWCF is increasingly heterogeneous and shaped by unique individual ecosystems, lifestyle behaviors impact all patients and crosscut this diversity. As CF science continues to advance toward curative therapies, parallel CF-specific research advances on modifiable lifestyle behaviors may support healthier aging and improve health outcomes. This paper outlines the current state of knowledge, identifies critical gaps, and highlights key opportunities for future research targeting modifiable lifestyle behaviors to promote healthy aging, preserve functional independence, and improve quality of life in the growing population of adults with CF.

items.title: Social Determinants of Sleep Health in Survivors of Childhood Cancer: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Survivors of childhood cancer frequently experience poor sleep quality, which affects behavioural, emotional, cognitive and physical health. Sleep health is multidimensional, encompassing regularity, satisfaction, alertness, timing, efficiency and duration, yet the influence of social, environmental and interpersonal factors on these dimensions remains poorly understood. This review examines sleep health dimensions among childhood cancer survivors and their associations with social determinants of health. A systematic review was completed in November 2025 using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and EBSCO databases. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts, assessing links between social determinants and sleep outcomes. The risk of bias was evaluated using the ROBINS-E tool. Of 485 publications screened, 14 met the inclusion criteria. Most studies assessed sleep disturbances (n = 10), with fewer examining sleep duration (n = 5), alertness (n = 3) and sleep efficiency (n = 2). Social determinants, including race/ethnicity (n = 5), education (n = 6) and employment (n = 4), were associated with specific sleep dimensions; however, comprehensive analyses across the full spectrum of sleep remain limited. Social determinants influence several sleep dimensions among childhood cancer survivors, yet research rarely considers the multidimensional nature of sleep health. We propose a socio-ecological, multidimensional model to guide the development of targeted interventions and reduce sleep health disparities in this population.

items.title: Anticipatory Cardiac Deceleration Is Related to Cautious Decision-Making after Threat Image Exposure.
items.abstract: Cautious decision-making can be an adaptive tendency in stressful environments and in certain individuals. We hypothesized that cautious decision-making is supported by anticipatory cardiac deceleration (ACD)- a brief cardiac slowing tied to preparation and action readiness. To test this hypothesis, we examined whether individuals with stronger ACD make more economically cautious choices after exposure to threat-depicting images. Participants (N = 97; 65% women, Mean age = 22.4 years) completed a threat priming decision-making task while electrocardiography was collected. To manipulate emotional contexts, every economic lottery choice was preceded by an affective image depicting a neutral, injury threat, or infection threat scene, and choice trials were presented in three separate blocks - one for each image type. Cardiac deceleration was assessed during 10-s countdown periods before each block. Results indicate that individuals with greater ACD before the infection threat block made more cautious choices after exposure to the infection threat images. This association was strongest when the infection block occurred last in the task sequence, i.e., when that image condition was more predictable. No significant relationships emerged for the other image conditions suggesting that anticipatory deceleration might only relate to behavioral caution in certain threat conditions. Results are consistent with the hypothesis that ACD is an autonomic correlate of preparation that is relevant to human performance and fear/anxiety theories.

items.title: Prenatal cocaine exposure alters synaptic plasticity of hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons in postnatal rats.
items.abstract: Prenatal cocaine exposure (PCE) severely affects brain development, psychology, and behavior in exposed offspring, while altering their susceptibility to drug addiction. however, the mechanisms underlying PCE-induced changes in cocaine-conditioned place preference (CPP) remain unclear. This study demonstrates that PCE attenuates cocaine-induced CPP, a process involving spatial memory and drug reward. We also investigated the dorsal hippocampus (dH), which is closely associated with spatial memory, and the ventral hippocampus (vH), which is linked to motivational reward mechanisms. Results indicate that PCE impairs long-term synaptic plasticity in the dH, suggesting that spatial memory deficits contribute to the attenuation of CPP. In contrast, PCE did not significantly inhibit synaptic plasticity in the vH, indicating that while the vH contributes to addiction susceptibility, it is less affected by prenatal exposure. Notably, acute cocaine exposure increased presynaptic plasticity in the vH regardless of prenatal history. These findings suggest that synaptic impairment in the dH drives spatial memory deficits in PCE offspring, while the vH retains sensitivity to acute drug challenge. This study elucidates the cellular mechanisms underlying PCE-induced cognitive changes and guides future molecular investigations.

items.title: Caffeine in Red Bull® selectively sustains the consumption of highly concentrated alcohol in energy drink-alcohol mixtures.
items.abstract: Mixing alcohol with caffeinated energy drinks is common among young people and is associated with heavier drinking. We previously found that rats self-administering Red Bull® consumed more alcohol and reached higher blood alcohol concentrations than rats given an isocaloric sucrose solution, but only when alcohol was highly concentrated. Here, we identified the beverage constituents associated with this effect. One hundred and eight male Wistar rats were trained in oral operant self-administration (30-min sessions, fixed ratio 1) and assigned to an energy-drink-flavoured vehicle, taurine, B vitamins, caffeine, sucrose, a laboratory reconstitution of the beverage (Lab-RB), or commercial Red Bull®. Solution concentration was escalated from 25% to 100%; alcohol was then added and escalated from 3% to 40% v/v in 4-day blocks. Without alcohol, only sucrose and Lab-RB sustained high responding, whereas caffeine, taurine, and B vitamins were indistinguishable from vehicle. With alcohol, sucrose increased alcohol intake only at low concentrations (3-6% v/v), whereas caffeine increased intake only at high concentrations (15-40% v/v), where sucrose was no longer effective (Group × Segment interaction: F(1,22) = 66.30, P 2 p = 0.751). Taurine and B vitamins had no detectable effect. These findings indicate that sucrose and caffeine contribute to alcohol intake at different parts of the concentration range and suggest that palatability alone is insufficient to explain the sustained consumption of highly concentrated alcohol.

items.title: Thermally unfavorable conditions of volatile existence in near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26, the Hayabusa extended mission's target
items.abstract: The near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26, the target of the Hayabusa2# extended mission, has been proposed as a dark comet that may host volatiles, particularly water, owing to an anomalous out-of-plane nongravitational acceleration that may result from outgassing. This asteroid, however, may also belong to a largely anhydrous taxonomic group. Whether outgassing-driven acceleration is possible strongly depends on how the asteroid stores volatiles in its interior and releases them upon heating at the surface. Thus far, the contentious topic of the existence of volatiles on 1998 KY26 that can cause outgassing has not been extensively examined from a thermophysical standpoint. Here, we show that all locations on the surface or in the interior of 1998 KY26 have orbit-averaged temperatures significantly above the sublimation point of volatiles in vacuum. Across 13 thermal characterizations, this observation is found to be consistent despite parameter variations in equivalent diameter, thermal conductivity, Bond albedo, specific heat capacity, and spin pole ecliptic latitude and longitude. Our temperature model results indicate that the water outgassing rate on 1998 KY26 would be too high to maintain buried ice, refining the understanding of the asteroid's composition.

items.title: The deuterium-rich atmosphere of a mature super-Jupiter
items.abstract: The deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio (D/H) has provided key insights into the origin and evolution of the Solar System. Using the James Webb Space Telescope, we detected deuterated methane at $48σ$ in a mature giant exoplanet, $ε$ Ind Ab. We measure the planet's D/H ratio to be $(4.4 \pm 0.7) \times 10^{-5}$, which is similar to those of Uranus and Neptune but about twice those of Jupiter, Saturn, and the protosolar nebula. $ε$ Ind Ab's heavy elements (C, O, N, and S) are uniformly enriched to a level similar to Jupiter's. These measurements require $ε$ Ind Ab to have accreted solids with $\mathrm{D/H} \gtrsim 1\%$, at least 30 times more deuterium-rich than typical Solar System comets. Such D/H values are found in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS and in organic molecules in star-forming regions, indicating that $ε$ Ind Ab accreted pristine solids formed in a very cold environment.

items.title: DMAJOR: A JWST Legacy Survey of Protoplanetary Disks
items.abstract: We propose an infrared imaging survey of resolved protoplanetary disks spanning a range of galactic environments, directly mapping the 3D structure of planet-forming disks across the IR. DMAJOR (Disk Motions and Architectures JWST Observational Reference survey), our legacy survey, will deliver a benchmark sample to reveal structure and connection to environment. The exquisite stability of JWST allows us to probe for variability with a time-scheduled revisit strategy, while its sensitivity and resolution open a window on disks unobservable from the ground. A uniform sample will reveal how small grains and ice are distributed in protoplanetary disks, how scattered light structures relate to large-scale environmental features, and identify new companions. To achieve this, DMAJOR takes advantage of model-based data analysis using telemetry and mutual calibration to enhance processed data products while minimizing telescope overheads.

items.title: Beyond node strengths: the topological content of weighted bipartite networks
items.abstract: Weighted bipartite networks encode the topology and intensity of interactions between two disjoint sets of nodes. However, it is unclear whether the observed pattern of connections is already explained by node interaction volumes or contains additional structural information. Here we introduce a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks that preserves node strengths alone, strengths and global density, or strengths and the complete degree sequence. Across economic, technological, ecological, social and lexical systems, we find that strength constraints alone are generally insufficient to reproduce empirical structures. Yet the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single constraint controlling network density frequently provides the most parsimonious description, whereas networks with stronger residual degree heterogeneity require node-specific constraints. Beyond downstream inference, we also show how the choice of topological resolution changes which interactions and projected relationships are identified as statistically significant. Our results indicate that topology is essential, but often compressible, in the statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and provide a scalable computational framework for fitting, sampling, model selection and validation within a common workflow.

items.title: What is compassion connected to, and does it differ by gender and age? A network analysis of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy and mental health
items.abstract: Abstract Compassion is an emotional state experienced in response to witnessing the suffering of others, accompanied by an internal motivation to help. When directed toward the self, it is referred to as self-compassion. Previous research suggests that compassion and self-compassion are closely related to mindfulness and empathy, contributing to reductions in anxiety and depression and to the enhancement of positive affect. Accordingly, this study employed network analysis to explore the complex structure of interactions among these psychological variables. A total of 1,020 Korean adults completed measures of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy, well-being, and negative affect (depression, anxiety, and stress). An EBICglasso network was estimated in R (version 4.5.1). Centrality indices were computed, and subgroup networks were constructed by gender and age to compare structural differences. The results showed that compassion was closely connected to empathy, whereas self-compassion was more strongly linked to mindfulness and well-being; the capacities to feel, tolerate, and alleviate suffering emerged as central nodes. In the gender-based networks, compassion and self-compassion among men tended to be organized primarily around cognitive factors, whereas women exhibited a pattern in which the behavioral motivation for compassion was activated relatively immediately, even in the absence of emotional responding. In the age-based networks, the influence of suffering tolerance was most pronounced in middle-aged adults, while the role of empathy diminished and the role of mindfulness expanded in older adults. By examining compassion at the level of its constituent elements and visualizing the interaction structure among related variables, this study provides an empirical foundation for extending theoretical understanding and for developing tailored intervention strategies.

items.title: Measuring what future physicians know about contraception: development and validation of the clinical contraceptive knowledge test (CCKT) in Vietnam using item response theory
items.abstract: Abstract Background Accurate measurement of contraceptive knowledge among medical students remains a critical challenge due to limitations of traditional assessment tools. This study aimed to develop and validate the Clinical Contraceptive Knowledge Test (CCKT) using a modern psychometric framework. Methods A cross-sectional multicenter study was conducted among undergraduate medical students in Vietnam (723 recruited; 636 retained for analysis). The instrument was developed through four sequential phases: (1) Item generation based on Bloom’s taxonomy and WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC), (2) expert review for content validity, (3) pilot testing using Classical Test Theory, and (4) large-scale validation using Item Response Theory. A two-parameter logistic (2PL) IRT model was applied to evaluate item characteristics, dimensionality, and measurement precision. Results The final instrument, CCKT-18, demonstrated strong psychometric performance. A unidimensional 2PL model was retained based on comparable fit to multidimensional models and high inter-factor correlations (r > 0.80). Model fit indices indicated good fit (CFI = 0.983, TLI = 0.980, RMSEA = 0.036, SRMR = 0.039). The scale showed high measurement precision across a broad range of ability levels, with peak information around the average proficiency level (marginal reliability = 0.844). Item parameters were stable in sensitivity analyses (ΔCFI = 0.003), supporting model robustness. DIF analyses supported measurement invariance across sex, although several items demonstrated DIF across the training stage. Conclusion The CCKT-18 is a valid, reliable, and robust instrument for assessing contraceptive knowledge among medical students. Its IRT-based framework enables precise, competency-oriented evaluation and provides actionable insights for targeted curriculum improvement in reproductive health education.

items.title: SoK: The Security-Safety Continuum of Multimodal Foundation Models
items.abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) integrate diverse data modalities to support complex and wide-ranging tasks. However, this integration also introduces distinct safety and security challenges. In this paper, we unify the concepts of safety and security in the context of MFMs by identifying critical threats that arise from both model behavior and system-level interactions. We propose a taxonomy grounded in information theory, evaluating risks through the concepts of channel capacity, signal, noise, and bandwidth. This perspective provides a principled way to analyze how information flows through MFMs and how vulnerabilities can emerge across modalities. Building on this foundation, we introduce a deterministic minimax formulation to analyze defense mechanisms and to study a structural asymmetry of defense in multimodal systems. Our analysis indicates that model-centric defenses, which primarily operate by suppressing noise or enhancing signal, tend to exhibit diminishing effectiveness against increasingly adaptive attacks. In contrast, system-level safeguards that constrain authorized information flow and agent behavior impose stronger limits on adversarial impact by reducing effective bandwidth. To operationalize this insight, our framework maps attacks and defenses onto information-theoretic axes, effectively organizing and reducing the defense search space. Using a proposed Defense Coverage Index (DCI) to evaluate 15 representative defenses, we observe that system-level bandwidth constraints provide stronger and more consistent protection across attack classes than brittle model-level mechanisms. Finally, we formalize an MFM ``self-destruction threshold'' that specifies when termination should be triggered, offering a concrete activation rule for circuit-breaker safeguards in multimodal systems.

items.title: An Image Is Worth K Topics: A Visual Structural Topic Model with Pretrained Image Embeddings
items.abstract: Abstract Political scientists are increasingly interested in analyzing visual content at scale. However, the existing computational toolbox is still in need of methods and models attuned to the specific challenges and goals of social and political inquiry. In this article, we introduce a visual structural topic model (vSTM) that combines continuous image embeddings with a structural topic model. This has important advantages compared to existing approaches. First, continuous embeddings allow the model to capture the semantic complexity of images, which is relevant to the study of politics. A consequence of using continuous embeddings is that we can directly use off-the-shelf pretrained deep learning models, offering state-of-the-art performance in image analysis tasks while saving time, cost and resources. Second, the structural topic model provides the ability to analyze how topics and covariates are related, while maintaining a nuanced representation of images as a mixture of multiple topics. In our experiments, we show that the vSTM is able to identify topics that are interpretable, coherent and relevant to the study of online political communication.

items.title: A dual-stream Pyramid ViT–ConvFormer architecture leverages dynamic early stopping to classify diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Accurate stratification of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) into MYC subtypes is crucial for determining therapeutic intensity. While Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel at capturing global tissue context, their quadratic computational complexity results in slow convergence. To address this, we developed PyConv, a dual-stream network designed to accelerate training while maintaining precise DLBCL classification. Methods: PyConv pairs local ConvFormer blocks with global Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) blocks, unifying cytological boundaries and macro-level tissue context via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention fusion layer. The architecture was evaluated using 180 whole-slide images (69,480 testing patches) against 13 state-of-the-art backbones. Results: PyConv achieved a multi-class accuracy and macro F1-score of 0.9962, an absolute decision boundary for benign cohorts, and a malignant stratification AUROC of 0.9999. It reached optimal generalization by epoch 20, an 83.5% reduction in convergence time over pure transformers. While pure hybrid models showed slightly higher raw throughput, DeLong’s testing confirmed performance variances were statistically non-significant. Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradient, and Attention Rollout verified that PyConv correctly prioritizes key cytological features like nuclear contours and prominent nucleoli. Conclusion: PyConv offers a highly accelerated, computationally balanced alternative for DLBCL stratification without sacrificing diagnostic accuracy or clinical interpretability.

items.title: Does the Unsafe Gradient Survive a Conversation? On the Fragility of Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection in Multi-Turn Dialogue
items.abstract: Safety-aligned language models are commonly deployed as multi-turn assistants, which lets adversaries spread unsafe intent across several user turns instead of a single prompt. Gradient-based jailbreak detectors such as GradSafe were developed for single prompts: they score an input by the alignment between its induced gradient and a fixed unsafe reference direction, and their effectiveness in multi-turn dialogue remains unclear. We conduct a controlled evaluation of gradient-based jailbreak detection in multi-turn settings. We extend GradSafe with a Context Window Scanner that applies the detector to fixed-size windows of user turns and uses the maximum window score as the conversation-level score. We evaluate different window sizes, attack families, benign conversation distributions, and target models. The results differ sharply between synthetic and realistic benign settings. Against synthetic benign conversations, the detector achieves an ROC-AUC of 0.98 on human-authored multi-turn jailbreaks. On WildChat benign conversations, ROC-AUC drops to 0.76, and a threshold calibrated on synthetic data flags more than 90% of benign conversations as unsafe. Under realistic benign distributions, single-turn windows give the highest separability, whereas longer windows and accumulated contexts reduce performance. The detector is also sensitive to the attack-generation method and target model: successful Crescendo attacks receive scores comparable to or lower than benign conversations, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct yields near-random separability with a different optimal window size. These findings show that gradient-based signals can support multi-turn jailbreak detection, but reliable deployment requires calibration on realistic benign conversations, short-window scoring, length-aware thresholds, and evaluation across attack types and model architectures.

items.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
items.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Changes Cognition Systems
items.abstract: Purpose of the study. Humanity is at a turning point in its development, which is reflected in the change in the regimes of global processes, the growth of global hypercompetition for the future. Digital transformation is also entering a new phase. The processes of automation, digitalization, and the formation of intellectual production are gradually transforming, and technological development is being replaced by socio-technological development. The world changing before our eyes is becoming more complex, knowledge about it goes beyond the set of individual disciplines and continuously develops as innovative digital transformations grow, including the formation of artificial intelligence. The purpose of the article is to formulate humanitarian problems in the implementation of AI technologies in science and to develop possible directions for their solution. Materials and methods. The research was carried out based on a study and a systematic review of the literature, using methods of comparative analysis and typologization, analysis of epistemic risks based on the synthesis of analyzed sources. The use of the conceptual modeling method made it possible to describe the iterative “datamodel-experiment” cycle as the basis of the Fifth paradigm and justify the key role of understanding in this process. Research results: the analysis made it possible to systematize modern ideas about AI scientists, as well as to highlight the fundamental limitations, risks and prospects for their integration into scientific practice. The article, based on the works of foreign researchers, reviewed the key issues of the use of AI in science and the development of AI scientists. The current trends in the development of AI technologies that form the use of artificial intelligence for scientific discoveries are analyzed, the best ways to use AI and the problems associated with them are considered. Key limitations and problems of the “AI-scientist” have been identified. General ideas and practical AI solutions that affect the cognition system are described; fundamental limitations and key problems in the use of AI scientists are reflected. Conclusion. Monitoring new knowledge, identifying, creating and storing key information and data from exponentially growing streams have become impossible without highly developed artificial intelligence. The fourth scientific paradigm actually ended: big data gave way to a cognitive system that organizes an interactive research process an iterative cycle of creating new knowledge. The model created on the basis of data during the experiment provides new data, further analysis of which, supplemented by expert knowledge and elements of interdisciplinary knowledge, allows it to improve and refine the initial hypothesis. Thus, the processes of cognition are continuously accelerated and changed. The study confirms that the world scientific community is at the point of bifurcation associated with the transition from the Fourth paradigm (based on big data and computing) to the Fifth paradigm, in which the central link is the cognitive system that implements the iterative cycle “data model experiment new knowledge”. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLM) act as catalysts for this transition, radically changing the methodology, speed and very nature of scientific search. The authors believe that new approaches and solutions can significantly advance the creation of AI capable of scientific reasoning. However, when working with AI scientists, it is necessary to take into account epistemic risks, as well as the fact that the landscape of AI technologies is changing extremely quickly, which requires constant updating of the obtained typologies and conclusions.

items.title: Childhood Trauma and APOEε4 Are Associated With Patterns of Developmental Frontal Alpha Connectivity, Posttraumatic Stress, and Alcohol‐Related Outcomes
items.abstract: Childhood trauma affects neurodevelopment and lifelong risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD). Changes in brain structures and function are observed in young carriers of APOEε4, the genetic factor most associated with Alzheimer's disease. Longitudinal studies of APOEε4, childhood trauma, and neural connectivity in adolescence have not been explored. We studied 837 trauma-exposed participants (53% female) from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism prospective sample, using latent growth curve models to assess associations of childhood trauma and APOEε4 on repeated measures of frontal alpha EEG coherence (EEGc) throughout adolescence and young adulthood. Young adult AUD and PTSD symptoms were also examined. Results indicate childhood sexual assaultive trauma (CSAT) and APOEε4 are linked to neural connectivity, with effects differing by brain region and direction. CSAT was associated with a higher EEGc baseline but less growth in three EEGc pairs, while APOEε4 associated with lower left frontocentral (LFC) EEGc baseline and higher slope. EEGc patterns and symptoms of PTSD and AUD were robustly associated. A significant interaction between CSAT-by-APOEε4 interaction also emerged, such that among APOEε4 carriers, childhood sexual assaultive trauma was associated with higher baseline PFI and diminished growth in PFI and LFC EEGc. No significant direct links between APOEε4 and PTSD or AUD were observed. Findings highlight how EEGc may help explain connections between genetics, trauma, and psychopathology, guiding at-risk group identification and informing prevention strategies.

items.title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction
items.abstract: Timely intervention for Alzheimer's disease (AD) requires early detection. The development of immunotherapies targeting amyloid-beta and tau underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. Here, we directly applied our previously developed MRI-based deep learning model for AD to the large Chinese SILCODE cohort (722 participants, 1,105 brain MRI scans). The model - initially trained on North American data - demonstrated robust cross-ethnic generalization, without any retraining or fine-tuning, achieving an AUC of 91.3% in AD classification with a sensitivity of 95.2%. It successfully identified 86.7% of individuals at risk of AD progression more than 5 years in advance. Individuals identified as high-risk exhibited significantly shorter median progression times. By integrating an interpretable deep learning brain risk map approach, we identified AD brain subtypes, including an MCI subtype associated with rapid cognitive decline. The model's risk scores showed significant correlations with cognitive measures and plasma biomarkers, such as tau proteins and neurofilament light chain (NfL). These findings underscore the exceptional generalizability and clinical utility of MRI-based deep learning models, especially in large and diverse populations, offering valuable tools for early therapeutic intervention. The model has been made open-source and deployed to a free online website for AD risk prediction, to assist in early screening and intervention.

items.title: Disentangling cognitive and emotional load in interpreting
items.abstract: Abstract This study employs a multimodal approach to investigate how emotional and cognitive load differentially impact interpreter stress. Twenty student interpreters consecutively interpreted four Turkish-to-English mental healthcare narratives of varying emotionality and difficulty, constructed using a 2×2 factorial design. Stress responses were measured using galvanic skin response (GSR), voice parameters (pitch and voice intensity), and self-report scales (PANAS, STAI, and NASA-TLX). Stimuli were normed for emotional valence and linguistic complexity using readability indices, expert ratings, and natural language processing (NLP) tools. Results showed that primarily cognitive load drove GSR arousal, particularly during later interpreting stages, whereas emotional load was reflected in pitch and self-reported negative affect. A pitch convergence between speaker and interpreter also emerged. None of the stress indicators predicted interpreting accuracy, suggesting a possible role for individual coping strategies.

items.title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
items.abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. However, additional measures may be needed. Fear, disgust, and avoidance of specific foods would likely distinguish an AVI pandemic from COVID-19. The threat of infected food triggers disgust, and so food-related disgust would likely be a prominent emotional reaction during an AVI pandemic. Public messaging from health authorities and others has the potential to either ease or exacerbate public concerns about food safety, depending on how the messages are crafted.

items.title: Philosophy Is Perfect
items.abstract: Abstract Philosophy Is Perfect offers a bold defense of philosophy against its pessimistic and moderate critics. Where “Flagellants” see futility and “Hedgers” see only piecemeal progress, Herman Cappelen advances a model of Hyper-Optimism: the claim that philosophy has been massively successful, foundational to all inquiry, and is flourishing precisely because of its characteristic disagreement. Part I argues that all disciplines ultimately “answer to philosophy” when their core concepts and methods are scrutinized, showing that pessimism about philosophy would undermine confidence in every branch of knowledge. Part II turns the standard critique on its head, arguing that persistent disagreement is not a defect but a structural virtue of philosophical inquiry: convergence would signal decay, not progress. Part III presents the positive thesis—that philosophy has already found the correct answers to the “Very Important Questions.” Cappelen argues that after centuries of systematic exploration, the correct answers are already articulated and defended in the philosophical commons. Part IV addresses objections. The result is a provocative re-evaluation of philosophy’s status. Rather than a discipline in crisis, Cappelen depicts philosophy as uniquely successful: it has discovered foundational truths, thrives on principled disagreement, and sets the terms for all other forms of inquiry. Philosophy Is Perfect is both a challenge to entrenched pessimism and a constructive vision of philosophy’s achievements and future.

items.title: Age-related amplification of spatial contextual influence on visual scene processing.
items.abstract: Older adults rely increasingly on prior knowledge to make sense of their deteriorating representation of the visual world, but how this shapes scene perception and spatial reorientation remains unclear. To address this issue, 28 young and 25 older adults viewed artificially generated rooms either before or after learning the position of a goal hidden in an adjacent room. We manipulated both the number and the eccentricity of navigational affordances (i.e., open doors) to investigate the interaction between bottom-up scene features and top-down spatial knowledge. Consistent with previous findings, younger adults showed decreased performance as the number of open doors increased, but only after learning the goal position, indicating a top-down interaction with the automatic processing of affordances. Door eccentricity did not affect this interaction, suggesting our findings were not due to a distractor effect. In older adults, this interaction between prior spatial information and navigational affordances was markedly amplified: reaction times increased at twice the rate observed in younger adults. These findings show that prior spatial knowledge interacts with the automatic extraction of navigational affordances, and that this influence is markedly amplified with age. While prior knowledge helps stabilize perception when sensory processing becomes less reliable, it can also increase the processing time for complex scenes, particularly when multiple action possibilities are present. By revealing how aging shifts the balance between top-down and bottom-up mechanisms, these results refine models of age-related spatial navigation decline and highlight a trade-off whereby increased reliance on prior knowledge supports perception but can also slow interaction with complex environments.

items.title: Rethinking Spatial Data Quality: A Socio-Technical and Lifecycle Framework for Trustworthy Geospatial Information
items.abstract: Spatial data quality (SDQ) is commonly assessed through technical verification. However, empirical evidence demonstrates that perceived data quality often diverges from objectively measured quality due to cognitive, institutional, and lifecycle-related factors. This paper proposes a multi-layered SDQ framework that integrates technical admissibility, process and lifecycle stewardship, visual and interpretive diagnostics, and governance indicators to enable holistic quality assessment within a socio-technical system. Rather than treating quality elements in isolation, the framework supports the diagnosis of emergent quality states and associated risk patterns. The framework is demonstrated through two empirical cases: validation of planned land use data using the OPIAvalid toolkit, and semantic conflation of multiple digital elevation models (DEMs) with heterogeneous lineage. Results show that governance failures, specification misuse, and degradation of lineage can undermine trust and decision-making even when datasets formally comply with ISO-based indicators. Visual spatial forensics and lineage-aware integration proved essential for detecting undocumented methodological shortcuts and restoring justified trust in authoritative data. Artificial intelligence is positioned as a diagnostic and explanatory support, assisting in anomaly detection, prioritization, and communication of quality risks, while deterministic validation and expert judgment remain mandatory. Overall, the framework shifts SDQ management from isolated technical validation toward lifecycle-oriented, transparent, and sustainable data governance.

items.title: Differential Mental Disorder Detection with Psychology-Inspired Multimodal Stimuli
items.abstract: Differential diagnosis of mental disorders remains a fundamental challenge in real-world clinical practice, where multiple conditions often exhibit overlapping symptoms. However, most existing public datasets are developed under single-disorder settings and rely on limited data elicitation paradigms, restricting their ability to capture disorder-specific patterns. In this work, we investigate differential mental disorder detection through psychology-inspired multimodal stimuli, designed to elicit diverse emotional, cognitive, and behavioral responses grounded in findings from experimental psychology. Based on this paradigm, we collect a large-scale multimodal mental health dataset (MMH) covering depression, anxiety, and schizophrenia, with all diagnostic labels clinically verified by licensed psychiatrists. To effectively model the heterogeneous signals induced by diverse elicitation tasks, we further propose a paradigm-aware multimodal framework that leverages inter-disorder differences prior knowledge as prompt-guided semantic descriptions to capture task-specific affective and interaction contexts for multimodal representation learning in the new differential mental disorder detection task. Extensive experiments show that our framework consistently outperforms existing baselines, underscoring the value of psychology-inspired stimulus design for differential mental disorder detection.

items.title: Quantifying the impact of groundwater fauna and temperature on the ecosystem service of microbial carbon degradation; a proof-of-principle approach
items.abstract: Abstract Groundwater ecosystems fulfil functions that humankind relies upon, e.g. for sustainable drinking water production. Quantification of these services is lacking so far. Thus, it is not possible to predict scenarios (e.g. future climates). Based on data from a comprehensive groundwater ecosystem study comprising four zones of varying land use and groundwater / surface water exchange, we parameterized a quantitative dynamic food web model (recharged organic carbon, microorganisms using the biodegradable fraction of this carbon, and fauna grazing on the microorganisms). With the model satisfactorily reflecting the field data, we calculated five further scenarios, three of which without fauna (mortality e.g. due to contamination, sudden peaks of temperature etc.). Two of the “fauna” and two of the “no fauna” scenarios were run with temperature elevated by 1.5°C and 3°C, respectively. The ecosystem service of carbon degradation was expressed as the difference in carbon concentration between the beginning of the simulation and the end of the simulation. In most scenarios, remaining carbon increased over time. The remaining carbon in some scenarios was up to 6.6 times as high in the “no fauna” scenarios compared to the reference case. Fauna was thus shown to fulfil a service by promoting microbial carbon degradation that may be substantial. Sustainable drinking water production is more reliable and less costly, the more active the groundwater fauna in the production area is. This model set up can serve to test other cases of varying physical and chemical variations and disturbances.

items.title: Genomic and dietary insights from non-invasive sampling of western capercaillie in Tyresta National Park (Sweden)
items.abstract: Abstract The Western Capercaillie ( Tetrao urogallus ), a boreal forest specialist, has experienced marked declines in southern Sweden due to habitat loss, fragmentation, and isolation. Tyresta National Park and the surrounding forests harbor one of the region’s last remnant southern populations, yet little is known about its genetic health, population structure, and dietary ecology. Here, we used low-coverage whole-genome sequencing of 272 non-invasively collected samples (feathers and faeces) to comprehensively assess the status of this population. Feather samples yielded high-quality genomic data, enabling sex identification, estimation of genome-wide heterozygosity, runs of homozygosity (ROH), and relatedness inference. Heterozygosity levels in Tyresta were comparable to other European Western Capercaillie populations, and inbreeding levels were generally low, although several individuals showed long ROH indicative of recent close-kin mating. Population structure analyses revealed a genetically distinct isolated unit with possible female-biased dispersal. Kinship analysis uncovered a highly interconnected social network, with males having, on average, more relatives than females. Recapture simulations based on genotype matching estimated a current maximum population size of 145–215 individuals. Faecal metagenomic analysis revealed a diverse diet, including key plant species such as blueberry, lingonberry, and alder, and a wide range of invertebrates critical for chick development. Despite its current genetic robustness, the Tyresta population is small, isolated, and at risk of inbreeding depression. Conservation efforts should prioritize maintaining habitat quality, promoting gene flow, e.g., by protecting migration corridors to neighbouring populations and ensuring a rich forest invertebrate community to support population resilience.

items.title: More than Leaves: Phylogenetic and Spatial Dimensions of Ritual Plant use in Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract The Povos e Comunidades Tradicionais de Terreiro e de Matriz Africana in Brazil (Traditional Peoples and Communities of Afro-Brazilian Terreiro and African Matrix religions, henceforth Povos de Terreiro ) are Afro-Brazilian religious communities in which plants play important ritual, therapeutic, and cultural roles. Their communities are organized around terreiros , sacred spaces where religious practices, ceremonies, and plant-related knowledge are maintained and transmitted. We investigated whether variation in the plants reported in Brazilian terreiros was associated with environmental context, geographic proximity, or shared cultural heritage. We compiled 643 species from 32 publications and compared taxonomic and phylogenetic composition across Brazilian biomes, tested spatial autocorrelation, and examined species frequencies and biogeographic status. Taxonomic composition differed among biomes, whereas phylogenetic composition did not. Geographic proximity was not associated with taxonomic or phylogenetic similarity. Ten species occurred in at least half of the analyzed terreiros , and the flora included similar proportions of species native (52%) and non-native (48%) to Brazil. The recurrence of the same species in geographically distant terreiros is consistent with a role for shared plant knowledge in shaping similarities among them. Non-native plants used in Afro-Brazilian religious practices have diverse biogeographic and historical origins.

items.title: Plant invasions in Natura 2000 habitats in Poland are driven primarily by macroclimatic factors
items.abstract: Invasive plants pose an ecological threat around the world. Their influence can also be observed in protected areas such as the European Ecological Network Natura 2000. Although invasions can endanger protected habitats, the specific impact of invasive species in such areas and the factors that determine their spread remain understudied. This study aimed to analyse the factors influencing the probability of plant invasion in five groups of habitat types protected under the EU Habitats Directive, based on Polish State Monitoring of Natura 2000 data. A total of 2,096 monitoring sites, with a balanced distribution across the country, were analysed, belonging to broadleaf forests, riverine habitats, dry grasslands, mesic and wet grasslands, and mires. The study confirmed the presence of 45 invasive species and two potentially invasive species. The most frequently observed species were Impatiens parviflora , Prunus serotina , Solidago gigantea , Erigeron canadensis , Solidago canadensis , and Bidens frondosa . The correlation between the presence of invasive species in monitored Natura 2000 sites and 38 variables was then analysed. The probability of invasion was much higher in regions with milder and wetter winters and, at the same time, in areas with a more continental climate. The importance of large rivers and their valleys and major roads as corridors facilitating plant invasions was also confirmed. Moreover, this study demonstrated the effectiveness of the State Monitoring Programme in detecting invasive species and analysing invasions. The programme could be used to inform the planning of future invasion management and prevention strategies.

items.title: Dynamic instabilities and pattern formation in chemotactic active matter
items.abstract: Collectives of actively-moving particles can spontaneously segregate into dilute and dense phases through a process known as motility-induced phase separation (MIPS). This captivating phenomenon is well-studied for randomly-moving particles with no directional bias. However, many active systems perform collective chemotaxis -- directed motion along a chemical gradient collectively generated by the particles themselves through consumption or production. Here, we use linear stability analysis, amplitude equations, and numerical simulations to study how MIPS is influenced by collective chemotaxis. We find that chemotaxis can either arrest or entirely suppress MIPS, or give rise to novel dynamic instabilities such as traveling waves and spirals. We predict the stability region of the stationary and oscillatory patterns and identify four types of bifurcation that can arise: pitchfork, saddle-node, infinite period, and supercritical Hopf. We also derive analytical expressions for the amplitude of the pattern and traveling wave velocity, yielding excellent quantitative agreement with simulations. Furthermore, we generalize our model to study particles that either consume or produce chemoattractant or chemorepellent, as well as mixtures of particles with different chemotactic behaviors. By establishing quantitative principles describing the competition between MIPS and chemotaxis, our study helps deepen understanding of the rich physics underlying chemically-responsive active matter systems.

items.title: When dose matters: Linking exposure, environment, and epidemic persistence in wildlife systems
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding how infectious disease spreads through exposure is key to predicting outbreaks and effective control measures. This is important for wildlife, where outbreaks often lead to devastating ecological consequences. Traditional epidemiological models often assume equal infection risk regardless of exposure dose and focus on a single infection stage. This assumption eventually overlook variations in initial doses and the role of environmental pathogen reservoirs. We hypothesized that higher exposure doses accelerate disease progression, increase mortality, and elevate pathogen shedding but reduce infectious periods. To evaluate this, we estimated key disease parameters - including latency period, disease-induced mortality, zoospore shedding rates, and transmission probability-from datasets of eastern newt ( Notophthalmus viridescens ) exposed to varying zoospore concentrations of fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans (Bsal) . Guided by the empirical evidence,we developed a novel mathematical model capturing dose-dependent transmission, multiple exposure stages, and environmental pathogen accumulation. This empirically driven modeling framework reveals how exposure levels shape disease trajectory, host outcomes and pathogen persistence. Our findings indicate that high initial doses lead to faster disease progression and higher mortality. On the other hand, environmental transmission can sustain outbreaks even under low direct contact rates. Integrating dose dependence with environmental transmission, our framework advances epidemiological modeling of pathogen persistence.

items.title: Divergent mercury accumulation dynamics in tropical dry and moist broadleaf forests
items.abstract: Abstract. Forests are major sinks for atmospheric mercury (Hg) due to the efficiency of stomatal uptake and litter deposition. Tropical forests, highly productive ecosystems, remain understudied despite their pronounced climatic and phenological variability. We investigated whether seasonal rainfall regimes and associated tree adaptations regulate the Hg dynamics – its uptake by leaves, deposition through litter, and storage in soils– in secondary tropical moist broadleaf (TMBF) and tropical dry broadleaf (TDBF) forests from Costa Rica. Seasonality strongly controlled Hg sequestration in TDBF. Deciduous trees showed 4.7 times higher foliar Hg concentration in the wet season, when leaves were mature, compared to the dry season, when newly flushed leaves emerged after leaf shedding. Evergreen trees in TDBF demonstrated 2.3 times lower foliar Hg concentrations in the dry season than in the wet season (23 vs. 53 µg kg-1), likely due to various associated physiological processes (e.g., leaf flushing). However, the primary mechanism remains unclear given the complex and unexplored Hg dynamics in TDBF. TMBF showed no clear seasonal variation in foliar Hg in either deciduous (dry: 48; wet: 54 µg kg-1) or evergreen trees (dry: 57; wet: 53 µg kg-1), likely due to longer leaf lifespan sustaining year-round transpiration and stomatal Hg uptake under high humidity. Atmospheric Hg concentrations in TDBF were two times higher than in TMBF (1.2 vs. 0.6 ng m-3) across both seasons, likely reflecting greater Hg capture per unit area in TMBF due to denser vegetation and enhanced wet deposition via rainfall. Foliar Hg was not correlated with stomatal density or specific leaf area in either forest type. Soil Hg concentrations, however, were correlated with litter-derived inputs, supporting litter as the dominant Hg transfer pathway. Higher seasonally averaged Hg inputs via litter (34 μg m-2) in TMBF than in the TDBF (19 μg m-2) resulted in 3.4 times higher soil Hg concentrations (0–30 cm) in TMBF (115 µg kg-1) than in TDBF (34 µg kg-1). Soil Hg stocks were 2.6 times lower at a previously deforested TMBF site, indicating persistent disturbance effects despite almost three decades of reforestation. Overall, seasonality regulated Hg sequestration in TDBF, yet both TDBF and TMBF serve as important global Hg sinks with contrasting dynamics that are potentially sensitive to climate change.

items.title: Effects of moss restoration on topsoil water dynamics in a temperate vineyard
items.abstract: Abstract. Climate change is intensifying pressure on vineyard soil and water management, particularly under-vine, where vegetation is commonly suppressed to minimize competition with grapevines. Bryophytes represent a promising but little-tested alternative to bare soil or cover crops. We evaluated moss restoration as an under-vine ground cover in a temperate, rainfed vineyard in southwestern Germany, comparing it with bare soil and cover crop (grass) over a 22-month field experiment. Continuous topsoil moisture measurements using time-domain transmission sensors were used to analyse the initial response time (the time between the onset of precipitation and the first increase in topsoil moisture) and the peak response time (the time between the onset of precipitation and the maximum topsoil moisture). We additionally quantified mean topsoil moisture and drying rates and monitored treatment development during and after maintenance. Moss restoration did not significantly delay topsoil moisture response times following precipitation compared to grass or bare soil. Initial response times followed the pattern grass > moss > bare soil; differences between treatments were most pronounced under light and moderate precipitation and declined with increasing intensity, with moss and bare soil converging under heavy events. Peak response times followed a similar pattern (grass > moss ≈ bare soil), with significant differences restricted to light and heavy precipitation events: grass exhibited longer peak response times than bare soil under light rainfall and longer times than both bare soil and moss under heavy rainfall. Mean topsoil moisture did not differ significantly among treatments, whereas drying rates were higher under moss and bare soil than under grass. Moss plots initially suppressed grass establishment and consistently exhibited the lowest variability in topsoil moisture response, although vegetation cover and functional differences between treatments gradually converged after maintenance ceased. Overall, moss restoration maintained topsoil moisture dynamics comparable to bare soil while avoiding the delayed infiltration and higher variability associated with grass cover. These results suggest that mosses may provide a low-maintenance under-vine ground cover with stable hydrological functioning, warranting further investigation into their long-term persistence and performance under future climate and management scenarios.

items.title: Forest or tundra? How different vegetation reconstructions of Last Glacial landscapes in Europe may shape our perception of early human dispersal processes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Regional variability and long‐term changes of past ecosystems likely had a strong impact on hunter–gatherer population dynamics, including the expansion of anatomically modern humans and the disappearance of Neanderthals. However, our understanding of these ecosystems remains limited, even when looking at large‐scale patterns, such as the extent and distribution of forested areas. Vegetation reconstructions are key to better understanding ecological preferences and their influence on the spatial distribution and dispersals of early humans. Here, we compare four different vegetation reconstruction techniques, two based on pollen data and two vegetation models, between 70 and 20 thousand years before present in Europe. Absolute values in forest cover can differ by up to 40% between reconstruction techniques, highlighting that the choice of method can make the difference between a boreal forest and a tundra. Besides method‐specific and statistical uncertainties, the reason for such a substantial offset lies in the loose definition of forest cover metrics, rendering a direct comparison between methods impossible. At the same time, we show that all reconstruction techniques accurately reconstruct ecosystem dynamics over time on continental to regional scales. We therefore highly recommend that researchers use relative forest cover measures as the more robust method to estimate past landscapes.

items.title: Soil heterogeneity modulates competitive interactions between Solanum rostratum and replacement control plants
items.abstract: Abstract Background Plant replacement control is an important ecological approach for managing the invasive weed Solanum rostratum , yet its effectiveness is strongly mediated by soil conditions. However, current screening of replacement species often overlooks how soil heterogeneity alters competitive outcomes and plant–soil nutrient feedbacks, limiting the stability and general applicability of this approach. We conducted a two-factor pot experiment using soils collected from typical regions in China where S. rostratum is widely distributed. Monocultures and mixtures of S. rostratum and six native forage species were established. Plant biomass and chlorophyll content were measured, competitive effects were quantified using the log response ratio (lnRR), and redundancy analysis was used to link plant performance with soil nutrient dynamics. Results Mixed planting consistently suppressed S. rostratum across all soils (lnRR < 0), although the magnitude of suppression and the most effective replacement species varied markedly among soil types. Soil nutrient variation explained 30.69% of the variation in S. rostratum traits. Leymus chinensis and Festuca arundinacea showed greater competitiveness in soils with higher organic matter or nitrogen availability, whereas Medicago sativa and Agropyron cristatum exerted stronger suppression where plant performance was closely associated with changes in nutrient availability. Notably, M. sativa maintained relatively stable suppressive effects even under nutrient-poor conditions. Conclusion Our results demonstrate that replacement control efficacy is jointly regulated by species-specific competitive ability and soil nutrient feedbacks under heterogeneous soil conditions. These findings highlight the importance of matching replacement species to soil environments to achieve stable and effective ecological control of S. rostratum .

items.title: From detections to demography: methodological challenges and opportunities in survival estimation from automated telemetry networks
items.abstract: Abstract Survival is a fundamental demographic process influencing individual fitness and population dynamics. Automated telemetry systems offer unprecedented opportunities to estimate survival of highly mobile organisms across broad spatial and temporal scales. However, the structure of these tracking networks creates systematic biases that render standard survival models inadequate. Receiver stations are distributed unevenly across landscapes and over time, meaning that individuals taking different movement paths encounter vastly different opportunities for detection. This spatial clustering also creates problematic dependencies: animals detected in receiver-dense areas are more likely to be detected again, while those in sparse areas may disappear from view despite being alive. These observation biases can easily be mistaken for genuine differences in survival, leading to incorrect ecological or conservation inferences. Here, we review the unique challenges posed by automated telemetry data for survival estimation, highlight existing methodological solutions including spatially explicit approaches and modified capture-mark-recapture frameworks, and provide recommendations for advancing this critical application of wildlife tracking networks.

items.title: Morphophysiological development, allometric growth, and early ontogeny of the Amazonian ornamental characid Moenkhausia oligolepis (Günther, 1864)
items.abstract: Abstract This study describes, for the first time, the morphophysiological development, allometric growth patterns, and the main initial ontogenetic events of Moenkhausia oligolepis , a species of ecological and ornamental importance in the Amazon region. Hatching occurred 16 hours after fertilization, under an average temperature of 25.36 ± 0.64°C with a pH of 7.28 ± 1.11. From hatching onward, the larvae were sampled at regular intervals (0–6 hours post-hatching with collections every 2 h; 6–22 h every 4 h; and subsequently, daily collections) for morphological, morphometric, meristic, and histological analyses. Larval development spanned from the vitelline stage to the post-flexion stage (0–30 days after hatching—DAH), with a well-defined sequence of events: mouth opening and initiation of exogenous feeding at 3 DAH, cannibalistic behavior at 4 DAH, notochord flexion at 15 DAH (mean CP = 6.33 ± 0.56 mm), and the larval–juvenile transition at 30 POE with the development of fin rays and the appearance of scales. Allometric analyses revealed positive cephalic growth relative to standard length (b = 1.389 for HL/SL), indicating prioritization of the development of structures associated with feeding and sensory perception. Notochord length and preanal distance showed growth close to isometry relative to standard length, while body height exhibited negative allometry. Histological analysis demonstrated progressive differentiation of the digestive tract, with the presence of a buccopharyngeal cavity, esophagus, segmented intestine (anterior, middle, and posterior regions), and mucosal cells at 3 DAH. Cytoplasmic vacuolization was observed in hepatocytes starting at 23 DAH, associated with the presence of digested material in the intestinal lumen. The secondary lamellae of the gills exhibited evident buds at 4 DAH, and the swim bladder was divided into two regions at the end of flexion (22 DAH). Gonadal evaluation indicated undifferentiated gonads up to 50 DAH and ovarian differentiation at 60 DAH, characterized by the presence of primary meiotic oocytes; testicular differentiation was not observed during the analyzed period. Based on the observed morphological and ontogenetic characteristics, four larval stages were described (yolk sac, pre-flexion, flexion, and post-flexion). The results expand knowledge of the species’ early biology, providing relevant insights for taxonomic, ecological, and conservation studies, as well as for improving management and larviculture strategies for native ornamental fish.

items.title: Characterization of the organelle genomes of mycoheterotrophic Thismia angustimitra and evidence suggesting horizontal gene transfer
items.abstract: Abstract Background Our knowledge about mitochondrial genome evolution in plants is lacking far behind our knowledge of plastome evolution. In heterotrophic plants, it is well-known that plastome degradation and reduced or lost photosynthesis go hand in hand, and there is little if any difference between plastome evolution in mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites. The mitochondrial genome appears less affected by a heterotrophic lifestyle, although exceptions occur. In contrast to plastome evolution, mitochondrial evolution may differ between mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites, in particular with regards to the occurrence of horizontal gene transfer. However, data from mycoheterotrophs are scarce, and complete mitogenomes are only known from three of ten clades. Results Here we present data from the complete plastome and mitogenome from Thismia angustimitra , representing a fourth clade of mycoheterotrophs. The 18,215 bp plastome is much reduced and includes only few genes. The mitogenome has a multicircular structure consisting of 22 chromosomes with a total length of 422,400 bp. The gene content and the pattern of RNA editing are normal. The mitogenome includes only few repeats and recombinational activity is limited. A search for foreign DNA did not reveal any fungal sequences, and the content of plastid DNA is low. Just a few inserts appear to have originated through intracellular transfer, whereas others most likely stem from horizontal gene transfer. Conclusion The highly reduced plastome of T. angustimitra fits completely the general picture of plastome degradation in heterotrophic plants. Whereas the mitogenome in many aspects appears unaffected by the lifestyle, the recombinational activity is unusually low. Surprisingly, we find evidence of horizontal gene transfer, suggesting that this phenomenon may be more common among mycoheterotrophic plants than previously thought.

items.title: Riverine biogeochemistry from the Andes to the ocean: longitudinal patterns along a Mediterranean Andean catchment in central Chile
items.abstract: Abstract. Rivers act as dynamic connectors between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, transporting and transforming materials along the aquatic continuum. We investigated longitudinal biogeochemical patterns across the Rapel catchment (central Chile) by integrating dissolved organic matter (DOM) characterization, dissolved metals and nutrients, and microbial community profiling from the Andean headwaters to the Pacific Ocean. Headwaters were characterized by low DOC and nutrient concentrations, high protein-like fluorescence, and diverse microbial assemblages dominated by Flavobacterium, Polaromonas, and Rhodoferax. Downstream, agricultural and mining activities increased nutrient and metal concentrations and altered microbial community composition with an increasing prevalence of hgcI_clade. The Rapel Reservoir emerged as a major biogeochemical discontinuity, promoting DOM transformation, restructuring microbial assemblages, and modifying downstream chemical conditions. Overall, tributary inputs, land use, and hydrological regulation disrupted simple longitudinal patterns and generated distinct biogeochemical processing zones. These findings highlight the interplay between downstream transport and local processing in shaping riverine functioning in Mediterranean Andean catchments and provide a basis for assessing future climate and land-use impacts on riverine biogeochemistry.

items.title: Is conservation AI ready? Quantifying the challenges of automated species identification in Colombia
items.abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly adopted by conservation organizations to overcome taxonomic bottlenecks. However, its reliability may systematically fail for sparsely documented and recently described taxa. This study evaluates automated species identification using 10,000 research-grade iNaturalist images of Colombian vertebrates across amphibians, birds, fishes, mammals, and reptiles. Testing OpenAI GPT-5.2 with localized prompts but no taxonomic metadata, we found that species-level accuracy scales non-linearly with global photographic representation and decays severely for recently recognized taxa. At the 10th percentile of data availability, predicted accuracy collapsed to 6–12% for most groups, with mammals performing best at 41%. Furthermore, severe taxonomic hallucinations frequently crossed class boundaries, particularly among fishes and reptiles. These findings demonstrate that AI errors are not random, but structurally inherent to the long-tail distributions of training data. While general-purpose AI offers immense value for rapid sorting, its operational integration requires strict safeguards, including forced abstention protocols, geographic filters, and mandatory expert escalation for rare or recently described species.

items.title: Short fire-return intervals modify fuel structure, changing flammability and fire behavior in dry forests of southeastern Australia
items.abstract: Abstract Shortening fire-return intervals are pushing fire-tolerant ecosystems in temperate Australia beyond their ecological limits, producing alternative vegetation states with markedly different composition and structure. While the structural effects of these regime shifts on fire-tolerant eucalypt forests are increasingly documented, their consequences for flammability remain largely untested. We compared fuel structure and load, surface fuel flammability, and modelled point-based fire behaviour between areas retaining a Eucalyptus overstorey under typical fire regimes (reference state) and alternative states in fire-tolerant native forests of southeastern Australia. Fuel hazard was visually assessed using an established field protocol, and surface fuels were sampled for laboratory flammability testing. Point-based fire behaviour was modelled using Vesta Mk2 across five weather scenarios spanning prescribed-burn to extreme wildfire conditions. Fuel hazard scores were significantly higher for surface and elevated strata in alternative states, but higher for near-surface and bark strata in reference states. However, laboratory flammability tests showed that surface fuels from alternative states were less ignitable, combustible, and consumable than those from reference states. Modelled fire behaviour showed consistently taller flames in alternative states across all weather scenarios, though rate of spread was greater only under the most extreme conditions. Spotting distances were consistently higher in reference states. These results show that alternative-state eucalypt forests produce a distinct fire behaviour signature: lower surface fuel flammability, greater flame height, but reduced spotting potential. The landscape-scale implications of this altered fire behaviour for subsequent fire regimes and the persistence of alternative states warrant further investigation.

items.title: Supplementation of Tannin Extracts and Islands of Plant Diversity on Cattle Grazing Brome Grass Monocultures: Influence on Behavior, Welfare, Performance and Health
items.abstract: Beef cattle grazing systems in the western United States often depend on grass monocultures that decline in nutritional quality during summer. As pasture quality decreases, cattle have fewer opportunities for selective foraging, grazing efficiency declines, and producers face increased supplementation costs to maintain animal performance, welfare, and effective pasture use. This dissertation examined whether interventions that provide phytochemicals either as a supplement or through the establishment of taxonomically diverse “hot spots” in otherwise monotonous landscapes could improve cow-calf pair performance and enhance the sustainability of agroecosystems. The study tested two strategies with free-grazing cow–calf pairs: supplementation with tannin extract and establishing of small patches, or “islands,” of diverse, phytochemically rich forage species within bromegrass pastures. Using combined GPS–tri-axial accelerometer collars, pedometers, and machine-learning methods, the study identified cattle behavioral responses to these feeding strategies with high accuracy. The study developed a monitoring system that combined GPS collars, motion sensors, and direct animal observations to classify cattle behavior while grazing. These tools were able to identify important activities such as grazing, resting, rumination, walking, and posture with high accuracy. Moderate tannin supplementation led cattle to graze longer during the evening, drink more water, change between lying and standing postures less often, and use the pasture more evenly than cattle that did not receive tannins. These responses suggest that tannin supplementation can influence grazing distribution and welfare, and may help reduce concentrated grazing pressure in free-grazing systems. Biological measurements also indicated changes in antioxidant activity, rumen microbial processes, and nitrogen use, showing that tannins had an impact on cattle through both behavioral and physiological pathways. When cattle grazed diverse forages in patches embedded in grass, their preference and selection changed over the summer. They did not graze all plants equally; instead, they showed a preference for sainfoin and adjusted their diets over time by mixing different forages. These findings show that diverse forage “hotspots” can expand feeding choices in otherwise monotonous pasture systems. By linking cattle behavior with welfare, performance, and health indicators, this dissertation shows that phytochemical-based strategies offer a practical way to improve grass monocultures during summer as forage nutritive value decline. Rather than relying solely on protein supplementation, integrating moderate tannin supplementation or establishing small patches of plant diversity can help cattle make better use of pasture resources while supporting more resilient and sustainable beef production systems.

items.title: Trends in phytoplankton communities uncovered by the Southern Ocean Continuous Plankton Recorder
items.abstract: Context Phytoplankton communities in the Southern Ocean are shifting as the region experiences rapid environmental change. Aims To investigate long-term trends or changes in Southern Ocean phytoplankton communities, and model abundance patterns of key dominant genera against sampling year and sea-surface temperature (SST). Methods Using 10 years of Southern Ocean Continuous Plankton Recorder (SO-CPR) data within a 15-year period (2007–21), we examined long-term trends in phytoplankton composition, with emphasis on six ecologically important diatom genera (Chaetoceros, Thalassiothrix, Fragilariopsis, Pseudo-nitzschia, Rhizosolenia and Corethron). Key results Overall diatom and dinoflagellate abundances increased significantly across the sampling domain, whereas the diatom:dinoflagellate ratio remained stable, suggesting little change in the relative contributions of these major phytoplankton groups despite increasing overall abundance. Patterns among focal genera differed, with distinct temporal trends and contrasting relationships with sea-surface temperature, indicating ecological differentiation among dominant Southern Ocean diatoms. Conclusions No single genus accounted for the observed increase in abundance, suggesting a community-wide response to environmental change. Implications These results demonstrated the value of long-term CPR observations for detecting trends, natural variability and ecological change in a rapidly warming Southern Ocean.

items.title: Cataxia on the edge: range contraction of endemic montane mygalomorph spiders in a biodiversity hotspot
items.abstract: Context Large shifts in species distributions are projected under future climate scenarios, yet long-term empirical evidence remains scarce, particularly for invertebrates. Aims We quantified changes in occupancy, abundance, and population structure over 22 years for four short-range endemic trapdoor spider species (Cataxia sandsorum, C. stirlingi, C. colesi, C. barrettae) and tested associations with microhabitat, environmental, and disturbance conditions. Methods Presence–absence surveys conducted in 2002 and 2024 across >250 km of replicated traverses were combined with burrow density and microhabitat assessments from 293 quadrats across 17 subpopulations. Species distribution models identified predictors of occupancy and burrow density. Key results All species showed severe contractions, with 49–67% reductions in area of occupancy and >98% declines in burrow abundance. Declines were greatest at lower elevations and in areas exposed to repeated intense fires. These areas also supported fewer juveniles and recruits. Remnant populations persist mostly in cool, moist, high-elevation gullies where orographic cloud, rocky substrates, and microhabitat complexity provide climate buffering and fire refuge. Occupancy and burrow density were strongly associated with topography and fine-scale microhabitat variables. Conclusions Despite historical persistence linked to longevity and deep-burrowing behaviour, these species have declined rapidly over the past two decades. Implications Narrow habitat requirements and limited dispersal capacity render these taxa highly vulnerable to escalating climate and fire pressures. Other co-habiting surface and shallow-burrowing relict taxa may face even greater risk. Urgent conservation action is required, including habitat protection and restoration, microhabitat enhancement, fire-regime management, assisted recolonisation, connectivity management, long-term monitoring, legislative integration, and stakeholder engagement.
