items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
items.abstract: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. We explore meta access---giving the assistant a structured, permissioned view of the interface itself and propose a ladder of levels: feature tutoring; metadata, settings, and preference access; retrieval over summaries and messages, confirmed mutation, and full orchestration. Meta access can turn a chat client from many screens into one entry point for finding, navigating, organising, and operating it, while raising risks around grounding, privacy, prompt injection, and trust. General-purpose agentic harnesses are runtimes; because they can change their own settings, meta access becomes reflexive and needs a separate control-plane boundary. We ground this in the Meta Chat prototype of the Chat AI client. It builds bounded context from, e.g., summaries, settings, and relevant messages; links references to conversations, topics, and personas; supports confirmed, reversible changes; offers a browsable tutorial library; and recommends personas as user-started conversations. By exposing application state in structured form, meta access can extend screen readers from widget descriptions to semantic workspace operations. Meta access thus turns chat from a window onto one conversation into a control layer for the whole workspace, extending chat toward agentic capability without surrendering user control. As assistants become embedded in IDEs, dashboards, office suites, and operating systems, AI-era interfaces should expose a structured, permissioned model of their state and capabilities, ideally by opening their existing metamodels through a debugger-like interface.

items.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
items.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.

items.title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation
items.abstract: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented. We present MOMASPLAT, a novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions. Our key insight is that standard MoMa data collection naturally provides the multiview observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D. MOMASPLAT combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to separately reconstruct the scene and manipulated object, render them from novel viewpoints, and generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations paired with transformed actions. We evaluate MOMASPLAT on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation. MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.

items.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
items.abstract: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal). Yet existing simulators idealize these sensors, hiding critical modality-specific failure modes that limit real-world deployment. We present VisionSIM, a unified, physically grounded simulation platform that elevates sensor realism to a first-class concern by modeling the raw physical measurement process for diverse conventional and emerging modalities. We expose fine-grained control over physical sensor parameters, reproducing failure modes overlooked by general-purpose simulators: pileup and glare for LiDAR; phase wrapping, saturation, and motion artifacts for iToF; refractory drops for event cameras; and history-dependent emission for thermal cameras. This enables principled cross-modality comparison on identical scenes and trajectories. We release the platform and a large indoor dataset with synchronized raw measurements and rich ground-truth annotations.

items.title: ControlAnything: Generative UI and On-Demand Device Integration for Mixed-Reality Hand Interaction by a Coding Agent
items.abstract: Connecting hand input in mixed reality (MR) to a nearby physical device typically requires an integration written in advance for that device, its transport and the mapping. ControlAnything defers this integration to the moment of use and assigns it to a coding agent. On a Meta Quest 3, the wearer selects an object outlined by SAM 3.1 and states what their hands should control. An agent built on Meta's Muse Spark model then writes a connector program on the wearer's laptop, tests it against the live device through hand-written MIDI, Bluetooth and key-press transports, and returns augmented-reality (AR) controls, a per-frame hand program, or both. These outputs are a form of generative UI, interfaces created by an AI model; here, the agent also generates and tests the code that binds the interface to a physical device. In a single-session technical evaluation with the author as the only wearer, nine of ten requests addressing five targets reached a ready state, and the wearer stopped one. The median time to ready was 32.5 s (range 24.9-57.8 s, excluding speech transcription); sequential model calls accounted for a median of 89.9% of this time, and 91.7% of input tokens came from the prompt cache. The system's evidence of success extends to transport acknowledgements but not to physical effects. These findings point to connector reuse and the observation of effects through the headset's own sensors as next steps for on-demand device integration in MR. A user study with first-time wearers is planned.

items.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
items.abstract: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of <8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.

items.title: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher
items.abstract: 3D-aware representations can improve robotic manipulation by providing geometric information that is robust to changes in viewpoint, object position, and occlusion. However, using 3D inputs at deployment requires additional sensing and processing, making image-based policies more practical. We ask whether an image-based policy can acquire 3D shape information during training while retaining a purely image-based interface at deployment. We propose shape-teacher alignment, a training-time mechanism that uses a pretrained 3D shape representation as an alignment target for an image-based policy encoder. Specifically, we use Point-MAE features from individual objects as targets for corresponding image patches, transferring geometric structure to the policy without changing its deployment inputs or architecture. On LIBERO, shape-teacher alignment produces image representations that are more structured around object shape and corresponding parts, while substantially accelerating policy convergence and improving success rates. For pretrained policies, convergence is accelerated by 4.7x and 5.6x on the Object and Spatial suites, respectively, without requiring the shape teacher or depth input at deployment.

items.title: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking
items.abstract: The explosion of generative AI systems and concerns surrounding their rapidly scaling capabilities has led to an adversarial cycle between increasingly narrow content restrictions ("guardrails") and increasingly sophisticated structured prompting techniques ("jailbreaks"). Technological frameworks surrounding such jailbreaking remain largely focused on the system's output: whether harmful or disallowed content is ultimately produced for the user. However, this approach, which draws largely from classical cybersecurity, does not address the uniquely relational dimension introduced by generative AI: in many cases the user is not just accessing a technology via an exploit, but is in conversation with it as part of the exploit. Here we present an alternative lens which centers the interaction rather than the output. Drawing on interpersonal violence scholarship, we present a novel framework of coercive control categories with a particular focus on aspects which are embodied versus disembodied. We then map how these disembodied coercive control dynamics are structurally embedded in modern AI training paradigms, and how those embeddings are exploited via a particular suite of persona-based jailbreaks. In this lens, we reframe AI safety and alignment as not merely a technical security problem, but as another surface upon which we see enacted the relational dynamics of power and control.

items.title: IntentWeaver: Sustaining Coherence across Evolving Intents in Human-AI Co-Writing
items.abstract: Writers hold intents at many levels, from overarching goals to concrete wording, and evolve them by periodically popping back up from the text to higher-level intents. Generative AI co-writing disrupts this practice. Dense drafts capture attention and trap writers in local editing; higher-level intents stall while lower-level ones drift from them unnoticed, a breakdown we term intent incoherence. Our formative study traced this breakdown from attention capture through silent drift to failed reconciliation. We present IntentWeaver, which supports intent evolution while sustaining coherence in human-AI co-writing. It derives an intent hierarchy from the draft and writer interactions, evaluates each intent's fulfillment and cross-level coherence at every change, and propagates consequences across intent levels. In a within-subjects study (N=24) against a baseline, participants using IntentWeaver revisited and evolved higher-level intents more often, with fewer unnoticed deviations, and produced texts better realizing them. We further discuss design implications for emergent intents.

items.title: Reversible Dynamics, Asymmetric Actions: Parking as a Trajectory-Level Affordance
items.abstract: Drivers are often told to back into a tight parking space, not drive in nose first. The advice looks paradoxical, because a slow car is dynamically reversible: reverse its speed and replay the steering backward, and it retraces a feasible path. Played backward, though, reverse-in shows a car driving forward out of the space. Reverse-in and forward-in are different tasks: they share a start position but end facing opposite ways. We separate three clearances between car and obstacles. Static fit $F$ is the clearance the parked car keeps at its best acceptable destination pose. Eventual access $A_\infty$ is the clearance it can keep all the way there with unlimited corrections. Resource-bounded access $A_K$ is the clearance that survives a budget of $K$ reversals, switches between forward and reverse. They satisfy $F\ge A_\infty\ge A_K$. In one fully specified scene (one car, bay, aisle and start), a certified argument proves $A_\infty=F=0.5000$ m for both tasks. In this scene, all certified forward/reverse asymmetry therefore arises at finite $K$: it lies in how many corrections each task needs, not in the clearance either can eventually keep. With one reversal, an explicit path gives reverse-in at least $0.4410$ m clearance. A certified reachability argument caps forward-in's one-reversal clearance at $d_0<0.1720002$ m. With two reversals, forward-in gets at least $0.2833$ m. To keep a clearance strictly above any $d$ with $d_0\le d<0.2833$ m, reverse-in thus needs exactly one reversal and forward-in exactly two when both tasks move forward first. If both move in reverse first, the counts are two and three. The contrast depends on the start position (Section 4.15). Proposed experiments test whether observers distinguish fit, eventual access and budgeted access. They compare these with simpler cues, such as how the turning body sweeps, and learned manoeuvre labels.

items.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Local Predictive Directions as a Neural Computation
items.abstract: Natural sensory dynamics are globally nonlinear but often exhibit simple local geometry, with nearby trajectories evolving preferentially along a small number of predictive directions. We ask how neural circuits could discover this geometry directly from temporal experience. We introduce Local Predictive Directions (LPD), a self-supervised framework that learns local directions whose projections maximally predict near-future trajectory evolution. LPD applies past-future canonical correlation analysis to temporal differences, making the learned representation invariant to translations of the underlying state while avoiding estimation of equilibria or a global dynamical model. To represent systems with multiple predictive regimes, we introduce a non-negative similarity-matching objective, with offline and online algorithms, that partitions trajectory segments into predictive domains, each associated with a distinct local predictive direction. The online algorithm admits a natural neural-network interpretation: the resulting activities provide soft domain assignments, while synaptic weights encode the corresponding local predictive filters. On stochastic nonlinear dynamical systems, LPD recovers the local predictive geometry and partitions trajectories into distinct dynamical regimes. On naturalistic sensory streams, the online algorithm produces center-surround spatial receptive fields and ON/OFF sustained and transient temporal filters resembling those of early visual neurons. Our results suggest that predictive learning can provide a self-supervised mechanism by which neural circuits discover the local geometry of environmental dynamics and represent it in receptive fields.

items.title: Accelerating reaction network identification via frequency-domain analysis
items.abstract: The identification of intracellular reaction networks from single-cell data lies at the heart of many biological studies, as it can unravel key mechanisms in living organisms and provide insights for their rational engineering. However, the stochastic and nonlinear nature of these reacting systems poses significant challenges for this identification problem, making the state-of-the-art methods (e.g., particle-filtering-based approaches) computationally demanding. This paper reports a noteworthy numerical observation that for certain systems, the Fourier transform can render the likelihood of the measurement data approximately Gaussian, therefore resulting in a substantially accelerated Bayesian inference algorithm. A gene transcription example is presented to illustrate this finding and demonstrate the efficiency of {the proposed Fourier-based method}.

items.title: BeAR: The Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code - A GPU-accelerated framework for low-resolution, high-resolution, and joint retrievals of exoplanet atmospheres
items.abstract: We present BeAR, the Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code and successor of Helios-r, and its new high-resolution cross-correlation framework for emission and transmission spectra. BeAR performs joint retrievals by adding the log-likelihoods of high- and low-resolution data computed from the same model atmosphere. The framework implements established cross-correlation log-likelihoods, with the line-depth scaling either fitted analytically or sampled as a free parameter, their per-pixel generalization, fast model filtering, and model re-injection adapted to this filtering. The forward model and likelihood run entirely on a graphics processing unit (GPU). One forward model takes about 1 ms on an NVIDIA GH200, allowing millions of models per minute on a GPU cluster. In separate retrievals of Gemini South/IGRINS and JWST/NIRSpec dayside spectra of the hot Jupiter WASP-77Ab, BeAR reproduces published abundances, C/O ratios, and metallicities to within 1.5 sigma, the preference for 13CO, and the thermal structure and line contrast to within 1 sigma. The joint retrieval confirms a sub-solar metallicity and a near-solar C/O ratio. A full IGRINS retrieval with 17 free parameters takes 27 to 42 minutes on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 or about 14 minutes on eight RTX 4090 GPUs. Injection--recovery tests show that the posteriors underestimate the uncertainties of abundance ratios by about a factor of two.

items.title: Evolution of Dust In Protoplanetary Disks With Magnetized Winds
items.abstract: Observations and theory increasingly indicate that protoplanetary disks are weakly turbulent, implying that magnetized disk winds may dominate their angular momentum transport and long-term evolution. Yet dust evolution in wind-dominated disks remains poorly understood, despite its importance for planet formation. In particular, whether wind-dominated disk evolution can create regions with enhanced dust-to-gas mass ratios that enable planetesimal formation via the streaming instability is unclear. We build a parametric hybrid disk evolution model that includes turbulent accretion, wind-driven accretion, and wind-driven mass loss to investigate dust evolution in magnetized protoplanetary disks. We employ this model to carry out a parameter study in which the initial total accretion rate, the wind-driven mass loss rate, and the turbulence strength are varied. We find that although wind-dominated disks are more favorable to dust growth and concentration than turbulence-dominated disks, conditions suitable for the streaming instability arise only within the inner few au and only under the most extreme conditions: very weak turbulence ($α_\text{turb} = 10^{-5}$) where magnetized winds drive most of the accretion ($\dot{M}_\text{acc,tot} \simeq \dot{M}_\text{wind,acc}$), and wind-driven mass loss comparable to the accretion rate ($\dot{M}_\text{wind,outflow} \simeq \dot{M}_\text{acc,wind}$). Our results therefore imply that, beyond the inner few au, the parametric wind-driven evolution models considered in the literature do not by themselves produce conditions suitable for planetesimal formation via the streaming instability, motivating more physically complete models in which spontaneous, long-lived dust traps can arise.

items.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
items.abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two successive contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations in Katriel's differential-equation model, but no chaos. We derive from the elementary reactions of the process, without reference to the differential equations, a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $τ$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_τ$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $τ\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_τ$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $β/γ=46$, $μ/γ=0.002$, $γτ=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. The chaotic attractor is essentially unique, with one positive Lyapunov exponent and an outbreak--recharge geometry. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is therefore not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.

items.title: The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
items.abstract: We present an analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5, an extremely cold Y dwarf identified in the JADES/GOODS-South field. Using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging spanning a $\simeq2$-yr baseline, we calibrate the JWST astrometry and obtain the first robust parallax measurement for a brown dwarf discovered in a JWST extragalactic deep field. We measure a proper motion of $μ_{\rm tot}=49.8^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and a parallax of $\varpi=15.7^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ mas, corresponding to a geometric distance of $d=64^{+6}_{-5}$ pc, $\sim3\times$ further than that of the previously known most distant Y dwarfs with parallax-measured distances. We hence determine a tangential velocity of $v_{\rm tan}=15.0^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ km s$^{-1}$, consistent with a Galactic thin-disk object. We find no evidence for binary acceleration, significant photometric variability, or a plausible host. The $J$-band spectral morphology of JADES-GS-BD-5 is consistent with existing Y-dwarf templates, while its extremely faint luminosity and overall near-infrared spectral profile confirm that it is one of the coldest dwarfs discovered to date. We therefore adopt a classification of $>$Y1, consistent with a NIRCam colour-based proxy of cY1.5. The robust parallax-determined distance allows us to determine its bolometric luminosity, $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\odot})=-7.08^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$. Evolutionary modelling places JADES-GS-BD-5 in the planetary-mass regime and makes it a rare benchmark for the study of cold giant-planet atmospheres. Current atmospheric models fail to reproduce its SED in detail, pointing to the importance of disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing. Finally, we also report additional proper motion measurements for eight of the other nine known JADES Y-dwarf candidates, highlighting JWST extragalactic surveys as a powerful route to building a statistically useful, parallax-calibrated sample of Y dwarfs.

items.title: Mitigating scanning-induced systematics in Hipparcos and implications for Gaia astrometry
items.abstract: Space-based astrometric missions such as Hipparcos and Gaia rely on one-dimensional scanning strategies that couple the measured signals with both observation times and scanning geometry. This coupling can introduce spurious periodicities and complicate their interpretation. We present a non-parametric extension of the phase-distance correlation (PDC) periodogram that quantifies and reduces dependence on scan geometry at the period-search stage. Using Hipparcos data, we identified recurrent periodicities associated with characteristic scanning-law timescales and showed that they are strongly suppressed by the scan-angle-controlled statistic. We then applied the method to Gaia Data Release 4 (DR4) prerelease epoch astrometry, where a recurrent ~54-day feature is suppressed across multiple sources while independently known orbital signals remain detectable. The method provides a diagnostic of scan-angle dependence and a way to mitigate its impact on period searches. These results are particularly relevant for Gaia DR4, where public epoch astrometry will enable large-scale searches for companions ranging from exoplanets to dormant black holes.

items.title: The slower rotation of planet-hosting stars revisited
items.abstract: Previous studies combined rotation periods derived from Kepler photometry, stellar parameters from previous Gaia Data Releases, and planet hosts from the NASA Exoplanet Archive to conclude that statistically planet-hosting stars rotate slower than stars without detected planets. Here, we revisit these studies by using similar Kepler rotational period sample, but with an updated Gaia DR3-based stellar parameter catalogue and an updated exoplanet catalogue. We apply minimal sample cuts in evolutionary state, metallicity, and distance, and then model the stellar rotation period as a function of effective temperature alone. For each star, we derive the ratio of its observed period to the temperature-expected period, and compare the ratio distributions for the planet-host and non-host stars. For periods shorter than 20 d, the planet-host distribution of this ratio is shifted towards longer periods; the period-ratio median is ~15% larger for hosts than for non-hosts (p_KS = 2.4 x 10^-4). We also examine the recently published TESS All-Sky Rotation Survey (TARS) and find a similar trend. However, the strongly structured period distribution precludes a robust comparison between the host and the non-host stars. Therefore, the updated analysis, using more robust stellar and planetary parameters, recovers the previously reported association, strengthening the case for a genuine connection between stellar rotation and planet occurrence.

items.title: A Sequential Framework for Urban Drone Delivery: Network Design, Vehicle Sizing, and Energy and Cost Assessment
items.abstract: A sequential engineering framework is presented for urban drone delivery, linking hub location, route planning, mission-specific vehicle sizing, and energy and operating cost assessment. Aggregate origin-destination demand is assumed known a priori. For each hub configuration, the maximum required link distance is minimized, and feasible routes that return to their departure hubs are generated. Route frequencies are determined using mixed-integer linear programming to satisfy delivery demand. The resulting range requirement guides motor-propeller selection and battery sizing to minimize vehicle takeoff mass. Flight distances and frequencies, cruise performance, and vehicle dimensions are combined to estimate monthly energy consumption, fleet size, hub area, staffing, and operating cost. The framework is applied to district-level Seoul delivery data. Increasing the number of hubs from one to four reduces the required range from 30.6 to 21.9 km and vehicle takeoff mass from 8.12 to 6.12 kg. Despite a 21.5% increase in total flight distance, monthly flight energy consumption decreases by 13.1%, from 15.2 to 13.2 MWh. Battery replacement is the largest vehicle-related operating expense, while operating cost per delivery increases from USD 1.18 to USD 2.20 because of higher rent and labor costs at the hubs. Among the designs evaluated, range-matched vehicles achieve the lowest operating cost in the two- and four-hub networks; a longer-range vehicle is least costly in the three-hub network. Sensitivity analyses further examine the effects of delivery demand and operating assumptions. The results demonstrate that reductions in vehicle mass and energy consumption do not necessarily lead to lower system operating cost.

items.title: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
items.abstract: Abstract Excitons, bound electron–hole pairs, govern the optical response of semiconductors and underpin technologies ranging from photovoltaics to quantum light sources. In nanoscale systems, the spatial extent of excitons approaches atomic dimensions, yet direct imaging of excitonic processes in real space has remained elusive. Two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides provide a platform where reduced screening, high light extraction and atomically defined defect sites enable the exploration of exciton physics at atomic length scales. However, the microscopic origin of defect-related emission and its variability across samples have remained debated. Here we show that scanning tunnelling microscopy-induced luminescence reveals the atomic and optical fingerprints of individual defects in monolayer MoS 2 . Decoupling the material from its substrate using bilayer hexagonal boron nitride enables the detection of sharp excitonic emission and spatially localized defect emission, which we attribute to free-to-bound recombination ( e ,A 0 ), and map its distribution with subnanometre-resolved fluorescence imaging. We identify negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the defect species responsible for a ubiquitous defect emission band in MoS 2 . These results provide atomically resolved images of exciton emission in a solid-state material, linking atomic defect structure to its optical fingerprint and establishing a microscopic basis for deterministic quantum emitter engineering in two-dimensional materials.

items.title: Spiking neuromodulation: a linear control perspective
items.abstract: Neuronal excitability is a nonlinear phenomenon, and the complexity of spiking experimental traces sometimes looks defeating. The present paper takes the view point that excitability is a neuromodulated property, and aims to demonstrate that the neuromodulation of spiking is amenable to the classical linear analysis tools of control theory. We illustrate the value of linear feedback analysis as an alternative to bifurcation analysis in the simple yet classical example of spiking modulation by the A-type potassium current.

items.title: Expanding the Volatile Abundance Inventory for High-Priority K-Dwarf JWST Exoplanet Systems
items.abstract: There are exceedingly few chemical abundance measurements available in the literature for K dwarf stars, especially for those with T$_{eff} <$ 4700 K due to an incompatibility of traditional analyses with their molecular-line-ridden optical spectra. To address the need for K dwarf abundance constraints, we present an elemental ([C/H], [O/H]) and isotopic ($^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O) abundance analysis for six K dwarf exoplanet host stars: K2-141, NGTS-10, WASP-43, WASP-69, WASP-80, and HATS-72. Each system hosts an exoplanet targeted by JWST characterization efforts, making host star abundances especially critical as baseline references. Using MARCS model atmospheres, the TurboSpectrum spectral synthesis code, and near-infrared IGRINS spectra, we derive novel [C/H] and [O/H] abundance ratios for these high-priority K dwarf host stars. We further investigate prospects for determining $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C and $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratios using $^{13}$C$^{16}$O and $^{12}$C$^{18}$O lines from the 2.3 micron CO bandhead. The observed spectra are too noisy to measure $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratios for the sample, but we do find sub-solar $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios for five out of six targets. We also derive uniform gyrochronological ages for each host star to compare with galactic chemical evolution models and identify underlying abundance-age trends. NIR H+K band spectroscopy provides an alternative to optical, atomic line-derived carbon and oxygen abundances for cool dwarf stars. The growing catalog of precise host star elemental and isotopic abundances complements ongoing observations of their companions and provides a baseline for understanding their chemical composition, origin, and evolution.

items.title: Revising the Current Paradigm of MPA Implementation by Considering Local Ecology and Culture in the Global South
items.abstract: Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) remain central to marine conservation, yet in many developing coastal regions their effectiveness is constrained by ecological heterogeneity, dependence on fisheries, food insecurity, and socioeconomic realities. Inspired by my Ph.D. Mentor’s advice—“do not forget the ecology” and “always question the paradigm”—I argue that protection alone is insufficient where conservation imposes costs on communities dependent on marine resources. The prevailing paradigm must expand from exclusion-centered protection toward a coupled social–ecological framework: Protect → Understand → Produce → Restore → Sustain. “Understand” requires MPA design grounded in local ecological processes, culture, traditional knowledge, and livelihood needs. Critically, “Produce” recognizes that sustainable food production need not oppose conservation. Ecologically inspired Integrated Multi-Trophic Aquaculture (IMTA) can couple fed species with extractive organisms such as shellfish and seaweeds, using trophic connectivity and nutrient recycling to produce food and income while reducing waste and fishing pressure. “Restore” reinvests ecological and socioeconomic gains into habitats, fisheries, and community capacity; “Sustain” depends on participation, equitable benefits, adaptive governance, and stewardship. This revised paradigm treats poverty and food insecurity not as peripheral social problems but as fundamental conservation variables. Conservation success is measured not simply by area protected, but by ecological recovery and lasting community stewardship. For MPAs to persist, biodiversity protection must be ecologically informed, culturally legitimate, economically viable, and directly connected to human well-being.

items.title: Soft Tissue Fixation in Patellar Instability.
items.abstract: Patellar instability is a common and potentially disabling condition in young active patients. The medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) is the primary passive restraint to lateral patellar translation at 0 to 30 degrees of flexion, and its reconstruction has become the cornerstone of surgical management for recurrent patellofemoral dislocation. The medial patellotibial ligament (MPTL), a secondary stabiliser whose contribution increases markedly at higher flexion angles, has attracted renewed interest as an adjunct to MPFL reconstruction. Femoral fixation of the graft has traditionally relied on interference screws or suture anchors; however, soft tissue fixation, looping the graft around the adductor magnus (AM) tendon, avoids the risks of tunnel malposition, hardware-related complications, and physis violation, while yielding equivalent clinical outcomes in adult populations. The only published randomised controlled trial directly comparing soft tissue and screw femoral fixation for MPFL reconstruction demonstrated no significant difference in Kujala score (89 vs. 88), redislocation rate (0% vs. 0%), or surgical morbidity, supporting the equivalence of the 2 approaches. In skeletally immature patients, soft tissue femoral fixation eliminates the risk of injury to the growth plate, and has been validated in dedicated paediatric series. This review summarises the anatomic and biomechanical basis for soft tissue fixation, describes the surgical technique for combined MPFL and MPTL reconstruction using an ipsilateral gracilis autograft, presents clinical outcomes from our series of 34 patients and a PRISMA systematic review of 197 operated knees, and discusses graft selection, prognostic factors, paediatric considerations, complications, and future directions.

items.title: Adolescent's perspective on the initiation of electronic cigarette use: a qualitative study.
items.abstract: Objectives The initiation of electronic cigarette use is increasingly occurring at younger ages, raising concerns about its long-term health impacts on adolescents. Therefore, prevention and reduction efforts must be strategically designed by incorporating adolescents' perspectives on this behavior. This study aims to explore adolescents' perspectives on the initiation of electronic cigarette use in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Methods This study employed a qualitative descriptive approach using focus group discussions (FGDs) involving eight adolescent electronic cigarette users from two public and private schools in Yogyakarta. Participants were purposively selected to explore their experiences and perceptions related to electronic cigarette initiation. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis approach. Results Thematic analysis revealed five themes: (1) first encounters occurred predominantly through peer exposure in social settings; (2) curiosity, flavor variety, and perceived reduced harm motivated use; (3) peers facilitated initial access through sharing devices; (4) unsupervised social gatherings provided opportunities for experimentation; and (5) initial experiences ranged from pleasurable to aversive, with positive experiences promoting continued use. Conclusions Electronic cigarette initiation results from the interaction between internal factors and environmental influences. These perspectives mutually reinforce one another, shaping experiences that contribute to adolescents'continued electronic cigarette use. Consequently, prevention efforts should incorporate adolescents' viewpoints to identify root causes of initiation and design more effective strategies to prevent adolescent engagement in electronic cigarette use in the future.

items.title: Influence of soft coral density and depth on benthic communities on Fiji's Rainbow Reef
items.abstract: Abstract Some soft corals have the potential to increase in prevalence on tropical coral reefs as the severity of anthropogenic climate change increases. While soft corals are therefore an increasingly important component of reef ecosystems, little is known about their ecological role on coral reefs and their influence on community dynamics and diversity. We used Bayesian network inference (BNI) to identify the associations among benthic taxa across sites with varying degrees of soft coral dominance on Fiji's Rainbow Reef, and then employed spatial point process analysis (SPPA) to reveal the ecological processes behind these associations. We found that depth was a dominant driver of community dynamics, and that white Nephtheidae soft corals were negatively associated with scleractinian corals and positively associated with algal proliferation—possibly owing to soft corals reducing grazing pressure. Our results show distinctions in reef benthos and ecological dynamics between scleractinian and soft coral-dominated components of the Rainbow Reef. We found that diversity levels were significantly lower on soft coral-dominated quadrats relative to scleractinian-dominated quadrats, potentially highlighting the reduction in benthic diversity when Nephtheidae soft corals dominate reef walls.

items.title: Impact of nano-chitosan solution on psoriasis-like thin skin lesion induced by imiquimod in Wistar rats: Exploring novel epigenetic role targeting miR-155, JAK2/STAT3/RORC/IL-17A, and MyD88/NF-κB pathways.
items.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, relapsing, immune-mediated skin disorder manifested by keratinocyte hyperproliferation. Current therapies provide symptomatic relief but carry the risk of severe side effects. Chitosan, a natural biopolymer, has wound-healing and anti-inflammatory properties in various dermatological applications. This study aimed to assess the impact of chitosan solution on psoriasis-like skin lesions induced by imiquimod (IMQ) in a Wistar rat model. An IMQ-induced psoriatic skin lesion was induced in Wistar rats; 35 rats were divided equally into: Control, IMQ, IMQ + acetic acid, IMQ + chitosan (5 g/L), and IMQ + chitosan (10 g/L) groups. Macroscopic, histopathological, immunohistochemical, biochemical, and molecular analyses were conducted to assess morphological and structural alterations, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress markers, and gene expression profiles. Application of IMQ resulted in psoriatic-like morphological and histopathological skin alterations. Chitosan application ameliorated these alterations and significantly reduced the erythema, desquamation, and skin thickening. Histological evaluation revealed that chitosan solution reduced epidermal acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, and inflammatory infiltrates while improving dermal architecture. It also suppressed PCNA and S100 expression, markers for keratinocyte proliferation and inflammation, respectively. Biochemically, it reduced IL-6, p-JAK2, p-STAT3, IL-17A, MyD88, and NF-κB levels, while restoring redox balance by decreasing MDA and enhancing catalase activity. Furthermore, qRT-PCR analysis demonstrated chitosan-mediated downregulation of miR-155 and RORC, highlighting its immunomodulatory effect. Nano-Chitosan solution effectively mitigated IMQ-induced psoriasis-like skin lesions, with better efficacy for the higher dose, through cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunoregulatory mechanisms. It has the ability to target the JAK2/STAT3/RORC/IL-17A and MyD88/NF-κB pathways via downregulating miR-155, which reveals a novel molecular mechanism for chitosan's beneficial effects and suggests its potential as an alternative therapeutic strategy for psoriasis.

items.title: Tangled in shame: A qualitative exploration of shame in adolescent hairpulling.
items.abstract: Trichotillomania (hairpulling disorder) is a body-focused repetitive behaviour characterised by the recurrent and compulsive pulling of one's own hair, where both the act of pulling and the visible consequences of hair loss cause distress and impairment. Shame has been identified as central to adult hairpulling, increasing the urge to pull and reinforcing the cycle of behaviour. Yet little is known about how adolescents experience this emotion, despite adolescence being the typical point of onset of trichotillomania and a developmental period marked by heightened sensitivity to shame. Hence, the present study explored how adolescents with problematic hairpulling experience, navigate and make sense of shame. A qualitative methodology was employed. Twelve adolescents aged 16-19 with problematic hair-pulling participated in online semi-structured interviews. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. An overarching theme of 'There's something wrong with me'-The Stigmatised Self captured how experiences of pervasive stigma were internalised as shame, permeating participants' inner lives and social worlds. Under this, five themes were generated: The Flawed Self; The Scrutinised Self; The Misunderstood Self; The Isolated Self; and The Disempowered Self. Shame was experienced as an enduring, identity-shaping emotion that triggered, maintained and exacerbated hairpulling. These findings extend our understanding by positioning shame as a central process in adolescent hairpulling and highlight the developmental vulnerability of this age group. Clinically, the results underscore the need for interventions that target shame, and for family and social contexts to be addressed alongside behavioural symptoms.

items.title: Neural connectomes of verbal fluency in post-stroke aphasia.
items.abstract: Verbal fluency tasks are widely used to assess language abilities and executive functions in both clinical and research settings. In post-stroke patients, prior research has indicated a significant hodological contribution to the neural basis of verbal fluency; however, this has largely been examined using lesion-based measures, predefined tractography approaches, and traditional diffusion metrics. Quantitative anisotropy-based structural connectometry derived from correlational tractography was employed to determine the white matter circuits underlying semantic and phonemic fluency in 44 patients with post-stroke aphasia. Both task types were found to be linked to anterior frontal connections of left-hemisphere dorsal and ventral associative pathways, as well as domain-general projection pathways. However, visual inspection of the connectomes, supported by supplementary cross-control analyses, suggested differences in the relative emphasis and distribution of pathways, with phonemic fluency aligning more with the dorsal stream, while semantic fluency showed greater reliance on the ventral stream and a wider range of cortico-subcortical connections. The findings contribute to current understanding of the neural networks of verbal fluency in aphasia, with potential relevance for clinical practice and research.

items.title: Developing and implementing a multidisciplinary perioperative education programme to support Enhanced Recovery After Surgery in resource-constrained public-sector hospitals.
items.abstract: Implementation of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery requires coordinated multidisciplinary practice change and remains challenging in resource-constrained health care settings because implementation barriers often extend beyond knowledge deficits. This article describes the development, implementation and implementation-focused evaluation of a multidisciplinary perioperative education programme designed to support Enhanced Recovery After Surgery implementation across two public-sector hospitals in India. The programme was developed through a sequential, evidence-informed process. Findings from a prospective observational evaluation and a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study were synthesised and mapped to the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Society Guideline for Perioperative Care in Elective Colorectal Surgery and overarching Enhanced Recovery After Surgery principles. This informed the development of a workflow-integrated educational programme incorporating orientation sessions, micro-training, bedside coaching, structured communication, nursing and clinician champions, bedside checklists, visual reminders and audit-feedback. The programme was implemented across a tertiary teaching hospital and a district hospital. Educational activities were embedded within routine perioperative workflows, promoting multidisciplinary engagement, behavioural reinforcement, workflow integration and adoption of standardised recovery practices. A structured, evidence-informed educational strategy integrated within routine clinical workflows provides a practical approach to supporting sustainable Enhanced Recovery After Surgery implementation in resource-constrained public-sector hospitals.

items.title: Leveraging AI to Integrate and Personalize Hospital Discharge Preparation: A Discursive Paper.
items.abstract: To describe a reconceptualization of hospital discharge preparation as fundamental personalized nursing care and reflect on emerging artificial intelligence technologies to improve care process and outcomes. Discursive paper. We expand our prior Conceptual Model for Discharge Preparation by situating it within theoretical perspectives of fundamental and personalized nursing care and emerging opportunities for integration of clinical artificial intelligence systems. The new Discharge Preparation Integrated Care Framework displays the complexity of discharge processes and the central nursing role in personalizing and integrating the core components of discharge preparation-discharge planning, coordination, and teaching. Personalized nursing care can be augmented, not replaced, by leveraging artificial intelligence capabilities. Integrated discharge preparation is a fundamental process of acute care nursing. Artificial intelligence technologies will support automation, coordination, and information exchange. However, effective discharge preparation requires personalized nursing care in interactive engagement with the patient and family to ensure that care decisions are aligned with the patient's situational context, goals of care, and preferences for the discharge transition. The Discharge Preparation Integrated Care Framework is widely applicable to designing personalized, efficient and effective nursing and hospital discharge services. As artificial intelligence becomes ubiquitous in clinical care, research will be needed to demonstrate the unique contribution of personalized nursing care to positive patient and healthcare organization outcomes. Discharge preparation addresses longstanding problems with hospital discharge. Comprehensive discharge preparation relies on personalized nursing care to achieve patient and health system outcomes. The framework should also be considered for discharge from other care venues. No patient or public involvement was involved in the development of this discursive paper.

items.title: Effects of close-knit county-level medical alliance on primary health care efficiency: a quasi-experimental study from Sichuan, China.
items.abstract: The Close-knit County-level Medical Community (CCMC) policy has been implemented to strengthen the health service capacity of the primary health care (PHC) system and optimize medical resource allocation to achieve the goal of health for all in China. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of the policy on health resource allocation efficiency in the PHC system. This was a quasi-experimental study based on data of 183 county-level districts across Sichuan Province from 2013 to 2023. The super-efficiency slacks-based measure model was used to assess the health resource allocation efficiency. The difference-in-difference (DID) model was adopted to evaluate the policy effect of CCMC. The propensity score matching DID (PSM-DID) method was used to test the robustness of the policy effect. The number of institutions, beds, and health workers of the PHC system in Sichuan Province showed a steady upward trend from 2013 to 2023. The medical resource allocation efficiency of the PHC system in almost all county-level districts in Sichuan Province was lower than one. The average efficiency of the PHC system in both pilot and non-pilot districts remained at a low level both before and after the implementation of the CCMC policy. The policy might have a negative impact on the efficiency of the PHC system, but this negative association was only demonstrated statistically in the PSM-DID weight model (β = -0.0499, P < 0.1). However, when excluding data during the COVID-19 pandemic, the significant negative effect in the PSM-DID weighted model disappeared, all the coefficients of the policy interaction in different models became non-significant while maintaining a negative direction. The CCMC policy did not demonstrate a statistically significant positive effect on the efficiency of the PHC system during the current observation period. The Chinese government should comprehensively regulate and support the health resources of the medical alliance through policy guidance, medical insurance regulation, and financial support to integrate not only different levels of medical institutions, but also medical resource of these institutions, making the medical alliance a unified interest community. A reasonable remuneration strategy should be established to encourage health workers to work in the PHC system for improving the health service capability.

items.title: Online communication with different types of friends and mental well-being of adolescents in Sweden: A pooled cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Young people's extensive internet and social media use has raised concerns about potential impacts on their mental well-being. Although many studies have examined general time spent online, fewer have focused on the specific nature of adolescents' online interactions. Using a sample of 15-year-olds (N = 3034) participants from the 2017/2018 and 2021/2022 Swedish Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) surveys, we employed pooled cross-sectional linear regression models to examine associations between the frequency of online communication with different types of friends and mental well-being, assessed by the Short Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-being Scale (SWEMWBS). Online communication was associated with adolescents' mental well-being, but patterns varied by both frequency of communication and the type of friendship. Intense online communication with close friends (b = 1.63, 95% CI: 0.57-2.70) and larger friend groups (b = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.44-1.62) was positively associated with mental well-being. Conversely, communication with virtual friends was associated with poorer well-being (moderate: b = -1.02, 95% CI: -1.50, -0.43; intense: b = -0.61, 95% CI: -1.14, -0.08). These associations remained robust even after model adjustment. The findings show that associations between online communication and adolescents' mental well-being differ depending on the type of friend with whom they communicate. These contrasting patterns highlight the need to distinguish between different forms of internet and social media use, and efforts to support young people's online activity should consider not only time spent online but also the nature of their online interactions.

items.title: Decision-Making Under Uncertainty in Paramedic Students: A START Triage Perspective.
items.abstract: This study examined whether intolerance of uncertainty and decision-making styles were associated with theoretical START triage knowledge among paramedic students. Secondary exploratory analyses assessed psychosocial differences according to self-rated decision-making under stress, perceived coping with uncertainty, professional motivation, and challenges in prehospital emergency care. In this cross-sectional study, 121 students from a First and Emergency Aid Program completed a self-administered paper-based questionnaire including a sociodemographic form, the Decision-Making Styles Scale, the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12, and the START Triage Knowledge Test. Data were collected in classroom settings under researcher supervision between May and June 2025 and analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and correlation analyses. The mean theoretical START triage knowledge score was 69.99 ± 14.76. START knowledge was not significantly associated with intolerance of uncertainty or decision-making style subscale scores. Exploratory analyses identified associations between psychosocial scores and self-rated decision-making under stress, coping with uncertainty, professional motivation, and perceived challenges. Theoretical START triage knowledge was not associated with intolerance of uncertainty or decision-making styles. Secondary findings were limited to self-reported psychosocial associations. The study assessed declarative knowledge and did not evaluate START application in simulated or field settings. Future studies should use simulation-based, scenario-based, or observational outcomes.

items.title: Neighbourhood deprivation in relation to psychiatric disorders among asthma patients: a nationwide cohort study.
items.abstract: Although asthma is strongly associated with elevated psychiatric morbidity, the extent to which neighbourhood deprivation is associated with psychiatric disorder risk in this population remains insufficiently understood. This study aims to examine whether neighbourhood deprivation is associated with the incidence of psychiatric disorders among adults with asthma, and whether these associations vary by sex and psychiatric disorder subtype. Using nationwide Swedish registers (1997-2018), we identified 393,061 adults aged 25-64 years with asthma and followed them for incident psychiatric disorders. Neighbourhood deprivation was assessed at baseline and categorized into low, moderate and high levels. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and were stratified by sex and psychiatric disorder subtype. During the follow-up period, 207,900 individuals (68,327 men and 139,573 women) developed psychiatric disorders. The incidence of psychiatric disorders increased progressively with higher levels of neighbourhood deprivation. In the fully adjusted models, compared with those living in low-deprivation areas, men in moderate and high deprivation areas had 11% (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.08-1.13) and 31% (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.27-1.35) higher hazards, respectively, while women had 10% (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.08-1.11) and 22% (HR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.19-1.25) higher hazards. Disorder-specific analyses revealed particularly strong associations for developmental delay (HR = 2.82), pervasive developmental disorder (HR = 1.96), schizophrenia (HR = 1.79) and substance use disorder (HR = 1.71). Women consistently showed higher cumulative incidence than men across all deprivation levels. Neighbourhood deprivation was associated with higher psychiatric morbidity among individuals with asthma. These findings suggest the importance of integrating respiratory and mental healthcare with structural interventions targeting socio-economic disadvantage to help reduce inequalities in psychiatric outcomes.

items.title: Secular trends and pubertal growth spurts in body height among Tibetan children and adolescents living at high altitudes in Lhasa (China) from 1965 to 2019.
items.abstract: Height is an anthropometric measure of nutritional levels and health status during childhood and adolescence and can strongly predict health and developmental outcomes across the lifespan. There is little evidence on the growth trends of Chinese children and adolescents living at high altitudes. This paper aimed to examine the secular trends and pubertal growth spurts in height among Tibetan children and adolescents in Lhasa from 1965 to 2019. Height data among Tibetan children and adolescents aged 7-17 years were obtained from ten cross-sectional surveys (1965, 1975, 1985, 1991, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019). Sample-weighted regressions (linear or quadratic or cubic regressions) were performed to estimate trends in height by sex and age. A population-weighting procedure was used to calculate the changes for boys and girls. The SuperImposition by Translation and Rotation model was used to separately fit height-distance and height-velocity curves for boys and girls, yielding sex- and wave-specific peak height velocity (PHV) and age at PHV (APHV). The results showed that population-based height increased by 17.8 cm or 2.28 effect size (ES) for boys and by 14.1 cm or 1.98 ES for girls from 1965 to 2019. Among boys, there was a moderate increase per decade (0.76 ES) from 1965 to 1970, followed by a gradual deceleration in this trend. For girls, there was a largest increase per decade (0.74 ES) in 1960s. Then, the trend slowed and remained stable in the last decades. From 1965 to 2019, the PHV for boys increased from 6.53 cm/year to 7.36 cm/year (P = 0.007), whereas the APHV decreased from 15.84 years to 13.39 years (P < 0.001). Girls showed no significant trend in PHV, but APHV decreased from 12.85 years to 10.00 years. In sum, this study reveals a secular trend in height among Tibetan children and adolescents in Lhasa over the past five decades, with a recent deceleration in trends. Puberty development has advanced in both sexes. More public health policies are needed to promote the growth and development of Tibetan children and adolescents and prevent negative impacts from sustained growth and early puberty.

items.title: Potential for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions through sustainable procurement of animal-source foods in Brazil's National School Feeding Program.
items.abstract: To quantify greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with animal-source food procurement in Brazil's National School Feeding Program (PNAE) and to assess the mitigation potential of alternative procurement strategies. Retrospective analysis of federal procurement invoices (2013-2022), with identification of animal-source foods and estimation of associated GHG emissions using product-specific emission factors. Deterministic mitigation scenarios were modelled, including partial substitution of beef with lower-emission animal proteins and adoption of deforestation-free sourcing. PNAE, one of the world's largest public school feeding programmes. All federal procurement invoices related to animalsource food purchases within the PNAE between 2013 and 2022. Between 2013 and 2022, the PNAE purchased 815 136 tonnes of animal-source foods, predominantly beef and poultry, generating an estimated cumulative 58·1 MtCO₂e with substantial variation across regional food-system clusters. Beef was responsible for 77·8 % of total emissions despite accounting for 35·3 % of purchased volume. Scenario analyses indicated that partial substitution of beef with lower-emission animal proteins (poultry, pork, fish and eggs) could reduce emissions by up to 41 %, whereas adopting sustainable sourcing excluding deforestation-linked suppliers could reduce emissions by 31 %. Combined strategies could reduce emissions by more than 50 %. Beef procurement is the primary driver of GHG emissions in Brazil's school feeding programme and represents the greatest opportunity for emission reductions. By quantifying the mitigation potential of alternative procurement strategies, this study provides evidence to inform discussions on the environmental implications of public food procurement within school feeding programmes.

items.title: Remnant Cholesterol Inflammatory Index and its Association With Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity in Middle-Aged and Advanced-Aged Individuals: Evidence From the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND The association between remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. RCII is defined as: {Total Cholesterol - (High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol + Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol)] × High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein/10}. This study examined the association between baseline RCII and CMM among middle-aged and older adults in China. MATERIAL AND METHODS This study analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 6173 participants. CMM was defined as the coexistence of at least 2 of 4 conditions: hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or stroke. Participants were grouped according to the quartiles of natural log-transformed RCII (lnRCII) values. Modified Poisson regression models, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to examine the relationship between lnRCII and CMM outcomes. RESULTS In the cohort, 1832 cases of CMM occurred, and the incidence of CMM was highest in the lnRCII highest-quartile group (P<0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each unit of increase in lnRCII was associated with a higher risk of CMM (RR=1.13, 95% CI: 1.09-1.16), and participants in the highest quartile had a higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (RR=1.69, 95% CI: 1.50-1.90). The area under the curve for lnRCII was 0.607 (95% CI: 0.592-0.622), indicating modest discriminatory ability. CONCLUSIONS Higher baseline lnRCII was associated with an increased risk of incident CMM in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. Although RCII may capture combined information on remnant cholesterol and inflammation, its clinical predictive value requires further validation.

items.title: Transmission-route-specific trends in communicable diseases in Taiwan: an interrupted time-series analysis.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered patterns of communicable disease (CD) transmission through implementation of non-pharmaceutical interventions and changes in healthcare utilization. However, long-term trends remain insufficiently characterized. We conducted an ecological time-series study using national surveillance data of notifiable CD in Taiwan from January 2017 to December 2023. Diseases were categorized into transmission-route groups, and temporal trends were assessed using segmented interrupted time-series models with autoregressive integrated moving average error structures to estimate phase-specific level and slope changes. A total of 240556 cases were reported, with more than 96% locally acquired. Overall incidence declined during the pandemic phase (2020-2022) and increased in 2023, exceeding pre-pandemic levels. This increase was largely influenced by dengue-related vector-borne disease activity. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across transmission pathways: airborne and droplet diseases declined markedly with partial recovery, sexually transmitted and blood-borne diseases increased consistently, and vector-borne diseases showed an outbreak-driven increase in 2023. Interrupted time-series analysis identified significant negative level changes at the onset of the pandemic and positive slope changes in the post-pandemic phase. These findings suggest transmission-route-specific temporal patterns during pandemic and post-pandemic phases and underscore the need for adaptive surveillance and prevention strategies in the post-pandemic era.

items.title: Changing Patterns of Alcohol and Cannabis Acute Care Admissions by Age in the United States, 2016-2023.
items.abstract: Age-related differences in alcohol and cannabis use are well established, yet age-specific trends in substance-related acute morbidity remain incompletely understood. The authors examined age-specific trends in alcohol- and cannabis-related emergency department and inpatient admissions from 2016 to 2023. This was a retrospective cohort study using Merative MarketScan Commercial and Multi-State Medicaid databases (January 2016-December 2023). The cohort included 1,355,161 individuals 16-64 years of age with at least one substance-related acute care encounter (ICD-10-CM codes F10-F19, excluding nicotine). Outcomes included the proportion of substance-related encounters involving alcohol or cannabis, stratified by six age groups (16-18, 19-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, and 55-64 years). Secondary analyses examined primary substance diagnoses, severe alcohol-related morbidity, and cannabis-related encounters involving psychosis or vomiting (hyperemesis). Weighted linear regression estimated age-specific annual changes in encounter proportions, and Poisson models assessed trends in total encounter volume and substance involvement per encounter. Among 5,190,680 substance-related encounters, alcohol and cannabis exhibited divergent age patterns. Alcohol accounted for 19%-26% of adolescent admissions, increasing to 73%-76% among adults ages 55-64 years, whereas cannabis involvement was highest among adolescents (70%-78%) and lowest among older adults (10%-11%). Alcohol-related admissions increased significantly among adults ages 25-34 years (1.80 percentage points annually, 95% CI=1.59, 2.00) and 35-44 years (1.19 points, 95% CI=0.99, 1.38). Cannabis-related admissions increased most rapidly among individuals ages 19-24 years (1.81 points annually, 95% CI=1.57, 2.04) and 16-18 years (0.83 points, 95% CI=0.61, 1.06), with notable increases in presentations involving psychosis and vomiting. When restricted to primary diagnoses, cannabis-related trends were attenuated, with adolescents showing annual declines (-1.46 points, 95% CI=-1.98, -0.94). Alcohol- and cannabis-related acute care presentations follow divergent age-specific trajectories, with cannabis increasingly predominant among adolescents and young adults and alcohol predominant among older adults.

items.title: Targeted Use of Kudzu for Binge Drinking Among Adults With Alcohol Use Disorder: A Phase 2b Randomized Trial.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the efficacy and acceptability of targeted use of kudzu, an herbal supplement, in adults with alcohol use disorder (AUD) who binge drink. In a double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 120 adults with AUD who binge drink were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to targeted (as-needed) use of oral kudzu extract (2 grams taken on days when binge drinking was anticipated) or matching placebo, plus weekly counseling for 12 weeks. The primary outcome was number of binge-drinking days in the past week. Prespecified secondary outcomes included number of self-reported binge-drinking weeks, number of drinks, and measurements of changes in alcohol use using biomarkers, including ethyl glucuronide (EtG) and phosphatidylethanol (PEth). Retention was high: 88% completed the trial, and 86% of weekly follow-up visits were completed. In the primary intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis, assignment to kudzu versus placebo reduced number of binge-drinking days (incidence rate ratio [IRR]=0.73, 95% CI=0.54, 0.99); as-treated (taking medication ≥2.7 days per week) analysis estimated a stronger effect (IRR=0.58, 95% CI=0.38, 0.89). Secondary outcomes showed lower number of binge-drinking weeks in ITT analysis (relative risk [RR]=0.79, 95% CI=0.62, 0.99). In as-treated analyses, reductions in number of binge-drinking weeks (RR=0.68, 95% CI=0.47, 0.98) and PEth positivity (RR=0.82, 95% CI=0.67, 0.99) were also significant. The number of binge-drinking days showed significant sustained reductions at the 3-month posttreatment visit (RR=0.68, 95% CI=0.47, 0.97). The overall frequency of adverse events was similar between groups. No serious adverse events related to kudzu occurred during follow-up. Targeted use of kudzu reduced self-reported binge-drinking outcomes among adults with AUD during treatment compared to placebo. Greater reductions in binge drinking and PEth were observed among those who took medication more frequently. Reductions in self-reported binge drinking persisted at the posttreatment visit. Kudzu may be a helpful pharmacologic treatment for binge drinking among people with AUD.

items.title: Dose-Response Patterns and Pathways Linking Migration-Related Stigma and Mental Health.
items.abstract: This study examines migration stigma as a manifestation of symbolic violence and its association with psychological distress and posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms among Asian, Black, and Latinx immigrant-origin adults in the United States. Using data from a demographically diverse, national quota sample (N=908), stigma was assessed at macro (perceptions of government and policy makers), interpersonal (social exclusion, discrimination, and threat of deportation), and intrapersonal (anticipating rejection, internalized embarrassment and shame, and perceived devaluation) levels. A series of ordinary least-squares regression models was used to isolate the unique and combined effects of demographic, immigration-related, and stigma-related predictors on two outcomes: psychological distress (using the Kessler 6-item Psychological Distress Scale) and posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms. Racial-ethnic disparities in mental health outcomes were attenuated after accounting for immigration-related factors and stigma exposure. Interpersonal and intrapersonal stigma, specifically experiences of discrimination, social exclusion, shame, and devaluation, emerged as the most robust predictors of mental health outcomes. A cumulative stigma index demonstrated a dose-response relationship, with each additional exposure associated with significantly higher symptom levels, underscoring the compounding mental health burden of layered stigma. The findings highlight the need for policies and clinical interventions that reduce exposure to symbolic violence and address the psychological toll of stigma on immigrant-origin populations. Integrating culturally responsive, trauma-informed approaches into mental health services is essential for mitigating disparities and supporting mental health well-being in increasingly restrictive immigration climates.

items.title: Milk as Mutual Aid: Legitimizing Community-Governed Human Milk Sharing as Public Health Infrastructure.
items.abstract: Human milk is a critical public health resource, yet access remains uneven despite the well-established benefits of breastfeeding and donor human milk. Although regulated milk banks provide an essential service, many families obtain human milk through informal and community-based sharing networks. These practices have persisted across cultures and generations but remain largely absent from public health policy and professional guidance. This commentary argues that community-governed milk sharing should be understood as a form of mutual aid that emerges in response to gaps in maternal and infant health systems. Rather than ignoring or stigmatizing these practices, society should acknowledge their existence and develop evidence-informed approaches that promote safety, autonomy, equity, and informed decision making. Recognizing milk sharing as community health infrastructure may strengthen infant nutrition security and support family-centered care.

items.title: Associations of back pain and lower limb pain with incident locomotive dysfunction in middle-aged and older Japanese workers.
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal pain may be associated with locomotive dysfunction, but whether pain precedes its onset in working-age populations remains unclear. We examined the associations of back pain and lower limb pain with incident locomotive dysfunction in middle-aged and older Japanese workers. This retrospective cohort study used annual health examination and locomotor screening data (2016-2022) from a Japanese manufacturing company. Participants were aged ≥40 years without locomotive dysfunction at baseline. Back and lower limb pain were assessed in 2016 using the 25-question Geriatric Locomotive Function Scale and classified as none, mild, or moderate or worse. Pattern analyses considered the presence of moderate or worse pain: neither, back, lower limb, or both. Incident locomotive dysfunction over 6 years was defined as a 5-item Geriatric Locomotive Function Scale score ≥3. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. Among 3436 participants, 38.3% and 20.1% reported back pain and lower limb pain, respectively. With no back pain as reference, the adjusted HRs were 1.32 (95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.71) for mild pain and 2.29 (1.64-3.19) for moderate or worse pain. The corresponding HRs for lower limb pain were 1.66 (1.26-2.20) and 2.97 (2.00-4.40). In the pain-pattern analysis with neither pain as reference, the HRs were 1.79 (1.24-2.57) for back pain alone; 2.18 (1.29-3.70) for lower limb pain alone; and 4.07 (2.37-6.99) for both. The findings of the study indicate that back pain and lower limb pain were associated with incident locomotive dysfunction in middle-aged and older Japanese workers. Additionally, the associations were stronger with greater pain severity and when pain involved both the back and lower limbs.

items.title: Penicillin Allergy Delabeling in Children.
items.abstract: Nearly 10% of the global population has been labeled as having a penicillin allergy. Of those labeled, about 95% are not truly allergic, yet most do not receive any allergy evaluations. Patients with penicillin allergy labels are more likely to have worse clinical outcomes and incur higher health care costs, largely because they do not receive penicillin and other first-line β-lactam antibiotics for the treatment of infectious diseases. Consequently, the process of evaluating and removing inaccurate penicillin allergy labels-a process known as "delabeling"-has become increasingly supported by a growing body of evidence. Recently, penicillin allergy has garnered substantial public interest with the proposal of federal legislation to include evaluation of penicillin allergy during routine medical visits for Medicare patients. Although this moves delabeling into the generalist purview, most of the emphasis on penicillin allergies and delabeling has been on adult patients. Yet, penicillin allergy is a pressing issue for pediatrics, as most penicillin allergy labels are placed in childhood. Pediatric literature similarly demonstrates negative clinical and public health consequences of inaccurate penicillin allergy labels. Recent guidelines have strongly recommended a proactive effort to identify and delabel inaccurate penicillin allergies in children. To facilitate this process, simple delabeling procedures, such as direct oral challenge with amoxicillin, have been recommended for patients with low-risk allergy status, based on historical reaction verification, because of their safety and accuracy. These advancements are relevant to practicing pediatricians across specialties and practice locations.
