items.title: Investigating the relationships between vegetation and climate across China and the regulatory role of terrain conditions
items.abstract: Terrestrial Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is pivotal to the global carbon cycle, and its response to climate change is strongly regulated by topographic conditions through complex, non-linear mechanisms that remain poorly quantified at macro scales. Integrating multi-source remote sensing data with structural equation modeling (SEM), geographical detectors, and generalized additive models (GAM), this study investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of GPP and its non-linear responses to coupled climate-topography gradients across China from 2001 to 2020. Results revealed a significant increasing trend in GPP across nearly 80% of China, with precipitation identified as the dominant driver, surpassing temperature and radiation. Topography significantly modulated climate sensitivity by redistributing hydrothermal resources. A distinct transition in dominant limiting factors was observed along the altitudinal gradient, shifting from water-limited ( 3000 m) regimes. Notably, mid-altitude regions (1000–2000 m) exhibited the highest sensitivity to precipitation, representing an ecological "sweet spot". Furthermore, we quantified critical ecological thresholds for climatic drivers, identified saturation points for temperature (~17.4°C) and precipitation (~1974 mm), and an inhibition threshold for solar radiation (>101 W/m²). These findings elucidate the transition mechanisms of climatic constraints and non-linear thresholds in complex terrain, providing robust scientific evidence for region-specific ecosystem and carbon management.

items.title: Biases and gaps in freshwater mollusks research in Latin America and the Caribbean: a multi-decadal bibliometric analysis (1976–2024)
items.abstract: Abstract Freshwater molluscs play key ecological roles in aquatic ecosystems, yet they are among the most threatened and least studied invertebrate groups worldwide. This study evaluates how scientific knowledge on freshwater molluscs is structured across Latin America and the Caribbean, testing the hypothesis that research effort is uneven and shaped by multiple knowledge shortfalls that constrain ecological understanding and conservation planning. We conducted a bibliometric review of peer-reviewed literature indexed in Web of Science, combining systematic screening with quantitative bibliometric analyses to assess geographic coverage, taxonomic focus, research themes, collaboration networks and gender representation in authorship. Our results reveal pronounced Wallacean and taxonomic shortfalls, with research concentrated in a limited number of countries and disproportionately focused on invasive species, whereas many native and threatened taxa remain poorly studied. We also detected thematic gaps related to evolutionary and physiological processes, alongside fragmented collaboration networks and persistent gender asymmetries, reflecting broader shortfalls in biodiversity research. These patterns indicate a mismatch between research effort and conservation priorities in a megadiverse region facing increasing environmental pressures. By identifying critical blind spots in current knowledge, this study offers a regional framework to guide future ecological research, conservation strategies and collaborative initiatives on freshwater mollusc management globally.

items.title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
items.abstract: Abstract Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. Some corals exhibited stochastic divergence consistent with dysbiosis, whereas others showed deterministic, thermally adaptive shifts. Heat stress generally reduced symbiont diversity and promoted predictable restructuring, supporting deterministic processes under moderate stress but stochastic dysbiosis under extreme conditions. We propose that adaptive and stochastic responses represent endpoints along a continuum of host-orchestrated symbiont sorting. This study bridges coral reef ecology with broader host–microbiome theory, offering an integrated perspective on how symbiotic systems may respond to environmental change. Teaser Long-term experiments reveal that corals follow distinct paths of symbiont change under heat stress, from adaptation to dysbiosis

items.title: Systematic Comparisons between Long-Read- and Short-Read-Based Amplicon Sequencing to Characterize Mixed Microalgal Communities
items.abstract: Abstract The 18S rRNA gene has emerged as the primary molecular marker for amplicon-based characterization of microalgal communities, including in wastewater treatment systems, yet trade-offs between short- and long-read approaches remain poorly defined. We systematically compared V8–V9 short-read sequencing (SR; Illumina MiSeq), near-full-length long-read sequencing with ss5ss3 primers (LR; PacBio Sequel II), and computationally extracted V8–V9 regions from LR data (LS). In silico evaluation of multiple primer pairs revealed differences in predicted taxonomic recovery, while incomplete reference sequences and taxonomic misannotations complicated performance assessments. In environmental samples, SR and LR captured different aspects of sequence diversity: SR recovered a broader set of sequence variants, whereas the longer LR amplicons retained greater sequence information and discrimination. Truncating LR sequences to V8–V9 collapses distinct ASVs. The taxonomic advantage of LR was classification-workflow-dependent and was particularly apparent at genus and species levels with the eukaryote-focused workflow. Differential-abundance analysis identified species-level Chlorophyta associations in LR, with consistent higher-level taxonomic patterns across periods, whereas SR additionally revealed largely period-specific associations with heterotrophic protists. Despite its finer taxonomic resolution, LR did not provide a clearer whole-community distinction between process performance states (i.e., phosphorus-removal, emphasizing that the sequencing approach should be selected according to the information required.

items.title: When cold-bloods heat up: meta-analytical evidence that climatic variability mediates behavioural fever in amphibians and reptiles
items.abstract: Abstract Fever is an adaptive defence response that enhances immune performance by elevating body temperature above normal values. In ectotherms, fever is expressed behaviourally through the selection of warmer microhabitats following infection, yet its magnitude and determinants vary widely across species and environments. We performed a phylogenetically informed meta-analysis to test whether behavioural fever expression is shaped by climatic thermal variability, pathogen identity and taxonomy in amphibians and reptiles. We predicted that species from thermally variable environments would exhibit stronger behavioural fever than those from stable environments and reptiles would exhibit stronger fever responses than amphibians owing to lower hydrothermal constraints. Across 47 studies encompassing 101 effect sizes, behavioural fever emerged as a widespread but context-dependent response. Behavioural fever was strongest in species from thermally variable habitats, suggesting that thermal opportunity and behavioural plasticity mediate the expression of fever. Contrary to our prediction, amphibians exhibited stronger fever responses than reptiles, possibly reflecting differences in thermoregulatory biology, environmental opportunity or methodological artefacts. Bacterial infections elicited larger body temperature increases than fungal or viral challenges. Our findings demonstrate that temperature is not a background condition for host–pathogen interactions, but an active and environmentally contingent component of immune defence in ectothermic tetrapods.

items.title: Physicochemical, carbohydrate, and ecological profiling of Iranian Sidr (Ziziphus spp.) honey: establishing baseline reference ranges for regional quality and authenticity assessment
items.abstract: Abstract Monofloral honeys, particularly Iranian Sidr honey, are highly valued for their unique sensory and medicinal properties; however, they are also prone to fraud. To address this issue, it is essential to create reference databases documenting the physicochemical and pollinological profiles of these honeys. This study analyzed Sidr honey samples from various regions in Iran to document their physicochemical and pollinological characteristics and to understand how ecological factors impact these properties. The analysis of 25 honey samples revealed that pollen from Ziziphus spp. was predominant, indicating a consistent botanical origin. A significant relationship was found between sugar composition, pH levels, and environmental factors, all of which considerably affect honey quality. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) showed that the first two components explained 50.6% of the total variance, highlighting distinct differences in physicochemical and ecological traits. In the first principal component (PCA1), strong positive correlations were identified among erlose, sucrose, pH, rainfall, and altitude. The second component indicated positive relationships between diastatic activity, phenolic compounds, moisture content, and the fructose-to-glucose ratio. Both PCA and hierarchical cluster analysis revealed that honey samples from the same counties did not cluster together, suggesting that environmental factors create unique physicochemical profiles, influencing both the quantity and quality of honey. These findings could enhance the authenticity and quality control of Iranian Sidr honey, improving its commercial value, competitiveness in international markets, and potential for grading.

items.title: Detoxification enzyme modulation and larvicidal efficacy of Klebsiella pneumoniae (PX652414) and Proteus mirabilis (PZ337687) metabolites in mosquito vectors
items.abstract: Abstract Mosquitoes of the Anopheles , Aedes , and Culex genera serve as vectors for significant human and animal diseases. The increasing prevalence of insecticide resistance, primarily mediated by detoxification enzymes, highlights the urgent need for innovative biocontrol strategies. This study assessed the larvicidal activity of secondary metabolites produced by Klebsiella pneumoniae PX652414 and Proteus mirabilis PZ337687, as well as their impact on esterase and glutathione-S-transferase (GST) enzyme activities in three major mosquito species: An. gambiae s.l., Ae. aegypti , and Cx. quinquefasciatus . Metabolites incubated for three and eight days were individually applied to separate cohorts of mosquito larvae. Larval mortality, lethal concentrations (LCs), and enzyme activities were evaluated following 72 hours of exposure. K. pneumoniae metabolites induced substantial larval mortality across all mosquito species, demonstrated by low LC50 values and decreased esterase and GST activity, particularly in Cx. quinquefasciatus. Conversely, P. mirabilis metabolites resulted in minimal mortality and elevated esterase and GST activity. These results demonstrate enzyme modulation by these metabolites and indicate that K. pneumoniae (PX652414) metabolites may serve as promising agents for integrated vector management.

items.title: Applicability of Sustainable Construction and Environmental Resilience in a Circular Built Environment in Southern Africa
items.abstract: Lately, sustainability has dominated academic, practice and policy discourse. The construction industry is singled out as one of the unsustainable sectors due to its linear methods of extract-use-dispose. Globally, linear construction practices are responsible for approximately 50% of raw material extraction, 36% of all emissions, 40% of energy consumption and 50% of waste resulting in natural resource scarcity and waste management catastrophes. In Africa, only 4% of the waste is recycled, whereas 90% is illegally dumped, and the balance is unaccounted for. Consequently, circular economy (circularity), anchored on reduce, reuse, and recycle principles, is widely perceived as a sustainable alternative to linearity. The primary objective of circularity in the construction industry is to advance sustainability by creating a circular built environment. Closely related to circularity, sustainable construction practices also pursue sustainability. On the other hand, environmental resilience from ecology explores how the natural environment adapts to external stressors, promoting sustainability. Nonetheless, the extent to which sustainable construction and environmental resilience non-conflicting factors jointly influence the attainment of a circular built environment remains unknown. The overarching aim of this study was to develop a tailored model for Southern Africa, demonstrating how sustainable construction, environmental resilience factors, and building lifecycle practices contribute to the region's circular built environment transition. To do so, the study was premised on pragmatic philosophy and adopted an exploratory sequential mixed-method research design. The study was divided into two phases. First, through a Delphi study, 11 purposively sampled circularity experts identified 73 drivers contributing to a circular built environment in Southern Africa. Second, a questionnaire comprising these practices was administered to a purposively random sample of 400 stakeholders in Southern Africa. Only 282 participants fully completed the survey. Data was cleaned and analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and structural equation modelling (SEM). Results show that, generally, there is an awareness of the sustainability concepts, namely circular economy, sustainable construction, and environmental resilience. However, environmental resilience is the most practiced concept, implying that the environmental-related policies enunciated across the region were bearing fruit. v Furthermore, 15 hypotheses were validated, and the results show that environmental resilience, design, construction, operation, and use practices significantly influenced the circular built environment transition. Sustainable construction only impacted design practices. Surprisingly, the results show that sustainable construction and environmental resilience were unrelated. Unlike environmental resilience, sustainable construction or circularity policies are yet to be fully adopted. In conclusion, the study proposes a Southern Africa Circular Built Environment Framework (SACBEF) that demonstrates the applicability of sustainable construction and environmental resilience practices throughout the design, construction, operation, and use phases. The framework also outlines significant barriers and stakeholders in promoting circularity transition. To the knowledge of the researcher, this study is the first of its kind to adopt a multidisciplinary thinking and explore and validate the relationship between cross-cutting concepts, circular economy, sustainable construction, and environmental resilience in promoting circular built environment transition in Southern Africa. Furthermore, the lifecycle assessment perspective provided an in-depth understanding of which building stages influenced circularity in Southern Africa. Future studies should explore the extent of convergence or divergence between sustainable construction and environmental resilience in promoting circularity.

items.title: Too threatened to try: how extinction risk drives research neglect in rays and skates
items.abstract: Global biodiversity loss demands that research effort be directed towards species most at risk. Yet conservation science is biased by species' accessibility and perceived charisma, raising concerns that threatened species may be overlooked. We apply a structured causal modelling framework to 651 species of rays (superorder Batoidea), a highly threatened yet understudied lineage of cartilaginous fishes, to disentangle the drivers of research effort. We quantify the causal effects of taxonomy, extinction risk, accessibility (range size, depth, economic context, year of description) and charisma (body size, shape, patterning and colouration) on species-level research outputs from more than 7000 publications. Research effort was strongly taxonomically biased, driven by accessibility and charisma, with shallow depth, broad geographic ranges, large body size and distinctive morphologies attracting disproportionate attention. Extinction risk exerted a counterintuitive nonlinear effect: Critically Endangered and Endangered species received significantly fewer publications than Near Threatened and Vulnerable species and were comparable to Data Deficient species. This effect is consistent with a 'Goldilocks' zone in which species are threatened enough to justify research but not so threatened that it becomes prohibitively challenging. Systematic research bias away from the species most in need undermines conservation efforts. Realigning research priorities is essential to combating the biodiversity crisis.

items.title: Phenological divergence between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera under climate change across Europe
items.abstract: Climate change is altering life-cycle timing and may disrupt coordinated interactions between flowering plants and flower-visiting insects. Using Global Biodiversity Information Facility observation records from Europe between 2000 and 2024, we compiled a continental-scale phenological dataset covering flowering periods of 707 angiosperm species and adult activity periods of 620 Lepidoptera species. We extracted the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles and activity-window width and used linear mixed-effects models to analyse spatio-temporal trends. The results showed that plant phenology advanced significantly, with the 10th and 50th percentiles shifting earlier by -0.597 and -0.507 d yr⁻¹, respectively, whereas the 90th percentile showed no significant change; flowering-window width increased by 0.361 d yr⁻¹. By contrast, Lepidoptera phenology advanced evenly across the season, with the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles shifting by -0.137, -0.153 and -0.155 d yr⁻¹, respectively, while activity-window width showed no significant change. Because flowering plants advanced faster than Lepidoptera in the early and middle season, plant-insect phenological overlap declined at 0.340 d yr⁻¹, indicating increasing mismatch across Europe. Further analyses identified temperature as the dominant driver of phenological advance in both groups, but flowering plants and Lepidoptera differed in their responses to other climatic factors. These results suggest that climate change is weakening phenological synchrony between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera, with potential consequences for pollination and ecosystem functioning.

items.title: Genomic mechanisms underlying Bombay duck's rapid population surge
items.abstract: Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), once a minor by-catch in the East China Sea, has bloomed into a dominant species, altering marine ecosystems. This study explored the genomic basis of its mysterious recent success via chromosome-level genome assembly, comparative and population genomics. The genome assemblies of H. nehereus and its closely related outgroup species Saurida undosquamis were of good quality, showing a 96.7-96.8% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologues completeness. Population resequencing supports a single panmictic population throughout the coast of China. Expanded gene families and genes under intensified and positive selection are related to osmoregulation, hypoxia tolerance, immune function and reproduction. Recent selective sweeps are mostly related to immune response. These molecular signatures are consistent with long-term adaptations to a hypoxic, polluted and fluctuating environment. These findings suggest that species genomically preadapted to environments affected by global change can suddenly become new native invaders.

items.title: When dates disagree: radiocarbon and sighting-based models reveal range-wide variability in great auk ( Pinguinus impennis ) extinction estimates
items.abstract: Methods for inferring extinction are well established for events that either occurred on millennial time scales (e.g. the late Quaternary) or are unfolding in the present. However, these methods employ distinct data types inherent to palaeontological or neontological settings, yielding a potentially disjointed view of the extinction process. We leveraged the historical extinction of the great auk (Pinguinus impennis)-a large, flightless seabird native to the Atlantic-as a test case to assess the effects of using varied data types (286 quality-scored occurrences) and models (Gaussian-resampled inverse-weighted McInerny, Solow and Beet) in inferring extinction across centennial time scales. While the last confirmed great auk was killed in 1844 CE in Iceland, the dynamics of species-wide range collapse in response to differing harvest practices have not been explored. Our sighting-based estimates suggest the species may have persisted a decade longer (1860 CE) in the Northwest Atlantic, highlighting the need for future research on this understudied portion of their range. Radiocarbon-based models estimate extinction later (post-2000 CE) across the species' range, suggesting that inherent uncertainties in radiocarbon dates and their calibration-particularly for marine samples-may constrain their applicability for detailing extinction processes on conservation-relevant time scales.

items.title: Modeling of Current and Future Low Flow Characteristics Under Climate Variability and Water Abstraction: Case of Likhubula River Catchment in Malawi
items.abstract: Abstract Water resources are essential in sustaining ecosystems, agriculture and the ever-growing water demands of human population. However, the delicate balance of water availability for these sectors is increasingly facing unprecedented present and future challenges due to climate change and anthropogenic pressures. This study was aimed at characterizing the current and future low flows under climate variability and water abstraction in the Likhubula River Catchment, key a sub-catchment of the major Shire River Basin in Malawi. The study employs a multi-faceted approach, where trend analysis is conducted using the Mann-Kendall test and the Sens Slope Estimator at α = 0.05 significance level. The SWAT hydrological model was set up for simulating future streamflow conditions and forced with RCP and SSP scenarios. Flow duration curves (FDCs) and low flow frequency curves (LFFCs) were employed to compute low flow indices, including the Q90, Q95, 7Q2 and 7Q10. The SWAT model exhibited a satisfactory performance with an R 2 , PBIAS, NSE and RMSE of 0.98, 3.6, 0.94 and 0.29 respectively during calibration and R 2 , PBIAS, NSE and RMSE of 0.96, -2.4, 0.84 and 0.42 respectively, during calibration and validation. Examination of low flow indices indicated substantial increases in low flow frequencies after 2007 with anticipated further increases in low flow duration, magnitude and frequencies after 2027. The RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 indicate less severe low flows as compared to historical periods. The combinations of RCP and SSP scenarios has shown varying results, RCP4.5 & SSP2 indicating significant improvements, while others (e.g., RCP4.5 & SSP4, RCP8.5 & SSP4) showing potential for highly severe low flows; an indication that climate change and intensification of water abstraction activities have a significant impact on the magnitude, duration and frequency of low flows in the Likhubula catchment. Despite the non-significant increasing trend in rainfall being observed, both significant positive trend in temperature and significant declining trend in streamflow imply radical environmental decision-making calls to deal with uncertain future using the 3-H approach. These findings provide crucial insights for sustainable water resource management as these low flow characteristics are critical for managing water quality and quantity.

items.title: Farmers’ perspectives of how farmer research networks shape behaviour and contribute to agroecological systems change in Eastern and Southern Africa
items.abstract: Introduction Farmer Research Networks (FRNs) are collaborative platforms that bring together diverse stakeholders to co-create knowledge and support agroecological innovation. While FRNs are increasingly recognised for enabling farmers to embrace sustainable practices and strengthen resilience, limited evidence exists on how they influence farmer behaviour and contribute to agroecological systems change. Methods This study draws on a single round of qualitative fieldwork conducted in 2024 with nine FRNs that had been operating since 2015 in Kenya, Malawi, and Uganda, comprising 99 interviews and focus group discussions with 182 farmers, researchers and extension or NGO staff, to examine how engagement in these FRNs shapes farmers’ attitudes, perceptions, intentions, and practices. The Theory of Planned Behaviour, the Model of Justified Behaviour, and the FAO’s 10 elements of agroecology were used as analytical lenses. Results The findings indicate that participants experience FRNs as dynamic learning ecosystems. Farmers linked their involvement in FRNs to stronger positive attitudes toward agroecology, enhanced perceived behavioural control through knowledge and skills development, and evolving subjective norms shaped by collective learning and peer influence. Behavioural intentions were reinforced by ecological awareness, emotional engagement, and future-oriented aspirations. Participants associated their engagement with progress across multiple agroecological dimensions, including soil fertility, system diversity, resilience, social cohesion, and economic agency. These outcomes were driven by participatory experimentation, knowledge co-creation, and relational processes such as trust, solidarity, and inclusive decision-making. However, the findings also reveal important limitations in what FRNs can address. Persistent constraints, including labour intensity, limited access to inputs and locally adapted seed, gender and youth inequalities, weak enforcement of community rules, tensions between short-term livelihood needs and long-term ecological goals, entrenched cultural norms and institutional gaps, often lie beyond the direct influence of FRNs. Discussion Overall, the study demonstrates that agroecological transitions are not linear processes of technology adoption, but socially embedded and contested transformations shaped by multiple factors. While FRNs play a critical role, sustaining and scaling these transitions requires complementary investments beyond the scope of the FRNs.

items.title: Editorial: The science of birding in Africa
items.abstract: Birding in Africa plays an increasingly important role in biodiversity monitoring, conservation planning, and environmental policy. The Research Topic, The Science of Birding in Africa, brings together studies that demonstrate how field observation, citizen science, ecological research, and emerging technologies contribute to evidence-based conservation across the continent. The articles in this collection highlight the scientific value of birding and its growing relevance for national and regional biodiversity frameworks, including protected area management, species-action planning, and community-based conservation.Bird Assemblages, Habitat Quality, and Land-Use Pressures A central theme across the contributions is the need for robust, long-term monitoring systems to inform conservation decisions. African countries face rapid land-use change, climate impacts, and biodiversity loss, making reliable data essential for meeting obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity, the African-Eurasian Waterbird Agreement, and national red-listing processes.One contribution examines seasonal variation, habitat protection, and disturbance effects on bird assemblages in the tropical Guinea Savanna (Ibrahim et al.). By quantifying how bird communities respond to habitat integrity and disturbance regimes, the authors provide insights directly relevant to landuse planning and protected area management.Another study documents a possible short-term but large-scale range contraction of the Brown-headed Parrot in Malawi (Chirwa et al.). As a cavity-dependent species, its decline signals broader ecosystem changes affecting forest structure and availability of nesting sites. The results highlight the urgency of targeted habitat protection and monitoring of cavity-nesting species.Community engagement and citizen science emerge as powerful tools for conservation in several contributions. The article Capacity building as a pathway to indigenous participation in tropical birding and citizen science (Ivande et al.) shows how inclusive approaches strengthen data quality, build local capacity, and enhance long-term sustainability of monitoring programs.Complementing this, the Opinion article Bridging Citizen Science and Policy for Bird Conservation in Africa (Iniuman et al.) highlights how atlas data can inform national conservation frameworks, guide species assessments, and support environmental decision-making. The authors illustrate how citizenscience generated data, when standardized and validated, can complement professional surveys and fill critical knowledge gaps.Species-specific ecological studies also contribute important insights. The research on nest-site selection and breeding ecology of the Wattled Crane in the Bale Mountains (Desta et al.) provides information essential for managing one of Africa's most threatened crane species. By identifying habitat requirements and breeding constraints, the study supports targeted conservation actions within Ethiopia's protected area network.Threatened species monitoring is further highlighted in the study on critically endangered vultures in N'Djamena, Chad (Djekadjim et al.). By documenting abundance, distribution, and threats, the authors provide urgently needed data for regional vulture conservation strategies. Their findings have direct implications for anti-poisoning campaigns, carcass management policies, and cross-border conservation initiatives.Urban environments, often overlooked in African conservation planning, are addressed in the study Large language models enable large-scale analysis of human-bird relationships in South African cities (Naidoo and Reynolds). By applying artificial intelligence to understand public perceptions and interactions with birds, the authors open new avenues for integrating social data into urban biodiversity policy.The Topic also includes methodological advances that support conservation science. The AfriAtlas R package (Danmallam, Brooks and Ottosson) offers automated visualization tools for African bird atlas data, enabling researchers and policymakers to interpret spatial patterns more efficiently.Complementing this, the study Ecological traits as predictors of avian reporting rates and monitoring gaps using iNaturalist data from Nigeria (Ringim et al.) demonstrates how citizen science platforms can reveal biases and gaps in monitoring coverage.The article Avifauna richness and detection reliability between structured scientific surveys and citizen science data (Afrifa et al.) evaluates the strengths and limitations of different monitoring approaches. Their findings support the integration of citizen science into national monitoring frameworks while emphasizing the continued importance of structured surveys for high-precision assessments.A brief research report on Fire-crested Alethes following humans and Bushbuck in Uganda's Budongo Forest (Freymann and Taylor) offers intriguing behavioural insights with potential implications for understanding human-wildlife interactions in protected forests.Together, these contributions illustrate the breadth and vitality of birding science in Africa. They also reveal that the field is developing at different stages across the continent: some regions continue to emphasize basic ecological research, others are expanding citizen-science participation and its integration into conservation practice. This diversity of approaches reflects both regional priorities and emerging opportunities, making it especially valuable for future editions of this Research Topic to explore how birding science continues to develop, connect, and diversify across Africa. The Topic demonstrates that birding is not only a scientific practice but also a strategic tool for achieving conservation outcomes across diverse African landscapes. We thank all authors for their valuable contributions and the reviewers for their thoughtful evaluations. We also acknowledge the Frontiers editorial team for their support. It has been a pleasure to co-edit this Research Topic, and we hope this collection will serve as a resource for researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and birding communities across Africa.

items.title: Moss Diversity and Soil Nature in Established Plots in the Montane Forest of Mt. Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary, La Union, San Isidro, Davao Oriental
items.abstract: The one-way effect of moss diversity on soil properties was investigated using belt transects in two established 1-ha plots located at 920–1,160masl in the montane forest of Mt. Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary, San Isidro, Davao Oriental. Moss species were identified, and diversity, dominance, and relative abundance were determined. Soil properties were assessed based on soil type, temperature, moisture, pH, and NPK macronutrient levels. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to determine relationships between moss diversity and soil physicochemical parameters. A total of 28 moss taxa from six orders and ten families were recorded, with 20 species identified in Plot 1 and 21 in Plot 2. The mean Shannon diversity index was 1.68, indicating moderately high diversity, while the mean Pielou’s evenness and McIntosh dominance indices were 0.55 and 0.83, respectively. Trismegistia calderensis and Braunfelsia sp. were the most abundant species. Most mosses occurred on epigeous or tree-based substrates rather than on the ground. Both plots had clay loam soil. Mean soil temperatures were 19.7°C and 21.5°C, while soil moisture values were 1.05% and 1.07%, and pH values were 5.4 and 5.3. NPK levels varied between plots. Correlations between moss diversity and soil parameters differed between plots, particularly for NPK. Temperature showed no correlation in either plot. Overall, the findings suggest that moss diversity influences certain soil properties through ecosystem functions rather than solely through direct substrate contact, supporting the ecological and functional importance of mosses in montane forest ecosystems.

items.title: Unstable carbon sink growth in alpine grasslands of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau
items.abstract: Introduction Alpine grasslands on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP) are central to regional carbon cycling and climate regulation. Although warming and increasing precipitation have driven widespread greening and greater carbon uptake, it remains uncertain whether these gains are accompanied by greater ecosystem stability. Methods We examined carbon sink capacity and temporal variability using net ecosystem productivity (NEP) and proportional variability (PV), and assessed recovery resilience indirectly using lag-one autocorrelation (TAC) as a conditional proxy. Grasslands were classified into eight types based on the trend directions of NEP, PV, and TAC. Multivariate spatial regressions were used to examine hydroclimatic associations with these trends. Results Annual NEP increased across 81.7% of the grassland area between 2000 and 2024, with significant increases (p < 0.05) across 31.7%. Plateau-scale mean annual NEP increased significantly at 0.553 g C m ⁻² yr ⁻² (p = 0.006). Regional mean PV and TAC also increased, indicating greater temporal fluctuations and potentially slower recovery under the assumptions underlying TAC. Robust sinks (T1), with increasing NEP and declining PV and TAC, covered 20.2% of grasslands, whereas 61.6% belonged to T2–T4, where increasing NEP co-occurred with rising PV, TAC, or both. Vulnerable sinks were the largest category (32.6%) and were concentrated in semi-arid alpine steppes and alpine deserts, whereas robust sinks occurred mainly in eastern alpine meadows. Mean annual precipitation was the strongest predictor associated with NEP trends, and vapor pressure deficit was the strongest predictor associated with PV and TAC trends. Discussion Stronger carbon uptake does not necessarily translate into a more stable ecosystem. Evaluating carbon uptake together with temporal variability and conditional resilience indicators can inform assessments of QTP alpine grasslands under climate stress.

items.title: Double gravity-assist rendezvous trajectory to Halley’s comet using deep-space low thrust
items.abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. A rendezvous trajectory would overcome this limitation, but the design is challenging due to the limitations of current propulsion technology. Given the lead times of spacecraft development and the long duration of the interplanetary transfer to the comet, it is imperative to start mission planning as soon as possible. We present a novel rendezvous strategy, combining unpowered Jupiter and Saturn gravity-assists with deep-space low-thrust arcs. It minimizes launch energy and propellant budget, constraining the arrival to occur before the onset of high activity. The double flyby strategy reduces the otherwise prohibitive cost of the plane change maneuver. Closed expressions for the optimal flyby geometry, together with an explicit low-thrust transcription technique, reduce the number of design parameter to three, improving computational efficiency. Crucially, this is the first rendezvous mission concept achievable with well-proven technology (standard radioisotope thermoelectric generators and an ion thruster) and compatible with several existing launchers. We describe the trajectory optimization strategy and perform a comprehensive exploration of the design space. Finally, we present two promising proof-of-concept trajectories in detail.

items.title: Spatially Resolved Cell-Fate Engineering through Nanoneedle-Mediated Optoporation
items.abstract: The development of advanced tissue models demands spatially resolved control over cell fate to provide deeper insights into complex biological processes, yet precise intracellular manipulation remains a critical bottleneck in cellular engineering strategies. Current approaches for gene delivery struggle in achieving the required localized resolution to control individual cell fate, while optogenetic approaches are constrained by the requirement for complex genetic engineering and limited modes of gene regulation. Here, we show that nanoneedle-mediated optoporation enables spatially resolved intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, locally directing cell fate. Through computational modeling and experimental validation, we investigated the dependence of electromagnetic field enhancement on wavelength, nanoneedle geometry, and porosity. We demonstrated the importance of surface chemistry for optoporation efficiency, achieving optimal transfection performance through thermal carbonization. This approach achieves efficient delivery for propidium iodide, 500 kDa dextran, and siRNA, alongside a 72% mRNA transfection efficiency, resulting in sustained protein expression after 24 h. Selective SNAIL1 mRNA transfection demonstrated localized cell-fate engineering, inducing a targeted epithelial to mesenchymal transition. This porous nanoneedle system presents a versatile and flexible approach for precise genetic manipulation through electromagnetic field tunability, offering new possibilities for studying complex biological processes and disease progression through spatially resolved control of cell fate.

items.title: Bearing, heading and the perceptual geometry of collective motion
items.abstract: Traditional models of collective motion commonly assume that animals turn to match their neighbours' directions of travel. In the harmonic theory, decisions follow from a neural representation of direction, and a neighbour enters only as a stimulus at a bearing, the direction in which it lies. Here we show that a neighbour's spatial extent allows its orientation to enter through projection geometry alone, and the theory generates a matrix of coupling coefficients indexed by the neighbour's bearing and aspect. Responses to bearing alone form one edge of this matrix, and classical heading matching is a special case on its diagonal, one ray through a two-parameter family. Independently, an animal that responds only to neighbour position, perceived with a delay, acquires an alignment coefficient set by the slope of its distance-weighted attraction profile, so that it can align, anti-align or reverse sign. Alignment need not be a rule to be measured. In schooling fish and walking pigeons with body orientation measured independently of travel, social responses are recovered, including bearing responses in the fish. Heading excess depends on how turning is measured, appearing in the fish with forward but not centred responses and remaining unresolved in pigeons. Controls show why neither outcome identifies a direct alignment rule. In fish recordings with motion-assigned body polarity, heading-dependent structure departs from Vicsek form and fails the coefficient test for a common angular potential. Whether animals align thereby becomes a measurable question, with geometric, perceptual and behavioural origins that can be distinguished.

items.title: The Composition of M-dwarf Exoplanet Hosts: Atmospheric Parameters and O, Mg, Si, and Fe Abundances from IR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Determining M-dwarf abundances is an important step to discerning the chemical evolution of the Milky Way and characterizing exoplanetary systems, especially since these objects commonly host small exoplanets. However, a dearth of M-dwarf abundance measurements exist compared to Sun-like stars, partially due to their complicated optical spectra dominated by molecular absorption lines and low luminosities. To overcome these issues, we have obtained high resolution H-band spectra of 40 planet-hosting M-dwarf stars and 2 M-dwarfs in wide binaries with FGK primaries with IGRINS on Gemini South and on the McDonald Observatory 2.7m telescope, and NIRSPEC on Keck. Abundances were derived by comparing each observed spectrum to synthetic spectral grids generated with MOOG and MARCS atmospheric models. Effective temperatures were derived using OH and H$_{2}$O lines and [Fe/H] from Fe I and FeH lines. Both Mg and Si abundances were determined using atomic features. Overall, we find that our abundances are broadly consistent with previous literature M-dwarf abundances. We complemented our abundances analysis with UVW velocities and Milky Way stellar population membership probabilities and identified 2 potential thick disk stars from our kinematic and chemical analysis: GJ 1252 and L181-1 which was a previously known thick disk star. Kinematic stellar population probabilities and a low [Fe/H] abundance makes Kepler 42 a likely thick disk star, although uncertain Mg and Si abundances make classification difficult. Lastly, we have determined Si/Mg and Fe/Mg molar ratios for M-dwarf exoplanet hosts and find the abundance distributions leads to exoplanet core-mass fractions between 20 - 40$\%$.

items.title: Permutation order governs basin entropy in critical one-input Boolean networks
items.abstract: Basin entropy measures uncertainty about a network's long-term behavior. For every critical one-input synchronous Boolean network with $m$ relevant nodes, we show that the permutation structure induced by its feedback loops determines basin entropy, up to a universal error. Although the loops oscillate independently, their relative phases can be offset, producing a deviation from additivity that can grow linearly in $m$. Yet at the ensemble level, a previously derived additive prediction is preserved through the first subleading term, with the discrepancy appearing at order $\ln m\ln\ln m$.

items.title: 3C-guided reflection combined with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among nursing students: a mixed methods study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Humanistic care is essential to nursing practice and directly influences patient outcomes. Since nursing students constitute the future clinical workforce, cultivating humanistic care competencies is an educational responsibility rather than a solely clinical issue. However, current training often faces challenges such as disconnection between theory and practice, highlighting the need for effective teaching models. Based on reflective practice theory, this study evaluates a multicomponent educational intervention integrating 3 C (Context, Content, Course) guided reflection with scenario simulation for humanistic care education among undergraduate nursing students. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was employed. In the first phase, all seven intact classes of first-year nursing students (total n = 350) from a medical university in Guizhou Province were included and randomly assigned using a random number table at the class level to either the intervention group (4 classes, n = 200) or the control group (3 classes, n = 150). The intervention group received a single, integrated 160-minute classroom-based session consisting of 40 min of theoretical instruction, 40 min of scenario simulation, 40 min of 3 C-guided reflection, and 40 min of summary and assessment activities, whereas the control group received traditional theoretical instruction within a 160-minute session that also included assessment activities. Outcomes were assessed using the Caring Ability Inventory, theoretical knowledge tests, and satisfaction questionnaires. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for class-level clustering; CAI models additionally adjusted for the corresponding baseline scores. In the second phase, 40 nursing students were purposively selected from the intervention group for semi-structured in-depth interviews, and data were analyzed thematically. Results The intervention group had a higher immediate post-intervention score on the self-report Caring Ability Inventory (CAI) than the control group (adjusted mean difference = 19.68 points, 95% CI 17.04–22.33; standardized effect size = 1.65; P < 0.001). Higher self-reported CAI scores were also observed for the Understanding, Courage, and Patience subscales. The intervention group also had a higher immediate post-intervention theoretical knowledge score (mean difference = 4.80 points, 95% CI 0.72–8.88, P = 0.021). Learner evaluations of the intervention were generally favorable. Qualitative analysis revealed four themes: empathy awakening, cognitive reconstruction through structured reflection, courage cultivation, and conceptual shift toward professional caring. Conclusion This sequential explanatory mixed methods study (a cluster randomized trial plus qualitative interviews) provides preliminary evidence that the multicomponent 3 C-guided scenario simulation model is associated with higher immediate post-intervention self-reported CAI scores and theoretical knowledge scores among undergraduate nursing students following a single-session intervention. Qualitative findings provided complementary insights into students’ experiences; however, the study design cannot establish long-term causality or sustained competency development. The independent contribution of 3C-guided reflection cannot be determined from this multicomponent intervention. The potential role of the “experience–reflection–abstraction” cycle warrants further investigation through multi-center, longitudinal studies incorporating objective behavioral assessments.

items.title: E-MODULE BIOLENDO BERBASIS INKUIRI TERBIMBING BERMUATAN POTENSI LOKAL UNTUK MENINGKATKAN BERPIKIR KREATIF DAN KOLABORASI SISWA
items.abstract: This research was motivated by the low creative thinking and collaboration skills of students in science subjects due to the minimal use of digital teaching materials and the lack of integration of local potential in learning. To address this issue, this study aimed to develop the BIOLENDO e-module based on guided inquiry integrated with the local potential of galendo on Ecology and Biodiversity topics. This study employed the Research and Development (R&D) method using the Lee and Owens model with a quasi-experimental Non-equivalent Control Group Design involving seventh-grade students at MTs Darul Ulum, Ciamis Regency. The results revealed that the average N-gain for creative thinking in the experimental class reached 0.514 (moderate category), which was significantly superior to the control class at 0.377 (t=4.005;df=58;p<0.001), with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.034). Furthermore, students' collaboration skills showed a marked improvement from an initial baseline of 55.00% to 80.06%, placing it in the high category. Thus, the BIOLENDO e-module is proven to be valid, practical, and effective in enhancing creative thinking skills as well as supporting students' collaborative capabilities. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan berpikir kreatif dan kolaborasi peserta didik pada mata pelajaran IPA akibat minimnya pemanfaatan bahan ajar digital serta belum terintegrasinya potensi lokal dalam pembelajaran. Untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut, penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan e-module BIOLENDO berbasis inkuiri terbimbing bermuatan potensi lokal galendo pada materi Ekologi dan Keanekaragaman Hayati yang teruji valid, praktis, dan efektif. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development (R&D) model Lee dan Owens dengan desain eksperimen semu Non-equivalent Control Group Design pada peserta didik kelas VII MTs Darul Ulum Kabupaten Ciamis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata N-gain berpikir kreatif kelas eksperimen mencapai 0,514 (kategori sedang), lebih unggul dibandingkan kelas kontrol sebesar 0,377 (kategori sedang), dengan perbedaan signifikan secara statistik (t=4,005;df=58;p<0,001) serta effect size Cohen's d sebesar 1,034 (efek besar). Sementara itu, kemampuan kolaborasi peserta didik meningkat nyata dari kondisi awal sebesar 55,00% menjadi 80,06% pada akhir pembelajaran dan berada pada kategori tinggi. Dengan demikian, e-module BIOLENDO terbukti valid, praktis, dan efektif dalam meningkatkan kemampuan berpikir kreatif serta mengoptimalkan kolaborasi peserta didik.

items.title: FinMamba: Market-Aware Graph Enhanced Multi-Level Mamba for Stock Movement Prediction
items.abstract: Recently, combining stock features with inter-stock correlations has become a common and effective approach for stock movement prediction. However, financial data presents significant challenges due to its low signal-to-noise ratio and the dynamic complexity of the market, which give rise to two key limitations in existing methods. First, the relationships between stocks are highly influenced by multifaceted factors including macroeconomic market dynamics, and current models fail to adaptively capture these evolving interactions under specific market conditions. Second, for the accuracy and timeliness required by real-world trading, existing financial data mining methods struggle to extract beneficial pattern-oriented dependencies from long historical data while maintaining high efficiency and low memory consumption. To address the limitations, we propose FinMamba, a Mamba-GNN-based framework for market-aware and multi-level hybrid stock movement prediction. Specifically, we devise a dynamic graph to learn the changing representations of inter-stock relationships by integrating a pruning module that adapts to market trends. Afterward, with a selective mechanism, the multi-level Mamba discards irrelevant information and resets states to skillfully recall historical patterns across multiple time scales with linear time costs, which are then jointly optimized for reliable prediction. Extensive experiments on U.S. and Chinese stock markets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed FinMamba, achieving state-of-the-art prediction accuracy and trading profitability, while maintaining low computational complexity. The code is available at https://github.com/TROUBADOUR000/FinMamba.

items.title: ContextClaim: A Context-Driven Paradigm for Verifiable Claim Detection
items.abstract: Automated fact-checking pipelines typically begin with a filtering stage that decides which claims are worth verifying, given that the later evidence retrieval and verification components are expensive to apply at scale. A central task in this stage is verifiable claim detection, which asks whether a statement is in principle checkable against external evidence. Prior work on this task, as well as on the closely related notion of check-worthiness, conditions its decisions only on the claim sentence itself. We argue that this is restrictive, because deciding whether a statement is checkable often depends on identifying the entities and events it mentions, and on whether external information about them is actually available in the first place. Motivated by how downstream verification systems rely on retrieved evidence, we move retrieval upstream into the detection stage and introduce ContextClaim. Given an input claim, the approach identifies entity mentions, queries Wikipedia as a structured background source, and uses large language models to compress the retrieved material into short contextual summaries that are then passed to a classifier. Experiments are conducted on two domains and genres, namely the CheckThat! 2022 Twitter collection and the PoliClaim corpus of political debates, and cover both encoder and decoder only models under fine-tuning, zero-shot, and few-shot settings. The added context yields gains on verifiable claim detection in several configurations, although the size of the improvement varies with the dataset, the backbone model, and the training setup. We further find that the same retrieved summaries are useful beyond detection. Feeding them into a downstream verification model on FEVER improves verification F1. Component level analyses, human annotation, and error inspection further clarify the conditions under which retrieved context helps, and where it does not.

items.title: Culture or cognition?
items.abstract: Abstract Gender languages assign nouns to a category, such as masculine, feminine, neuter or common. Gender assignment is complicated and difficult to learn, as languages do not have specific rules for assigning a noun to one or the other gender. This study looks at gender assignment from the perspective of semantics and lexical semantic evolution, exemplified on the Indo-European family. Gender assignment has a semantic core, in which animate nouns are more likely to be masculine, inanimate nouns feminine and neuter, nature nouns masculine, and culture nouns feminine or neuter. To investigate how these patterns emerge, we study the evolutionary dynamics of these semantic properties on a gender-coded lexical data set for Indo-European. We find that masculine is a stable gender that remains in its semantic category and does not change. Feminine is also a stable category which may get lost or transfer to masculine. Neuter and common are unstable categories, which continuously alter or get lost in gender assignment. In sum, our result shows that the semantic core of gender — affected both by cognitive and cultural factors — remains stable and does not vacillate in evolution.

items.title: Understanding Biodiversity in Acer Forests: From Species Diversity to Sustainable Conservation
items.abstract: The genus Acer comprises more than 110 tree and shrub species distributed throughout the Northern Hemisphere and represents an important component of temperate forest ecosystems. This review evaluates biodiversity patterns, ecological functions, environmental pressures, and conservation approaches associated with Acer forests. A systematic literature search conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases on 20 January 2026, without publication-year restrictions. After screening and eligibility assessment, 688 publications were included and analyzed using bibliometric methods and qualitative thematic synthesis. The literature increased substantially over the last four decades, with climate change, biodiversity conservation, forest dynamics, and sustainable management among the principal research themes. The selected studies covered species and genetic diversity, forest composition and dynamics, associated plant, fungal, and animal communities, environmental change, and conservation and management. Native Acer forests were frequently associated with structurally complex habitats, diverse understory communities, nutrient cycling, and multiple ecosystem functions, whereas habitat loss, fragmentation, climate change, atmospheric pollution, and biological invasions were identified as major pressures. Introduced species, particularly Acer negundo, were also frequently examined in relation to impacts on native biodiversity. Important research gaps concerned poorly studied endemic species, long-term monitoring, multitrophic interactions, and the effectiveness of conservation measures under environmental change. Future research should integrate ecological, genetic, physiological, and remote-sensing approaches to support evidence-based conservation and sustainable management of Acer forests. This review provides a systematic and bibliometric synthesis of the indexed English-language literature retrieved using the specified search strategy and identifies major research patterns, evidence gaps, and conservation priorities relevant to Acer forests biodiversity under environmental change.

items.title: Decompression With or Without Fusion Across Subgroups With Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis : A Target Trial Emulation.
items.abstract: Background Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. Objective To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. Design Cohort study using the target trial framework. Setting Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. Patients Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months. Intervention Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. Measurements The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. Results Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m 2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. Limitation Possible residual confounding. Conclusion Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. items.title: Mapping three decades of consciousness research in neuroscience: a scientometric synthesis of intellectual evolution and emerging frontiers.
items.abstract: Over the past three decades, consciousness research in neuroscience has expanded into a broad and increasingly diverse field. Despite significant progress, a quantitative understanding of how these research areas have collectively evolved has remained limited. In this study, we conducted a large-scale scientometric analysis of consciousness research in neuroscience based on 22,836 publications and 639,975 cited references retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection spanning 1998-2025. We identified three major research paths: neural correlates of conscious contents and states, internal awareness and self-consciousness, and integrative approaches bridging these two paths. Emerging hotspots included neural mechanisms of consciousness, subjective experience, disorders of consciousness (DoC), and interoception. Despite increasing boundary-spanning research across different areas, bibliometric connections between DoC and other major topics, particularly subjective experience and interoception, remain comparatively sparse. These findings provide a field-level synthesis of consciousness research in neuroscience, offering a quantitative framework for understanding its development and emerging research directions.

items.title: Exploring resident doctors' experience, attitudes, perceptions and beliefs about the serious incident investigatory process within mental health settings.
items.abstract: Background Serious incidents, such as patient suicide, profoundly impact clinicians. In mental health settings, these events are uniquely distressing. Despite policy shifts towards learning from serious incidents, many doctors report inadequate support and significant emotional distress. Resident doctors, already vulnerable to burnout and emotional exhaustion, are particularly at risk. Aims This study aimed to understand resident psychiatry doctors' experiences of serious incidents. It sought to gather in-depth insights about how resident psychiatrists navigate the serious incident process, and the effect the process has on their professional and personal lives. Method A qualitative study recruited 10 participants via email in 1 National Health Service (NHS) trust. Semi-structured online interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, employing an iterative, constant comparative approach. Results Descriptive characteristics of the participants are reported. Three overarching themes were identified: (a) when the process becomes the experience, with subthemes focusing on how open and transparent the investigation process was, about communication during the process and how doctors felt the process impacted their clinical role; (b) from theory to practice: when training meets reality. Subthemes here reflected on whether resident doctors felt prepared and knowledgeable about the process. There was also focus on the experience itself being a learning opportunity; (c) the emotional undercurrents: trauma, grief and support. Here the subthemes focused on the emotional toll of an incident and investigation, the grief and wider impact of a patient death and lastly, the need for support to resident doctors including supervisor and peer-to-peer support. Themes are reported accompanied by verbatim quotes from participants. Conclusions Findings confirm prior studies investigating the negative impact of serious incidents on resident doctors' well-being and career confidence, highlighting the need for robust support. The study adds to the literature through emphasising the inadequacy of current support and highlights rectifiable issues such as the need for structured peer support and improved supervisor/resident training for emotional and professional complexities. Future research should compare these findings with experiences under the new Patient Safety Incident Framework (PSIRF) system to assess improvements.

items.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Maternal-Infant (Dyadic) Attachment, Postpartum Depression, and Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Purpose This scoping review explores intersecting relationships among the concepts of postpartum depression, maternal-infant (dyadic) attachment (or bonding), and breastfeeding self-efficacy within postpartum populations and how often these concept relationships are examined among predominantly historically marginalized populations (non-White, low-income, low education level). Background To address the ongoing public health concern of postpartum depression, we must understand its relationship with dyadic attachment and breastfeeding self-efficacy. Discussion Four studies met inclusion criteria, examining the relationships between the concepts of postpartum depression, dyadic attachment, and breastfeeding self-efficacy. Because these 4 studies had heterogeneous study designs, study measures, and study time points, the exact nature of the relationship between these 3 concepts is difficult to parse. Furthermore, only 1 study evaluated these concepts in historically marginalized populations (low-income). Future research using rigorous study design approaches is warranted. Implications for research and practice While studies found a relationship between increased breastfeeding self-efficacy and increased dyadic attachment, mixed results remain regarding the relationships between postpartum depression and dyadic attachment or breastfeeding self-efficacy. Nevertheless, dyad-focused interventions have shown the potential to improve breastfeeding self-efficacy and dyadic attachment while reducing postpartum depression. The scoping review findings suggest that these concepts collectively need more research attention, given their potential effects on improving maternal-child dyadic outcomes.

items.title: Medicating inhibitory control? Treatment with serotonergic antidepressants predicts stop-N200 amplitudes in major depressive disorder.
items.abstract: Background Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent chronic mental illness often treated by serotonergic pharmacotherapy and complicated by sex differences and comorbid anxiety disorders (COMs). Deficits in inhibitory control are a transdiagnostic feature of MDD and COM, though the presentation of these deficits may be impacted by competing cognitive demands, symptoms severity, sexes, and medication status. Methods This project includes 233 participants from the Tulsa 1000 study who completed concurrent electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic functional resonance imaging (MRI) during a stop signal task (SST). We examined how serotonergic antidepressants, biological sex, and comorbidity with an anxiety disorder uniquely relate to neural indices of inhibitory control for healthy controls (HCs), MDD, and COM using linear mixed effect models, type III ANOVAs, and optimal full propensity matching. N200, P300, and correct-related negativity (CRN) components were extracted and analyzed to index conflict monitoring, conflict resolution, and performance monitoring, respectively, in response to stop signals and their absence. Results Our results revealed that HCs exhibited larger stop-P300 amplitudes than MDD and COM ( η 2 = 0.068); females had smaller stop-N200 amplitudes than males ( η 2 = 0.027); MDD/COM participants taking a serotonergic antidepressant exhibited less negative N200 amplitudes than those who were not (LME, B = 1.95; η 2 = 0.044; ATE, B = 2.47). Conclusions Our findings suggest being treated with serotonergic antidepressants are associated with neural differences in the conflict monitoring of inhibitory control in pure and comorbid depression.

items.title: Dietary fibre intake and suicide in Japanese adults: the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study.
items.abstract: Dietary fibre intake has been reported to be inversely associated with depression in a meta-analysis. However, most studies were cross-sectional, and none examined the association with suicide, a severe outcome of depression. We investigated the association of dietary fibre intake with suicide risk among Japanese adults. Participants were 40 630 men and 48 178 women aged 44-76 years who responded to the second survey (baseline of the present study) of the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study (1995-1998). Dietary fibre intake was assessed using a validated FFQ. Hazard ratios of suicide through December 2018 were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis. During a mean follow-up of 18·7 years, we identified 459 deaths from suicide. Dietary fibre intake was associated with lower suicide risk after adjustment for covariates, including intakes of vitamin B12, vitamin D, Ca, Zn and n-3 PUFA. The multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for suicide of the highest v. lowest quartile of total dietary fibre intake was 0·65 (95 % CI 0·46-0·93). Similar inverse associations were observed for vegetable and fruit fibre intake but not cereal or bean fibre. However, these associations were substantially attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for nutrients highly correlated with dietary fibre intake, including folate, vitamin B6, Mg and Fe; the corresponding value for total dietary fibre intake was 0·85 (95 % CI 0·55-1·31). Our findings suggest that greater consumption of foods rich in dietary fibre and related nutrients, rather than dietary fibre per se, may play a protective role against suicide.

items.title: An analysis of 20 years of retracted articles in psychiatry.
items.abstract: To characterise recent trends in retractions of publications in the psychiatric literature. We examined the Retraction Watch Database for publications with the subject term 'psychiatry' between 2003 and 2023. We then characterised publication type, subject, country of origin, reason for retraction and time between publication and retraction. A total of 315 psychiatry publications were retracted; the annual number and rate (relative to publications) rose steadily across the study period. The median number of days from publication to retraction was 643 (interquartile range 223.0-2966.0). Reasons for retraction were unclear in 20 (6.3%) cases only; most commonly they were attributed to data error (42.5%) or problems relating to peer review (11.4%) - the period between publication and retraction was particularly long for the latter studies (median 3082 days, interquartile range 575-3364). A total of 4.4% were retracted because of falsification, and 6.32% because of plagiarism. Retracted items frequently focused on mood disorders (24.4%), psychosis (14.9%) and neurodevelopmental disorders (13.7%). Clinicians and policy makers rely on academic literature, but should be aware of the ethical, legal, business and professional dilemmas often encountered, yet not reported, in the process of considering retractions of unreliable data. Contested and unreliable findings may persist in the scientific record, with potential negative consequences for evidence based-care and policy, including the erosion of public trust.

items.title: Inflammatory signature of subcutaneous fat after weight loss and regain in women undergoing repeated bariatric surgery.
items.abstract: Repeated metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS, r-BS) represents 10-25% of all MBS and is commonly-performed for weight regain after prior significant weight-loss. It remains unclear how adipose tissue adapts to surgically-induced weight-loss-regain in obesity. We hypothesized that compared to primary bariatric surgery (p-BS), women undergoing r-BS exhibit a distinct adipose tissue signature. Subcutaneous/visceral adipose tissues (SAT/VAT, respectively) from female MBS patients were assessed histologically/molecularly/functionally (activation of human microglia cells by SAT-secretome). Elective MBS in a public university hospital. Women undergoing either p-BS, or r-BS with documented >15% weight-loss after prior MBS. MBS. Inflammation in SAT. Women undergoing r-BS (n=21) trended to be older than those undergoing p-BS (n=35)(47.2 vs. 40.5y, p=0.06), with a lower BMI (42.3 vs. 45.6 kg/m2, respectively, p=0.103), and a trend for improved cardiometabolic risk parameters (fasting insulin, CRP and HDL-c). Adipocyte size, adipose tissue fibrosis, macrophage and crown-like structures abundance were similar, while mast-cells were slightly more prevalent in r-BS. Single-nucleus RNA-seq-based deconvolution algorithm applied unto bulk RNA-seq confirmed the absence of a major shift in adipose tissue cell-type composition. Yet, RNA-seq revealed unique transcriptome of r-BS SAT, with activation of inflammatory pathways. Consistently, SAT explants from r-BS secreted higher protein concentrations of NFκB-regulated cytokines IL6/IL8. Functional impact of the more inflammatory-secretome was suggested by its increased ability to inflammatory-activate human microglia cells. Prior BS-induced weight-loss and subsequent regain in women is associated with inflammatory transcriptome and secretome of SAT that can activate cultured human microglia cells.

items.title: Predictors of Antibiotic Overuse in Febrile Children: A Sub-analysis of the Prospective, Multicenter AutoPilot-Dx Study.
items.abstract: Antibiotic overuse contributes to antimicrobial resistance. Mechanisms that drive overuse, including diagnostic uncertainty, are thought to be complex. We aimed to investigate predictive factors for antibiotic overuse in a large pediatric cohort. This is a subanalysis from the AutoPilot-Dx study, which enrolled febrile children 90 days to 18 years old presenting to the pediatric emergency department with respiratory tract infection or fever without source, including both hospitalized children and those discharged home. We analyzed patient flow from being treated with antibiotics at recruitment to definitive antibiotic treatment after assessment, depending on physician judgment. Variables significantly associated with antibiotic overuse in univariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to identify independent predictors of antibiotic overuse, defined as receipt of antibiotic treatment following clinical assessment in cases with viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis. Diagnostic uncertainty was assessed by treating physicians. Upon recruitment, 127/1008 (12.6%) were receiving antibiotic treatment. Overall, 186 of 628 cases with a viral panel-adjudicated diagnosis were judged to have antibiotic overuse. Factors with significant association in univariate analysis were diagnostic uncertainty, nonexudative tonsillitis, rales and younger age. Presence of a diagnostic test result upon presentation to the hospital and current antibiotic treatment were found not to be associated with overuse. Among 566 of 1008 cases with complete data on all model covariates, multivariable logistic regression yielded diagnostic uncertainty [odds ratio (OR), 2.09; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-3.93; P = 0.015], nonexudative tonsillitis (OR, 2.78; 95% CI: 1.72-4.59; P < 0.001) and rales (OR, 1.82; 95% CI: 1.15-2.86; P = 0.01) to be positively associated with antibiotic overuse, while age showed a negative association in complete-case analysis (OR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.85-0.99; P = 0.038), which attenuated and was no longer significant in a multiple imputation sensitivity analysis (OR, 0.96; 95% CI: 0.91-1.01; P = 0.150). Diagnostic uncertainty contributes to antibiotic overuse, alongside clinical factors. Future studies should investigate the impact of improved diagnostic algorithms on antibiotic prescribing in patients with respiratory tract infections in whom physicians experience diagnostic uncertainty.

items.title: Prognostic Value and Clinical Outcomes of Spread through Air Spaces in Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study in Türkiye.
items.abstract: Spread through air spaces (STAS), first described in lung adenocarcinomas in 2013, has been identified as a prognostic factor in numerous studies. We investigated the prognostic effect of STAS positivity and its potential role in staging and treatment strategies. We retrospectively reviewed prospectively collected data from patients who underwent surgery at our hospital and were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma between 2018 and 2021. Patients were classified into 2 groups, STAS-negative and STAS-positive. Overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) were compared between the groups. Of the 480 patients, 123 (25.6%) were STAS-positive. STAS positivity was associated with significantly worse survival outcomes in early-stage disease, although this association diminished in stage III. Mean DFS was 50.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 47.7-52.4) in the STAS-negative group and 35.1 months (95% CI, 31.2-39.1) in the STAS-positive group (p<0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, STAS positivity was an independent adverse prognostic factor for both OS and DFS, with hazard ratios of 1.574 and 2.345, respectively. Analyses stratified by stage showed that the prognostic impact of STAS positivity was strongest in stage I disease, in which it was associated with worse OS, DFS, and LRFS; formal interaction testing supported this finding. In early-stage disease, STAS is a significant adverse prognostic factor. This finding suggests that early-stage STAS-positive tumors may warrant upstaging in future staging systems and that STAS status may help individualize surgical and follow-up strategies.
